L41: ## I. Executive Summary
L42: ## 1. Overview
L43: ## 1.1. Summary of Regulatory Action
L44: The Applicant (Ionis Pharmaceuticals) submitted an NDA for donidalorsen (proposed tradename: Dawnzera), an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) targeting prekallikrein mRNA, for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and adolescent patients 12 years and older at a dose of 80 mg subcutaneous (SC) every 4 weeks; a dosing interval of once every (b) (4) may be considered (b) (4).
L45: The ASO is conjugated to a ligand containing three N-acetylglucosamine (GalNAc) residues to enable delivery of the ASO to hepatocytes, where prekallikrein is synthesized, supporting a lower dose than for nonconjugated ASOs. The NDA was reviewed by a multidisciplinary review team; no issues were identified from any discipline that preclude approval.
L46: Substantial evidence of effectiveness of donidalorsen in patients with HAE was established using data from a single adequate and well-controlled trial (CS5) studying two dosing regimens (80 mg every 4 weeks [Q4W] and 80 mg every 8 weeks [Q8W]) and placebo, and confirmatory evidence (CE) based on mechanistic data; see the description in Section 1.2. The available safety data demonstrated that donidalorsen is safe for its intended use. Anaphylaxis occurred in one subject. Common adverse reactions included injection site reactions, upper respiratory tract infection, urinary tract infection, and abdominal discomfort. Laboratory findings with donidalorsen treatment included decreased platelet counts and increased liver enzymes, consistent with the ASO class effect. The safety profile for donidalorsen is acceptable for an HAE population and can be adequately managed through labeling and further evaluated during routine pharmacovigilance. A clinical postmarketing requirement will be included with this approval to complete the ongoing multi-year open-label extension (OLE) trials (CS3 and CS7) to evaluate the potential for drug-induced liver injury with donidalorsen.
L47: Based on the positive dose response relationship of the 80 mg Q4W dosing regimen, the recommended dosage of donidalorsen is 80 mg administered subcutaneously every 4 weeks. Because Q8W also independently met the primary efficacy endpoint and some secondary endpoints a dosage of 80 mg every 8 weeks may also be considered at the discretion of the prescriber.
L48: The NDA includes appropriate preapproval nonclinical studies, but a nonclinical postmarketing requirement will be included with this approval to complete the ongoing 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats administered donidalorsen (see Section 24).
L49: The submitted clinical program is adequate to support the efficacy and safety of donidalorsen for the proposed indication. The clinical review team concludes that the reduction in acute HAE attacks observed with donidalorsen treatment compared to placebo outweighs the risks, and that
L50: donidalorsen will provide a novel option in the treatment armamentarium for HAE prophylaxis. The benefit-risk assessment is favorable and supports the approval of donidalorsen for “prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older.” The recommended dose is 80 mg administered subcutaneously every 4 weeks. A dosage of 80 mg every 8 weeks may also be considered.
L51: The action for this application will be an **Approval**, with nonclinical and clinical postmarketing requirements.
L52: ## 1.2. Conclusions on Substantial Evidence of Effectiveness
L53: Substantial evidence of effectiveness (SEE) was established with one adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation and confirmatory evidence.
L54: The single adequate and well-controlled trial (CS5), was a 24-week multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating 90 adult and adolescent subjects with HAE Type I or II. Subjects were randomized to one of the following treatment arms:
L55: - Donidalorsen 80 mg SC every 4 weeks (hereafter referred to as the donidalorsen-4 group).
- Donidalorsen 80 mg SC every 8 weeks (hereafter referred to as the donidalorsen-8 group).
- Placebo SC every 4 or 8 weeks (hereafter referred to as the pooled placebo group).
L56: Trial CS5 met its primary endpoint, demonstrating a statistically significant and clinically meaningful reduction in the number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks in the donidalorsen-4 group (least squares [LS] mean =0.44, 95% CI =0.27, 0.73) and the donidalorsen-8 group (LS mean =1.02, 95% CI =0.65, 1.59), compared to the pooled placebo group (LS mean =2.26, 95% CI =1.66, 3.09); this represents a percentage reduction in the means relative to placebo for the donidalorsen-4 group of 81% (95% CI =65%, 89%) and for the donidalorsen-8 group of 55% (95% CI =22%, 74%). These findings were supported by the results of secondary endpoints, including the proportion of subjects with a \ge 70\% reduction in attacks, attack-free subjects, moderate-to-severe HAE attacks, and HAE attacks requiring on-demand therapy. While both dosing regimens demonstrated efficacy compared to placebo, donidalorsen-4 demonstrated greater efficacy compared to donidalorsen-8 across primary and secondary endpoints.
L57: The CE providing strong mechanistic support includes the well-established pathophysiology of the disease and the mechanism of action of the therapy. Donidalorsen is conjugated to a ligand containing three GalNAc residues that target the ASO to the liver. Donidalorsen inhibits production of prekallikrein, a key protein in the contact/kallikrein-kinin system pathway that is primarily synthesized in the liver, thereby reducing the downstream production of bradykinin, the main mediator of angioedema in HAE. The mean percentage reduction from baseline to Week 24 in trough plasma prekallikrein (PKK) concentrations were 73% and 47% following treatment in the donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 groups, respectively, compared with a slight increase (2%) observed in the pooled placebo group. The mean percentage reduction from baseline at Week 4 across both treatment groups was 48%. Based on the well-understood
L58: NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
L59: pathophysiology of this genetic disease, demonstrated pharmacologic effect of donidalorsen on the kallikrein-kinin pathway, and established efficacy of numerous approved HAE therapies (for prophylaxis and acute attacks) that inhibit plasma kallikrein, the Applicant has provided adequate mechanistic data to serve as CE to support SEE for the proposed indication.
L60: Extrapolation of efficacy from adults with HAE to adolescent patients 12 to 17 years of age with HAE is supported by the identical disease pathophysiology, mechanism of action, anticipated treatment response, and clinical manifestations across age groups.
L61: Overall, SEE was demonstrated by the results from Trial CS5 and the mechanistic data provided by the Applicant. The use of a single adequate and well-controlled trial plus CE to demonstrate SEE is supported by: (1) hereditary angioedema being a rare, serious, and potentially life-threatening condition; (2) the efficacy results from the single trial are statistically significant and clinically meaningful across primary and secondary endpoints; and (3) conduct of a second trial would be infeasible. Use of a single adequate and well-controlled trial to demonstrate SEE is consistent with the approach used for other HAE drug development programs.
L62: ## 2. Benefit-Risk Assessment
L63: ## 2.1. Benefit-Risk Framework
L64: Table 2. Benefit-Risk Framework
L65: Dimension	Evidence and Uncertainties	Conclusions and Reasons
Analysis of condition	HAE is a rare condition caused by autosomal dominant mutations in the SERPING1 gene, resulting in deficiency or dysfunction of C1-INH protein.
Approximately 85% of patients have Type I HAE, characterized by low production of normal C1-INH protein. The remaining 15% of patients have Type II HAE, characterized by production of dysfunctional C1-INH. Types I and II have the same clinical phenotypes and responses to available treatments.
Insufficient quantities of functional C1-INH lead to dysregulation of the kallikrein-kinin system, a plasma protease cascade initiated by Factor XII and culminating in the generation of bradykinin. Uncontrolled bradykinin production leads to increased vascular permeability and the subcutaneous/submucosal swelling seen in acute HAE attacks.
Acute HAE attacks are sporadic, recurrent, unpredictable, and typically self-resolve after 48 to 72 hours. Attacks often involve the gastrointestinal and genitourinary tract, extremities (hands/feet), and face/upper airway. Attacks are associated with significant morbidity due to pain, impact on daily functioning, and disfigurement, and can be life-threatening in cases of laryngeal edema resulting in airway compromise.1
HAE is a rare, genetic, potentially life-threatening disease characterized by unpredictable, recurrent, and self-limited skin and submucosal swelling attacks.
The pathophysiology of the disease is well-characterized.
L66: 1 U.S. Food and Drug Administration's Patient-focused drug development meeting summary report: September 25, 2017, externally led Patient-Focused Drug Development for Hereditary Angioedema
L67: Dimension	Evidence and Uncertainties	Conclusions and Reasons
Current treatment options	No cure exists; however, there are several approved therapies for prophylaxis, as well as for on-demand treatment of acute attacks.
Approved therapies for HAE prophylaxis include plasma-derived C1-INH replacement therapies (intravenous and subcutaneous), attenuated androgens (oral), a factor Xlla inhibitor (subcutaneous), and plasma kallikrein inhibitors (oral and subcutaneous).
Although there are numerous approved prophylactic therapies for patients with HAE, the availability of additional treatment options from a new pharmacologic class is desirable.
Benefit	Efficacy for both donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 dosing regimens is based on the results from a single, adequate and well-controlled trial (CS5) in 90 adults and adolescents with Type I or II HAE. Treatment with both dosing regimens of donidalorsen resulted in statistically significant and clinically persuasive reductions in the primary endpoint, number of HAE attacks per month, throughout the 24-week Treatment Period compared to placebo.
Clinically meaningful secondary endpoints, such as number of attack-free subjects, number of moderate to severe HAE attacks, and number of attacks requiring acute treatment, further supported the beneficial treatment effect of donidalorsen compared to placebo.
Confirmatory evidence is provided by mechanistic data for the well-established role of prekallikrein in the pathophysiology of HAE attacks: this is supported by the effectiveness of approved products of the same pharmacological class (kallikrein inhibitors).
Efficacy in adolescents is based on extrapolation from adults.
Donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 dosing regimens demonstrated statistically significant and clinically relevant treatment benefits on the reduction of number of acute HAE attacks in adult and adolescent subjects with Types I and II HAE, with further support from secondary endpoints.
Donidalorsen-4 demonstrated greater efficacy than donidalorsen-8 across primary and secondary endpoints, although both dosing intervals independently met the primary efficacy endpoint.
Although both dosing regimens are being approved, based on the greater efficacy of the donidalorsen-4 dosing regimen, the recommended dosage of donidalorsen is 80 mg administered subcutaneously every 4 weeks. A dosage of 80 mg every 8 weeks may also be considered at the discretion of the prescriber.
SEE is based on efficacy results from a single adequate and well-controlled clinical trial, with confirmatory evidence from mechanistic data.

L69: Dimension	Evidence and Uncertainties	Conclusions and Reasons
Risk and risk management	Treatment-emergent adverse events that were serious, severe, or led to treatment discontinuation were rare.
Common TEAEs were injection site reactions, upper respiratory tract infection, urinary tract infection, and abdominal discomfort. The majority of TEAEs were mild or moderate in severity.
Anaphylaxis occurred in one subject.
Platelet count decreased; no donidalorsen-treated subjects had a platelet count of <50,000/mm3. No major bleeding events were associated with a low platelet count.
Increases in liver enzymes were observed.
The safety profile of donidalorsen for the proposed HAE population and intended use is favorable.
Due to the known ASO class effect of hepatotoxicity, the accumulation of ASOs in the liver over time, the small safety database, and the unknown consequences of lifetime treatment with ASOs, a clinical PMR is included with this approval to evaluate the potential for drug-induced liver injury with donidalorsen.
A nonclinical PMR is included with this approval to assess carcinogenicity.
No REMS is proposed.
The other potential risks can be managed through labeling and routine pharmacovigilance.

L71: ## 2.2. Conclusions Regarding Benefit-Risk
L72: Hereditary angioedema is a rare, autosomal dominant condition, most often caused by pathogenic variants in the *SERPING1* gene that encodes C1-esterase inhibitor (C1-INH), a serine protease-inhibitor involved in the kallikrein-kinin pathway, as well as the classical and lectin complement, contact system/intrinsic coagulation, and fibrinolytic pathways. Under homeostatic circumstances, activated Factor XII (FXIIa) triggers the kallikrein-kinin system, resulting in the downstream production of bradykinin, a potent vasodilator and enhancer of vascular permeability. C1-INH normally serves as an inhibitory check on the system by inhibiting both kallikrein and FXIIa; in the absence of sufficient quantities of functional C1-INH, bradykinin production is relatively unchecked and leads to recurrent subcutaneous and submucosal swelling (or angioedema). Clinically, HAE is characterized by episodic, spontaneous, unpredictable attacks of nonhistaminergic angioedema involving the subcutaneous and submucosal tissues, and can include the face, gastrointestinal tract, genitourinary tract, extremities (hands/feet), and/or throat and upper airway, the last of which can be particularly serious and potentially life-threatening. Several products are approved for the prophylaxis of HAE attacks as well as for the treatment of acute HAE attacks; however, breakthrough attacks still occur, and additional prophylactic therapy options for HAE patients are beneficial.
L73: Substantial evidence of effectiveness for donidalorsen in the prophylactic treatment of HAE is based on the efficacy results from the single adequate and well-controlled clinical trial (CS5), with confirmatory evidence from mechanistic data, as presented in Section 1.2. Although the donidalorsen-4 dosing regimen demonstrated greater efficacy than the donidalorsen-8 dosing regimen across primary and secondary endpoints, because both dosing intervals independently met the primary efficacy endpoint, both dosing options are being approved for use. However, based on the greater efficacy of the donidalorsen-4 dosing regimen, the recommended dosage of donidalorsen is 80 mg administered subcutaneously every 4 weeks. A dosage of donidalorsen 80 mg administered subcutaneously every 8 weeks may also be considered, as included in labeling, at the discretion of the prescriber.
L74: Although the safety database is small, strengths include the placebo-controlled design, use of two doses to assess dose-response, the 6-month treatment duration with additional long-term exposure in the open-label extension period, the low study drop-out rate, and the small amount of missing data. The safety assessment of donidalorsen revealed no concerning safety signals that would preclude approval. No deaths occurred in the clinical development program. Serious adverse events, severe adverse events, and adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation were rare with no major imbalances between treatment groups. Anaphylaxis occurred in one subject. Overall, treatment-emergent adverse events were predominantly mild or moderate in severity, with the most common adverse reactions being injection site reactions, upper respiratory tract infection, urinary tract infection, and abdominal discomfort.
L75: As with other GalNac-ASOs, effects on clinical laboratory results including decreased platelet counts, increased liver enzymes, and an increase in international normalized ratio (INR) were observed, but these did not result in a safety signal in terms of adverse events. Generally, the safety profile of donidalorsen is consistent with expected class effects of ASOs and kallikrein-directed therapeutics. Potential risks can be addressed through labeling and routine
L76: NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
L77: pharmacovigilance, as well as postmarketing requirements to assess for drug-induced liver injury in the multi-year OLE trials (CS3 and CS7) and to complete the ongoing 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats.
L78: Although Trial CS5 enrolled a limited number of adolescent subjects (seven in the donidalorsen group and zero in the placebo group), the efficacy and safety of donidalorsen in adolescent patients 12 to &lt;18 years of age is based on extrapolation from adults and matching pharmacokinetic (PK) exposure and pharmacodynamic (PD) response. Extrapolation of efficacy is supported by the same underlying pathophysiology and clinical manifestations of disease, mechanism of action of donidalorsen, and similar expected response to treatment across age groups.
L79: Overall, the Agency concludes that the benefit-risk assessment is favorable and supports the approval of donidalorsen 80 mg SC every 4 weeks or every 8 weeks for the proposed indication of prophylaxis to prevent HAE attacks in adults and adolescents 12 years of age and above.
L80: ## II. Interdisciplinary Assessment
L81: ## 3. Introduction
L82: This review serves as the interdisciplinary assessment for the NDA for donidalorsen. Donidalorsen is a new molecular entity, first-in-class chimeric GalNAc-conjugated 2'-O-methoxyethyl-modified antisense oligonucleotide targeting prekallikrein mRNA. The proposed indication is for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of HAE in adult and adolescent patients aged 12 years and older. The proposed dosage is 80 mg administered SC (b) (4). A dosing interval of 80 mg (b) (4) may also be considered (b) (4).
L83: Hereditary angioedema is a rare genetic condition characterized by recurrent episodes of swelling in various body parts, including the hands/feet, genitals, gastrointestinal tract, face, and/or throat (USHAA 2024). It is most often caused by pathogenic variants in the *SERPING1* gene that encodes C1-INH, resulting in either low levels of C1-INH (Type I) or normal levels of dysfunctional C1-INH (Type II) (Busse et al. 2021). The inheritance of HAE is autosomal dominant, with approximately 25% of patients having de novo mutations. Patients with HAE experience recurrent episodes of swelling that typically last for 2 to 3 days, but occasionally up to 5 days. Symptom onset usually occurs in childhood, with 50% of patients experiencing angioedema episodes by 10 years of age, and symptoms often increase after puberty. There is a high degree of inter- and intrapatient variability in both the frequency and severity of attacks. Characteristically, HAE symptoms do not respond to mast-cell targeted treatments, such as antihistamines, corticosteroids, or epinephrine. Pharmacologic treatment of HAE consists of access to on-demand therapies to treat acute episodes of angioedema and consideration for long-term prophylaxis on an individual basis. Approved therapies for the on-demand treatment of acute attacks consist of products that target the kallikrein-kinin pathway (i.e., C1-INH replacements, plasma kallikrein inhibitors (ecallantide and sebetralstat), and a bradykinin B2-receptor antagonist (icatibant)). Similarly, approved therapies for maintenance prophylaxis to prevent acute attacks consist of products that target the kallikrein-kinin pathway (i.e., C1-INH replacement, a Factor XIIa inhibitor (garadacimab), and plasma kallikrein inhibitors (lanadelumab and berotralstat)). Danazol, an attenuated androgen, is also approved for prophylaxis, although its mechanism of action in HAE is unclear.
L84: The Applicant submitted an IND application (IND 142564; July 15, 2019) to investigate donidalorsen for the prophylaxis of HAE attacks. To support the NDA, the Applicant submitted the results of a single, adequate, and well-controlled phase 3 trial (CS5). This 24-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated 90 adult and adolescent subjects with HAE Type I or II. The primary efficacy endpoint was the time-normalized number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks per 4 weeks from Week 1 to Week 25.
L85: During the course of the application review, the Agency identified several key efficacy and safety review issues, as listed below. In-depth analyses and assessments of these issues can be found in Sections 6.3 and 7.7.

L117: ## 5. Pharmacologic Activity, Pharmacokinetics, and Clinical Pharmacology
L118: ## 5.1. Nonclinical Assessment of Potential Effectiveness
L119: The unconjugated human PKK ASO parent compound of donidalorsen, ISIS 546254, which has the same nucleobase sequence as donidalorsen, is perfectly matched to only PKK mRNA in the human transcriptome (targets site free of meaningful sequence variation).
L120: Donidalorsen does not align perfectly to the mouse PKK gene sequence and is not pharmacologically active in the mouse. The human sequence targeted by donidalorsen has a single-base sequence mismatch within the binding site of monkey PKK mRNA (position 19). Despite this mismatch, donidalorsen demonstrated dose-dependent inhibition of liver target mRNA expression and reductions in PKK protein and activity levels in peripheral circulation of Cynomolgus monkeys.
L121: Incubation of donidalorsen with HepatoPac® (co-culture system of primary human hepatocytes and stromal cells [mouse fibroblasts]) reduced PKK mRNA in a dose-dependent manner and resulted in a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC_{50}) value of 0.19\mu M.
L122: In an in vivo study in human KLKB1/PKK transgenic mice, single SC administration of donidalorsen on Day 0 resulted in a dose- and time-dependent reduction of plasma PKK protein that approached 91% at the highest dose tested (10 mg/kg) on Day 14 after treatment. PKK levels were still 20% below baseline levels by Day 56 (last time point evaluated) at 10 mg/kg.
L123: The established pharmacologic class (EPC) for donidalorsen has been designated as “prekallikrein-directed antisense oligonucleotide” based on in vitro and in vivo pharmacology data.
L124: ## 5.2. Clinical Pharmacology/Pharmacokinetics
L125: Donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) is a chimeric GalNAc-conjugated 2'-O-methoxyethyl (2'-MOE)-modified ASO. The ASO is covalently bound to GalNAc via a tris(hexamethoxyamino) (THA) linker. GalNAc is a ligand with affinity for the hepatocyte-specific asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR). This GalNAc conjugate approach results in ASO delivery to hepatocytes. The modifications in ASO chains have been seen in other approved ASO products, such as eplontersen (NDA 217388), tofersen (NDA 215887), inotersen (NDA 211172), and olezarsen (NDA 218614). Eplontersen also contains an identical THA linker to that used in donidalorsen.
L126: **Table 5. Summary of Clinical Pharmacology and Pharmacokinetics**
L127: Characteristic	Drug Information
Pharmacologic Activity
EPC	Prekallikrein-directed antisense oligonucleotide (FDA 2025)
Mechanism of action	Donidalorsen is an ASO-GalNAc conjugate that causes RNase H1-mediated degradation of PKK mRNA through binding to PKK mRNA, which results in reduced production of PKK protein. PKK is mainly synthesized by the liver and it is a pro-enzyme for plasma kallikrein, which results in the release of bradykinin, a vasodilator causing swelling and pain in HAE.
Active moieties	Unconjugated ASO of donidalorsen (ISIS 546254)
QT prolongation	At the maximum recommended dose of donidalorsen 80 mg Q4W, clinically significant QTc interval prolongation was not observed.
L128: General Information
Bioanalysis	The plasma concentrations of donidalorsen, including fully conjugated, partially conjugated (i.e., with 1, 2, or 3 GalNAc sugar deletions), and unconjugated donidalorsen, was assessed with a validated hybridization ECL method (b) (4) with an analytical range of 0.1735 to 86.73 ng/mL. In addition, dilutions up to 10,000-fold were evaluated and deemed acceptable.
The plasma PKK concentrations in Trials CS3, CS5, and CS7 were assessed by a validated ELISA method with a detection range of 3.76 µg/mL to 480 µg/mL after a MRD of 1:8000. Plasma PKK in CS1 and CS2 were analyzed by a chromogenic ELISA method with a detection range between 7.52 and 2560 µg/mL (b) (4).
See Section 14.3 for more details.
Healthy subjects versus patients	Following the same dosing regimen of 80 mg Q4W, the pharmacokinetics of donidalorsen was similar between subjects with HAE and healthy subjects (mean C_{\text{trough,ss}} for both populations was around 1 ng/mL), while the maximum plasma PKK reduction from baseline was greater in healthy subjects (94%) compared to subjects with HAE (73%). The baseline plasma PKK concentrations were similar between subjects with HAE and healthy subjects.

L133: ## NDA 219407
## Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
L134: Characteristic	Drug Information
Range of effective dose(s) or exposure	Two dosing regimens, 80 mg Q4W and 80 mg Q8W, were evaluated and both demonstrated efficacy and safety for the prevention of HAE attacks in the pivotal phase 3 trial (CS5). Refer to Section 6 for more details.
Maximally tolerated dose or exposure	80 mg SC Q4W was the highest dose tested in the phase 3 trial (CS5). One subject received 100 mg Q4W in Trial CS3, an open-label extension to the phase 2 trial (CS2).
Dose proportionality	Donidalorsen AUC_{\tau_{au,ss}} increased in a greater than dose-proportional manner between dosages of 20 mg Q4W and 80 mg Q4W. Donidalorsen AUC_{\tau_{au,ss}} increased by about 6-fold for a 4-fold increase in dose.
Accumulation	No accumulation in C_{max} and AUC was observed following administration of 4 doses of 80 mg Q4W donidalorsen in healthy subjects as well as in subjects with HAE. However, a 2-fold increase in mean C_{trough} was observed in both healthy subjects and subjects with HAE at steady state. Of note, the observed C_{trough} is about 1% of the value of C_{max}.
Time to achieve steady-state	The steady-state C_{trough} following administration of 80 mg Q4W was reached by Day 85 for healthy subjects and by Day 113 for subjects with HAE. The steady state for change from baseline in plasma PKK was reached by around Day 85 in subjects with HAE following administration of 80 mg Q4W or Q8W donidalorsen.
Bridge between to-be-marketed and clinical trial/study formulations	The drug product used in clinical trials was a vial product while the to-be-marketed formulation is proposed as a prefilled syringe with autoinjector. Bioequivalence based on C_{max} and AUC between the drug product presentations was demonstrated in Trial CS9 conducted in healthy subjects.
Bioavailability	Absolute bioavailability after SC administration of donidalorsen has not been determined.
T_{max}	Following a single SC dose of 80 mg in healthy subjects, the median (range) T_{max} for donidalorsen in plasma is 2 (0.25, 8) hours.
Food effect (fed/fasted)
Geometric least square mean and 90% CI	Not applicable.
Volume of distribution	Central compartment volume (Vc/F) is 69.8 L
Peripheral compartment volume (Vp/F) is 1840 L
Plasma protein binding	Donidalorsen is highly plasma protein bound (>98%) with minimal change in protein binding over a concentration range of 5 to 150 µg/mL.
Drug as substrate of transporters	Donidalorsen is not a substrate of P-gp, BCRP, OAT1, OAT3, OCT1, OCT2, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, MATE1, MATE2K, and BSEP.
THA-linker major metabolite M8 is not a substrate of OAT1, OAT3, OCT1, OCT2, OATP1B1, MATE1, MATE2-K, BCRP, and P-gp. However, M8 is a substrate of BSEP and OATP1B3.
L135: Characteristic	Drug Information
Elimination
Mass balance results	Human mass balance study was not conducted.
Clearance	Apparent clearance (CL/F) is 12.8 L/h
Half-life	Terminal elimination half-life is 31.4 days, which likely reflects the half-life in tissue (i.e., liver). The apparent half-life in plasma, reflecting tissue distribution, is estimated to be 4 to 5 hours.
Metabolic pathway(s)	The unconjugated ASO portion is expected to be metabolized by endo- and exo-nucleases to form fragmented oligonucleotide metabolites. The GalNAc-THA linker moiety is hydrolyzed intracellularly following uptake into tissue. After hydrolysis, GalNAc sugars undergo endogenous carbohydrate catabolism, while the THA linker undergoes oxidative metabolism. No specific CYP enzyme was identified to majorly contribute to the metabolism of donidalorsen. Minimal linker-related metabolites (e.g., M8 and M12) were detected in human plasma, with mean concentrations <2% of those determined for parent drug at 2-hours postdose.
Primary excretion pathways (% dose)	The mean fraction of donidalorsen (including fully conjugated, partially conjugated, and unconjugated donidalorsen) excreted in the urine within 24 hours is <1% of the administered dose in healthy subjects. The fragmented oligonucleotide metabolites formed by metabolism of unconjugated ASO are excreted in urine or feces. Metabolites of the THA linker are also excreted in the urine, representing ≤6.4% of the dose detected in urine samples collected over 24 hours following the four doses of 80 mg Q4W on Day 85.
Intrinsic Factors and Specific Populations
Body weight	No clinically meaningful differences in the pharmacokinetics or pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen were observed based on body weight (37 to 152 kg).
Based on population PK analysis, the estimated steady-state plasma donidalorsen systemic exposure (C_{max,ss}, AUC_{tau,ss} and C_{trough,ss}) in a subject weighing 100 kg is about 38% to 54% lower as compared to that in a subject weighing 70 kg.
Age	No clinically meaningful differences in the pharmacokinetics or pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen were observed based on age (12 to 68 years).
Renal impairment	No clinically meaningful differences in the pharmacokinetics or pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen were observed in subjects with mild renal impairment (i.e., eGFR ≥60 to <90 mL/min/1.73 m2) compared to subjects with normal renal function.
Donidalorsen was not studied in subjects with moderate renal impairment, severe renal impairment, or ESRD.
Hepatic impairment	No clinically meaningful differences in the pharmacokinetics or pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen were observed in subjects with mild hepatic impairment (defined using NCI-ODWG criteria: total bilirubin ≤1× ULN and AST >1× ULN, or total bilirubin >1 to 1.5× ULN and any AST) compared to subjects with normal hepatic function.
Donidalorsen was not evaluated in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment. Given that the site of action of donidalorsen is in the liver, the long-term safety and efficacy in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment is not known.
L136: Characteristic	Drug Information
Drug Interaction Liability (Drug as Perpetrator)
Inhibition/induction of metabolism	In vitro, donidalorsen did not inhibit CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP2E1, or CYP3A4. Donidalorsen did not induce CYP1A2, CYP2B6, or CYP3A4.
In vitro, THA-linker major metabolite M8 did not inhibit CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP2E1, or CYP3A4. M8 did not induce CYP1A2, CYP2B6, or CYP3A4.
Inhibition/induction of transporter systems	In vitro, donidalorsen did not inhibit OAT1, OAT3, OCT1, OCT2, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, MATE1, MATE2-K, BCRP, P-gp, or BSEP.
In vitro, THA-linker metabolite M8 did not inhibit OAT1, OAT3, OCT1, OCT2, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, MATE2-K, BCRP, P-gp, or BSEP. M8 inhibited MATE1 with an IC50 of 62.7µM.
Immunogenicity (if Applicable)
Bioanalysis	Antidrug antibodies against donidalorsen in human plasma were assessed using a validated multitiered ELISA.
Incidence	In the pivotal trial (CS5) with a treatment duration of 24 weeks, the incidence rates of treatment-emergent ADAs were 20% (9 out of 45 subjects) and 22% (5 out of 23 subjects) among subjects who received donidalorsen 80 mg Q4W and 80 mg Q8W, respectively.
In the ongoing OLE trial (CS7), subjects who were rolled over from Trial CS5 continued treatment with donidalorsen in 80 mg Q4W or Q8W groups for up to 3 years (median exposure duration of 227 days). The incidence rate of treatment-emergent ADAs was 35% (22 of 63 subjects) in the Q4W group, including subjects initially randomized to Q4W (36%, 16 out of 44 subjects) in Trial CS5 and subjects initially randomized to placebo in Trial CS5 (32%, 6 out of 19 subjects). The incidence rate of treatment-emergent ADAs was 21% (3 of 14 subjects) among subjects who received Q8W in both Trial CS5 and Trial CS7.
Clinical impact	The presence of ADAs was not found to impact the pharmacodynamics (i.e., change from baseline in plasma PKK), safety, or efficacy of donidalorsen. An increase in donidalorsen plasma Ctrough was observed in ADA-positive subjects with high titers. Because of the small sample size, the effect of ADAs on the PK, PD, safety, and effectiveness of donidalorsen is inconclusive.

L143: The donidalorsen-4 (every 4 weeks) and donidalorsen-8 (every 8 weeks) dosing regimens were investigated in one phase 3 trial (CS5), while switching from donidalorsen-8 to donidalorsen-4 was evaluated in the open-label extension trial for CS5 (Trial CS7). L145: (b) (4) switching from a more frequent dosing regimen (donidalorsen-4) to a less frequent dosing regimen (donidalorsen-8) for all patients based on the disease control for at least 3 months, (b) (4) However, as a positive dose response relationship was demonstrated between donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 in CS5, the donidalorsen-4 is the preferred dosing regimen. The donidalorsen-8 may also be considered for some subjects based on the efficacy demonstrated in Trial CS5 and the sustained efficacy demonstrated in CS7.
L146: (b) (4)

L148: ## Exposure/Pharmacodynamics-Response Relationship
L149: In Trial CS5, a positive dose-response relationship was observed for HAE attack rate reduction between the donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 dosing regimens, with a greater HAE attack rate reduction observed with donidalorsen-4 compared to donidalorsen-8. Subjects randomized to both the donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 dosing regimens demonstrated a reduction in HAE attack rate as compared to subjects who received placebo (Figure 1).

L168: ## **Trial CS7**
L169: In the open-label Trial CS7 (an extension of the pivotal trial [CS5]), no subject was switched from the donidalorsen-4 to donidalorsen-8 dosing regimen. Subjects who received the donidalorsen-8 dosing regimen during Trial CS5 remained in the same dosing regimen (donidalorsen-8) if well controlled (N=14), or were switched to a more frequent dosing regimen (donidalorsen-4) if they experienced any attack between Week 17 to Week 25 during Trial CS5 (N=6); subjects who received the donidalorsen-4 dosing regimen during Trial CS5 remained in the same dosing regimen (donidalorsen-4) (N=44). In addition, subjects who received placebo during Trial CS5 received the donidalorsen-4 dosing regimen during Trial CS7 (N=19). For additional details, refer to Section 14.2.6.
L170: A total of 14 subjects in the donidalorsen-8 group who were adequately controlled during Trial CS5 (i.e., no HAE attack \ge8 weeks after last dose in Trial CS5 [Week 17 to Week 25]) continued on the donidalorsen-8 regimen in Trial CS7. In these 14 subjects, the mean percent change from baseline (i.e., Run-In Period for Trial CS5) in plasma PKK concentration was -45% at Week 9 in Trial CS7; this is similar to the mean percent reduction in plasma PKK concentrations observed among subjects in the donidalorsen-8 group in Trial CS5 (i.e., -47.2% at Week 25). Although subjects in the donidalorsen-8 group had a smaller percent reduction in plasma PKK concentrations as compared to subjects in the donidalorsen-4 group (mean -73.8% at Week 25 in Trial CS5), no subject who continued receiving the donidalorsen-8 dosing regimen in Trial CS7 was reported to have switched to a more frequent regimen by the NDA cutoff date.

L177: ## Trial CS3
L178: Switching from the donidalorsen-4 to donidalorsen-8 dosing regimen was investigated in the open-label Trial CS3 (an extension of the phase 2 trial [CS2]). In Trial CS3, Rollover subjects from Trial CS2 initially entered a 12-week Fixed Treatment Period where all subjects received the donidalorsen-4 dosing regimen. Following completion of the Fixed Treatment Period, the dosing regimen could be switched in the subsequent Flexible Dosing Period. For additional details, refer to Section 14.2.5. In Trial CS3, eight subjects who were attack free for at least 12 weeks on the donidalorsen-4 regimen during the Fixed Treatment Period were switched to the less frequent donidalorsen-8 regimen during the Flexible Treatment Period. However, three of these eight subjects switched back to the donidalorsen-4 regimen due to experiencing HAE attacks.
L179: Thus, based on observations from Trial CS3, it is not clear that subjects who were responsive on the donidalorsen-4 regimen would also be responsive to the donidalorsen-8 regimen. Therefore, as three out of eight subjects experienced an HAE attack after extension of the dosing interval despite being controlled for &gt;12 weeks on the donidalorsen-4 regimen, the available data are not sufficient to support a recommendation to switch from the donidalorsen-4 to the donidalorsen-8 regimen based on HAE attack incidence. Given that HAE is a heterogeneous disease, the response from the more frequent donidalorsen-4 dosing regimen may not be predictive of who may benefit from the longer donidalorsen-8 dosing interval.
L180: Although a positive dose-response relationship was observed in Trial CS5 between the donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 dosing regimens, both for the mean percent reduction from baseline in plasma PKK concentrations and HAE attack rate, variability in these responses was observed at the individual level within each dosing group (Figure 2 and Figure 3). The data suggest that there is heterogeneity in the disease and response to donidalorsen. While the reduction in plasma PKK trough concentrations following donidalorsen treatment was generally associated with the reduction in HAE attack rate, there are no dedicated data showing a clear association between the magnitude of change from baseline in plasma PKK trough concentration and HAE attack rate at the individual level.
L181: Taken together, the effectiveness of both the donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 dosing regimens compared to placebo are supported by efficacy data from the pivotal trial (CS5). However, the available data do not support the switch from the donidalorsen-4 to the donidalorsen-8 dosing
L182: regimens for all subjects who are responsive with the donidalorsen-4 regimen. The positive dose-response relationship between donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 observed in CS5 supported that donidalorsen-4 is the preferred regimen. In addition, as there were subjects who remained controlled and continued treatment with donidalorsen-8 when rolling over from CS5 to CS7, donidalorsen-8 regimen may also be considered.
L183: ## 6.2. Clinical Studies/Trials Intended To Demonstrate Efficacy
L184: ## 6.2.1. Results of Pooled Analyses
L185: The evaluation of efficacy was based on the analyses of the individual trials. Pooled efficacy analyses will not be discussed in this review.
L186: ## 6.2.2. Trial CS5
L187: ## 6.2.2.1. Design and Conduct, Trial CS5
L188: Results of the pivotal trial (CS5) served as the basis for efficacy evaluation. This was a 24-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, phase 3 trial that treated 90 subjects aged 12 years or older with Type I or II HAE who had \ge 2 HAE attacks during the Screening Period. Subjects were randomized 2:1 to either Cohort A (donidalorsen-4 or matched placebo) or Cohort B (donidalorsen-8 or matched placebo), respectively (see Figure 4). Within each cohort, subjects were randomized 3:1 to receive donidalorsen or a matching volume of placebo. Treatment was provided over a 24-week Treatment Period. Data from subjects receiving placebo in Cohorts A and B were pooled for analyses, and this is referred to as the pooled placebo group for primary analyses.
L189: Figure 4. Randomization Schema, Trial CS5
L190: Source: FDA Clinical Data Scientist and Clinical Reviewer
L191: * One subject in 80 mg Q4W withdrew consent after randomization but prior to receiving trial drug.
L192: Abbreviations: Q4W, every 4 weeks; Q8W, every 8 weeks
L193: As shown in Figure 5, the trial consisted of three periods: the Screening Period (up to 8 weeks in duration; this period provided the baseline HAE attack rate for each subject), the Treatment Period (24 weeks in duration), and the Post-Treatment Period (up to 13 weeks in duration). Subjects were allowed to choose to enroll in an OLE trial (CS7 [see Section 15.2]), rather than complete the Post-Treatment Period. The length of trial participation for each subject was up to 11 months. Written and signed informed consent (and assent for minors) was obtained prior to the performance of any trial-related procedures, including Screening. Each enrolled subject was randomized to begin trial treatment as soon as the subject experienced \ge 2 HAE attacks during the Screening Period.
L194: Figure 5. Trial Design, Trial CS5
L195: Source: CS5 clinical study report
L196: Abbreviations: ET, early termination; PD, pharmacodynamics; PK, pharmacokinetic; SC, subcutaneous; Tx, treatment
L197: Subjects who experienced \ge 5 attacks per month for 2 consecutive months after Week 5 (deemed lack of efficacy) had the opportunity to discontinue from treatment in the current trial and either progress to the Post-Treatment Period or enroll in the OLE trial (CS7). If a subject chose to enroll in Trial CS7, the subject was discontinued from Trial CS5.
L198: Subjects not participating in Trial CS7 entered a 13-week Post-Treatment Period. Subjects who discontinued treatment prior to the end of the scheduled Treatment Period attended the Early Termination Visit and were encouraged to complete the Post-Treatment Period unless consent or assent (subjects not of legal age) was withdrawn.
L199: The End of Study was defined as the date of the last visit of the last subject in the trial. For individual subjects, the End of Study was defined as the date of their last trial visit.
L200: NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
L201: For details regarding the collection and investigator confirmation of HAE attacks, see Section 15.1.1.
L202: The overall design of Trial CS5 is consistent with previous programs for HAE prophylaxis. The duration of the controlled Treatment Period (24 weeks) is acceptable for this indication.
L203: ## **Concomitant Medications**
L204: Consistent with the eligibility criteria, continued use of a stable dose of androgens or tranexamic acid for HAE prophylaxis was allowed while on trial; this differs from some HAE products' development programs, which disallow the use of these agents. Once enrolled, including during the Screening Period, subjects were not allowed to use other HAE prophylaxis agents, such as lanadelumab or berotralstat. Other disallowed concomitant therapies included angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and estrogen-containing medications with systemic absorption.
L205: Subjects were required to have access to, and the ability to use, on-demand medication to treat acute HAE attacks, per the recommendation of their treating physician.
L206: ## **Primary Objective and Endpoint**
L207: The primary objective of Trial CS5 was to evaluate the efficacy of donidalorsen as prophylaxis in patients with HAE. The primary efficacy endpoint was the time-normalized number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks per 4 weeks during the Treatment Period (from Week 1 to Week 25) for the donidalorsen-4 group compared to pooled placebo. The primary endpoint was calculated per subject as:
L208: [\text{number of HAE attacks} \div \text{length subject contributed to analysis period in days}] \times 28
L209: Length subject contributed to analysis period (in days) was calculated as:
L210: [\text{End date of Treatment Period (if completed) or Date of 25 weeks after first dose (if did not complete) or Date of follow-up discontinuation or Date of end of participation (whichever is first)}] - \text{Date of first dose}
L211: Treatment Period in the above formula is defined as the period from the first dose date/time to the last dose date/time +28 days for Cohort A and +56 days for Cohort B.
L212: The selected primary endpoint is acceptable and consistent with previous programs for HAE prophylaxis.
L213: ## **Secondary and Exploratory Objective and Endpoints**
L214: The secondary objectives included characterizing the efficacy of donidalorsen (donidalorsen-4 or donidalorsen-8) on the quality and pattern of HAE attacks and their impact on quality of life. Only investigator-confirmed HAE attacks, as defined in Section 15.1.1, were included in the efficacy evaluation. The secondary endpoints, in the order of the multiplicity control hierarchy, were:
L215: - The time-normalized number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks per 4 weeks from Week 5 to Week 25 for the donidalorsen-4 group compared to pooled placebo
- Subjects with \ge 70\% reduction from baseline in investigator-confirmed HAE attack rate between Week 5 to Week 25 in the donidalorsen-4 group compared to pooled placebo
- The percentage of investigator-confirmed HAE attack-free subjects from Week 5 to Week 25 in the donidalorsen-4 group compared to pooled placebo
- The time-normalized number of moderate or severe investigator-confirmed HAE attacks per 4 weeks from Week 5 to Week 25 in the donidalorsen-4 group compared to pooled placebo
- The number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks requiring acute HAE therapy per 4 weeks from Week 5 to Week 25 in the donidalorsen-4 group compared to pooled placebo
- Change in Angioedema Quality of Life (AE-QoL) total score at Week 25 in the donidalorsen-4 group compared to pooled placebo
- The time-normalized number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks per 4 weeks during the Treatment Period (from Week 1 to Week 25) for the donidalorsen-8 group compared to pooled placebo
- The time-normalized number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks per 4 weeks during the Treatment Period (from Week 5 to Week 25) for the donidalorsen-8 group compared to pooled placebo
- Subjects with \ge 70\% reduction from baseline in investigator-confirmed HAE attack rate between Week 5 to Week 25 in the donidalorsen-8 group compared to pooled placebo
- The percentage of investigator-confirmed HAE attack-free subjects from Week 5 to Week 25 in the donidalorsen-8 group compared to pooled placebo
- The time-normalized number of moderate or severe investigator-confirmed HAE attacks per 4 weeks from Week 5 to Week 25 in the donidalorsen-8 group compared to pooled placebo
- The number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks requiring acute HAE therapy per 4 weeks from Week 5 to Week 25 in the donidalorsen-8 group compared to pooled placebo
- Change in AE-QoL total score at Week 25 in the donidalorsen-8 group compared to pooled placebo
- Change in AE-QoL domain score of Functioning at Week 25 in the donidalorsen-4 group compared to pooled placebo
L216: - Change in AE-QoL domain score of Fears/Shame at Week 25 in the donidalorsen-4 group compared to pooled placebo
- Change in AE-QoL domain score of Fatigue/Mood at Week 25 in the donidalorsen-4 group compared to pooled placebo
- Change in AE-QoL domain score of Nutrition at Week 25 in the donidalorsen-4 group compared to pooled placebo
- Change in AE-QoL domain score of Functioning at Week 25 in the donidalorsen-8 group compared to pooled placebo
- Change in AE-QoL domain score of Fears/Shame at Week 25 in the donidalorsen-8 group compared to pooled placebo
- Change in AE-QoL domain score of Fatigue/Mood at Week 25 in the donidalorsen-8 group compared to pooled placebo
- Change in AE-QoL domain score of Nutrition at Week 25 in the donidalorsen-8 group compared to pooled placebo
- Percent of subjects who are well controlled on the Angioedema Control Test (AECT) at Week 25 in the donidalorsen-4 group compared to pooled placebo
- Percent of subjects who are well controlled on the AECT at Week 25 in the donidalorsen-8 group compared to pooled placebo
L217: The secondary endpoints encompass the most clinically relevant endpoints that are typically evaluated in HAE prophylaxis programs. Some objectives/endpoints aimed to evaluate quality of life via the clinical outcome tools AE-QoL and AECT. These tools have not been found to be fit-for-purpose for the regulatory assessment of efficacy in HAE (see Section 6.2.2.4.6.2), and as such, these endpoints are not appropriate to support efficacy or appear in product labeling.
L218: ## 6.2.2.2. Eligibility Criteria, Trial CS5
L219: Key eligibility criteria are summarized below. Trial CS5 enrolled subjects \ge 12 years of age with clinically confirmed HAE and an attack frequency that would likely warrant prophylactic HAE therapy. The inclusion and exclusion criteria are acceptable and consistent with those used in previous trials of approved products for HAE prophylaxis.
L220: ## **Key Inclusion Criteria**
L221: - Male or female \ge 12 years of age at the time of informed consent.
- Diagnosed with clinically confirmed C1-INH (Type I or Type II) HAE based on all of the following:Documented clinical history consistent with HAE (SC or mucosal, nonpruritic swelling episodes without accompanying urticaria).
- C1-INH functional level &lt;40\% normal level. Patients with a functional level of 40% to 50% of normal could be enrolled if their complement factor C4 level was below the lower limit of normal (LLN) or when a known pathogenic mutation in the *SERPING1* gene had been demonstrated.
- At least one of the following: age at HAE onset \le 30 years, family history consistent with Type I or II HAE, or complement component 1q within the normal range.
- Experienced \ge 2 HAE attacks during the Screening Period.
- Female subjects: nonpregnant, nonlactating, and either surgically sterile, postmenopausal, abstinent, or using acceptable contraceptive methods.
- Male subjects: either surgically sterile or using an acceptable contraceptive method.
L222: ## **Key Exclusion Criteria**
L223: - Concomitant diagnosis of another form of angioedema, such as idiopathic or acquired angioedema, recurrent angioedema associated with urticaria, or Type III HAE.
- Exposure to any of the following medications:ACE inhibitors or any estrogen containing medications with systemic absorption (such as oral contraceptive or hormonal replacement therapy) within 4 weeks prior to Screening.
- Chronic prophylaxis with Takhzyro® (lanadelumab), Haegarda® (C1-esterase inhibitor SQ), Cinryze® and Ruconest® (C1 esterase inhibitor), or Orladeyo® (berotralstat) within 5 half-lives prior to Screening (i.e., Takhzyro within 10 weeks prior to Screening, Haegarda/Berinert 2000/3000® subcutaneously/Cinryze/Ruconest within 2 weeks prior to Screening, or Orladeyo within 3 weeks prior to Screening).
- Oligonucleotides within 4 months of Screening (if a single administration) or 12 months of Screening (if multiple doses received); does not apply to vaccines.
L224: - Any clinically significant abnormalities in Screening laboratory values that would render a patient unsuitable for inclusion; the following values are exclusionary:Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) or aspartate aminotransferase (AST) &gt;3\times upper limit of normal (ULN).
- Total bilirubin &gt;1.5\times ULN or, if due to Gilbert's syndrome, &gt;5 mg/dL.
- Platelet count &lt;130 K/mm^3.
- For patients \ge 18 years old: eGFR &lt;45 mL/min (per Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration formula).
- For patients 12 to &lt;18 years old: eGFR &lt;60 mL/min (per Bedside Schwartz formula).
- History of acquired coagulopathies or bleeding diathesis, inherited bleeding disorders, hypercoagulability.
- Any clinically significant renal or hepatic diseases.
L225: ## 6.2.2.3. Statistical Analysis Plan, Trial CS5
L226: The statistical analysis plan (SAP) for Trial CS5 was Version 2 dated December 13, 2023. The primary efficacy endpoint was the time-normalized HAE attack rate per month (28 days) comparing the donidalorsen-4 group to pooled placebo for the full analysis set (FAS). The FAS was defined as all randomized subjects who received at least one dose of trial drug; subjects were analyzed according to the treatment group to which they were randomized. The definition of the Safety set was the same as the FAS. Only investigator-confirmed HAE attacks were included in the evaluation of efficacy for all primary and secondary endpoints. Treatment policy strategy was used for the intercurrent events of use of not allowed concomitant therapy or procedures and early termination of treatment, which included subjects escaping early to the OLE trial (CS7) due to experiencing \ge 5 recurrent HAE attacks per month for 2 consecutive months during the Treatment Period, subjects discontinuing the trial treatment early due to recurrent HAE attacks and not enrolling in Trial CS7, and subjects discontinuing trial treatment early due to COVID-19 or war-related events.
L227: ## Primary Analysis
L228: The primary analysis used a Poisson regression model and Pearson chi-square scaling of standard errors to account for potential overdispersion on the FAS, including subjects from the donidalorsen-4, donidalorsen-8, and pooled placebo groups. The model included fixed effects for treatment group (three categories), baseline (the time-normalized Run-In Period attack rate, continuous), and the treatment-by-baseline interaction as covariates, and the logarithm of time each subject was observed from Week 1 to Week 25 as an offset variable.
L229: From this model, the least squares mean rate, the standard error, and the corresponding 95% confidence interval for each treatment group, as well as the model adjusted mean rate ratios of donidalorsen-4 relative to the pooled placebo group and the corresponding 95% confidence interval were estimated. The comparison between donidalorsen-8 and pooled placebo was calculated from this model as a key secondary endpoint. These estimates were reported as mean
L230: event rates per 4 weeks by transforming the estimates using the exponential function. The p-value of the Wald-based chi-square test was reported for testing the hypothesis.
L231: The percentage difference in mean HAE attack rate between donidalorsen-4 and the pooled placebo was calculated as 100\% \times (\text{model adjusted mean rate ratio} - 1). Similarly, the estimated upper and lower confidence limits for the model adjusted mean rate ratio were transformed by subtracting 1 and multiplying by 100% to calculate 95% confidence intervals for the percentage change.
L232: ## Sensitivity and Supplementary Analyses
L233: A sensitivity analysis was prespecified that investigated whether the results for the primary endpoint were robust to departures from the assumption that the mean and variance are equal, as in Poisson regression. The analysis was the same as the primary analysis, except that negative binomial regression was performed instead of Poisson regression.
L234: The primary analysis assumed missing data were missing at random for subjects who discontinued the Treatment Period early. A sensitivity analysis was prespecified to investigate the robustness of the conclusions to the missing at random assumption. The analysis was performed on imputed data by using a multiple imputation method assuming jump to reference, used the Poisson regression model of the primary analysis, and combined the results using Rubin's rules.
L235: A tipping point sensitivity analysis was prespecified to investigate the effect of missing data on the reliability of the primary efficacy analysis. A range of progressively more conservative assumptions about the number of events occurring in the post withdrawal period was explored to search for the assumption which would reverse the conclusion.
L236: A supplementary analysis repeated the primary analysis and the negative binomial sensitivity analysis on the per-protocol set, which included all subjects in the FAS who were treated according to the protocol without any major deviations that could compromise the interpretation of efficacy.
L237: ## Subgroup Analyses
L238: The Applicant prespecified subgroup analyses based on the following:
L239: - Age category in years (12 to 17, 18 to 39, 40 to 64, \ge 65)
- Sex (male, female)
- Race (Caucasian, Other)
- Regions (North America, Europe, Middle East)
- Taken any predefined prophylactic therapy, including lanadelumab, berotralstat, C1-esterase inhibitor? (Yes, No)
L240: The Agency conducted subgroup analyses by race (American Indian or Alaska Native, Asian, Black or African American, Multiple, White, Other), by ethnicity (Hispanic or Latino, Not
L241: Hispanic or Latino), and by HAE type (Type I, Type II). The final SAP specified that HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) from Week 1 to Week 25 would be summarized by each subgroup. The primary endpoint was also analyzed by adding region and the interaction of region and treatment group as covariates. The Agency analyzed all other subgroups similarly to the prespecified analysis of region.
L242: A subgroup analyses that excluded subjects considered to be not “typical patients” was prespecified. These subjects were identified prior to trial unblinding based on clinical history and/or Screening Period characteristics considered to be atypical for Type I/II HAE. The analyses restricted the analysis set to “typical patients” and reevaluated the primary endpoint of time-normalized number of HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) from Week 1 to 25, as well as the secondary endpoints from Week 5 to 25 of time-normalized number of HAE attacks (per 4 weeks), time-normalized number of moderate or severe HAE attacks (per 4 weeks), and time-normalized number of HAE attacks requiring acute therapy (per 4 weeks).
L243: Additional analyses by HAE attack location and severity were completed by the Agency to inform regulatory decision-making, presented in Section 6.2.2.4.6.4.
L244: ## Secondary Endpoints
L245: The Applicant prespecified key secondary endpoints for both the comparison between donidalorsen-4 and pooled placebo, and the comparison between donidalorsen-8 and pooled placebo. All methods used data from all subjects in the FAS and for each endpoint the same model was used to calculate comparisons between both treatment groups and pooled placebo. Section 6.2.2.1 describes the order of multiplicity-controlled hierarchical testing of the secondary endpoints. At each level of the hierarchy, a test was performed at two-sided alpha of 5% if the test of the previous null hypothesis was rejected.
L246: The time-normalized number of HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) from Week 5 to Week 25 was analyzed using the same methods as described for the primary efficacy endpoint, based on the Poisson regression model on FAS with the treatment policy strategy. The time-normalized number of moderate or severe HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) from Week 5 to Week 25 and the time-normalized number of HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) requiring acute therapy from Week 5 to Week 25 were analyzed similarly.
L247: A responder analysis was conducted for subjects who achieved a clinical response, defined as a \ge 70\% reduction from baseline in HAE attack rate. The percentage reduction is defined as:
L248: \frac{\text{Postbaseline rate} - \text{Baseline rate}}{\text{Baseline rate}} \times 100\%
L249: The postbaseline is the HAE attack rate from Week 5 to Week 25 and baseline is Run-In Period HAE attack rate.
L250: The odds ratio, corresponding 95% confidence intervals, and p-value were calculated using a logistic regression model with the baseline, treatment, and the treatment by-baseline interaction as covariates. The clinical response of HAE attack-free from Week 5 to Week 25 was analyzed using a similar logistic regression model. Exploratory analyses which defined clinical response as \ge 50\% and \ge 90\% reduction from baseline in HAE attack rate were conducted similarly.
L251: ## 6.2.2.4. Results of Analyses, Trial CS5
L252: This section summarizes subject disposition, baseline demographics and clinical characteristics, and the primary, secondary, and exploratory efficacy results for the endpoints listed in Section 6.2.2.1. The results of additional analyses of interest to the Agency are also reported.
L253: ## 6.2.2.4.1. Subject Disposition, Trial CS5
L254: Disposition information is presented in Table 8 and Table 9. A total of 91 subjects were randomized. One subject withdrew consent prior to receiving trial drug and 90 subjects received at least one dose of trial drug. Lack of efficacy was defined per protocol as subjects who experienced at least five HAE attacks per month for 2 consecutive months after Week 5. One subject in each of the donidalorsen groups and three subjects in the pooled placebo group discontinued the trial drug due to lack of efficacy, and these subjects were rolled over into the open-label extension trial (CS7). One subject in the donidalorsen-8 group discontinued trial drug due to the adverse event of ALT increased. One subject in the pooled placebo group discontinued trial drug due to pregnancy.
L255: Most subjects completed the Trial CS5 treatment and then rolled over to Trial CS7 for open-label extended treatment.

L267: ## 6.2.2.4.2. Baseline Demographics and Clinical Characteristics, Trial CS5
L268: The demographics and clinical characteristics of the Full Analysis Set at baseline are summarized in **Table 10** and were reasonably similar between the treatment groups given the small sample size. Seven adolescents were enrolled, with none randomized to the placebo group; acknowledging that this is small, note that the pathophysiology of HAE Type I or II is similar across age groups. Racial and ethnic group representation in Trial CS5 is congruent with the overall subject population. Most subjects had Type I HAE (93%) and a history of laryngeal HAE attacks (52%; data not shown). Some subjects (17%) were previously on prophylaxis treatment. A total of seven (8%) subjects continued their allowed androgen or tranexamic acid prophylaxis (six (7%) on danazol and one (1%) on tranexamic acid; data not shown). Enrollment occurred at sites in the United States (20%) and outside the United States.

L274: ## 6.2.2.4.3. Primary Efficacy Results, Trial CS5
L275: The primary efficacy endpoint was the time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks from Week 1 to Week 25. This endpoint is clinically meaningful and consistent with previous programs for HAE prophylaxis. Details regarding the reporting, collection, and investigator confirmation of HAE attacks are provided in Section 15.1.1.
L276: Table 11 summarizes the efficacy results for the time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks from Week 1 to Week 25 for the primary endpoint comparison between donidalorsen-4 and pooled placebo, as well as the key secondary results for the comparison between donidalorsen-8 and pooled placebo. Note that the latter comparison was tested eighth in the Applicant's prespecified testing hierarchy, and all preceding endpoints achieved statistical significance. After adjusting for baseline attack rate by treatment group, the estimated least square mean time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks was lower in both the donidalorsen-4 (LS mean =0.44, 95% CI =0.27, 0.73) and donidalorsen-8 (LS mean =1.02, 95% CI =0.65, 1.59) groups compared to pooled placebo (LS mean =2.26, 95% CI =1.66, 3.09). The estimated attack rate ratio relative to placebo was 0.19 (95% CI =0.11, 0.35) for the donidalorsen-4 group and 0.45 (95% CI =0.26, 0.78) for the donidalorsen-8 group. Additionally, the percentage reduction in the means for the donidalorsen-4 group was 81% (95% CI =65%, 89%) and for the donidalorsen-8 group was 55% (95% CI =22%, 74%) relative to placebo.

L289: ## 6.2.2.4.4. Key Secondary Efficacy Results, Trial CS5
L290: Table 12 presents the results for the time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks from Week 5 to Week 25 for the comparison of both donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 to pooled placebo. After adjusting for baseline attack rate by treatment group, the estimated least square mean time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks was lower in both the donidalorsen-4 (LS mean =0.30, 95% CI =0.15, 0.58) and donidalorsen-8 (LS mean =0.90 95% CI =0.53, 1.52) groups compared to pooled placebo (LS mean =2.25, 95% CI =1.59, 3.18). Additionally, the percentage reduction in the means for the donidalorsen-4 group was 87% (95% CI =72%, 94%) and for the donidalorsen-8 group was 60% (95% CI =25%, 79%) relative to placebo. The results of analyses of this secondary endpoint agree with the primary efficacy results. This provides limited additional information for evidence of effectiveness of the trial drug as it is the same as the primary endpoint with a shortened time window starting at Week 5.

L299: **Table 13** presents the results for the clinical response of ≥70% reduction from baseline in HAE attack rate from Week 5 to Week 25 for the comparison of both donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 to pooled placebo. After adjusting for baseline HAE attack rate by treatment group, the odds ratio of clinical response of ≥70% reduction from baseline in HAE attack rate relative to pooled placebo was 34.74 (95% CI =7.32, 164.87) for donidalorsen-4 and 9.17 (95% CI =2.05 41.09) for donidalorsen-8. Exploratory analyses considered the clinical response of ≥50% and ≥90% reduction from baseline in HAE attack rate between Week 5 to Week 25 and the proportion of responders, respectively, were 42/45 (93%) and 28/45 (62%) in the donidalorsen-4 group, 19/22 (83%) and 11/22 (48%) in the donidalorsen-8 group, and 6/23 (27%) and 2/23 (9%) in the pooled placebo group. These results provide further evidence supporting the efficacy of donidalorsen.

L330: The Applicant proposed to include the endpoint of change in AE-QoL total score at Week 25 in the testing hierarchy. However, AE-QoL has been determined to be not fit-for-purpose for HAE (see Section 6.2.2.4.6.2), and so results related to AE-QoL are not presented here.
L331: ## **Multiplicity-Controlled Testing**
L332: Hierarchical testing at two-sided alpha of 5% was performed. The primary endpoint of the time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks from Week 1 to Week 25 comparing donidalorsen-4 to pooled placebo was statistically significant. Secondary endpoint comparisons between donidalorsen-4 and pooled placebo considering data from Week 5 to Week 25 were statistically significant for time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks, clinical response of \ge 70\% reduction from baseline in HAE attack rate, clinical response of being HAE attack-free, time-normalized number of moderate or severe HAE attacks per 4 weeks, and time-normalized number of HAE attacks requiring acute therapy per 4 weeks. Although change in AE-QoL total score at Week 25 was specified next in the testing hierarchy and statistically significant per the Applicant's analysis, AE-QoL has been determined to be not fit-for-purpose for HAE (see Section 6.2.2.4.6.2). Secondary endpoints comparing donidalorsen-8 to pooled placebo were statistically significant for the time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks from Week 1 to Week 25, the time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks from Week 5 to Week 25, and clinical response of \ge 70\% reduction from baseline in HAE attack rate. Clinical response of being HAE attack-free from Week 5 to Week 25 comparing donidalorsen-8 to pooled placebo was not statistically significant, and so no further hierarchical testing was conducted.
L333: The efficacy endpoints in the multiplicity control hierarchy are generally supportive and are clinically and statistically convincing of the efficacy of donidalorsen at either donidalorsen-4 or donidalorsen-4 dosing regimens compared to placebo.
L334: ## 6.2.2.4.5. Subgroup Analyses, Trial CS5
L335: The rate ratio of the time-normalized number of HAE attacks for the prespecified subgroups are presented in Figure 7. No subjects aged 12 to 17 or \ge 65 years of age were randomized to pooled placebo, and so no estimation of comparisons between donidalorsen and pooled placebo could be performed; these subgroups are not depicted in Figure 7. One subject was enrolled in each of the race subgroups of Asian, Multiple, and Other, and so these subgroups have no comparisons between treatment groups; these subgroups are not depicted in Figure 7. The rate ratios of the time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks from Week 1 to Week 25 comparing both donidalorsen groups to pooled placebo were generally consistent across subgroups defined by age group, sex, race, ethnicity, region, predefined prophylactic therapy use, and HAE type.

L339: The rate ratio of time-normalized HAE attacks from Week 1 to Week 25 favored donidalorsen-4 compared to pooled placebo for all subgroups and for most subgroups. The 95% confidence
L340: intervals overlapped with the null value of 1 for the female, Black or African American, Hispanic or Latino, and Yes predefined prophylactic therapy subgroups. The sample sizes in these four subgroups were small.
L341: The rate ratio of time-normalized HAE attacks from Week 1 to Week 25 favored donidalorsen-8 compared to pooled placebo for all subgroups, but the 95% confidence intervals excluded the null value of 1 for most subgroups. Subgroups with 95% confidence intervals that excluded the null value of 1 were age group 18 to 39 years, male, White, Not Hispanic or Latino, region Europe, No predefined prophylactic therapy, and HAE Type I. The overall sample size was smaller for the donidalorsen-8 group than the donidalorsen-4 group by design, and so the subgroup sample sizes are small.
L342: Given that the pathophysiology of the disease and response to therapy are expected to be the same across age groups, the efficacy of donidalorsen in adolescents is extrapolated from the adult efficacy results and supported by matching PK and PD exposure between the age groups (refer to Section 8.1.1).
L343: The efficacy of donidalorsen in geriatric patients was not adequately explored in Trial CS5 due to the limited enrollment of subjects aged 65 years and older (n=2; one enrolled in each donidalorsen treatment arm, 0 randomized to placebo). Although efficacy in this age group has not been established by direct evidence, it may be inferred from the overall efficacy results.
L344: ## **Conclusion**
L345: The interpretation of the subgroup analyses above is limited by small sample sizes. However, the treatment benefit of donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 based on the primary endpoint appears to be similar across subgroups based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, region, predefined prophylactic use, and HAE type.
L346: ## **6.2.2.4.6. Additional Efficacy Analyses, Trial CS5**
L347: ## **6.2.2.4.6.1. Sensitivity Analysis, Trial CS5**
L348: Results of the sensitivity analyses based on negative binomial regression and multiple imputation using jump to reference were consistent with the primary analysis of the primary endpoint of time-normalized number of HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) from Week 1 to 25.
L349: The number of subjects who discontinued early from the FAS was four in the pooled placebo group, one in the donidalorsen-4 group, and two in the donidalorsen-8 group. Of these subjects, three had at least 5 months of follow-up, three had between 3 and 5 months of follow-up, and one had almost 3 months of follow-up. The tipping point analysis investigated the effect of this missing data on the results of the primary analysis. The range of plausible assumptions explored did not identify a tipping point that would reverse the conclusion of the primary analysis.
L350: Six subjects who were from the FAS were excluded from the per-protocol set. Results of the supplementary analysis based on the per-protocol set using both Poisson and negative binomial regression were consistent with the primary analysis.
L351: ## 6.2.2.4.6.2. Angioedema Quality of Life Total Score,
## Trial CS5
L352: ## Issue
L353: Determine whether the AE-QoL total score is fit-for-purpose for the context of use, that is, to support regulatory evaluation of effectiveness (b) (4)
L354: (b) (4)
L355: ## Background
L356: HAE is characterized by unpredictable, recurrent episodes of angioedema, which impact quality of life and daily functioning. At the HAE Patient-Focused Drug Development meeting held at the Agency on September 25, 2017 (CBER 2018), patients with HAE shared the aspects of the disease that had the greatest impact on their lives, including the unpredictability of attack occurrence, the painful abdominal attacks, the dramatic change swelling had on their physical appearance, and the emotional toll the disease had on their lives.
L357: The AE-QoL was used to derive secondary and exploratory endpoints, (b) (4)
L358: There is currently no fit-for-purpose patient-reported outcomes (PROs) for use in HAE prophylaxis clinical trials.
L359: (b) (4)
L360: During the course of the donidalorsen clinical development program, other developers of HAE therapies have also positioned AE-QoL as supportive of efficacy in their respective programs. During the FDA review of another prophylaxis HAE product, AE-QoL total score was reviewed by the Division of Clinical Outcomes Assessment (DCOA). Important deficiencies with the COA tool were identified, rendering AE-QoL unfit for purpose for the regulatory evaluation of efficacy. These deficiencies (outlined below) cannot be overcome with the supportive evidence dossier provided in the donidalorsen NDA.
L361: ## Assessment
L362: During development, the Applicant requested Agency feedback on the AE-QoL and endpoints. The NDA submission includes exact copies of the tool, associated materials, and a supportive evidence dossier.
L363: The AE-QoL questionnaire was developed to assess quality of life impairment in recurrent angioedema patients, including patients with HAE (Weller et al. 2012). This 17-item instrument uses a 5-point Likert scale with response options of never, rarely, sometimes, often, and very often, rated over a recall period of the last 4 weeks. The 17 items within the AE-QoL are organized into 4 distinct domains labeled as follows: functioning, fatigue/mood, fears/shame, and food/nutrition.
L364: Each domain has its own score, and a total score can also be calculated. The items are scored from 0 to 4, and they are summed to provide raw domain scores, which are then transformed into linear scores ranging from 0 to 100. The total score is the sum of all 17 items. Higher scores in the AE-QoL domains and total scores indicate greater levels of impairment of quality of life. In
L365: Trial CS5, the AE-QoL was administered using electronic forms, displayed via a tablet device, on Days 1, 85, and 169 in the Treatment Period, and on Day 91 of the Post-Treatment Period.
L366: There is inadequate qualitative evidence in the published literature, including (Weller et al. 2012), to support the content validity of the AE-QoL for efficacy evaluation in the Applicant's drug development program. In addition, the domains of the AE-QoL are not well-defined and reliable to inform regulatory decision-making. Specifically, for the AE-QoL functioning domain, asking patients about restrictions in their daily lives due to swelling episodes, regardless of whether or not they have actually experienced swelling episodes during the 4-week recall period, will not provide useful information for assessing treatment benefit in the context of a clinical trial. While the core concepts of disease-related symptoms and physical function are reasonable PRO measurement strategies for demonstrating treatment benefit, emotional impacts (such as anxiety and embarrassment) as assessed by the AE-QoL fears/shame domain are distal concepts, and as such, they may be affected by factors external to HAE disease or effect of the investigational product. In addition, the 4-week recall period of the AE-QoL is not appropriate as patients may not reliably recall the occurrence of their HAE attacks during this timeframe. As such, the AE-QoL is not content valid for this context of use.
L367: ## Conclusion
L368: Based on the construction of the instrument, the AE-QoL is not well-defined and reliable to inform regulatory decision-making (b) (4)
L369: ## 6.2.2.4.6.3. Adequacy of Trial Blinding, Trial CS5
L370: ## Issue
L371: Trial CS5 studied two different dosing regimens: donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8. Donidalorsen 80 mg was matched to a placebo group with the same dosing regimen. Subjects and investigators were aware of the assigned dosing regimen. An alternative design to maintain blinding to the dosing regimen is double dummy dosing, in which all subjects take either placebo or the donidalorsen-4 regimen. In the absence of double dummy dosing, it is of interest to examine the sensitivity of the results to the assumption that the two placebo groups were equivalent and trial blinding was adequate.
L372: ## Background
L373: Trial blinding is a fundamental feature of removing bias from experimental results. Because subjects in Trial CS5 were blinded to receipt of drug versus placebo but were aware if their dosing interval was donidalorsen-4 or donidalorsen-8, we sought to evaluate any potential bias introduced to the efficacy results by awareness of dosing interval.
L374: ## Assessment
L375: As an exploratory analysis, the Agency analyzed the time-normalized HAE attack rate (per 4-weeks) as in the primary analysis except that the placebo every 4 weeks and placebo every 8 weeks arms were considered as separate treatment groups. The comparison of each donidalorsen
L376: 80-mg regimen was to its matched placebo. The results of this analysis are presented in Table 17. Although the confidence intervals are wider for this exploratory analysis than in the primary analysis (Table 11), the conclusions remain unchanged. This supports the robustness of the results despite the lack of blinding to the treatment interval. Additionally, an investigator-confirmed HAE attack is considered an objective clinical outcome, and as such, less susceptible to bias from knowledge of assigned treatment interval.
