L388: ## 6.2.2.4.6.4. Efficacy in Reducing HAE Attacks by Location, Trial CS5
L389: ## Issue
L390: An exploratory analysis of efficacy of donidalorsen in reducing HAE attack incidence, analyzed by anatomic location of the attack, was conducted.
L391: ## Background
L392: HAE attacks can result in serious and/or life-threatening sequelae if they affect certain anatomic locations, particularly the larynx. Laryngeal attacks can result in asphyxiation and death. Given this potentially serious outcome, we sought to analyze the efficacy by anatomic location of HAE attacks that occurred during Trial CS5.
L393: ## Assessment
L394: A summary of the history of attacks by location (abdominal, laryngeal, peripheral) is provided in Table 18. Almost all subjects had a history of abdominal (94%) and peripheral (94%) attacks, and the majority of subjects had a history of laryngeal attacks (52%).
L395: A summary of the HAE attacks experienced during the Treatment Period by location and severity is provided in Table 19. The percentage of subjects experiencing abdominal attacks (regardless of severity) were approximately equal in all three treatment groups, while a lower percentage of subjects experienced laryngeal or peripheral attacks in the donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 groups compared to placebo. Few subjects experienced laryngeal attacks, so limited conclusions can be drawn from this data. The severity of attacks in each location followed a trend consistent with the results regardless of severity.

L413: ## 6.2.2.4.6.5. Durability of Treatment Effect, Trial CS5
L414: ## Issue
L415: Because HAE is a chronic disease, the durability of the efficacy of donidalorsen is of particular interest and was explored during the development program.
L416: ## Background
L417: The Applicant conducted two OLE trials: Trial CS7 (extension of the pivotal trial [CS5]) and Trial CS3 (extension of the phase 2 trial [CS2]). See Table 3 for more information. Long-term data from these trials allowed for exploration of durability of efficacy.
L418: ## Assessment
L419: A total of 44 subjects on the donidalorsen-4 regimen for Trial CS5 were enrolled in the open-label extension trial (CS7) and continued the donidalorsen-4 regimen. An additional 14 subjects on the donidalorsen-8 regimen for Trial CS5 who were attack-free for Weeks 17 to 25 were enrolled in the open-label extension Trial (CS7) and continued on the donidalorsen-8 regimen. Figure 9 presents the mean time-normalized HAE attack rate (per 4-weeks) during Trial CS5 and Trial CS7 for these subject groups.
L420: **Figure 9. Exploratory Analysis: Plot of Time-Normalized HAE Attack Rate Per 4 Weeks in Full Analysis Set Population Rolled Over to Trial CS7, Trial CS5, and Trial CS7**
L421: Source: Statistical Reviewer Analysis; adef.xpt
Abbreviations: HAE, hereditary angioedema; n, number of subjects
L422: The time-normalized HAE attack rate was generally consistent across Trial CS7 for the subjects who maintained the treatment as assigned in Trial CS5. However, Trial CS7 lacks a control group and blinding, and therefore these results should be interpreted with caution. Additionally, caution is needed in interpreting the results for the donidalorsen-8 group because the subjects who continued on the donidalorsen-8 regimen in Trial CS7 were a subset of the subjects randomized to the donidalorsen-8 regimen in Trial CS5. Subjects who experienced an HAE attack during Weeks 17 to 25 of Trial CS5 were switched to the donidalorsen-4 regimen for Trial CS7 and their data are not examined here in the evaluation of the durability of the treatment effect.
L423: Although small in sample size, long-term data from Trial CS3 (not presented) were consistent with the results of Trial CS7 and supportive of the durability of efficacy.
L424: ## **Conclusion**
L425: While the OLE trial data are limited by the lack of randomization or a control comparator, due to the well-established natural history of HAE, these data remain useful for characterizing the durability of effectiveness over the longer treatment duration. The HAE attack rate in Trial CS7 supports the longer-term durability of efficacy of donidalorsen, at both donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 dosing intervals, for HAE.
L426: ## 6.3. Key Efficacy Review Issues
L427: ## 6.3.1. Dosing Interval
L428: (b) (4)
L429: ## Issue
L430: The Applicant proposed a dosing interval extension from donidalorsen-4 to donidalorsen-8 in subjects who are attack free with donidalorsen-4 for at least 3 months. The proposed labeling language for dosing states: “The recommended dosage of donidalorsen is 80 mg administered subcutaneously
L431: (b) (4)
L432: (b) (4)
L433: (b) (4) ”
L434: ## Background
L435: The pivotal phase 3, placebo-controlled trial (CS5) evaluated both safety and efficacy of two dosing regimens (donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8) in comparison to placebo. The phase 2, open-label extension trial (CS3) enrolled Rollover subjects from the phase 2 trial (CS2) who previously received either placebo or the donidalorsen-4 regimen and placed them all in the donidalorsen-4 regimen for 12 weeks; subjects then either continued the donidalorsen-4 regimen or received the donidalorsen-8 regimen based on clinical response. The phase 3, open-label extension trial (CS7) included enrollment of Rollover subjects from the phase 3 trial (CS5) who previously received the donidalorsen-8 regimen and placed them on the donidalorsen-8 regimen if they are attack free for \ge 8 weeks (Weeks 17 to 25 in Trial CS5) and otherwise placed them on the donidalorsen-4 regimen.
L436: ## Assessment
L437: Both the donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 dosing regimens demonstrated significantly better efficacy compared to placebo based on the results of Trial CS5. On the primary endpoint, the donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 regimens showed greater reduction in HAE attack rate compared to placebo (-81\% and -55\%, respectively [Table 11]). Thus, the donidalorsen-4 demonstrated greater efficacy compared to donidalorsen-8, but both dosing intervals can be considered effective.
L438: PK/PD results from Trial CS5 showed that the mean donidalorsen steady-state trough concentrations following administration of donidalorsen-4 (0.81 ng/mL) was about 2-fold higher than that following administration of donidalorsen-8 (0.39 ng/mL). In addition, the mean percent reduction from baseline in PKK following the donidalorsen-4 regimen was numerically greater than that following the donidalorsen-8 regimen during the Treatment Period (at Week 25: -73.8\% and -47.2\% for donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8, respectively). The smaller PKK reduction following the donidalorsen-8 compared to the donidalorsen-4 dosing regimen is consistent with the dose response relationship for efficacy between these two regimens. Despite the positive dose-response relationship observed for mean change from baseline in plasma PKK trough concentrations and HAE attack rate, there was variability in these responses at the individual level, suggesting heterogeneity in the disease and response to donidalorsen. While the reduction in plasma PKK trough concentrations following donidalorsen treatment was generally
L439: associated with the reduction in HAE attack rate, there are no dedicated data showing clear association between the magnitude of change from baseline in plasma PKK trough concentration and HAE attack rate at the individual level. See Section 6.1 for more details.
L440: For subjects in the donidalorsen-8 group, fluctuations were observed in the change from baseline in plasma PKK trough concentrations, with an increase in PKK trough concentrations observed just prior to administration of the next dose (i.e., at Week 9 and Week 17). The data suggest that this fluctuation may be associated with the longer dosing interval. Nevertheless, the fluctuation in PKK reduction did not appear to affect clinical response, as no increase in HAE attacks was observed at predose, around the time when PKK was increased (in the donidalorsen-8 group). See Section 14 for more details.
L441: Subjects who were attack-free with donidalorsen-4 for \ge 12 weeks may not respond well with donidalorsen-8 based on Trial CS3, as three out of eight subjects who switched from the donidalorsen-4 to the donidalorsen-8 regimen switched back to the donidalorsen-4 regimen due to experiencing an HAE attack. Despite the small sample size leading to limited data, the Applicant's proposal to switch regimens if "attack free for at least 3 months" does not appear to be well supported.
L442: Subjects who were attack free with donidalorsen-8 for Weeks 17 to 25 in Trial CS5 and rolled over to Trial CS7 on donidalorsen-8 (n=14) had a mean baseline HAE attack rate of 2.87 (SD 2.06) per 4 weeks and mean of 32.6 (SD 19.3) HAE attacks in the 12 months prior to Screening in Trial CS5. This group was comprised of five females (36%) and had a mean age of 30.2 (SD 9.0). Subjects who were not attack free with donidalorsen-8 for Weeks 17 to 25 in Trial CS5 and rolled over to Trial CS7 on donidalorsen-4 (n=6) had a mean baseline HAE attack rate of 4.32 (SD 2.44) per 4 weeks and mean of 34.8 (SD 27.3) HAE attacks in the 12 months prior to Screening in Trial CS5. This group was comprised of five females (83%) and had a mean age of 37.7 (SD 16.1). The Agency did not identify characteristics defining a difference between these two groups.
L443: ## Safety
L444: The risks of both dose intervals are similar and can be mitigated through labeling. See Sections 7.6.1 and 7.7 for more information.
L445: ## Conclusion
L446: Availability of both regimens will permit flexibility in dosing at the physician's discretion and permit engagement in shared decision-making with each patient.
L447: The Agency recommends the following labeling for the dosing regimen: "Donidalorsen can be administered as either 80 mg Q4W or 80 mg Q8W."
L448: ## 6.3.2. Confirmatory Evidence
L449: ## Issue
L450: The substantial evidence of effectiveness of donidalorsen for HAE is established by the single adequate and well-controlled clinical trial (CS5) and CE based on mechanistic data. The purpose of this review issue is to evaluate the source(s) of CE.
L451: ## Background
L452: The CE providing strong mechanistic support includes the well-established pathophysiology of HAE: defective C1-INH leading to dysregulated activity of bradykinin-mediated angioedema. Donidalorsen is an ASO-GalNAc conjugate that causes RNase H1-mediated degradation of PKK mRNA through selective binding to PKK mRNA, which results in decreased production of PKK protein. PKK is a pro-enzyme for plasma kallikrein, which results in the release of bradykinin, a vasodilator causing swelling and pain in HAE. Less substrate for the bradykinin-mediated angioedema pathway leads to less HAE attacks. PKK is a target of several approved HAE therapies.
L453: Additionally, CE is derived from the in vitro and in vivo pharmacology data, the PD data, and clinical dose-ranging data that were reviewed with the NDA.
L454: ## Assessment
L455: ## In Vitro Pharmacology
L456: Treatment of HepatoPac® (co-culture system of primary human hepatocytes and stromal cells [mouse fibroblasts]) with ISIS 721744 and ISIS 546254 (unconjugated parent compound of ISIS 721744) resulted in a dose-dependent reduction of PKK mRNA. The IC50 for ISIS 721744 and ISIS 546254 were 0.19µM and 8.73µM, respectively, indicating that ISIS 721744 is about 46-fold more potent than ISIS 546254 (likely due to cellular uptake through hepatocyte-specific ASGPR).
L457: ## In Vivo Pharmacology
L458: ISIS 721744 does not have perfect alignment to the mouse PKK gene sequence. As such, an unconjugated mouse-specific ASO (i.e., ISIS 482584) was used for in vivo pharmacology studies in mice.
L459: Male C57Bl/6 albino mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle or PKK ASO ISIS 482584 (5, 10, 20, 40, 80, or 160 mg/kg/week) for 3 weeks. ISIS 482584 inhibited PKK liver mRNA and PKK plasma protein expression in a dose-dependent manner.
L460: Permeability assays were performed in male C57Bl/6 albino mice treated with PKK ASO ISIS 482584 (80 mg/kg/week) for 3 weeks. Evans Blue tracer was injected into the tail vein of mice and analyzed for its accumulation in the colon tissue. Some mice were also treated intraperitoneally with the ACE inhibitor captopril (1 mg/kg) at the time of Evans Blue tracer injection or with a C1-inhibitor ASO (40 mg/kg/week for 3 weeks) to enhance vascular
L461: NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
L462: permeability. ISIS 482584 inhibited basal vascular permeability. Further ISIS 482584 inhibited vascular permeability induced by either captopril or C1-inhibitor ASO.
L463: Male C57Bl/6 albino mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle or PKK ASO ISIS 482584 (5, 10, 20, 40, 80, or 160 mg/kg/week) for 3 weeks. ISIS 482584 (10 to 160 mg/kg for 3 weeks) reduced basal activated high molecular weight kininogen cleavage in blood of male mice.
L464: Human KLKB1/PKK transgenic mice were treated by SC administration with ISIS 721744 (0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, or 10 mg/kg) on Day 0 and plasma was collected on Day -1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 42, and 56. A single dose of ISIS 721744 resulted in a dose and time-dependent reduction of plasma PKK protein in human KLKB1/PKK transgenic mice that approached 91% at 10 mg/kg on Day 14 after treatment. After reaching the lowest point at Days 7 to 14, plasma PKK levels were fully restored by Day 42 for the 1.0 mg/kg dose or Day 56 for the 3 mg/kg dose. PKK levels were still 20% below baseline levels by Day 56 for the 10 mg/kg dose.
L465: ## Pharmacodynamic Data
L466: In healthy subjects, a dose-dependent reduction in plasma PKK concentrations from baseline was observed between dosages of 20 and 80 mg SC Q4W. After 4 doses of donidalorsen-4 (last dose administered on Day 85), the nadir in plasma PKK reduction was achieved between Day 71 and Day 99. The mean percent change from baseline for plasma PKK on Day 99 was -53%, -65%, -87%, and -94%, respectively, for 20 mg, 40 mg, 60 mg, and 80 mg Q4W.
L467: In subjects with HAE Type I or II who were treated in either the donidalorsen-4 or donidalorsen-8 groups for 25 weeks, the steady-state PKK change from baseline was achieved by Week 13 (Day 85) and maintained thereafter. The mean percent reduction in plasma PKK from baseline at Week 25 was greater with the donidalorsen-4 regimen (73%) relative to the donidalorsen-8 regimen (47%). With the donidalorsen-8 regimen, a greater fluctuation in plasma PKK change from baseline was observed with smaller reduction from baseline was observed prior to administration of the next dose. This greater fluctuation in plasma PKK is likely associated with the longer donidalorsen-8 dosing interval.
L468: ## Clinical Dose Ranging
L469: Refer to Section 6.3.1 for discussion of increased efficacy with more frequent dosing, in support of clinical dose ranging.
L470: ## Conclusion
L471: The mechanistic data are sufficiently strong and consistent to serve as CE contributing to SEE for this program.
L472: ## 7. Safety (Risk and Risk Management)
L473: ## 7.1. Potential Risks or Safety Concerns Based on Nonclinical Data
L474: The nonclinical safety of donidalorsen was evaluated in good laboratory practice (GLP)-compliant safety pharmacology (cardiovascular, respiratory, and central nervous system [CNS] in monkeys and human ether-a-go-go related gene [hERG] in human embryonic kidney-293 [HEK-293] cells), repeat-dose toxicity (13-week mouse, 26-week mouse, and 13-week interim/39-week monkey), genotoxicity (Ames, chromosome aberration, and mouse bone marrow micronucleus), carcinogenicity (6-month Tg.rasH2 mouse), and reproductive and developmental toxicity (combined fertility and development mouse and pre- and postnatal development [PPND] mouse) studies. Donidalorsen does not align perfectly to the mouse PKK gene sequence, so the mouse toxicity studies also evaluated mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 to assess on-target effects.
L475: ## Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion
L476: Unconjugated donidalorsen was measurable in the liver and kidney after SC administration in mice and monkeys. Donidalorsen was highly bound (\ge 96.81\%) to whole blood plasma proteins in human, monkey, and mouse.
L477: As determined by the Applicant, the primary route of elimination of donidalorsen is initial rapid hydrolysis of the GalNAc conjugate in tissues, followed by slow nuclease-mediated metabolism of the unconjugated oligonucleotide, and subsequent excretion of chain-shortened metabolites, as well as full-length oligonucleotides, albeit minor in urine and feces. There were no unique metabolites found in humans compared to animal species. For donidalorsen linker-related metabolites, the GalNAc moiety is hydrolyzed intracellularly following uptake into tissues and the THA linker undergoes extensive oxidative metabolism, and is nearly completely eliminated via biliary excretion, and to a lesser extent, renal excretion, within 24 hours after administration.
L478: ## Safety Pharmacology
L479: Donidalorsen (single doses of 12 and 30 mg/kg SC) had no adverse effects on cardiovascular, respiratory, or CNS parameters in monkeys. Donidalorsen did not statistically inhibit hERG current in HEK-293 cells stably transfected with hERG cDNA with an estimated IC_{50} greater than 300\mu M. In general, oligonucleotides are not thought to interact with the hERG channel.
L480: ## General Toxicology
L481: Donidalorsen-related toxicity findings in the 26-week mouse study and/or the 13-week interim/39-week monkey study included effects on thrombocytopenia and hematology (monkeys), coagulation (monkeys), liver (mice and monkeys), kidney (monkeys), and injection site (mice and monkeys).
L482: ## Thrombocytopenia, Hematology, and Coagulation
L483: In monkeys, severe thrombocytopenia was noted in one female and one male at 12 and 30 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, respectively. Thrombocytopenia was not seen in either animal during the recovery period. Platelet decreases were accompanied by mild to marked decreases in red cell mass with mild to moderate increases in reticulocyte counts and/or increased polychromasia. The female had mild SC tissue necrosis with fibrin and hemorrhage at one of the injection sites, and both the female and male had red nasal discharge, red skin discoloration, bruising, and/or petechial hemorrhage at various body sites, which may have accounted for the decrease in red cell mass and the increase in reticulocyte counts. Complement Bb levels (marker of alternative pathway activation) were slightly elevated in males at 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and in females at 12 and 30 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen. Minimal prolongations in mean activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) time were seen in males and females at 30 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen but were not evident by 24 hours postdose.
L484: ## Liver
L485: In mice, liver histopathology findings included minimal or slight centrilobular hepatocellular hypertrophy in males (1, 4, and 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen) and one female (12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen), which correlated with increased mean liver weights (4 and 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen) and liver enzymes (AST, ALT, and/or ALP). There was also an increase in the severity (slight to marked) of hepatocyte vacuolation in males (4 and 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen), which correlated with gross pathology findings of liver discoloration at all dose levels. These findings were consistent with uptake of donidalorsen.
L486: In monkeys, liver histopathology findings included hepatocyte hypertrophy (\ge 6 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen terminal), accumulation of basophilic granules in hepatocytes (\ge 2 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen terminal and \ge 6 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen interim) and Kupffer cells (\ge 6 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen interim and terminal), and sporadic perivascular/vascular inflammation in one male (at 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen interim).
L487: ## Kidney
L488: In monkeys, kidney histopathology findings included accumulation of basophilic granules in tubular epithelial cells (\ge 2 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen interim and terminal).
L489: ## Injection Sites
L490: In mice, injection site histopathology findings included increased incidences and/or severity of infiltrates of vacuolated macrophages, mononuclear cells, and mixed cells, as well as fibrocyte vacuolation in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and/or 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. These findings at the SC injection sites correlated with increased leukocyte counts.
L491: In monkeys, injection site histopathology findings at interim and/or terminal sacrifices (generally at all doses with dose-related incidence and/or severity), included: basophilic granules, macrophages, fibrosis, mixed leukocyte infiltration, mononuclear cell infiltration, mixed cell
L492: NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
L493: infiltration/inflammation, perivascular/vascular inflammation, myofiber degeneration/regeneration, hemorrhage, and necrosis.
L494: ## **Reproductive and Developmental Toxicology**
L495: The potential reproductive and developmental toxicity of donidalorsen and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 were evaluated in combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice and a PPND study in mice. No adverse effects on reproductive and developmental parameters were seen.
L496: ## **Genotoxicity**
L497: Donidalorsen was negative for genotoxicity (mutagenicity or clastogenicity) in the in vitro bacterial reverse mutation test (Ames assay), in vitro chromosome aberration assay in cultured Chinese Hamster Lung (CHL) cells, and bone marrow micronucleus assay in mice.
L498: ## **Carcinogenicity**
L499: In a 6-month carcinogenicity study in transgenic (Tg.rasH2) mice, SC administration of donidalorsen (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg for males and 10, 20, or 60 mg/kg for females) or mouse-specific surrogate ISIS 722059 (10 mg/kg) once every 2 weeks (Q2W) did not result in a statistically significant increase in tumors compared to the vehicle control in male mice. The carcinogenicity study was inadequate for female mice because a maximum tolerated dose (MTD) was not achieved and no other valid basis to support the high dose was discernable. Of note, at the time of the special protocol assessment (SPA) for the 6-month carcinogenicity protocol, the Executive Carcinogenicity Assessment Committee could not recommend doses for female mice for the proposed study, as no acceptable basis for dose selection could be identified in the non-GLP-compliant 14-week dose range finding (DRF) study in Tg.rasH2 mice.
L500: A 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats is ongoing. At the time of the pre-NDA meeting, the Division agreed that it would be acceptable to submit a summary of the in-life data for the 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats at the time of the NDA submission and to submit the final report as a postmarketing requirement (PMR).
L501: ## **7.2. Potential Risks or Safety Concerns Based on Drug Class or Other Drug-Specific Factors**
L502: Donidalorsen is a prekallikrein-directed GalNAc-conjugated ASO. The potential safety concerns for donidalorsen are based on both the molecule and the target.
L503: ## **ASOs**
L504: FDA-approved ASOs for intravenous or subcutaneous administration include mipomersen, inotersen, eteplirsen, golodirsen, vilpolarsen, casimersen, tofersen, defibrotide, and nusinersen. Safety risks associated with systemically administered ASOs have included injection site reactions, liver toxicity (Boxed Warning for mipomersen), thrombocytopenia (Boxed Warning
L505: NDA 219407
Dawnzera (donidalorsen)
L506: for inotersen), coagulation abnormalities, and kidney toxicity (Boxed Warning for inotersen). Hypersensitivity reactions have also been reported.
L507: Approved GalNAc conjugated ASOs include eplontersen and olezarsen. GalNAc conjugation is thought to enhance the safety of ASOs by targeting delivery to hepatocytes which improves the activity of ASO, allowing for lower dosages and potentially improved safety. It is not known if liver-targeted ASOs accumulate in the liver over time. The known class effects of ASOs (liver toxicity, thrombocytopenia, and glomerulonephritis) were not identified as risks for eplontersen. Olezarsen is labeled for hypersensitivity reactions, decreased platelet counts, and increased liver enzymes.
L508: ## **Kallikrein Inhibitors**
L509: Approved HAE products which target prekallikrein include lanadelumab and berotralstat for prophylaxis, and sebetrolstat for acute treatment of HAE attacks. Safety risks include coagulation abnormalities and hypersensitivity reactions.
L510: ## 7.3. Potential Risks or Safety Concerns Identified Through Postmarket Experience
L511: Not applicable. This drug is not yet commercially available in any country.
L512: ## 7.4. FDA Approach to the Safety Review
L513: The sources of the clinical trial safety database are shown in Table 3.
L514: The clinical data scientists and clinical reviewer within the Agency performed independent safety analyses using R Studio 4.1.3, JMP, MAED, and Office of Computational Science Analysis Studio software programs. The safety assessment is primarily based on data from Trial CS5; only safety data from Trial CS5 is included in labeling. Supportive safety data is provided by Trial CS2 part A and the OLE trials (CS7, a continuation of CS5, and CS3, a continuation of CS2) and is discussed in Section 17. Given the differences in design and duration across trials safety from each trial was reviewed independently. Given the small sample size of the clinical program, pooled safety data was used to support the review of the Key Safety Review Issues in Section 7.7. The pooled safety analysis incorporates data from Trials CS2, CS3, CS5, and CS7.
L515: All safety analyses were conducted in the safety population, which consisted of any subject who received at least one dose of donidalorsen. For both Trial CS5 and Trial CS2, the safety population and the intent-to-treat (ITT) population were the same.
L516: ## 7.5. Adequacy of the Clinical Safety Database
L517: No data quality or integrity issues were identified in the submitted datasets or CRFs. Definitions of adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) were consistent with Code of Federal Regulations 312.32 (21 CFR 312.12 2004). The Applicant coded AEs using the Medical
L518: Dictionary for Regulatory Activities version 26.1, and determined AE severity using the FDA guidance for industry *Toxicity Grading Scale for Healthy Adult and Adolescent Volunteers Enrolled in Preventive Vaccine Clinical Trials* (September 2007). Any AE not listed in that grading scale was graded as mild, moderate, or severe (see Section 15.1.6 for definitions). The Applicant's translation of verbatim terms to the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities preferred terms (PTs) for the events reported in the trial was reviewed and found to be acceptable. Safety monitoring in the clinical program was adequate to inform the risks of donidalorsen. See Section 15.1.5 for the schedule and review of safety assessments.

L578: ## 7.7. Key Safety Review Issues
L579: ## 7.7.1. Injection Site Reactions
L580: ## Issue
L581: Injection site reactions are a common adverse reaction from SC injectable drug products and for antisense oligonucleotide products. Injection site reactions were observed during the donidalorsen development program. The Applicant proposes to include injection site reactions (ISRs) in the common adverse drug reaction table in Section 6 of the PI.
L582: ## Background
L583: Injection site reactions are a known class effect of ASOs, with reported rates as high as 84% for some ASOs (mipomersen).
L584: ## Assessment
L585: Findings at the SC injection site were noted in the 26-week mouse study with donidalorsen and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059, and the 39-week monkey study with donidalorsen.
L586: Our primary safety review focuses on Trial CS5, with supportive safety analysis from the other clinical trials in the development program (see Table 3 under Section 3) due to the small size of the safety database.
L587: In terms of ISR AEs in Trial CS5, there was an increased incidence of events in the donidalorsen-4 group, with 11 (24%) subjects experiencing an ISR based on the Local Administration Reaction narrow OCMQ compared to 4% for donidalorsen-8 and 5% for placebo (see Table 24). When accounting for the number of injections, the incidence remained higher for donidalorsen-4 (11/270 (6 injections x 45 subjects) = 4%) compared to donidalorsen-8 (1/69 (3 injections x 23 subjects) = 1%). Injection site erythema was the most frequently reported of the OCMQ AEs (n=6, 13%), followed by injection site discoloration, injection site pain, and injection site pruritus (n=3, 7% for each). All ISRs were nonserious, mild in severity, and did not result in discontinuation of IP. In contrast, only one subject per group in the donidalorsen-8 and placebo groups experienced an ISR.
L588: In Trial CS7 (the OLE trial following Trial CS5), which lacked a placebo control group, a greater proportion of subjects in the Rollover donidalorsen-4 group (16%) experienced ISRs compared with the Rollover donidalorsen-8 group (6%) per the Local Administration Reaction narrow OCMQ. All ISRs were nonserious and did not result in any action taken with the trial drug. Except for one event of moderate severity, all ISRs were mild. Of Naïve subjects, 37% experienced ISRs per the Local Administration Reaction narrow OCMQ. Although this is the highest incidence noted in any cohort across the donidalorsen HAE program, all ISRs in Naïve subjects were non-serious and did not result in any action taken with the trial drug. The majority of ISRs were mild (25%) or moderate (6%) in severity.
L589: In Trial CS3 (the OLE trial following Trial CS2), which lacked a placebo control group, 35% of subjects in the HAE-1/HAE-2 group (6/17 subjects, 40 events) experienced at least one ISR per the Local Administration Reaction narrow OCMQ. One subject in the HAE-1/HAE-2 group (donidalorsen 100 mg Q4W [Flexible Dosing Period]) permanently discontinued IP due to six moderate TEAEs of injection site discoloration.
L590: The Applicant provided a pooled safety analysis of 173 subjects who received donidalorsen across Trials CS2, CS3, CS5 and CS7. The three subjects enrolled in Trial CS2 part B are excluded from the Agency's analysis due to their diagnosis with HAE Type III, bringing the sample size for the pooled safety analysis to 170 subjects.
L591: Out of these 170 subjects, 44 (26%) subjects experienced at least one ISR, with the number of individual ISR events totaling 237. Thus, those subjects who do experience ISR may experience multiple and/or repeated events over time. Incidence of ISRs compared across dosing arms shows the highest incidence in the donidalorsen-4 dosing interval (28%), while donidalorsen-8 is similar to placebo (7% for both groups). The incidence of ISR appears generally stable with subsequent injections, i.e., a higher incidence of ISR was not observed with increased number of previous injections. The most common ISR reported in the any donidalorsen treatment group
L592: were Injection site erythema [20 (11.8%)], Injection site discoloration [12 (7.1%)], Injection site pruritus [11 (6.5%)], and Injection site pain [10 (5.9%)].
L593: Regarding the timing of onset of ISRs, ISRs occurring after the first dose of donidalorsen occurred in 11 (25%) of the 44 subjects who developed ISRs: nine (21%) on the same day as the first dose and two on Day 2 after the first dose. Out of 44 subjects, 36 (82%) subjects experienced 135 ISRs within 2 days after the most recent dose of donidalorsen.
L594: Regarding outcome and duration of ISRs, out of 237 ISRs, 209 (88%) were resolved at the time of database lock, with the remaining 28 (12%) ongoing. Out of 209 resolved ISRs, 45 (22%) ISRs resolved within 2 days and 84 (40%) ISRs resolved within 7 days. The most common ongoing ISRs were injection site discoloration (21 events in four subjects). As noted previously, one (2%) subject out of 44 experienced an ISR leading to permanent trial drug discontinuation; this subject received donidalorsen 100 mg Q4W and experienced six moderate events of injection site discoloration.
L595: Regarding severity, out of 237 ISRs, 203 (86%) ISRs in 43 subjects were reported as mild, and 34 (14%) ISR in 7 subjects were reported as moderate. No serious or severe ISRs were reported. The severity of ISRs appears generally stable with subsequent injections, i.e., an increased severity of ISRs was not observed with increased number of previous injections.
L596: Overall, the cumulative, pooled data regarding ISRs indicates that the pivotal trial safety data may provide an accurate overview of this observed risk of donidalorsen use, with additional supportive data about the characteristics of observed ISRs.
L597: ## **Conclusion**
L598: ISRs were observed in 24% of subjects in the donidalorsen-4 group of the pivotal trial (CS5), while 4 to 5% of subjects in the donidalorsen-8 and placebo groups experienced ISRs. The features of ISRs were similar between Trial CS5 and the cumulative, pooled safety data from the four clinical trials. ISRs were nonserious, with the vast majority mild in severity. The incidence and severity of ISRs did not vary with number of past injections. The most frequent AE PTs were injection site erythema, discoloration, pain, and pruritus. ISRs developed upon exposure to the first dose in 25% of subjects who eventually developed ISRs, and whether on the first or subsequent injection, they most commonly occurred within 1 to 2 days of the injection. The majority of ISRs resolved within 7 days. Treatment discontinuation due to ISRs was infrequent; across the program, one subject permanently discontinued donidalorsen due to six moderate ISR events. Availability of donidalorsen-8 provides options for prescribers to mitigate the risk of injection site reactions with donidalorsen-4.
L599: ## 7.7.2. Bleeding Events, Thrombocytopenia, and Coagulation
L600: ## Issue
L601: Bleeding risks, including thrombocytopenia and effects on the clotting cascade (prolonged aPTT) (Crooke et al. 2019) are known ASO class effects (regardless of the target protein). The donidalorsen clinical program was designed to monitor and mitigate this potential risk.
L602: ## Background
L603: ASO class effects, including thrombocytopenia, are generally thought to be dose-dependent, transient, and self-limited. Though the precise mechanism of thrombocytopenia is not known, it is thought to be due to ASOs binding to platelets and causing increased platelet clearance. Importantly, with chronic ASO administration, nonhuman primate and human clinical trials have revealed a risk of sporadic, unpredictable, severe thrombocytopenia. To our knowledge, such events have not been observed in humans receiving GalNAC-conjugated ASOs, which allow for reduced systemic dosage via increased potency, with the goal of reducing overall toxicities.
L604: Additionally, some kallikrein inhibiting products are known to cause asymptomatic prolongation of aPTT in clinical use; however, bleeding events are not associated with this laboratory abnormality. The aPTT assay primarily evaluates the intrinsic coagulation pathway, which includes kallikrein and other clotting factors. Meanwhile, PT and INR evaluate the extrinsic pathway, and in the donidalorsen program they were utilized as a means to assess hepatic synthetic function.
L605: ## Assessment
L606: In the 13-week interim/39-week monkey study with a 26-week recovery period, severe thrombocytopenia was noted in one female and one male at 12 and 30 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, respectively. Thrombocytopenia was not seen in either animal during the 26-week recovery period.
L607: In the 13-week interim/39-week monkey study with a 26-week recovery period, minimal prolongations in mean aPTT time were seen in males and females at 30 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen but were not evident by 24-hours postdose.
L608: Our primary safety review focuses on Trial CS5, which permits placebo-controlled analysis over 24 weeks, with supportive safety analysis from the other clinical trials in the development program (see Table 3). These other clinical trials, though they have limitations such as a shorter duration (for Trial CS2) and lack of placebo control (for the OLE trials), are useful due to the small size of the safety database and the longer-term data of the OLE trials. For each individual trial, and for pooled results from Trials CS5, CS2, CS7, and CS3, TEAEs and laboratory results were reviewed for signals of bleeding risk, thrombocytopenia, and aPTT prolongation.
L609: ## **Bleeding Adverse Events**
L610: Bleeding TEAEs were identified by the Hemorrhage OCMQ (Narrow).
L611: In Trial CS5, there was a slight trend towards an increased incidence of bleeding TEAEs in the donidalorsen-4 group (see Table 25). However, the three TEAEs occurring in the donidalorsen-4 group were all mild and self-limited, without concomitant clinically significant abnormalities in coagulation laboratory results (including platelet counts, PT, and INR), and none led to treatment discontinuation. The events in donidalorsen-8 and placebo both started on Day 1, making them very unlikely to be related to the trial drug.

L622: In Trial CS3 (the OLE trial following Trial CS2), which lacked a placebo control group, two (10%) subjects experienced bleeding TEAEs, which were mild. These events required no action to be taken with the trial drug.
L623: The Agency also examined concomitant use of anticoagulants, antiplatelet or blood-thinning medications in subjects with bleeding TEAEs; no subjects with concomitant use of such medications were identified.
L624: Review of the 120-day safety update report did not reveal substantive, new information about bleeding TEAEs. Given the difference in exposure between the donidalorsen treatment groups and placebo in Trials CS5, CS2, CS7, and CS3, the Applicant conducted an exposure-adjusted analysis of bleeding TEAEs with the 120-day safety update report. The incidence rate (per 100 patient years of exposure) of bleeding TEAEs (per the Hemorrhages broad search SMQ) was 14% in the donidalorsen-4 group, 5% in the donidalorsen-8 group, and 26% in the placebo group. Thus, the incidence of bleeding TEAEs was higher in the placebo group than in the donidalorsen treatment groups.
L625: These results do not suggest an increased risk of bleeding TEAEs with donidalorsen exposure.
L626: ## Platelet Counts
L627: The effect of donidalorsen on platelet counts was also evaluated. There was no apparent exposure response between donidalorsen systemic exposure and change in platelet counts according to the clinical pharmacology analysis; see Section 8.1.2 for details.
L628: Aggregate data on platelet counts over time were reviewed. Figure 11 shows the mean absolute change from baseline for platelet count; the mean values at each timepoint are displayed in the text box below the figure. Treatment with donidalorsen at both doses tended to decrease platelet counts, with a sharper downward slope in the donidalorsen-4 group, which converged with the donidalorsen-8 slope by Week 25. The platelet counts in the donidalorsen-4 group reached a plateau by Week 17, with the mean absolute value having decreased by 15,000 cells/mm3.

L656: ## Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time
L657: In Trial CS5, mean aPTT remained within the reference range, and no imbalance in prolonged aPTT was observed compared to placebo. No clinically relevant changes in aPTT values were noted in Trial CS5. Review of safety data from Trials CS7, CS2, and CS3 showed, similarly, no apparent safety signal related to aPTT values.
L658: ## Conclusion
L659: ## Bleeding
L660: In Trial CS5, there was a slight trend towards an increased incidence of bleeding TEAEs in the donidalorsen-4 group (see Table 25). However, the three TEAEs occurring in the donidalorsen-4 group were all mild and self-limited, without concomitant clinically significant abnormalities in coagulation laboratory results (including platelet counts, PT, and INR), and none led to treatment discontinuation.
L661: In Trial CS7, 17 (12%) of all subjects experienced one or more bleeding TEAEs, with none occurring in the subjects who received the donidalorsen-8 dosing regimen. These events were typically mild or moderate in severity, did not lead to treatment discontinuation, and were not associated with concomitant clinically significant abnormalities in coagulation laboratory results. Results from Trials CS2 and CS3 were consistent with Trials CS5 and CS7.
L662: ## Platelet Counts
L663: The placebo-controlled safety data from Trial CS5 revealed a sustained decrease in platelet counts, with a magnitude of approximately 15,000 to 20,000 cells/\text{mm}^3, that stabilized in approximately 4 months and did not typically result in clinically significant thrombocytopenia or bleeding events. The donidalorsen treatment arms demonstrated a greater mean percent change in platelet count at Week 25 (9.6% for donidalorsen-4, 7.9% for donidalorsen-8) compared to placebo (1.4%). Results from CS2, CS3, and CS7 were consistent with Trial CS5.
L664: Overall, although no serious clinical sequelae related to bleeding or thrombocytopenia were observed in the clinical program, the theoretical risk of uncommon, severe thrombocytopenia or
L665: bleeding remains, due to the ASO class effects. Therefore, the decreased platelets observed in Trial CS5 will be included in labeling.
L666: ## 7.7.3. Hepatic Function Effects
L667: ## Issue
L668: Due to the known ASO class effect of hepatotoxicity and donidalorsen's pharmacologic mechanism, which relies on GalNAC binding hepatocytes, the occurrence of clinically significant hepatocellular injury risk with donidalorsen use was investigated.
L669: ## Background
L670: Antisense oligonucleotide class effects, including hepatotoxicity, are generally thought to be dose-dependent, transient, and self-limited. Risk of hepatotoxicity with elevations of ALT and AST, and hepatic steatosis were seen in the development programs for mipomersen and inotersen, which are ASOs targeting hepatic gene expression. Inotersen labeling recommends baseline and monthly monitoring of liver enzymes.
L671: Olezarsen, a GalNAC-conjugated ASO for familial chylomicronemia, was approved in 2024 with a postmarketing requirement to evaluate the potential for drug-induced liver injury (DILI) with long-term use of this product. Olezarsen is labeled for increase in liver enzymes. Olezarsen was associated with average increases in ALT, AST, and gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) within the first 3 months which stabilized and remained within reference range. There were a higher proportion of olezarsen-treated subjects in whom serious hepatic events occurred and increases in liver enzymes led to discontinuation or interruption of the trial drug. Liver enzymes returned towards baseline with discontinuation of olezarsen. There were no cases of Hy's Law, an indicator of drug-induced liver injury.6
L672: ## Assessment
L673: ## Nonclinical
L674: In the 26-week mouse study, liver histopathology findings included minimal or slight centrilobular hepatocellular hypertrophy (1, 4, and 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen), which correlated with increased mean liver weights (4 and 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen) and liver enzymes (AST, ALT, and/or ALP). There was also an increase in the severity (slight to marked) of hepatocyte vacuolation in males (4 and 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen), which correlated with gross pathology findings of liver discoloration at all dose levels. These findings were consistent with uptake of donidalorsen.
L675: In the 13-week interim/39-week monkey study, liver histopathology findings included hepatocyte hypertrophy (\ge 6 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen terminal), accumulation of basophilic granules in hepatocytes (\ge 2 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen terminal and \ge 6 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen
L676: 6 See FDA Summary Review for Olezarsen (NDA 218614), dated December 19, 2024, available at https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/218614Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf.
L677: interim) and Kupffer cells (\ge 6 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen interim and terminal), and sporadic perivascular/vascular inflammation (12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen interim).
L678: Our primary safety review focuses on Trial CS5, which permits placebo-controlled analysis over 24 weeks, with supportive safety analysis from the other clinical trials in the development program (see Table 3, under Section 3). These other clinical trials, though they have limitations such as a shorter duration (for Trial CS2) and lack of placebo control (for the OLE trials), are useful due to the small size of the safety database and the longer-term data of the OLE trials. For each individual trial, and for pooled data from Trials CS5, CS2, CS7, and CS3, TEAEs and laboratory results were reviewed for signals of hepatotoxicity.
L679: ## Adverse Events
L680: In Trial CS5, there were no clear imbalances between subjects receiving donidalorsen versus placebo in the incidence of TEAEs such as ALT and AST elevations, jaundice, PTs in the hepatic injury OCMQ (narrow or broad), or cases meeting Hy's Law criteria.
L681: Overall, analysis of TEAEs did not reveal a signal of hepatic injury. However, given that this result could be consistent with products resulting in DILI, in which premarket clinical trials reveal only laboratory abnormalities not rising to the level of an imbalance in adverse events, further investigation was completed.
L682: ## Liver Function Tests
L683: Because DILI is most commonly asymptomatic and diagnosed by laboratory testing, laboratory results for AST, ALT, ALP, GGT, bilirubin, and PT/INR were reviewed for each clinical trial.
L684: Figure 13 shows the mean absolute change from baseline for AST, ALT, ALP, and GGT during Trial CS5; total and direct bilirubin are not shown as these did not reveal a notable trend. The mean change from baseline and absolute values at each timepoint are displayed in the text boxes below each figure. Subclinical increases in AST and ALT were observed at a magnitude that was similar at both doses of donidalorsen, while the increases in ALP and GGT were of larger magnitude at higher doses. The increases in AST, ALT, and ALP appeared to reach a plateau during the trial, while there is not a clear plateau in GGT increase.

L711: ## INR
L712: No subject in any treatment group experienced INR elevations &gt;1.5× ULN. A greater proportion of subjects in the donidalorsen-4 group (17.8%) and donidalorsen-8 group (17.4%) experienced mild INR elevations (&lt;1.5× ULN) compared with the placebo group (9.1%). INR values shifted from normal to mildly elevated (&gt;1 to 1.5× ULN) in 16% of donidalorsen-4 and 17% of donidalorsen-8 subjects.

L722: One TEAE, moderate related ALT increased, led to permanent treatment discontinuation in one subject in the donidalorsen-8 group (plotted in the Temple's Corollary quadrant in Figure 14). The subject was a 45-year-old White female with HAE type I and a history of cholecystectomy in (b) (6), enrolled in the donidalorsen-8 group. Relevant prior medications included danazol (taken for years and discontinued 3 weeks before starting trial treatment), desogestrel (started 3 weeks prior to first dose of trial treatment), and icatibant acetate. Relevant concomitant medications, taken while on trial, included C1 esterase inhibitor (Cinryze), icatibant acetate, and desogestrel. LFT results for the subject over the trial are shown in Figure 15. The subject received her Week 9 dose of donidalorsen on Day 58, when ALT was elevated to 97 U/L (1.8\times ULN), and the AE of ALT increased of mild intensity was reported. No treatment was recorded for the AE. On Day 92, ALT peaked at 230 U/L (4.3\times ULN) and the AE severity worsened from mild to moderate. By Day 100, ALT decreased to 137 U/L (2.6\times ULN), and the severity improved to mild. No treatment was reported for these AEs. AST, GGT, and total bilirubin were within normal range throughout the trial, except on Day 92, AST was elevated at 81 U/L (1.9\times ULN). On Day 170, trial treatment was permanently discontinued due to the AE of ALT increased; the subject had received a total of two doses, on Days 1 and 58. On Day 204, ALT returned to normal at 26 U/L, and a liver ultrasound revealed that the liver was slightly enlarged with smooth contours and increased parenchymal echogenicity, consistent with grade 1 hepatic steatosis (judged by the investigator to be mild, not related to trial treatment). On Day 211, the subject's ALT was 31 U/L, and the subject completed her final trial visit.

L757: ## Bilirubin and GGT
L758: One subject in Trial CS7 who was Naïve to donidalorsen, treated with donidalorsen-4, experienced severe bilirubin &gt;1.5\times ULN, which was also a \ge 2-grade shift from normal, and GGT &gt;5.0\times ULN with concurrent elevations in AST to &lt;3.0\times ULN. The subject also had multiple comorbidities.
L759: GGT elevation (\ge 5\times ULN) was reported in two subjects in Trial CS7. Both of these subjects experienced elevated GGT at baseline. No action was taken with donidalorsen as a result, and these subjects continued in the trial. Other confounding factors include long-term use of danazol, and congestive heart failure.
L760: ## ALP
L761: Across Trials CS2, CS3, CS5, and CS7, no subject in any treatment group experienced ALP elevations \ge 2\times ULN.
L762: ## INR
L763: In Trial CS7, one subject (b) (6) experienced concurrent TEAEs for increased PT (severity fluctuated between mild to moderate over 140 days with no dose change) and increased INR (mild, resolved after 92 days with no dose change); no bleeding events were recorded for this subject.
L764: ## Integrated Summary
L765: Due to the small sample size of the pivotal trial, safety data from the additional trials (the phase 2 Trial CS2 and the ongoing open-label Trials CS3 and CS7, including data from the 120-day
L766: safety update) were included in evaluation of hepatic effects of donidalorsen. This summary incorporates findings across the program.
L767: Regarding TEAEs, all abnormal liver function TEAEs were nonserious and mild to moderate in severity. Two subjects discontinued the trial drug due to these TEAEs: one for ALT increase related to donidalorsen, despite not meeting a stopping rule, and one for ALT increase that did meet a stopping rule.
L768: No subject met criteria for Hy's law. Clinically relevant levels of LFT elevation occurred infrequently, while subclinical elevations in ALT, AST, GGT, and INR were observed more frequently with donidalorsen compared to placebo. Low-level elevations in AST and ALT (&lt;3\times ULN) are common, nonspecific, and not concerning for DILI.
L769: A total of eight donidalorsen recipients (five in the donidalorsen-4 group and three in the donidalorsen-8 group) experienced ALT or AST elevations \ge 3\times ULN. Of these, two subjects had ALT levels that peaked at a level \ge 5\times ULN (one also experienced an AST \ge 3\times ULN), and one subject peaked at ALT &gt;8\times ULN (possibly due to acute EBV infection). Two subjects discontinued donidalorsen due to LFT abnormalities.
L770: Two subjects experienced severe (\sim 1.5\times ULN) elevations of bilirubin and two subjects experienced severe (\ge 5.0\times ULN) increases in GGT, but these did not require treatment discontinuation. Plausible etiologies were present for these subjects, including Gilbert syndrome, multiple comorbidities, elevated GGT level at baseline, prior long-term use of danazol, and congestive cardiac failure.
L771: ## **Conclusion**
L772: There was no clear imbalance for liver related TEAEs between donidalorsen and placebo. There were no cases of Hy's law. Clinically relevant levels of LFT elevation occurred infrequently, while subclinical elevations in ALT, AST, GGT, and INR were observed more frequently with donidalorsen compared to placebo. Low-level elevations in AST and ALT (&lt;3\times ULN) were common, nonspecific, and not concerning for DILI. A total of three subjects had ALT \ge 5\times ULN.
L773: Due to the known ASO class effect of hepatotoxicity, the accumulation of ASOs in the liver over time, the small safety database, and the unknown consequences of lifetime treatment with ASOs, a PMR will be issued to assess the potential for chronic drug-induced liver injury with long-term treatment.
L774: ## 7.7.4. Hypersensitivity Reactions
L775: ## **Issue**
L776: During the NDA review process, an adverse reaction of anaphylaxis in a subject enrolled in the ongoing trial (CS7) was reported as a Safety Report to IND 142564. The safety assessment relies on the response to an Information Request that was sent to the Applicant to provide relevant information to evaluate this safety signal.
L777: ## **Background**
L778: Hypersensitivity reactions are a known, labeled AE for several FDA-approved ASO products. Hypersensitivity reactions are listed in the Warning and Precautions section of labeling for at least four of these products: defibrotide, inotersen, eteplirsen, and golodirsen. The observed symptoms include rash, urticaria, skin exfoliation, chills, flushing, dysphagia, tachycardia, and bronchospasm. Serious hypersensitivity reactions occurred in the development program for volanesorsen, including suspected anaphylaxis in one subject.8
L779: ## **Assessment**
L780: For donidalorsen, the subject was a 20-year-old White female who received donidalorsen-4 in Trial CS5 and Trial CS7. The SAE with PT Hypersensitivity (Verbatim: Allergic reaction) occurred on Trial CS7 Day 816 and resulted in permanent treatment discontinuation. Per the case narrative, the event started 5 minutes after donidalorsen injection. The subject developed a red rash covering most of her body, dyspnea, perioral swelling, and chest pain. The investigator administered oral diphenhydramine and subcutaneous epinephrine. Her baseline vital signs were normal and she developed tachycardia to 145 bpm at the time of the event, but blood pressure was not measured. Thirty minutes later, when symptoms had subsided, heart rate was 113 and BP was 126/82 mm Hg. Tryptase was not drawn. The subject had also taken ibuprofen 200 mg to prevent postinjection site pain; she reported having tolerated ibuprofen in the past. The narrative states that a skin allergy test conducted with donidalorsen demonstrated a negative reaction, without providing details on the quality/results of this test, so this cannot be interpreted as meaningful. Given the fulfillment of Sampson's criteria (Sampson et al. 2006), the temporal relationship to donidalorsen, and the lack of an alternative diagnosis, this event is consistent with anaphylaxis due to donidalorsen.
L781: Using a cumulative cutoff date of February 24, 2025, a search of the clinical and safety databases was conducted using the OCMQs of Hypersensitivity (broad) and Anaphylactic Reaction (broad) to identify potential cases of hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis, from two completed trials (CS2 and CS5) and two ongoing clinical trials (CS3 and CS7) in the donidalorsen clinical development program. The cumulative exposure across the four trials at the cutoff date was 177 subjects. Out of 53 events meeting the Hypersensitivity (broad) OCMQ criteria, the Applicant identified five events (PTs: four Hypersensitivity and one Rash) in three subjects (all in Trial CS7) that are consistent with non-serious hypersensitivity to donidalorsen (i.e., the temporal association and lack of alternate diagnosis make this the most likely diagnosis). One of these events led to treatment discontinuation.
L782: There was no clear correlation between hypersensitivity and antidrug antibody (ADA) titers or systemic concentration.
L783: 8 See FDA Summary Review for Olezarsen (NDA 218614), dated December 19, 2024, available at https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2025/218614Orig1s000IntegratedR.pdf.
L784: ## Conclusion
L785: Overall, six AEs (one serious and five non-serious) in three (2%, 3/177) subjects who received donidalorsen were assessed as hypersensitivity reactions from Trials ISIS 721744-CS2, ISIS 721744-CS3, ISIS 721744-CS5, and ISIS 721744-CS7. One subject (0.6%, 1/177) experienced a serious event of Hypersensitivity which fulfills NIAID criteria for the diagnosis of anaphylaxis was reported across all donidalorsen clinical trials. Two out of six AEs of hypersensitivity reactions led to permanent treatment discontinuation in two (1%) subjects.
L786: This risk of donidalorsen use is important to communicate in labeling and will be described in Section 5 of the USPI.
L787: ## 8. Therapeutic Individualization
L788: ## 8.1. Intrinsic Factors
L789: Population PK and PD analyses showed no clinically meaningful differences in the pharmacokinetics or pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen based on age, body weight, sex, race, ethnicity, disease status (i.e., healthy subjects or HAE patients), mild renal impairment (eGFR \ge 60 to &lt;90 mL/min/1.73 m^2), or mild hepatic impairment (total bilirubin \le 1 \times ULN and AST &gt; 1 \times ULN, or total bilirubin &gt; 1 to 1.5 \times ULN and any AST). Donidalorsen has not been studied in patients with moderate or severe renal impairment, end-stage renal disease, or moderate or severe hepatic impairment.
L790: ## 8.1.1. Age
L791: No dosage adjustments based on age are recommended.
L792: The proposed indication for donidalorsen is for prophylaxis to prevent HAE attacks in adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older. No dose adjustment was proposed for adolescent subjects. Based on the Applicant's population PK analysis, the steady-state exposures following administration of the donidalorsen-4 regimen was similar across different age groups, as shown in Figure 21. A higher mean exposure (area under the concentration-time curve [AUC]_{\tau,ss} and maximum plasma concentration [C_{max}]_{ss}) was estimated for adolescents as compared to adults. The difference in body weight may contribute to this exposure difference (refer to Section 8.1.2). The mean body weight for adolescents (12 to 17 years) and adults enrolled in Trial CS5 were 67.98 kg and 81.78 kg, respectively.

The systemic exposure (trough concentration [Ctrough]) in adolescent subjects was similar to that in adults who received the same dosing regimen. L817: ## 8.1.2. Body Weight
L818: No dosage adjustments based on body weight are recommended.
L819: No dosage adjustments were proposed based on body weight. Based on the Applicant's population analysis, body weight was identified as a significant covariate on donidalorsen pharmacokinetics. In general, donidalorsen exposure is higher in subjects with lower body weight. As compared with a reference subject with a body weight of 70 kg, the median donidalorsen exposure (AUC_{\tau, ss}, C_{max, ss}, C_{trough, ss}) for a subject at the 10th percentile of the body weight distribution (i.e., 60 kg) is expected to increase by 26%, 39%, and 23%, respectively. A subject at the 90th percentile of the body weight distribution (i.e., 100 kg) is expected to have a 42% lower AUC_{\tau, ss}, 54% lower C_{max, ss}, and 38% lower C_{trough, ss} compared with a reference subject with a weight of 70 kg, as shown in Figure 23.

L842: Other PK parameters including C_{\text{max,ss}} and \text{AUC}_{1344\text{h,ss}} were also used for the exposure-response (E-R) safety analysis. The Applicant's E-R analyses were consistent with the observed data in Trial CS5, where subclinical elevations in LFTs were observed with both donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 groups with no imbalance between treatment groups in clinically relevant LFT elevation: two subjects (9%) treated with donidalorsen-8 were reported to have ALT &gt;3 \times \text{ULN}, while one subject (2.2%) treated with donidalorsen-4 was reported to have total bilirubin &gt;2 \times \text{ULN}. The body weight of these subjects ranged from 60 kg to 93.7 kg.
L843: However, in the 120-day safety update, three Rollover subjects from Trial CS5 (Index) to the OLE trial (CS7) experienced an increase in ALT &gt;3 \times \text{ULN} (one from Index Q8W/OLE Q4W, one from Index/OLE Q4W, and one from Index placebo/OLE Q4W). At the time of NDA data cutoff, these subjects had normal ALT levels at baseline and elevations were experienced after receiving donidalorsen for a longer duration (around over one year). See Section 7.7 for more details. Although two out of three subjects were treated with a greater dosing frequency
L844: (donidalorsen-4) in Trial CS7 compared to their previously assigned regimen in Trial CS5 (placebo or donidalorsen-8), it is unclear whether the increase in dosing frequency, the duration of exposure, or both contributed to the ALT elevations.
L845: As described above, platelet lowering is a class effect for oligonucleotide therapeutics. Therefore, the E-R relationship for platelet counts was also assessed based on data from Trial CS5, as shown in Figure 26. Based on C_{\text{trough,ss}}, all exposure tertiles demonstrated a reduction in platelet counts as compared to placebo. However, no clear exposure-dependent trend was identified (i.e., greater reductions in platelets with higher C_{\text{trough,ss}}).

L851: AEs related to platelet reduction and liver enzyme elevations were reported across a wide range of body weights. In addition, there was no clear exposure-response relationship for these safety events. Therefore, the body weight-associated changes in donidalorsen plasma exposures are not likely to affect the safety of donidalorsen.
L852: Thus, although body weight was identified as a significant covariate on donidalorsen pharmacokinetics, there was no clinically significant difference in PD response (PKK reduction from baseline), efficacy, or safety across different body weights. Therefore, no dosage adjustments based on body weight are recommended.
L853: ## 8.1.3. Hepatic Impairment
L854: No dosage adjustments are recommended for patients with mild hepatic impairment.
L855: Donidalorsen has not been studied in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment. Use of donidalorsen is not recommended in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment.
L856: The effect of hepatic impairment on the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen was not assessed in a dedicated clinical pharmacology trial. No dose adjustment was proposed for subjects with mild hepatic impairment. Donidalorsen has not been studied in subjects with moderate or severe hepatic impairment. However, the Applicant has not proposed a restriction on the use of donidalorsen in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment.
L857: In the pivotal trial (CS5), two subjects (Subject 1 and Subject 2) with mild hepatic impairment (based on National Cancer Institute-Organ Dysfunction Working Group classification; total bilirubin \le 1 \times ULN and AST &gt; 1 \times ULN, or total bilirubin &gt; 1 to 1.5 \times ULN and any AST level) were treated with donidalorsen-4. One subject (Subject 1) had normal total bilirubin but elevated AST &gt; 1 \times ULN at baseline (Week 1). The other subject (Subject 2) had elevated bilirubin (&gt; 1 to 1.5 \times ULN) but normal AST at baseline (Week 1). Both subjects also had mild elevation of ALT (1.1 to 1.2 \times ULN) at Week 1. No subject with moderate or severe hepatic impairment (i.e., total bilirubin &gt; 1.5 \times ULN irrespective of AST level) was included in the donidalorsen clinical program.
L858: The systemic exposure of donidalorsen and PD response (i.e., PKK concentrations) in these two subjects were within the range of those observed in subjects with normal hepatic function in the same dosing group (i.e., donidalorsen-4), as shown in Figure 27. Subjects with mild hepatic impairment achieved &gt; 80\% reduction from baseline in HAE attack rate between Week 5 and Week 25, which is similar to what was observed in subjects with normal hepatic function.
L859: Figure 27. Box Plot of Observed Plasma Donidalorsen C_{\text{trough}} (Top) and Percent Change in Plasma Trough PKK Concentration (Bottom) Over Time in Subjects With Normal Hepatic Function and Two Subjects With Mild Hepatic Impairment Following Q4W Dosing, Trial CS5
L860: ## **A) Plasma Donidalorsen C_{\text{trough}} Over Time**
L861: ## **B) Percent Change in Plasma Trough PKK Concentration Over Time**
L862: Source: Reviewer-generated graph based on adpc.xpt and adpd.xpt for CS5
L863: Red represents mild hepatic impairment (N=2). Blue represents normal subjects (N=43).
L864: Abbreviations: C_{\text{trough}}, trough plasma concentration; HI, hepatic impairment; PKK, prekallikrein; Q4W, every 4 weeks
L865: Similar to other GalNAc-conjugated oligonucleotide products, donidalorsen is mainly distributed to the liver after subcutaneous administration with an initial rapid distribution phase followed by a much slower elimination phase. Therefore, the liver concentrations of donidalorsen and its metabolites are expected to be higher than those in plasma. Hepatic impairment may thus impact the accumulation of GalNAc-conjugated products in the liver. In addition, the production of PKK may be impaired in patients with hepatic impairment, which indicates that a lower dose of donidalorsen may also be effective in this patient population. As donidalorsen has not been evaluated in subjects with moderate to severe hepatic impairment, the long-term safety and efficacy of donidalorsen in subjects with moderate to severe hepatic impairment is not known.
L866: Both subjects with mild HI enrolled in Trial CS5 and later rolled over into Trial CS7 and continued on the same donidalorsen-4 dosing regimen. Both subjects had ALT levels trending upwards in Trial CS7, although no ALT value exceeded &gt;3\times ULN as of the date of NDA data cutoff. Neither of these two subjects presented with any new ALT elevations after NDA data cutoff in the 120-day safety update. See Section 7.7 for more details regarding safety evaluation. The small sample size of mild HI subjects (N=2) limits the evaluation of safety in this population.
L867: In subjects with normal hepatic function, although there was no clear exposure-response relationship observed between LFT elevation and plasma donidalorsen concentration in Trial CS5, subclinical elevations in LFTs were observed more frequently with donidalorsen compared to placebo. Some subjects with normal ALT at baseline who were treated with donidalorsen for a longer duration (&gt;1 year) throughout Trial CS5 and Trial CS7 experienced clinically relevant ALT elevations (\ge 5\times ULN). This observation increases the uncertainty regarding the long-term safety of donidalorsen in patients with moderate to severe hepatic impairment who may be more vulnerable to hepatic toxicity. Therefore, the use of donidalorsen is not recommended in patients with moderate to severe hepatic impairment from a safety perspective.
L868: ## 8.1.4. Renal Impairment
L869: No dosage adjustments are recommended for patients with mild renal impairment. Donidalorsen has not been studied in patients with moderate or severe renal impairment or end-stage renal disease.
L870: The effect of renal impairment on the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen was not assessed in a dedicated clinical pharmacology trial. Donidalorsen is highly bound to plasma proteins (&gt;98\%) and less than 1% of the administered dose is excreted as total full-length oligonucleotide in urine within the first 24 hours after the fourth dose administered every 4 weeks. In addition, linker-related metabolites accounted for \le 6.4\% of the administered dose in urine. Renal impairment did not impact the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen. In the pivotal trial (CS5), five subjects with mild renal impairment (eGFR 60 to 89 mL/min/1.73 m^2) were enrolled. Three of these subjects received donidalorsen-4. The remaining two received donidalorsen-8. Based on observed data from Trial CS5, the plasma Ctrough of donidalorsen and change from baseline in plasma PKK were similar between subjects with normal renal function and subjects with mild renal impairment, as shown in Figure 28.

L876: Mild renal impairment did not impact the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen based on observed data from Trial CS5. Therefore, no adjustment is recommended for subjects with mild renal impairment. Donidalorsen has not been studied in subjects with moderate severe renal impairment or end stage renal disease.
L877: ## 8.2. Extrinsic Factors
L878: ## 8.2.1. Drug Product Presentation
L879: The proposed to-be-marketed presentation is solution for injection (80 mg/0.8 mL) in a single-dose autoinjector (AI). The clinical formulation used in the pivotal phase 3 trial (CS5) is donidalorsen solution (100 mg/mL) for injection in stopper glass vial.
L880: To bridge the proposed AI and vial product, the Applicant evaluated plasma PK profiles of donidalorsen in healthy adult subjects following administration of a single dose of donidalorsen using vial and AI in a phase 1 bioequivalence trial (CS9).
L881: The results of the bioequivalence trial demonstrated comparable systemic exposure between AI and vial presentations (geometric mean ratio [90% CI] for AI versus vial products were 113% [105, 121] for C_{max} and 107% [104, 111] for AUC_{0-336}). PD results based on PKK concentrations were also similar between both products. Refer to Section 14.2.1 for details. The AI and vial products are adequately bridged. The results therefore support use of the AI product as the to-be-marketed drug product.
L882: ## 8.2.2. Injection Site
L883: The Applicant proposes that donidalorsen can be administered SC into the abdomen, upper thigh, or the back of the upper arm.
L884: Based on the Applicant's population PK analysis, injection into the arm is predicted to yield a 12% lower geometric mean C_{max,ss} (440 ng/mL) as compared to injection into the abdomen (495 ng/mL) but a similar C_{max,ss} following injection into the thigh (451 ng/mL). Injection into the arm is also predicted to yield a similar mean AUC_{tau, ss} and C_{trough, ss} compared to those following injection into the abdomen or thigh. The range of post hoc estimates for steady-state exposure of C_{max}, AUC_{tau, ss}, and C_{trough, ss} were overlapping between subjects with injection into the arm, abdomen, and thigh in the Applicant's population PK analysis.
L885: In the pivotal phase 3 trial (CS5), donidalorsen could be administered into any of three injection sites (abdomen, arm, or thigh) and alternating injection sites were used in some individuals. The range of donidalorsen concentrations collected 2 hours postdose at steady state (Week 21) following donidalorsen-4 administration was overlapping across injections. Although, a slightly higher median value was noted following injection into the arm as compared to the abdomen or thigh injection, in contrast to population PK predictions (Figure 29).

L899: ## 8.2.3. Drug-Drug Interactions
L900: No dose adjustment strategies with respect to drug-drug interactions are warranted for donidalorsen.
L901: In vitro studies indicate that donidalorsen and its main linker-related metabolite (i.e., M8) are not inducers or inhibitors of CYP-mediated oxidative metabolism. Donidalorsen was not identified to be a substrate of any CYP enzymes. Linker-related metabolite M8 was determined to be a substrate of CYP3A4. With respect to transporters, donidalorsen was not found to be a substrate or inhibitor of major drug transporters. Linker-related metabolite M8 was identified as a substrate of the transporters organic anion transporting polypeptide 1B3 and bile salt export pump (BSEP). Linker-related metabolite M8 was also determined to be an inhibitor of multidrug and toxin extrusion protein (MATE) 1. Notably, although M8 was identified as the main linker-related metabolite, its abundance in human plasma is low (1.3% relative to parent). Lastly, no in vitro DDIs were observed with regards to plasma protein binding displacement between donidalorsen and other highly plasma protein-bound drugs, such as ibuprofen and warfarin. For additional details, refer to Section 14.1.
L902: ## 8.3. Plans for Pediatric Drug Development
L903: An initial pediatric study plan (iPSP) was submitted by the Applicant on June 3, 2022, and an agreement letter for the agreed iPSP was issued on July 6, 2022. The Applicant requested a waiver for pediatric patients under 2 years of age on the grounds that clinical manifestations of the disease state (HAE attacks) do not exist in this age group. Ages 12 to less than 18 years were included in Trial CS5 and Trials CS7. The Applicant requested a deferral for ages 2 to less than 12 years; this age group will be targeted in a future open-label clinical trial (CS8) that will target enrolling 20 patients for a treatment duration of 25 weeks.
L904: On September 19, 2023, donidalorsen received orphan designation for the treatment of HAE exempting pediatric studies under PREA.
L905: ## Nonclinical
L906: A juvenile toxicity study was not needed to support usage in pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. A repeat-dose 13-week toxicity study in juvenile mice has been conducted (report pending)
L907: (b) (4) The design of the juvenile toxicity study was discussed with the Applicant in the context of the iPSP.
L908: ## 8.4. Pregnancy, Lactation, and Females/Males of Reproductive Potential
L909: The potential reproductive and developmental toxicity of donidalorsen was evaluated in GLP-compliant combined fertility and embryofetal (embryo-fetal development [EFD]) developmental and PPND studies in mice. Donidalorsen does not have perfect alignment to the mouse PKK gene sequence and mice are not considered a pharmacologically relevant species. As such, the reproductive and developmental toxicity studies in mice also evaluated mouse surrogate antisense oligonucleotide ISIS 722059, which targets mouse PKK, to assess potential toxicities related to the intended pharmacology of PKK inhibition.
L910: The following nonclinical information was used in support of the drug's labeling. Additional details are available in Section 13.
L911: **Table 32. Nonclinical Data Supporting Labeling on Fertility, Pregnancy, and Lactation**
L912: Labeling Section	Nonclinical Data
8.1 Pregnancy	
In a combined fertility and EFD study, male and female F0 mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection), donidalorsen (1, 4, or 10 mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4 mg/kg/week) weekly, prior to and during mating, and continuing every other day in females throughout the periods of implantation and organogenesis (GD 0 to 16). There were no adverse effects on embryofetal development. There was no evidence of maternal toxicity. The NOAEL for developmental toxicity was the high dose of 10 mg/kg/week donidalorsen.
In a PPND study, F0 female mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection), donidalorsen (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (5 mg/kg/week) every other day from GD 6 to GD 18 and weekly from LD 1 to LD 20. There were no adverse effects on behavioral, fertility, and reproductive development parameters in the F1 offspring. There was no evidence of maternal toxicity. The NOAEL for the PPND study was the high dose of 20 mg/kg/week donidalorsen.
The unconjugated form of donidalorsen was not detected (i.e., was below the limit of quantitation) in fetal tissues. It was unclear if donidalorsen or unconjugated donidalorsen crossed the placenta to reach fetal tissues.

8.2 Lactation	
In the PPND study in mice, the concentrations of donidalorsen in breast milk from lactating mice on LD 15 increased in a dose-dependent manner at doses \ge10 mg/kg/week, but these concentrations of donidalorsen in breast milk were lower than the observed tissue concentrations in the liver where the drug is preferentially taken up. Even though donidalorsen was detected in the maternal mouse milk, systemic exposure in pups was not expected due to the lack of oral absorption of donidalorsen.

13. Carcinogenesis, Mutagenesis, Impairment of Fertility	
In the combined fertility and EFD study in mice, fertility and reproductive performance were unaffected by SC administration of donidalorsen up to 10 mg/kg/week or a mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4 mg/kg/week) to male and female F0 mice weekly, prior to and during mating, and continuing every other day in females throughout the periods of implantation and organogenesis.

L942: ## **Product**
L943: Donidalorsen injection product is a sterile, single-dose, ready-to-use parenteral solution containing an ASO in prefilled syringe within an AI device. The drug/device combination product is intended for subcutaneous injection by the patient or caregiver at home and is indicated for the prophylaxis of HAE attacks in adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older. Donidalorsen, an ASO, reduces the production of PKK protein. Each product unit contains 80 mg/0.8 mL of donidalorsen drug. The labeling recommends a starting dose for patients aged 12 years and older of 80 mg donidalorsen (b) (4) (equivalent to 84 mg of donidalorsen sodium), (b) (4).
L944: All excipients in the product are of USP/NF grade and in quantities that do not exceed the maximum daily amounts approved for other injection drug products or products, according to the Inactive Ingredient Report. None of the excipients are novel and none are derived from animal sources.
L945: The product is manufactured through a process involving several key steps: (b) (4). The manufacturing process is based on prior knowledge for similar approved products from the same Applicant with similar oligonucleotide-based drugs.
L946: The specification for the product is aligned with the relevant ICH guidances for industry, *Q6A Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria for New Drug Substances and New Drug Products: Chemical Substances* (December 2000) and *Q3B(R2) Impurities in New Drug Products (Revision 3)* (August 2006), and the acceptance criteria are adequate with respect to the batch release and stability data in the application. The non-compendial analytical methods and associated validation reports have been evaluated and the methods are deemed suitable for regulatory purposes.
L947: The primary container closure system for the product consists of a 1 mL staked needle syringe barrel and a plunger stopper. The filled primary container is assembled into an AI and packaged in an opaque carton (donidalorsen is photolabile). The AI is based on the (b) (4).
L948: AI. This AI platform has been used as part of other approved combination products. Refer to the Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH) consult review for a review of the (b) (4) AI/device from an engineering/device perspective (recommended approvable).
L949: A vial was used for clinical trials CS2, CS3, and CS5. Trial CS7 used both the vial and AI. To bridge the proposed AI and vial product, the Applicant evaluated plasma PK profiles of donidalorsen in healthy adult subjects following administration of a single dose of donidalorsen using vial and AI in a phase 1 bioequivalence trial (CS9); the results are presented in Section 14.2.2.
L950: An HF study validation study was conducted with the AI and the instructions for use were modified based on the identified use errors. Refer to the Office of Surveillance and Epidemiology review dated May 23, 2025.
