All batches were manufactured using the proposed commercial manufacturing process (Section 3.2.P.3.3) and they all met the specification acceptance criteria.
L952: Stability studies were conducted to evaluate the product at long-term (2 to 8°C) and accelerated (25°C/60%RH) storage conditions. Registration stability studies are ongoing for product batches CP721744-004-AI-A, CP721744-005-AI-B, and CP721744-006-AI-A. Based on the long-term and accelerated stability data available, an expiration dating period of 30 months is granted when stored in the proposed container closure system and carton at 2 to 8°C (36°F to 46°F). Data have also shown that the product may also be stored at room temperature (up to 86°F or 30°C) in the original carton for up to 6 weeks.

L984: ## 12. Summary of Regulatory History
L985: On July 15, 2019, Ionis Pharmaceuticals submitted IND 142564 with a proposed trial, ISIS 721744-CS2, entitled “A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Phase 2a Study to Assess the Clinical Efficacy of ISIS 721744, a Second-Generation Ligand-Conjugated Antisense Inhibitor of Prekallikrein, in Patients with Hereditary Angioedema,” which was allowed to proceed on August 14, 2019. A phase 1 study, Protocol No. ISIS 721744-CS1, was previously conducted in Canada to assess the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of ISIS 721744 in healthy volunteers.
L986: On August 30, 2021, an end-of-phase 2 meeting was held to discuss the adequacy of the nonclinical and clinical development to support a marketing application. FDA recommended an increase in the safety database size, evaluating an alternative lower dosing regimen, shared concerns and requested additional information regarding regulatory acceptability of the proposed PRO tools (AE-QoL and AECT), and recommended evaluating mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment and/or pre-existing hepatic diseases for generalizability. FDA stated the acceptability of a single pivotal trial to provide substantial evidence of effectiveness would be a review issue. Regarding the nonclinical development, FDA recommended that prior to the start of phase 3 clinical trials, a characterization of the metabolism of ISIS 721744 and its THA linker should be provided, as recommended by the Pharmacology and Toxicology and Clinical Pharmacology Reviewers within the Agency. Further, a toxicologic assessment of the liver inflammation and necrosis in female mice in the 26-week toxicity study should be provided. It was also agreed that an EFD study of ISIS 721744 in rabbits is not needed. The meeting minutes were issued on October 18, 2021.
L987: On July 6, 2022, FDA provided initial agreement on the pediatric trial plan for a partial waiver for &lt;2 years old, assessment of 12 to less than 18 years old as part of the proposed phase 3 trial, and a deferred trial of patients 2 to &lt;12 years old postmarketing.
L988: SPA 1 for the 2-year study in rats was submitted on August 5, 2022, and was subsequently denied due to lack of the Standard for Exchange of Nonclinical Data datasets for the supporting 16-week dose range finding study in rats and resubmitted on September 30, 2022, with the Standard for Exchange of Nonclinical Datasets. FDA agreed with the proposed 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats on November 4, 2022. SPA 2, which proposed a 6-month carcinogenicity study in Tg.rasH2 mice, was submitted on October 12, 2022, and was agreed upon for male mice but not for female mice (as no acceptable basis for dose selection could be identified) on November 16, 2022.
L989: Ionis requested a use-related risk analysis review on January 20, 2023, and included information on the target disease and human factors (HF) development. In the June 17, 2024, response, FDA did not identify any new or unique risks for the proposed product ISIS 721744 AI for intended adults as compared to currently approved Wainua AI and noted prematurity in determining the need for additional HF validation trials for adolescent users. FDA recommended submission of the full results report for the HF validation trial with the marketing application.

L998: ## 13. Pharmacology Toxicology
L999: ## 13.1. Summary Review of Studies Submitted With the Investigational New Drug Application
L1000: The pivotal and supporting pharmacology (primary and safety), absorption and distribution, and toxicology (repeat-dose toxicity, genotoxicity, carcinogenicity, and reproductive and developmental toxicity) studies submitted with both IND 142564 and NDA 219407 have been reviewed under either the IND or NDA and are summarized here.
L1001: ## 13.1.1. Pharmacology
L1002: ## 13.1.1.1. Primary Pharmacodynamics
L1003: Donidalorsen is a triantennary GalNAc3-conjugated ASO that causes ribonuclease H1 (RNase H1)-mediated degradation of PKK messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) through binding to PKK mRNA, which results in reduced production of PKK protein. PKK is a pro-enzyme for plasma kallikrein, which results in the release of bradykinin, a potent vasodilator causing swelling and pain in HAE. In patients with HAE, C1-INH deficiency or dysfunction leads to excessive plasma kallikrein activity, bradykinin generation, and angioedema attacks. Donidalorsen lowers PKK concentration, which is intended to prevent excessive bradykinin production in patients with HAE.
L1004: The primary pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen have been evaluated in both in vitro and in vivo primary pharmacology studies.
L1005: ## In Vitro Primary Pharmacology Studies
L1006: As described by the Applicant, over 1300 ASOs were designed to target various sites within the human PKK gene and were evaluated for their ability to inhibit the level of PKK mRNA in vitro in the human hepatocellular carcinoma cell line HepaRG. Of those ASOs, ISIS 546254, an unconjugated 2'-O-methoxyethyl (2'-MOE) gapmer ASO with a uniform phosphorothioate (PS) backbone was identified as a lead candidate. Donidalorsen was derived from ISIS 546254 as a 2'-MOE gapmer ASO with the same nucleobase sequence as ISIS 546254 but with a mixed PS and phosphodiester (PO) backbone and conjugated to a trivalent GalNAc3.
L1007: ## **In Silico and In Vitro Characterization of Human PKK ASO ISIS 721744 Specificity**
## (Study No. ECID129370)
L1008: The specificity of donidalorsen to PKK mRNA was characterized in silico and in vitro with the unconjugated human PKK ASO parent compound, ISIS 546254, which has the same nucleobase sequence as donidalorsen. ISIS 546254 is perfectly matched to only PKK mRNA in the human transcriptome (targets site free of meaningful sequence variation). Based on the in silico Basic Local Alignment Search Tool analysis, there were no identified potential off-target genes with a 0-, 1-, or 2-base mismatch or a 3-base mismatch with 17 matched bases in a row. Alignment of the ISIS 546254 sequence against the human transcriptome and mRNA reference sequences predicted seven human genes (i.e., ACACA, CTAGE5, IFIH1, PRKN, ANKS1B, CDH4, and LOC442028) with mismatched counts of two bases. Of these, one gene (i.e., LOC442028) had no reported expression in human tissues and two genes (ANKS1B and CDH4) were reported to be expressed only in the human brain, which is not a preferential tissue for GalNAc3 ASO accumulation. The effect of ISIS 546254 on the expression of PKK mRNA and the remaining four predicted off-target mRNAs (i.e., ACACA, CTAGE5, IFIH1, and PRKN), which are ubiquitously expressed in human tissue, was evaluated in the human hepatocellular cell line Hep3B. In this experiment, ISIS 546254 (doses up to 20\muM) potently reduced PKK mRNA (IC50=0.35\muM) and in comparison, only minimally reduced ACACA, CTAGE5, IFIH1, and PRKN mRNA (IC50=&gt;20, &gt;20, 9.1, and 8.8\muM, respectively). These data show that ISIS 546254 is selective for PKK mRNA compared to potential off-target mRNAs.
L1009: ## In Vitro Characterization of Human Prekallikrein Antisense Oligonucleotide ISIS 721744 Activity (Study No. ECID129371)
L1010: The in vitro characterization of donidalorsen to reduce human PKK mRNA was based on an experiment using two human hepatocellular carcinoma cell lines (HepaRG and Hep3b) treated with ISIS 546254 (unconjugated human PKK ASO parent compound of donidalorsen with the same nucleobase sequence) or ISIS 141923 (control oligonucleotide with no matches to any sites within the human transcriptome). ISIS 546254 reduced human PKK mRNA levels in human hepatocellular cell lines HepaRG and Hep3b by greater than 90% in a concentration-dependent manner with IC_{50} of 0.31\mu M and 0.35\mu M, respectively (Figure 32). In comparison, the control oligonucleotide ISIS 141923 did not reduce PKK mRNA in either cell line.

L1014: ## Characterization of ISIS 721744 Pharmacology in Primary Human Hepatocytes Co-Cultured With Mouse Fibroblasts (HepatoPac®) (Study No. GEN2.5-RS83 (PART F))
L1015: Treatment of HepatoPac® (co-culture system of primary human hepatocytes and supporting stromal cells [mouse fibroblasts]) with donidalorsen (6.4 to 20000nM) and ISIS 546254 (unconjugated human PKK ASO parent compound of donidalorsen with the same nucleobase sequence) reduced PKK mRNA in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 33). L1020: Donidalorsen does not align perfectly to the mouse PKK gene sequence. As such, the unconjugated PKK ASO mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 was used for in vivo pharmacology studies in mouse disease models.

L1034: ## **Recommendation for Designation of the Established Pharmacological Classification**
L1035: The recommended EPC for donidalorsen is “prekallikrein-directed antisense oligonucleotide.” Donidalorsen is an ASO that binds to PKK mRNA to cause degradation of PKK mRNA, which reduces PKK protein production. The recommended EPC for donidalorsen is consistent with the EPC of other approved ASO products (both with and without GalNAc).
L1036: ## **13.1.1.2. Secondary Pharmacodynamics**
L1037: The secondary pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen were not evaluated in secondary pharmacology studies as the off-target actions of ASOs are expected to be minimal.
L1038: ## **13.1.1.3. Safety Pharmacology**
L1039: The safety pharmacology of donidalorsen was evaluated in a GLP-compliant study in Cynomolgus monkeys assessing cardiovascular, respiratory, and CNS parameters, and a GLP-compliant in vitro hERG assay.
L1040: ## **Evaluation of Cardiovascular, Respiratory, and Central Nervous Systems Following Subcutaneous Administration of ISIS 721744 in Cynomolgus Monkeys (Study Nos. 11752; 721744-AS03)**
L1041: Male Cynomolgus monkeys (n=4/group) received single SC injections of either the vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection) or escalating dose of donidalorsen (12 and 30 mg/kg) with a minimum 1-week washout period between administration of the vehicle control and each dose level of donidalorsen. The cardiovascular and respiratory assessments were performed in conscious telemetered monkeys and evaluated arterial blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, core body temperature, and lead II electrocardiogram (ECG) at timepoints that were about 2 hours predose through 24 hours postdose (60, 120, 240, 300, 360, 720, and 1440 minutes); arterial blood gases were measured at predose and 2 hours postdose. The CNS assessment included a Functional Observational Battery (FOB) performed in conscious nontelemetered monkeys at predose and 1, 4, and 24 hours postdose.
L1042: Based on cardiovascular and respiratory assessments, there were no test article-related effects in conscious telemetered monkeys on arterial blood pressure parameters (systolic, diastolic, and mean arterial pressure), heart rate, respiratory rate, core body temperature, or ECG parameters (PR interval, QRS duration, QT interval, and RR interval) for up to 24 hours after dosing, or arterial blood gases for up to 2 hours after dosing, with 12 and 30 mg/kg donidalorsen.
L1043: Based on CNS assessments, there were no treatment-related effects in conscious nontelemetered monkeys noted by FOB for up to 24 hours after dosing with 12 and 30 mg/kg donidalorsen.
L1044: ## **Effect of ISIS 721744 on Cloned hERG Potassium Channels Expressed in Human Embryonic Kidney Cells (Study Nos. 210830.JTJ; 721744-IS08)**
L1045: HEK-293 cells were stably transfected with hERG cDNA and treated with donidalorsen (30 and 300µM) at near-physiological temperature to measure the effect on ionic currents by whole-cell
L1046: patch-clamp technique. Donidalorsen inhibited hERG current by 0.5% and 1.9% at 30\muM and 300\muM, respectively (not statistically significant) versus 2.4% for the vehicle control. The IC50 for the inhibitory effect of donidalorsen on hERG potassium current was not calculated but was estimated to be greater than 300\muM. The positive control article (60nM terfenadine) inhibited hERG potassium current by 85.6%. In general, oligonucleotides are not thought to interact with the hERG channel.
L1047: ## 13.1.2. Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion/Pharmacokinetics
L1048: The absorption and distribution, PK, and toxicokinetic (TK) profiles of donidalorsen were evaluated both in vitro and in vivo (mice and monkeys).
L1049: ## 13.1.2.1. Absorption
L1050: The plasma TK profile of SC administration of donidalorsen was evaluated in a GLP-compliant 13-week interim/39-week repeat-dose toxicity study in Cynomolgus monkeys with a 26-week treatment-free recovery period.
L1051: ## A 39-Week Repeat Dose Toxicity Study of ISIS 721744 in Cynomolgus Monkeys With a 13-Week Interim Necropsy and 26-Week Recovery (Study Nos. 727-081; 721744-AS02)
L1052: Cynomolgus monkeys received SC doses of vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection) or donidalorsen (2, 6, 12, or 30 mg/kg/dose with loading doses on Days 1, 5, 9, and 14 and once weekly thereafter) for 13-week interim (monkeys at 30 mg/kg/dose were dosed only until the interim sacrifice) or 39-weeks followed by a 26-week treatment-free recovery period. Validated hybridization electrochemiluminescence (ECL) or high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (HPLC-MS/MS) methodologies were used to measure total full-length donidalorsen (including fully conjugated, partially conjugated, and unconjugated donidalorsen) in plasma.
L1053: Donidalorsen was rapidly absorbed into systemic circulation with median time to maximum concentration (Tmax) from 1 to 4 hours across dose levels after single-dose (Day 1) and repeat-dose (Days 91 and 273) administration. Mean Cmax and AUC0-48hr increased between dose levels. After the first dose (Day 1), the 15th dose (Day 91), and the 41st dose (Day 273), AUC0-48hr increased in a greater than dose proportional manner between doses. There was some accumulation of drug at the 12 mg/kg/dose, based on increased AUC0-48hr on Day 273 versus Day 91. There were no clear differences in donidalorsen plasma TK between males and females. The majority of total fully conjugated full-length donidalorsen was cleared within hours from plasma, with a mean residence time (MRT)0-48hr of about 3 to 10 hours.
L1054: ## 13.1.2.2. Distribution
L1055: The distribution of donidalorsen was evaluated in vitro for plasma protein binding in human, monkey, and mouse plasma, and in vivo into the kidney cortex and liver as part of the GLP-compliant 13-week interim/39-week repeat-dose toxicity study in Cynomolgus monkeys with a 26-week treatment-free recovery period.
L1056: ## In Vitro Evaluation of the Extent of Plasma Protein Binding of ISIS 721744 in Human, Monkey, and Mouse Plasma by Ultrafiltration (Study Nos. IIS-M4-298; 721744-IS03)
L1057: The in vitro protein binding of donidalorsen at 0.5, 5, and 150 µg/mL was evaluated in the whole plasma from human, Cynomolgus monkey, and mouse by ultrafiltration methods and a nuclease-dependent hybridization ELISA detection method. Donidalorsen was highly bound (≥96.81%) to whole plasma proteins in human, monkey, and mouse at all three concentrations evaluated. The extent of plasma protein binding of donidalorsen was similar across all species.
L1058: ## A 39-Week Repeat Dose Toxicity Study of ISIS 721744 in Cynomolgus Monkeys With a 13-Week Interim Necropsy and 26-Week Recovery (Study Nos. 727-081; 721744-AS02)
L1059: Cynomolgus monkeys received SC doses of vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection) or donidalorsen (2, 6, 12, or 30 mg/kg/dose with loading doses on Days 1, 5, 9, and 14, and once weekly thereafter) for 13-week interim (monkeys at 30 mg/kg/dose were dosed only until the interim sacrifice) or 39-weeks followed by a 26-week treatment-free recovery period. Validated hybridization ECL or HPLC-MS/MS methodologies were used to measure unconjugated donidalorsen in kidney cortex and liver.
L1060: After SC administration, donidalorsen distributed to kidney cortex and liver in mostly similar concentrations (less than 2-fold difference in concentrations between tissues). After the 15th dose (Day 91) and the 41st dose (Day 273), the concentration of unconjugated donidalorsen in kidney cortex and liver was dose-dependent across doses. The Applicant claims steady-state tissue concentration (kidney cortex and liver) based on comparable mean tissue concentrations on Days 9, 93, and 275. There were no apparent differences in unconjugated donidalorsen tissue concentrations (kidney cortex or liver) between males and females.
L1061: ## 13.1.3. Toxicology
L1062: The potential toxicity of donidalorsen was evaluated in GLP-compliant repeat-dose toxicity (13-week and 26-week in mice and 13-week interim/39-week in monkeys), genotoxicity (in vitro Ames assay, in vitro chromosome aberration assay, and in vivo bone marrow micronucleus assay in mice), carcinogenicity (6-month in Tg.rasH2 mice), and reproductive and developmental toxicity (combined fertility and development in mice and PPND in mice) studies. The main nonclinical species used in the toxicology studies were monkeys and mice. Donidalorsen does not align perfectly to the mouse PKK gene sequence and is not pharmacologically active in the mouse. As such, the toxicity studies in mice evaluated donidalorsen and the conjugated PKK ASO mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (with the same GalNAc-conjugated 2'-MOE ASO chemical backbone structure as donidalorsen) to assess both potential off-target and on-target effects, respectively. The human sequence targeted by donidalorsen has a single-base sequence mismatch
L1063: within the binding site of monkey PKK mRNA (position 19). Despite this mismatch, donidalorsen demonstrated dose-dependent inhibition of liver target mRNA expression and reductions in PKK protein and activity levels in peripheral circulation of Cynomolgus monkeys, which supports the use of the monkey as a pharmacologically relevant species for evaluation of on-target effects (i.e., effects related to PKK reduction). There were no single-dose toxicity studies with donidalorsen.
L1064: ## 13.1.3.1. Repeat-Dose Toxicity
L1065: The pivotal GLP-compliant repeat-dose toxicity studies of longest treatment duration with donidalorsen included a 26-week study in mice and a 13-week interim/39-week study in monkeys.
L1066: ## A 39-Week Repeat Dose Toxicity Study of ISIS 721744 in Cynomolgus Monkeys With a 13-Week Interim Necropsy and 26-Week Recovery (Study Nos. 727-081; 721744-AS02)
L1067: ## Key Study Findings
L1068: - Cynomolgus monkeys received SC doses of vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection) or donidalorsen (2, 6, 12, or 30 mg/kg/dose with loading doses on Days 1, 5, 9, and 14, and then once weekly thereafter) with a 13-week interim sacrifice (monkeys at 30 mg/kg/dose were dosed only until the interim sacrifice) or 39 weeks followed by a 26-week treatment-free recovery period.
- There were no deaths during the study.
- Hematology changes included thrombocytopenia (defined as platelet counts &lt;150000 cells/mL) that was considered test article-related and adverse in one male at 30 mg/kg/dose and one female at 12 mg/kg/dose. The male animal had marked decreases in platelet counts compared to individual pretest 2 values on Days 80 and 87 (22 and 30 \times103/mL, respectively). The female animal had marked decreases in platelet counts relative to individual pretest 2 values on Days 65, 70, 74, 79, and 87 (ranging from &lt;10000 cells/mL to 66\times103/mL). Thrombocytopenia was not seen in these two animals during the respective recovery periods. The platelet decreases in these animals were accompanied by mild to marked decreases in red cell mass with mild to moderate increases in reticulocyte counts and/or increased polychromasia (of note, the 12 mg/kg/dose female had mild SC tissue necrosis with fibrin and hemorrhage at injection site 4 and both the 12 mg/kg/dose female and the 30 mg/kg/dose male had red nasal discharge, red skin discoloration, bruising, and/or petechial hemorrhage at various body sites, which may account for decrease in red cell mass and increase in reticulocyte counts).
- Coagulation changes included minimal prolongations in mean aPTT time in males and females at 30 mg/kg/dose relative to pretest on Day 1 (4 hours postdose) and Day 91 (4 hours postdose). These changes were not seen by 24 hours postdose on both Day 1 and Day 91.
- Clinical chemistry changes included increases in C-reactive protein in females at 12 mg/kg/dose on Day 65 through Day 275 and females at 30 mg/kg/dose on Day 65 and Day 93 (up to a greater than 600% change or more than 7-fold increase relative to control
L1069: and pretest 2 values). Increases in C-reactive protein was not seen at the recovery period time points.

- Complement Bb levels were slightly elevated for 12 mg/kg/dose males on Days 182 and 273, 12 mg/kg/dose females on Day 273, and at 30 mg/kg/dose on Day 91.
- Organ weight changes included effects on liver, kidney, and mesenteric lymph nodes. Increases in liver (with gallbladder) weight were noted in males and females at the time of the interim sacrifice on Day 93 (seen at 12 and 30 mg/kg/dose in males and at 6, 12, and 30 mg/kg/dose in females) and at the time of the terminal sacrifice on Day 275 (seen in all groups for males and at 6 and 12 mg/kg/dose in females). Increases in mesenteric lymph node weight were noted in females at 12 and 30 mg/kg/dose at the time of interim sacrifice (Day 93). Increases in kidney weight were noted in males and females at 12 mg/kg/dose at the time of the terminal sacrifice on Day 275.
- Histopathology examination identified test article-related findings in the kidneys, liver, lymph nodes (mandibular and mesenteric), and injection sites. In the kidneys, findings included accumulation of basophilic granules in tubular epithelial cells (at all doses). Liver findings included hepatocyte hypertrophy at the time of terminal necropsy (\ge 6 mg/kg/dose), accumulation of basophilic granules in hepatocytes (\ge 6 mg/kg/dose at interim sacrifice and \ge 2 mg/kg/dose at terminal sacrifice), and accumulation of basophilic granules in Kupffer cells (\ge 6 mg/kg/dose). Mesenteric lymph node findings included accumulation of basophilic granules in macrophages (at all doses). Injection site findings at the time of interim and terminal sacrifices (mostly at all doses with dose-related incidence and/or severity), included: (1) basophilic granules; (2) macrophages; (3) fibrosis; (4) mixed leukocyte infiltration; (5) mononuclear cell infiltration; (6) mixed cell infiltration/inflammation; (7) perivascular/vascular inflammation; (8) myofiber degeneration/regeneration (terminal sacrifice only); (9) hemorrhage (terminal sacrifice only); and (10) necrosis (terminal sacrifice only). Accumulation of basophilic granules in macrophages (tissue histiocytes) was seen in numerous tissues at the interim and terminal sacrifices (seen primarily at \ge 6 mg/kg/dose). Perivascular/vascular inflammation (with sporadic occurrence) was noted in the liver (one male at 12 mg/kg/dose on Day 93), heart (one male at 6 mg/kg/dose, one male at 12 mg/kg/dose, and one female at 30 mg/kg/dose on Day 93), injection sites (males at 6, 12, and 30 mg/kg/dose and females at 12 mg/kg/dose on Day 93), and vagina (one female at 30 mg/kg/dose on Day 93 and one female at 12 mg/kg/dose on Day 275).
- There were dose-dependent decreases in liver PKK mRNA expression and dose-dependent and time-dependent decreases in PKK plasma protein after treatment with donidalorsen \ge 2 mg/kg/dose at the interim and/or terminal sacrifices. Both liver PKK mRNA expression and PKK plasma protein increased by the end of the recovery periods. This showed pharmacological activity of donidalorsen in Cynomolgus monkeys.
- Donidalorsen was rapidly absorbed into the systemic circulation with median T_{max} at 1 to 4 hours postdose. Mean C_{max} and AUC_{0-48hr} were dose-dependent and greater than dose-proportionally between doses. The majority of total fully conjugated full-length ASO was cleared within hours from plasma, with a MRT_{0-48hr} of about 3 to 10 hours. Tissue concentrations of unconjugated donidalorsen in liver or kidney increased in a dose-dependent
L1070: manner. The Applicant claims steady-state tissue concentrations were achieved based on comparable mean tissue concentrations on Days 9, 93, and 275.
L1071: - The no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL) was 6 mg/kg/dose based on the following:Basophilic granules seen by histopathology throughout the body appeared consistent with oligonucleotide uptake and in the absence of correlating histopathology were not considered adverse.
- The NOAEL was based on thrombocytopenia seen in two monkeys at 12 mg/kg/dose and 30 mg/kg/dose.
- The NOAEL corresponds to a C_{max} of 6.57 µg/mL and an AUC_{0-48hr} of 37.6 µg*hr/mL on Day 273.
L1072: ## **A 26-Week Repeat Dose Toxicity Study of ISIS 721744 in Mice With a 13-Week Recovery (Study Nos. 8405032; 721744-AS04)**
L1073: ## **Key Study Findings**
L1074: - Mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection), donidalorsen (1, 4, or 12 mg/kg/dose), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4 mg/kg/dose) Q2W for 26 weeks with a 13-week treatment-free recovery period (vehicle control and 12 mg/kg/dose of donidalorsen only).
- There were no unscheduled deaths during the study that were considered related to treatment with donidalorsen or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
- Changes in hematology parameters at the end of the 26-week Treatment Period included increases in white blood cells, neutrophils, lymphocytes, and/or monocytes in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. At the end of the 13-week recovery period, increases in hematology parameters were no longer seen at the 12 mg/kg/dose of donidalorsen.
- Changes in clinical chemistry parameters at the end of the 26-week Treatment Period included increases in ALT, AST, and/or ALP in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose of donidalorsen. Effects on clinical chemistry parameters (including ALT, AST, and ALP) were less clear at 4 mg/kg/dose of ISIS 722059. At the end of the 13-week recovery period, increases in ALT and/or AST were still seen in males and/or females at 12 mg/kg/dose of donidalorsen, while increases in ALP were no longer seen. The toxicological significance of increases in ALT and AST were unclear as histopathology findings in the liver appeared to be partially reversible and levels of unconjugated donidalorsen had declined below the lower limit of quantitation.
- Gross pathology findings after the 26-week Treatment Period with donidalorsen were seen in the liver (discoloration in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and enlargement in males at 4 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen) and inguinal lymph nodes (enlarged in males at 1 and 4 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen). There were no clear gross pathology findings seen after the 26-week Treatment Period with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059. Gross pathology findings after the 13-week recovery period at 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen were noted in the liver (discoloration in males) and subcutaneous injection site (discoloration in males).
L1075: - Organ weight changes after the 26-week Treatment Period with donidalorsen included increases in liver weights in males and/or females at 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose and increases in spleen weights in males at 12 mg/kg/dose. There were no organ weight changes after the 26-week Treatment Period with 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. At the end of the 13-week recovery period for 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, liver weights were still increased in males and/or females.
- Histopathology findings after the 26-week Treatment Period with donidalorsen were seen in the liver, skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, inguinal lymph nodes, and spleen. Histopathology findings after the 26-week treatment with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 were seen in the skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, spleen, and testis.Liver: Minimal or slight centrilobular hepatocellular hypertrophy was noted in males at 1, 4, and 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and in one female (moderate) at 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen. This finding correlated with increased mean liver weights at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and increased liver enzymes (AST, ALT, and/or ALP). Despite a background incidence of hepatocyte vacuolation in vehicle control males, there was an increase in the severity (slight to marked) of hepatocyte vacuolation in males at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, which correlated with gross pathology findings of liver discoloration at all dose levels. These findings were consistent with uptake of donidalorsen.
- Skin/subcutis: Increased incidences and/or severity of infiltrates of mononuclear cells, mixed cells, and/or vacuolated macrophages in the skin/subcutis were noted in males and/or females at 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and/or 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. Increased incidences and/or severity of vacuolated fibrocytes in the skin/subcutis were noted in males and/or females at 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. Slight to moderate inflammation in the skin was noted in females at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen. These findings in the skin/subcutis correlated with increased leukocyte counts.
- Subcutaneous dose sites: Increased incidences and/or severity of infiltrates of vacuolated macrophages, mononuclear cells, and mixed cells, as well as fibrocyte vacuolation at the SC injection sites were noted in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and/or 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. These findings at the SC injection sites correlated with increased leukocyte counts.
- Inguinal lymph nodes: Increased incidences and severities (minimal to marked) of increased lymphocytes in males at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and one female at 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen were noted in the inguinal lymph node. This finding in the inguinal lymph node correlated with increased leukocyte counts. Amyloid in the inguinal lymph node was noted in one male at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
- Spleen: Increased incidence and/or severity of extramedullary hematopoiesis in the spleen was noted in males and/or females at 1, 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059 and correlated with increased mean spleen weight in males administered 12 mg/kg/dose of donidalorsen.
- Testis: Moderate interstitial cell hyperplasia, minimal sperm stasis, and minimal vacuolation were noted in the testis of males at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
L1076: - Histopathology findings after the 13-week recovery period at 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen were still noted in the liver as hepatocellular vacuolation in males and females, which correlated with increased liver weights. Histopathology findings in the skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, inguinal lymph nodes, and spleen at 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen were not seen at the end of the recovery period.
- Unconjugated donidalorsen was measurable in a dose-dependent manner in the kidney (greater than dose proportional) and liver (dose proportional) after 26 weeks of treatment with donidalorsen. The mean concentrations of unconjugated donidalorsen were similar in the kidney and liver except at 12 mg/kg/dose where mean unconjugated donidalorsen concentrations were greater in the kidney than in the liver. Mean unconjugated donidalorsen concentrations were higher in females than in males in the kidney but similar in the liver. After the 13-week recovery period at 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, mean unconjugated donidalorsen concentrations were below or near the lower limit of quantitation of 0.107 µg/g, suggesting complete clearance of donidalorsen.
- Mouse PKK mRNA in mouse liver was reduced by 77% (statistically significant) compared to vehicle control in mice treated with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 at 4 mg/kg/dose for 26 weeks.
- The NOAEL was 12 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, as test article-related findings were considered related to the oligonucleotide uptake.
L1077: ## 13.1.3.2. Genotoxicity
L1078: The genotoxicity of donidalorsen was evaluated in a complete battery of GLP-compliant genotoxicity studies (i.e., in vitro Ames assay, in vitro chromosome aberration assay in CHL cells, and in vivo bone marrow micronucleus assay in mice).
L1079: ## **ISIS 721744: Bacterial Reverse Mutation Assay (Study Nos. G115138; 721744-IS01)**
L1080: The in vitro Ames assay, using the plate incorporation method, evaluated vehicle, positive controls, and donidalorsen (15 to 5000 µg/plate) in *Salmonella typhimurium* TA98, TA100, TA1535, and TA1537, and *Escherichia coli* WP2uvrA tester strains (with or without 10% S9 mix for metabolic activation). There was no increase in the number of revertant colonies in any tester strain, at any donidalorsen concentration, with or without metabolic activation. There was no toxicity up to highest donidalorsen concentration, in any tester strain, with or without metabolic activation. Donidalorsen was negative for mutagenicity up to 5000 µg/plate ± S9 metabolic activation.
L1081: ## **ISIS 721744: In Vitro Chromosome Aberration Assay in CHL Cells (Study Nos. G115139; 721744-IS02)**
L1082: The in vitro chromosome aberration assay evaluated vehicle, positive controls, and donidalorsen at 62.5 to 500 µg/mL in CHL cells for 6 hours (with or without 2% S9 mix for metabolic activation) and for 22 hours (without S9 mix). No cytotoxicity was noted at up to 500 µg/mL after 6 hours with or without 2% S9 mix and 22 hours without S9 mix. There was no significant increase in the number of metaphases with structural or numerical aberrations up to 500 µg/mL
L1083: after 6 hours (with or without 2% S9 mix) and 22 hours (without S9 mix). Donidalorsen was negative for clastogenicity up to 500 µg/mL in cultured CHL cells.
L1084: ## **Mammalian Micronucleus Assay in Bone Marrow Erythrocytes Following Subcutaneous Injection of ISIS 721744 to ICR Mice (Study Nos. G120005; 721744-AS05)**
L1085: The in vivo mammalian micronucleus assay evaluated vehicle, positive control, and donidalorsen (500, 1000, and 2000 mg/kg SC) administered on Days 1 and 3 (48 hours postdose on Day 1) to ICR mice. Mice were sacrificed on Day 4 (24 hours postdose on Day 3) for bone marrow collection. There was no statistically significant increase in the incidence of micronucleated polychromatic erythrocytes at any dose of donidalorsen tested compared to the vehicle control (negative control) group. Donidalorsen was negative in the in vivo bone marrow micronucleus assay in mice.
L1086: ## **13.1.3.3. Carcinogenicity**
L1087: The SPAs for the proposed protocols for the 6-month carcinogenicity study in hemizygous transgenic (Tg.rasH2) mice and the 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats included recommendations on dose selection based on a non GLP-compliant 14-week DRF study in Tg.rasH2 mice and 16-week DRF study in Sprague Dawley rats, respectively.
L1088: ## **A 14-Week Repeat Dose Toxicity Study of ISIS 721744 and ISIS 722059 IN CBYB6F1-TG(HRAS)2JIC Hemizygous Transgenic Mice (Study No. 721744-AS07P)**
L1089: Tg.rasH2 mice received SC injections of vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection), donidalorsen (6, 18, or 36 mg/kg/dose), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (6 mg/kg/dose) Q2W. Animal numbers were noted to be low (n=6/sex/group) and the histopathology examination was limited (i.e., sternum bone marrow and bone, heart, injection sites, kidneys, liver, lung, spleen, testes, thymus, gross lesions, and tissue masses). Donidalorsen resulted in dose-dependent increases in ALP (up to 1.6-fold over control), AST (up to 5.4-fold over control), and ALT (up to 5.1-fold over control) in males at all dose levels. These increases correlated with a dose-dependent increase of minimal karyocytomegaly in the liver in males at ≥6 mg/kg Q2W. In females, only minimal and non-dose-dependent increases in liver enzymes (up to 1.9-fold over control) were seen and there were no microscopic correlates in the liver. For male mice, the high dose selection of 20 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen was based upon incidences of karyocytomegaly and increases of ALT, AST, and ALP at ≥18 mg/kg/dose in the 14-week DRF study. For female mice, there were no histopathological findings in the liver and there were minimal non-dose-related elevations of ALT, AST, and ALP in the 14-week DRF study. No dose-limiting toxicity was identified for female mice in the 14-week DRF study. To evaluate pharmacological effects in the 6-month carcinogenicity study, male and female mice will receive the mouse surrogate, ISIS 722059, at a dose of 10 mg/kg/dose, although only a single dose level of 6 mg/kg Q2W was evaluated in the 14-week DRF study. A MTD for ISIS 722059 was not determined. At 10 mg/kg Q2W, the mouse surrogate ISIS 722059, is expected to achieve ~&gt;80% reduction in liver PKK mRNA expression.
L1090: The Executive Carcinogenicity Assessment Committee (ECAC) concurred with doses of 0 (0.9% sodium chloride for injection), 5, 10, and 20 mg/kg Q2W via SC injection in male mice with the
L1091: high dose based on a MTD (i.e., incidences of karyocytomegaly and increases of ALT, AST, and ALP in male mice at higher doses in the 14-week DRF study). The mid and low doses are based on adequate dose spacing. For female mice, the Committee could not recommend doses for the proposed study, as no acceptable basis for dose selection could be identified. If the Applicant would like ECAC concurrence for dose selection, a new DRF study should be conducted to identify an acceptable high dose as outlined in the ICH guidances for industry, *SIC(R2) Dose Selection for Carcinogenicity Studies of Pharmaceuticals* (September 2008) or *SIB(R1) Addendum to SIB Testing for Carcinogenicity of Pharmaceuticals* (November 2022).
L1092: ## **A 16-Week Repeat-Dose Toxicity Study of ISIS 721744 in Sprague Dawley Rats (Study Nos. 721744-AS08P)**
L1093: Sprague Dawley rats received SC injections of vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection) or donidalorsen (10, 30, or 90 mg/kg) Q2W with one additional loading dose on Day 8. Animal numbers were noted to be low (vehicle control =3/sex/group; test article-treated groups =5/sex/group) and the histopathology examination was limited (e.g., gross lesions, adrenal glands, bone marrow, heart, injection sites, kidneys, liver, lung, lymph nodes, spleen, and thymus). Decreased body weight gains (&gt;10% from control) were seen in males at \ge 30 mg/kg/dose and females at \ge 10 mg/kg/dose. In the kidneys, histopathology findings in males and females at \ge 10 mg/kg/dose included minimal to marked basophilic granules in the proximal convoluted tubule, minimal to mild accumulation of eosinophilic (hyaline) droplets in the proximal convoluted tubule, and minimal to mild mononuclear interstitial infiltrates.
L1094: The Committee concurred with the Applicant's proposed doses of 0 (0.9% sodium chloride for injection), 1.5, and 5 mg/kg Q2W via SC injection for both male and female rats. The high dose was identified as the MTD based on the decrease in body weight gain (i.e., &gt;10% from control in females at \ge 10 mg/kg Q2W) and also class experience with ASO, which suggests that the observed histopathology lesions in the kidneys (seen in male and female rats at \ge 10 mg/kg Q2W) can progress with longer treatment duration and adversely impact survival in a 2-year study. The low dose for both male and female rats was approximately one-third of the high dose.
L1095: ## **13.1.3.4. Reproductive and Developmental Toxicity**
L1096: The potential reproductive and developmental toxicity of donidalorsen were evaluated in GLP-compliant combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice with donidalorsen and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059, a combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice with the unconjugated parent compound of donidalorsen (ISIS 546254) and the corresponding unconjugated mouse surrogate (ISIS 482584), and an EFD study in rabbits with the unconjugated parent compound of donidalorsen (ISIS 546254).
L1097: ## **A Combined Fertility and Developmental Toxicity Study of ISIS 721744 in Mice Via Subcutaneous Administration (Study Nos. 727-134; 721744-AS06)**
L1098: ## **Key Study Findings**
L1099: - Mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection), donidalorsen (1, 4, or 10 mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4 mg/kg/week). Males were dosed once weekly during the premating (beginning 28 days prior to mating), mating, and postmating phases (10 weeks total). Females were dosed beginning 14 days prior to mating. Females were dosed weekly (Days 1, 8, 15, and 22, as needed) during the premating phase and through the mating phase until positive evidence of copulation was observed, and every other day during the gestation period from Gestation Day (GD) 0 to GD 16 (i.e., GDs 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, and 16). Unmated females continued to be dosed weekly until termination (following the last GD 18 necropsies).
- There were no estrous cycle changes (i.e., mean number of cycles and mean cycle length) related to treatment with donidalorsen or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
- Percent abnormal sperm was increased at 10 mg/kg/week donidalorsen (15.6%, statistically significant) and 4 mg/kg/week ISIS 722059 (13.4%), compared to the vehicle control (10.1%), and outside of the conducting laboratory historical control ranges of 3.4% to 10.2%. It did not appear that an increase in percent abnormal sperm affected pregnancy indices at 10 mg/kg/week donidalorsen or 4 mg/kg/week ISIS 722059.
- There were no effects of donidalorsen or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on male or female mating performance; the number of corpora lutea, implantations, preimplantation and postimplantation losses, or live fetuses; fetal body weights; or fetal external, visceral, or skeletal variations or malformations (i.e., no fetal anomalies) in mice.
- Unconjugated donidalorsen concentrations in the parental liver of males and females increased with increasing dose of drug. Unconjugated donidalorsen concentrations in the fetal liver were below the limit of quantitation in all donidalorsen-treated groups. Notably, unconjugated donidalorsen concentrations in the placenta (up to 0.31 µg/g) and testes (up to 1.61 µg/g) were much lower than in the liver (i.e., 3 to 43 µg/g for 1 to 10 mg/kg/week donidalorsen in F0 females on GD 18 and 7 to 47 µg/g for 1 to 10 mg/kg/week for males on Day 73). It was unclear if donidalorsen or unconjugated donidalorsen crossed the placenta to reach fetal tissues.
- Treatment of F0 male and female mice with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 at 4 mg/kg/week statistically decreased liver mRNA expression of KLKB1/PKK by 80% and 75%, respectively.
- The NOAEL for donidalorsen on male and female fertility and mating performance, as well as developmental toxicity, was the high dose of 10 mg/kg/week.
L1100: ## **A Combined Fertility and Developmental Toxicity Study of ISIS 546254 and ISIS 482584 Administered by Subcutaneous Injection in CD-1 Mice (Study Nos. (b) (4)090.60; 546254-AS04)**
L1101: ## **Key Study Findings**
L1102: - CD-1 mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection), ISIS 546254 (10.5, 42, or 84 mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 (84 mg/kg/week). As described in the study report, animals were dosed every other day and received three or four doses per week; thus, the weekly dose (mg/kg/week) was equivalent to 3.5 times the single mg/kg/dose. Males were dosed every other day during the pre mating (beginning 4 weeks prior to mating), mating, and post mating phases (10 weeks total). Females were dosed every other day for two weeks prior to mating, during the mating phase, and throughout GD 15 (encompassing the period of organogenesis).
- There was one unscheduled death during the study, which was considered incidental and unrelated to treatment with mouse surrogate ISIS 482584. All other animals survived to scheduled termination.
- Body weight decreases were noted in females on GD 18 at 10.5 and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 (less than 10% difference from vehicle control). The decreases were not considered adverse.
- There were no effects of ISIS 546254 or mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 on estrous cyclicity.
- There were no effects of ISIS 546254 or mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 on fertility (mating index) or fecundity (pregnancy index).
- At the time of Cesarean section, mean gravid uterus weights were decreased at 10.5, 42, and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 (-11%, -5%, and -7% difference from vehicle control respectively; not statistically significant) and at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 (-24% difference from vehicle control; statistically significant).
- The number of live fetuses was decreased at 10.5, 42, and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 (12 live fetuses in each group; statistically significant only at 10.5 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254) and at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 (11 live fetuses; statistically significant) compared to the vehicle control (14 live fetuses). This is not likely biologically significant. In addition, the fetal viability percentage at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 was statistically decreased compared to the vehicle control (86% versus 96%).
- There were no effects of ISIS 546254 on mean fetal weight (male or female) although at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 mean fetal weight was decreased for males and females (-11% and -10% difference from vehicle control, respectively; statistically significant in females only).
- The number of early resorptions was increased at 10.5, 42, and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 (one in each group; not statistically significant) and at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 (one; statistically significant) compared to the vehicle control (zero). This is not likely biologically significant. The percent early resorptions/animal was increased at 10.5, 42, and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 and at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 compared to the vehicle
L1103: control. The embryo-fetal mortality index was increased at 10.5, 42, and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 and at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 compared to the vehicle control. As described in the study report, although these changes were noticeable and statistically significant in some groups, they were consistent with what is noted in the control animals in these types of studies, therefore, a clear relationship to either test article cannot be established.

- Overall, there were no fetal external findings, visceral variations or malformations, or skeletal variations or malformations attributed to treatment with ISIS 546254 or mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 in mice.
- There were no effects of ISIS 546254 or mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 on sperm motility, morphology, or sperm count.
- ISIS 546254 concentrations in the parental liver of vehicle control males and females were below the limit of quantitation. ISIS 546254 concentrations in the parental liver of males and females increased with ISIS 546254 dose with higher concentrations in male mice than female mice. ISIS 546254 concentrations in the fetal liver were below the limit of quantitation in all ISIS 546254-treated groups.
- ISIS 546254 concentrations in the placenta were below the limit of quantitation, 6.73, and 22.3 µg/g with doses of 10.5, 42, and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254, respectively. Notably, ISIS 546254 concentrations in the placenta were lower than in the liver (52 to 612 µg/g for 10.5 to 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 in males and females).
- Treatment of male and female mice with mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 at 84 mg/kg/week statistically decreased liver mRNA expression of KLKB1/PKK by 94% and 87%, respectively.
- Overall, SC administration of ISIS 546254 (up to 84 mg/kg/week) or mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 (84 mg/kg/week) did not affect fertility, pregnancy, or embryofetal development in mice.
L1104: ## **An Assessment of Effects of ISIS 546254 on Embryo-Fetal Development in New Zealand White Rabbits (Study Nos. (b) (4)090.61; 546254-AS05)**
L1105: It was agreed upon at the time of the EOP2 meeting that an EFD study in rabbits with donidalorsen would not be needed. This was based on the availability of an EFD study in rabbits with ISIS 546254 (unconjugated parent compound of ISIS donidalorsen, which has the same sequence as donidalorsen).
L1106: ## **Key Study Findings**
L1107: - Pregnant New Zealand white rabbits were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection) or ISIS 546254 (12.5, 25, or 75 mg/kg/week) every other day from GD 6 to GD 18 (i.e., GDs 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, and 18) encompassing the period of organogenesis. As stated in the study report, animals were dosed every other day, thus, the weekly dose (mg/kg/week) was equivalent to 3.5 times the single mg/kg dose.
- There were no unscheduled deaths during the study.
L1108: - ISIS 546254 concentrations in the maternal liver of vehicle control females on GD 28 were below the limit of quantitation. ISIS 546254 concentrations increased in the maternal liver of females on GD 20 (TK animals) and GD 28 with increase in ISIS 546254 dose, with concentrations on GD 28 about half of the concentrations on GD 20 (TK animals). ISIS 546254 concentrations in the fetal liver were below the limit of quantitation in all ISIS 546254-treated groups. ISIS 546254 concentrations in the placenta were below the limit of quantitation at 12.5 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 and at &lt;10% of maternal exposures at 25 and 75 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254.
- There was no effect of ISIS 546254 on fecundity as the fecundity index was similar between 12.5, 25, and 75 mg/kg/week (88%, 100%, and 84%, respectively) and the vehicle control (91%).
- There were no effects of ISIS 546254 on gravid uterine weight, the number of corpora lutea, the number of implantations, the implantation index, percent of early or late resorptions, live fetuses, the sex ratio, or fetal viability.
- Mean fetal weight appeared to decrease at 75 mg/kg/week for males (-12.3% difference from vehicle control; statistically significant), females (-10.4% difference from vehicle control), and combined (-11.6% difference from vehicle control; statistically significant). The embryo-fetal mortality index at 12.5, 25, and 75 mg/kg/week (5.0%, 5.7%, and 6.7%, respectively) was increased (not statistically significant) compared to the vehicle control (1.3%). The percent of dead fetuses/implantation site at 12.5, 25, and 75 mg/kg/week (1.3%, 0.3%, and 5.8%, respectively) was increased (statistically significant at 75 mg/kg/week only) compared to the vehicle control (0%). As stated in the study report, although these changes were noticeable and statistically significant at 75 mg/kg/week, they were consistent with what is noted in the vehicle control animals in these types of studies, therefore, a clear relationship to test article cannot be established.
- Overall, there were no fetal external findings, visceral variations or malformations, or skeletal variations or malformations attributed to treatment with SC administration of ISIS 546254 (up to 75 mg/kg/week) in rabbits.
L1109: ## 13.2. Individual Reviews of Studies Submitted With the New Drug Application
L1110: Pivotal and supporting pharmacology (primary), absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME), toxicology (carcinogenicity, reproductive and developmental toxicity, and other toxicity), and extractables and leachables studies submitted with NDA 219407 and not previously submitted with IND 142564 have been reviewed and evaluated under the NDA and are summarized here.
L1111: ## 13.2.1. Pharmacology
L1112: ## 13.2.1.1. Primary Pharmacodynamics
L1113: The primary pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen were evaluated in an in vivo primary pharmacology study in human KLKB1/PKK transgenic mice.
L1114: ## In Vivo Primary Pharmacology Studies
L1115: ## In Vivo Evaluation of ISIS 721744 Activity in Human KLKB1/PKK Transgenic Mice-Analysis of Plasma PKK Protein Levels (ELN 23-100d)
L1116: The effects on human PKK plasma protein levels were evaluated following single dose SC administration of donidalorsen (0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, and 10 mg/kg) to transgenic mice expressing the human KLKB1/PKK gene. A single dose of donidalorsen reduced plasma PKK protein in human KLKB1/PKK transgenic mice in a dose- and time-dependent manner (Figure 37). Plasma PKK protein levels were reduced up to a maximum of about 91% on Day 14 after treatment with 10 mg/kg donidalorsen. After Day 14, plasma PKK protein levels gradually increased to baseline levels and were restored by Day 42 or Day 56 at 1 mg/kg or 3 mg/kg donidalorsen, respectively. At Day 56, plasma PKK protein levels at 10 mg/kg were still 20% below baseline levels.
L1117: Based on nonlinear curve fit analysis, the median effective dose 50 (ED_{50}) at Days 7 and 14 after treatment with donidalorsen was 0.67 and 0.75 mg/kg, respectively (Figure 38).

L1123: ## 13.2.2. Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion/Pharmacokinetics
L1124: The ADME, PK, and TK profiles of donidalorsen were evaluated both in vitro and in vivo (mice and monkeys).
L1125: ## 13.2.2.1. Absorption
L1126: The plasma pharmacokinetics of donidalorsen was evaluated in a GLP-compliant single-dose SC ADME study in rats with radiolabeled [3H]donidalorsen and a GLP-compliant 6-week repeat-dose SC study in mice.
L1127: ## ADME of [3H]ISIS 721744 Following a Single Subcutaneous Dose Administration to Sprague Dawley Rats (Study Nos. IPI/06; 721744-APK02)
L1128: Nonpigmented Sprague Dawley rats were treated with single SC doses of [3H]donidalorsen (2 or 10 mg/kg).
L1129: Following a single SC dose of [3H]donidalorsen at 2 mg/kg to male nonpigmented Sprague Dawley rats, Cmax of 0.375 and 0.538 µg equivalent/mL were reached in the blood and plasma, respectively, at 1 hour for both, after which radioactivity declined in a biphasic manner. The blood:plasma ratio calculated from AUC0-∞ was 0.76. Cmax (µg equivalent/g) of 24.40 at 24 hours and 14.89 at 168 hours were reached in the liver and kidney, respectively. Most tissues achieved concentrations similar to or slightly above the blood radioactivity concentrations. Tissue:blood ratios at 24 hours were highest in the liver and kidney (1877 and 850, respectively) consistent
L1130: with uptake of donidalorsen. The thyroid gland, pancreas, large and small intestine, spleen, lymph node, and bone marrow had tissue:blood ratios between 24.2 to 69.2 at 24 hours.
L1131: Following a single SC dose of [^{3}\text{H}]donidalorsen at 2 mg/kg to male nonpigmented Sprague Dawley rats, the mean cumulative recovery (0 to Day 56) of radioactivity in excreta was 76.8% (17.14% from urine +57.46% from feces +2.16% from cage wash). Residual radioactivity in the carcass on Day 56 accounted for 5.84% of the administered dose resulting in an overall recovery of 82.6%.
L1132: Following a single SC dose of [^{3}\text{H}]donidalorsen at 10 mg/kg to male and female nonpigmented rats, radioactivity was distributed to tissues by the first sampling time at 2 hours and reached maximal concentrations within 2 to 48 hours postdose with highest concentrations of radioactivity in the kidney, liver, intestinal mucosa, salivary gland, bone marrow, lymph nodes, and splenic red pulp. Concentrations of radioactivity in most organs/tissues decreased by the end of the sampling period at 336 hours, except for the kidney where radioactivity levels remained at similar levels throughout the sampling period.
L1133: Recovery of radioactivity in urine and feces from nonpigmented rats following a single SC dose of [^{3}\text{H}]donidalorsen at 10 mg/kg was 0.35% and 1.37% of dose, respectively for males and 0.30% and 1.31% of dose, respectively for females.
L1134: ## **A 6-Week Subcutaneous Repeat-Dose Pharmacokinetic Study of ISIS 721744 in CD-1 Mice (Study Nos. G122111; 721744-APK03)**
L1135: Male ICR mice were treated by SC administration with donidalorsen (10 or 20 mg/kg/week once weekly) for 6 weeks (Days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29, 36, and 43) to determine the PK profile and distribution of donidalorsen to kidney and liver. As described in the study report, concentrations of total full-length donidalorsen, including fully conjugated, partially conjugated (minus 1-, 2-, and 3-GalNAc sugars), and unconjugated donidalorsen (ISIS 780124), were determined in mouse plasma by a validated hybridization ECL assay, while concentrations of unconjugated donidalorsen in kidney and liver samples were analyzed by a validated HPLC-MS/MS bioanalytical method.
L1136: Median T_{\text{max}} was 0.5 hours on Days 1 and 43 at 10 and 20 mg/kg donidalorsen. Mean C_{\text{max}} and AUC increased in a slightly greater than dose proportional manner on Days 1 and 43. There was lack of accumulation after repeat dosing.
L1137: Concentrations of unconjugated donidalorsen were higher in the kidney than in the liver. Concentrations of unconjugated donidalorsen in the liver were similar at 10 and 20 mg/kg/week possibly due to saturation of tissue uptake at these dose levels.
L1138: ## 13.2.2.2. Distribution
L1139: The distribution of donidalorsen was evaluated in vitro for the whole blood and plasma concentration ratio of donidalorsen in human, monkey, and rat.
L1140: ## In Vitro Evaluation of Whole Blood and Plasma Concentration Ratio of ISIS 721744 (Donidalorsen) in Human, Monkey, and Rat (Study Nos. IIS-P2-008; 721744-IS11)
L1141: The in vitro mean blood to plasma ratio of donidalorsen (tested neat, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1, and 2 µg/mL in human whole blood and neat, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100, and 200 µg/mL in monkey and rat whole blood) was between 0.630 and 0.824 in human, 0.468 and 0.566 in monkey, and 0.501 and 0.661 in rat, suggesting that donidalorsen distributes primarily in the plasma compartment across the concentrations tested in all three species.
L1142: ## 13.2.2.3. Metabolism
L1143: The metabolism of donidalorsen was evaluated after single SC administration of [3H]donidalorsen to rats, as well as from select urine samples from studies in mice, monkeys, and humans. Further, the metabolism of donidalorsen linker-related metabolites was evaluated in select plasma, urine, and fecal samples from studies in mice, monkeys, and humans, as well as from liver and kidney samples from rat.
L1144: ## Metabolite Profiling and Identification Studies Following a Single Subcutaneous Dose Administration of [3H]ISIS 721744 to Male and Female Rats (Study Nos. IPI/07; 721744-APK02)
L1145: This study evaluated the metabolic profile of donidalorsen in rat whole blood and plasma, liver and kidney tissues, and in the excreta (urine and feces) by liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LC-MS) after single SC administration of [3H]donidalorsen at 10 mg/kg to male and female nonpigmented rats.
L1146: Donidalorsen was seen in the liver, kidney, plasma, and whole blood. Donidalorsen was the major component at 2 hours in plasma and blood but was not detected at 24 hours in plasma and blood. Unconjugated donidalorsen (i.e., ISIS 780124) was the major component in liver (2 and 24 hours) and kidney (24 hours). Two major components were present in the kidney at 2 hours: unconjugated donidalorsen (i.e., ISIS 780124) and donidalorsen minus 3 GalNAc sugars (i.e., ISIS 721744 -3 GalNAc). Two major components were detected in feces samples at 0 to 24 hours: ISIS 780124 3'N-18 and ISIS 780124 3'N-17. Several ISIS 780124 shortmers were identified as major components in urine at 0 to 24 hours, from ISIS 780124 3'N-10 to ISIS 780124 3'N-14. As described in the study report, all identified metabolites were consistent with nuclease-mediated metabolism to chain shortened oligonucleotides with full, partial, or without GalNAc or linker-conjugation.
L1147: ## **Metabolic Profiling and Identification of ISIS 721744 Oligonucleotide-Related Metabolites by HPLC-High-Resolution Mass Spectrometer in Select Urine Samples From Mice, Monkeys, and Humans (Study Nos. 727-085, 727-081, ISIS 721744-CS1; 721744-IS10)**
L1148: This study identified donidalorsen oligonucleotide containing metabolites (full-length or chain-shortened) from urine samples at steady state from mice, monkeys, and humans treated with multiple SC doses of donidalorsen (i.e., 10 mg/kg from 13-week repeat-dose toxicity study in mice [Study No. 721744-AS01]; 30 mg/kg from 39-week repeat-dose toxicity study in monkeys [Study No. 721744-AS02]; and 80 mg from phase 1 trial in humans with dosing every 4 weeks for four total doses [Study No. ISIS 721744-CS1]) using liquid chromatography with a tandem ultraviolet detector and high-resolution mass spectrometer method.
L1149: As described in the study report, the oligonucleotide portions of conjugated ASO molecules are metabolized by hydrolysis of the phosphodiester bonds via endonuclease and/or exonuclease (either 5' and/or 3') enzymes. Metabolism of the GalNAc-conjugation component of donidalorsen typically occurs by a sequential loss of the three GalNAc sugar moieties (-1, -2, and -3 GalNAc), followed by the loss of a portion, or all the remaining THA linker (Shemesh et al. 2016; Weidolf et al. 2021). Complete loss of the THA linker results in the formation of ISIS 780124, the unconjugated version of donidalorsen. The metabolism of the two portions of donidalorsen (oligonucleotide and GalNAc) may occur simultaneously resulting in many potential metabolites with multiple potential metabolic pathways responsible for a single metabolite compound.
L1150: A diagram of the proposed putative metabolism of donidalorsen is shown in Figure 39.
L1151: **Figure 39. Diagram of Putative Metabolism of Donidalorsen**
L1152: Source: Study No. 721744-IS10, Figure 1
