L1154: Abbreviations: GalNAc, N-acetyl galactosamine; PO, phosphodiester; PS, phosphorothioate; THA, tris(hexylamino)
L1155: ## Mouse Urine
L1156: Donidalorsen was the major component (about 53% of total oligonucleotide signal) in mouse urine samples when administered at 10 mg/kg. As described by the Applicant, other oligonucleotide metabolites included the full-length ASO with partial conjugations, fully and partially conjugated donidalorsen with loss of nucleotides from the 3'-end (referred to as 3'-deletion chain-shortened metabolites), and unconjugated donidalorsen with loss of nucleotides from the 5'-end (referred to as 5'-deletion chain-shortened metabolites).
L1157: ## Monkey Urine
L1158: Donidalorsen was the major component (about 41% of total oligonucleotide signal), followed by ISIS 780124 (unconjugated version of donidalorsen; about 14% of total oligonucleotide signal) in the monkey urine samples when administered at 30 mg/kg. As described by the Applicant, other identified metabolites were 3'-deletion chain-shortened metabolites of donidalorsen (with GalNAc sugar moieties and THA linker attached), as well as metabolites of unconjugated donidalorsen with loss of nucleotides from the 5'-end.
L1159: ## Human Urine
L1160: ISIS 780124 (unconjugated version of donidalorsen) was the major component (about 38% of total oligonucleotide signal) in human urine samples when administered at 80 mg/kg.
L1161: Donidalorsen was not detected. As described by the Applicant, the other most abundant metabolites were from unconjugated donidalorsen with loss of nucleotides from the 5'-end. However, 3'-deletion chain-shortened metabolites of donidalorsen (with GalNAc sugar moieties and THA linker attached) were also seen.
L1162: There were no unique metabolites found in humans compared to mice or monkeys.
L1163: ## **Profiling, Identification, and Quantitation of ISIS 721744 Linker-Related Metabolites by HPLC-MS/MS in Select Plasma, Urine, and Fecal Samples From Mice, Monkeys, and Humans (Study No. 721744-IS12)**
L1164: This study identified linker-only-related metabolites of donidalorsen (no full-length or chain-shortened oligonucleotide components) from plasma (monkey and human), urine (mouse, monkey, and human), and feces (monkey) after SC dosing of donidalorsen (i.e., 2 and/or 10 mg/kg from 13-week repeat-dose toxicity study in mice [Study No. 721744-AS01]; 2 and/or 30 mg/kg from 39-week repeat-dose toxicity study in monkeys [Study No. 721744-AS02]; and 80 mg from phase 1 trial in humans with dosing every 4 weeks for four total doses [Study No. ISIS 721744-CS1]) by a HPLC-MS/MS method. Eleven total linker metabolites (putative linker metabolites M4 to M14) were monitored in these studies.
L1165: Six linker metabolites were detected in monkey plasma (M5 and M8 to M12) and three linker metabolites were detected in human plasma (M5, M8, and M12).
L1166: Ten linker metabolites (M5 to M14) were similarly detected in mouse, monkey, and human urine. The linker metabolites with the highest peak area ratios were M8, M5, and M12, which were consistent across the three species.
L1167: Ten linker metabolites (M5 to M14) were detected in monkey feces. The linker metabolites with the highest peak area ratios were M8, M10, M11, and M5.
L1168: As described by the Applicant, the THA-linker-related metabolism is mostly similar across species with oxidative metabolites being formed and eliminated through urine and bile. The overall metabolic pathways for the THA-linker-related metabolites of donidalorsen involve hydrolysis of GalNAc sugars and oligonucleotide moieties to form M4 metabolite, followed by internal cyclization of M4 to form cyclized linker M5 metabolite which would then undergo mono- and di-oxidation to form M6 and M7 metabolites. Dephosphorylation of M4 metabolite resulted in the formation of M8 metabolite followed by sequential oxidation at each branching arm of M8 metabolite to form mono-, di-, tri-, and tetra-oxidation metabolites (M9 to M12 metabolites). Additional metabolites resulting from dealkylation (M13 metabolite), or deamination (M14 metabolite) were also detected. The proposed pathway for the metabolism of linker-related moieties of donidalorsen is shown in Figure 40 (Shemesh et al. 2016).
L1169: **Figure 40. Proposed Biotransformation Pathway for the Linker-Related Metabolism of Donidalorsen**
L1170: Figure 40 illustrates the proposed biotransformation pathway for the linker-related metabolism of Donidalorsen (ISIS 721744). The pathway shows the conversion of the parent compound (ISIS 721744) into various metabolites (M4 through M14) via enzymatic and oxidative reactions.

The pathway starts with ISIS 721744, which undergoes dephosphorylation (Phosphatase) to form M4. M4 is then converted to M5 via the loss of \text{H}_2\text{O}. M5 is sequentially converted to M6 and M7 via oxidative reactions ([\text{O}]).

Separately, M5 is also converted to M8 via an oxidative reaction ([\text{O}]). M8 is then converted to M9, M10, M11, and M12 via sequential oxidative reactions ([\text{O}]).

M8 is shown to be a precursor for M13 and M14 via a dashed line indicating a potential alternative pathway involving hydroxyl group addition (\text{HO}).

The structures of M4, M5, M6, M7, M8, M9, M10, M11, M12, M13, and M14 are displayed, showing the progressive loss of the phospho group and subsequent oxidative modifications on the linker moiety.
L1171: Source: Excerpted from the Applicant's submission
L1172: ## **Method Development, Qualification and Sample Analysis of a Bioanalytical Method for the Determination of M8 in Liver and Kidney Samples Generated From Rat Using LC-MS/MS (Study Nos. IPI/08; 721744-IS17)**
L1173: This study developed a liquid chromatographic-tandem mass spectrometric (UPLC/MS/MS) bioanalytical method to determine the donidalorsen THA linker-related metabolite M8 (chemical formula = \text{C}_{42}\text{H}_{81}\text{N}_5\text{O}_{12}; molecular weight = 847.5882) in liver and kidney samples from rats treated with single SC dose levels of donidalorsen at 2 and 10 mg/kg (Study Nos. IPI/06 and IPI/07; Study No. 721744-APK02).
L1174: Mean M8 concentrations were below the limit of quantitation in liver and kidney from rats treated with a single SC dose level of donidalorsen at 2 mg/kg. Mean M8 concentrations from rats treated with a single SC dose level of donidalorsen at 10 mg/kg were 211 ng/g at the 2-hour timepoint and below the limit of quantitation at the 24-hour timepoint in the liver, and 526 ng/g at the 2-hour timepoint and 317 ng/g at the 24-hour timepoint in the kidney.
L1175: ## **13.2.3. Toxicology**
L1176: The potential carcinogenic toxicity of donidalorsen and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 were evaluated in a 6-month study in Tg.rasH2 mice. A 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats is ongoing. At the time of the pre-NDA meeting, the Division agreed that it would be acceptable to
L1177: submit a summary of the in-life data for the 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats at the time of the NDA submission and to submit the final report as a PMR.
L1178: ## 13.2.3.1. Carcinogenicity
L1179: ## A 6-Month Study of ISIS 721744 by Subcutaneous Bolus Injection in CBvB6F1-Tg(HRAS)2Jic Hemizygous Transgenic Mouse (Study Nos. 727-140; 721744-AS07)
L1180: ## Key Study Findings
L1181: - Tg.rashH2 mice (n=25/sex/group) were administered vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection), donidalorsen (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg/dose for males and 10, 20, or 60 mg/kg/dose for females), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (10 mg/kg/dose) Q2W for up to 6 months by SC injection. A positive control group was included in which Tg.rashH2 mice (10/sex) were administered urethane (500 mg/kg/dose) via intraperitoneal injection on Days 1, 3, and 5. The mouse was not a pharmacologically relevant species with donidalorsen, and this study evaluated off-target effects. The mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 was included to assess inhibition of PKK and potential on-target effects.
- There was no statistically significant increase or decrease in mortality dose response across the vehicle control and donidalorsen-treated groups, in either male or female mice. The pairwise comparisons showed a statistically significant decrease in mortality in the male 5 mg/kg/dose group (low dose) compared to the vehicle control group (p=0.0160). The pairwise comparisons showed no statistically significant increase or decrease in mortality between the mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 group and the vehicle control group, in either male or female mice.
- There were no donidalorsen-related or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059-related effects on body weights.
- Effects on clinical chemistry included increases in AST, ALT, and glutamate dehydrogenase in males at 10 and 20 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and females at 60 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, which correlated with histopathology findings in the liver.
- A MTD was achieved at the high dose of 20 mg/kg Q2W in males based on histopathology findings in the liver and elevations of glutamate dehydrogenase. The high dose of 60 mg/kg Q2W in females did not meet the criteria for an MTD.
- Gross pathology findings included liver mass in one male at 5 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and one male at 20 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, which correlated with neoplastic histopathology findings of hepatocellular adenoma in the liver of both mice.
- Neoplastic histopathology findings included hepatocellular adenoma in the liver in 1/25 males at 5 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, 2/25 males at 20 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, and 1/25 males at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. The hepatocellular adenoma seen in the males at 5 and 20 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen were accompanied by increases in AST and ALT, gross pathology findings in the liver, and non-neoplastic histopathology findings in the liver of microvesicular hepatocellular vacuolation, basophilic focus of cellular alteration, hepatocellular single cell necrosis, and/or basophilic pigmented macrophage. There were no
L1182: correlating gross pathology or non-neoplastic histopathology findings for the male at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
L1183: - Non-neoplastic histopathology findings were noted in the liver (microvesicular hepatocellular vacuolation, basophilic pigmented macrophages, hepatocellular single cell necrosis, karyocytomegaly, and/or basophilic focus of cellular alteration in males at 5, 10, and/or 20 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, and/or females at 10, 20, and/or 60 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, and/or males and/or females at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059); kidney (epithelial vacuolation in females at 60 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, and epithelial basophilic granules in males at 20 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and females at 20 and 60 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen); injection site (macrophage granular vacuolation in males and females at all donidalorsen doses, and in males and females at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059); urinary bladder (urothelial vacuolation in males at 10 and 20 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and females at 20 and 60 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen); and the axillary and/or mesenteric lymph nodes (macrophage vacuolation in females at 60 mg/kg/dose donidalorsen). The histopathology findings were attributed to or a consequence of oligonucleotide uptake.
- The positive control (urethane) group confirmed the carcinogenic responsiveness of the Tg.rasH2 model. Urethane treatment resulted in a decrease in body weight in both male and female mice and a statistically significant increase in unscheduled deaths (i.e., decrease in survival) compared to the vehicle control group in both male and female mice. Neoplastic findings included hemangiosarcoma (whole body in male and female mice), malignant lymphoma (hemolymphoreticular tissue in male mice), and bronchioloalveolar adenoma and carcinoma (lungs in male and female mice). These findings are consistent with known effects of urethane administration (National Toxicology Program 2021).
- Toxicokinetic parameters were not evaluated.
- Donidalorsen concentrations in the kidney and liver of males and females were mostly increased with increasing donidalorsen dose following 6-months of treatment.
- Liver PKK mRNA expression was statistically reduced in male and female mice treated with 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059 Q2W for 26 weeks by 94% and 79%, respectively, compared to controls.
- The ECAC concurred with the doses for the study in male mice but could not recommend doses for female mice. The Applicant did not conduct a new DRF study to identify an acceptable high dose or seek ECAC concurrence for their final dose selection in female mice. The ECAC concluded that the carcinogenicity study was adequate for male mice but inadequate for female mice because a MTD was not achieved and no other valid basis to support the high dose was discernable.
L1184: ## 13.2.3.2. Reproductive and Developmental Toxicity
L1185: The potential reproductive and developmental toxicity of donidalorsen was evaluated in a GLP-compliant PPND study in mice with donidalorsen and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
L1186: ## **Study for Toxic Effects of ISIS 721744 on Pre- and Postnatal Development, Including Maternal Function in Mice (Study Nos. 727-142; 721744-AS09)**
L1187: ## **Key Study Findings**
L1188: - F0 female mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection), donidalorsen (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (5 mg/kg/week) every other day from GD 6 to GD 18 (GDs 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, and 18) and weekly from Lactation Day (LD) 1 to LD 20 (LDs 1, 7, 13, and 20).
- There were no deaths in any of the F0 females attributed to treatment with donidalorsen or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
- AST (3\times and 2\times of control, respectively) and ALT (5\times and 4\times of control, respectively) were increased in F0 females on LD 22 at 10 and 20 mg/kg/week donidalorsen that was consistent with uptake into the liver.
- Mean donidalorsen concentrations in milk from F0 females was below the limit of quantitation for the vehicle control and 5 mg/kg/week donidalorsen groups, and 7.63 and 24.63 ng/mL at 10 and 20 mg/kg/week donidalorsen, respectively.
- There were no effects of donidalorsen or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on parturition parameters (gestation index, live newborn pups/litter, live birth index, uterine implantation sites, and gestation length).
- Kidney, liver, and/or spleen weights (absolute and/or relative to terminal body weight) on LD 22 were increased in F0 females treated with 5, 10, and/or 20 mg/kg/week donidalorsen. Increases of kidney and liver weights were consistent with uptake of donidalorsen.
- Unconjugated donidalorsen concentrations in the kidney and liver of F0 females on LD 22 increased with donidalorsen dose, which was consistent with uptake of donidalorsen.
- Treatment of F0 females with mouse surrogate 5 mg/kg/week ISIS 722059 statistically decreased liver mRNA expression of KLKB1/PKK by 82% on LD 22.
- There were no effects of donidalorsen or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on F1 pups (preweaning) based on evaluation of survival, clinical signs, body weights, sex ratios, physical development, and gross pathology.
- There were no effects of donidalorsen or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on the F1 generation based on evaluation of survival, clinical signs, sexual maturation, body weights, food consumption, behavioral evaluations (motor activity, Morris Water Maze, acoustic startle response), estrous cyclicity, mating/reproductive/fertility performance indices, GD 13 corpora lutea/uterine implantation data, organ weights, and gross pathology evaluations.
- The NOAEL for maternal toxicity and the PPND study was the high dose of 20 mg/kg/week donidalorsen.
L1189: ## 13.2.3.3. Other Toxicity Studies
L1190: The potential toxicity of donidalorsen-related impurities was evaluated in a GLP-compliant 13-week repeat-dose SC toxicity study in mice with donidalorsen and associated test article mixtures (TAMs).
L1191: ## 13.2.3.3.1. Impurities
L1192: In the 13-week repeat-dose SC toxicity and impurity qualification study, ICR mice were treated with vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection/solution [saline]) or [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg total oligonucleotide dose level of donidalorsen, TAM 1, or TAM 2 Q2W. The two TAMs were made up of donidalorsen and associated impurities (i.e., [REDACTED] (b) (4) impurities for TAM 1 and [REDACTED] (b) (4) impurity for TAM 2).
L1193: ## Key Study Findings
L1194: - There were no unscheduled deaths during the study.
- Red blood cell values were minimally decreased only in females at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose TAM 2.
- BUN values were decreased in males and females at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose TAM 2; AST values were increased only in males at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, TAM 1, and TAM 2; ALT values were increased only in males at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, TAM 1, and TAM 2; and triglycerides were decreased in females at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and males at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose TAM 2.
- Liver weights (absolute and/or relative to body weight) were increased only in males at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose donidalorsen and TAM 1, and [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose TAM 2.
- Histopathology findings attributed to treatment with donidalorsen, TAM 1, and/or TAM 2 were noted in the liver and injection site.Liver: Minimal to slight mononuclear cell infiltration in males and/or females at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, TAM 1, and/or TAM 2. Minimal karyocytomegaly in males only at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, TAM 1, and TAM 2, which correlated with minimally increased ALT and AST and increased liver weight in males. Liver karyocytomegaly was attributed to uptake and accumulation of ASOs into the liver.
- Injection Site: Minimal to slight vacuolated granular macrophages in males and females at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose donidalorsen, [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose TAM 1, and [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose TAM 2. Injection site findings were attributed to uptake and accumulation of ASOs into the macrophages.
- Mean concentrations of unconjugated donidalorsen in the mouse liver on Day 87 were comparable for donidalorsen-, TAM 1-, and TAM 2-treated groups.
L1195: In summary, the findings in TAM 1- and TAM 2-treated groups were similar to those in donidalorsen-treated groups, which included increases in AST and ALT, increases in liver weights, and histopathology findings of mononuclear cell infiltration and karyocytomegaly in the liver and vacuolated granular macrophages at the injection site. Overall, there were no
L1196: meaningful differences between the findings in either of the TAM groups (donidalorsen + associated impurities) compared to the donidalorsen group alone, and it did not appear that the added impurities affected the toxicity profile of donidalorsen.

L1228: ## 13.2.3.4. Extractables and Leachables
L1229: The donidalorsen drug product is a sterile, single-dose, ready-to-use parenteral solution for SC administration. The drug product is packaged in a staked needle glass PFS closed with a (b) (4) rubber plunger stopper. The PFS is assembled into an AI for the final drug product presentation. The AI delivers a single dose of 80 mg donidalorsen in 0.8 mL (100 mg/mL). Extractables and leachables studies were conducted to assess the donidalorsen drug product container closure system, which were evaluated (see Nonclinical Primary Review dated July 25, 2025). There were no nonclinical safety concerns with the potential leachables from the primary container closure system of donidalorsen.

L1244: ## 14. Clinical Pharmacology
L1245: ## 14.1. In Vitro Studies
L1246: ## 14.1.1. Metabolism and Excretion of the Antisense Oligonucleotide Moiety of Donidalorsen (Studies ISIS 721744-IS10 and ISIS 721744-APK02)
L1247: Donidalorsen contains a 2'-O-methoxyethyl (MOE)-modified chimeric gapmer ASO with a mixed backbone of phosphodiester (PS) and phosphorothioate (PO) internucleotide linkages. These have been used in previously approved GalNAc-ASO products, such as Eplontersen (NDA 217388), Nusinersen (NDA 209531), Tegsedi (NDA 211172), and Tofersen (NDA 215887). The ASO moiety of donidalorsen is expected to share the same metabolic pathway as other approved GalNAc-conjugated ASO moieties with similar modifications in the oligonucleotide backbone. Therefore, the ASO moiety is majorly metabolized by endo- and exonucleases in tissues to shortmer oligonucleotide metabolites and minimally modulated by major cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes (AstraZeneca 2023).
L1248: The metabolic profile of ASO related metabolites was evaluated in human plasma and urine samples collected following four doses of donidalorsen-4 in Trial ISIS721744-CS1 (see Section 14.2 for more details). Shortmer oligonucleotide metabolites were not detected in plasma 2 hours postdose. Total full length donidalorsen (fully conjugated + partially conjugated + unconjugated) in urine represents &lt;1% of administered dose collected within 24 hours after the fourth dose administered every 4 weeks. The metabolic profiling results for human urine showed that various shortmer metabolites together constitute more than 50% of all drug-related species detected in urine, while the full-length unconjugated donidalorsen constitutes about 38% of all drug-related species. Although shortmer metabolites appear to have a slightly higher relative abundance compared to full length donidalorsen in urine based on the metabolic profiling results, the percent of the dose excreted as shortmer metabolites in urine is not likely to exceed 30% of the dose. This is primarily as full-length donidalorsen represented &lt;1% of the dose in human urine while constituting 38% of all drug-related species detected in urine over 24 hours postdose. Overall, the fragmented ASO metabolites were slowly formed and were subsequently excreted in the urine. The renal elimination of ASO and its related metabolites is considered a minor route.
L1249: ## 14.1.2. Metabolism and Excretion of Linker and Its Related Metabolites (Studies ISIS 721744-IS12 and ISIS 721744-IS16)
L1250: The GalNAc moiety is covalently conjugated to the ASO portion of donidalorsen via a THA linker. The GalNAc conjugate undergoes hydrolysis once distributed to the tissue and is detached from the parent drug. The GalNAc sugar undergoes endogenous carbohydrate catabolism, while the THA linker undergoes extensive oxidative metabolism based on a study in animals (monkey
L1251: and rats) (Shemesh et al. 2016). The proposed metabolic pathway for the GalNAc-linker moiety is shown in Figure 41.
L1252: **Figure 41. Proposed Metabolic Pathway for Linker Portion of Donidalorsen**
L1253: Source: Report 721744-IS12
L1254: The metabolic profile of the linker portion was assessed in plasma, urine, and feces samples across species (monkey, mice, and human). In total, 11 GalNAc-linker-related metabolites were detected from various specimens (i.e., urine, plasma, and feces) across species and the metabolic profiles were generally consistent across species. Among these metabolites, metabolite M4, the THA linker, is formed by hydrolysis of the GalNAc sugars and hydrolysis from the ASO moiety. Metabolite M8 is formed by hydrolysis of the phosphate moiety from the linker M4. M8 can be further metabolized by oxidation to form other metabolites (M9 to M12).
L1255: Of the 11 linker-related metabolites, the 3 metabolites with the highest peak area ratio in human plasma and urine were M5, M8, and M12. Concentrations of major THA-related metabolites M8 and M12 were quantified in human plasma and urine samples collected following four doses of donidalorsen-4 from Trial ISIS721744-CS1. The concentrations of THA-related metabolites were assessed in human plasma at hours 2 and 24, as well as in human urine over 0 to 24 hours. Data are summarized in Table 40.
L1256: **Table 40. Median (Range) Concentration (nM) of M8 and M12 in Human Plasma and Urine**

Abbreviations: h, hour; M, metabolite; N, number
L1259: In human plasma, mean concentrations of M8 and M12 were &lt;2% of those determined for parent drug. In human urine collected over 24 hours, ≥100-fold higher concentrations of M8 and M12 were observed compared to their plasma concentrations (Table 40). However, the amount of M8 and M12 excreted in the urine over 24 hours only accounted for 6.4% and 2.2% of the total administered dose, respectively.
L1260: In vitro cytochrome P450 phenotyping for linker metabolite M8 was conducted in human liver microsomes and recombinant CYP enzymes (rCYP1A2, 2B6, 2C8, 2C9, 2D6, 3A4). After 60 minutes incubation with M8 at concentrations of 1µM and 3µM in human liver microsomes, there was little NADPH-dependent consumption of M8. Following incubation with recombinant CYP enzymes, M8 remained stable with most recombinant enzymes except rCYP3A4, where an approximate 30% reduction in M8 was observed after 60 minutes. In a repeat study with rCYP3A4 using 10µM M8, oxidative metabolites were detected with a low signal to noise ratio. The study suggests that CYP3A4 may contribute to the metabolism of M8. However, M8 is not considered a major metabolite as M8 demonstrated a low abundance in human plasma (1.3% relative to parent drug) and urine (6.4% of administered dose).
L1261: ## 14.1.3. Plasma Protein Binding and Distribution
## (Studies ISIS 721744-IS03, ISIS 721744-IS05, and
## 721744-IS11)
L1262: The extent of plasma protein binding of donidalorsen was evaluated at three nominal concentrations of 0.5, 5, and 150 µg/mL in human plasma. The degree of donidalorsen bound to plasma proteins was similar across all concentrations and was ≥98%.
L1263: The potential interaction of donidalorsen with warfarin and ibuprofen due to plasma protein binding was assessed in vitro using an ultrafiltration method. The plasma protein binding of donidalorsen at 1 µg/mL was similar irrespective of the presence of warfarin (30 µg/mL) and ibuprofen (300 µg/mL), while the plasma protein binding of warfarin at 3 µg/mL or ibuprofen at 30 µg/mL was also similar irrespective of the presence of donidalorsen (10 µg/mL).
L1264: The blood-to-plasma ratio was assessed at six concentrations (0, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1, and 2 µg/mL) in human whole blood incubated over approximately 1 hour. At all evaluated concentrations, the blood-to-plasma distribution ratio of donidalorsen was between 0.63 to 0.82, suggesting that donidalorsen mostly distributes in the plasma compartment.
L1265: ## 14.1.4. Drug-Drug Interaction Potential for
## Donidalorsen (Studies ISIS 721744-IS06, ISIS
## 721744-IS07, and ISIS 721744-IS09)
L1266: An in vitro study was conducted with cryopreserved human primary hepatocytes to assess the potential of donidalorsen to induce CYP1A2, CYP2B6, and CYP3A4. The study demonstrated that donidalorsen did not cause induction of mRNA of these CYP enzymes in all three donors up to 30µM after 48 hours of incubation. The concentration of 30µM is around 43-fold higher than
L1267: peak donidalorsen plasma concentration (around 0.7\mu\text{M}) and is also higher than the Applicant's estimated liver concentration of donidalorsen (&lt;10\mu\text{M}) following administration of 80 mg Q4W.
L1268: An in vitro study was conducted with cryopreserved human primary hepatocytes to evaluate cellular uptake of donidalorsen and the inhibition potential of donidalorsen on CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, CYP2E1, and CYP3A4. The uptake of donidalorsen into hepatocytes at 1, 10, and 50\mu\text{M} were up to 4.73\mu\text{M}, 12.3\mu\text{M}, and 43.3\mu\text{M} at 120 minutes, suggesting high cellular uptake during the 120-minute incubation period. The inhibition study results indicated that donidalorsen did not inhibit these CYP enzymes in human hepatocytes at concentrations up to 50\mu\text{M}.
L1269: An in vitro study was conducted with transporter-transfected cells (Madin-Darby Canine Kidney [MDCK-II]) compared to control cells for solute carrier family and adenosine triphosphate binding cassette transporters or BSEP vesicles made from *Spodoptera frugiperda* 9 membrane, to assess the potential of donidalorsen as an inhibitor or a substrate of major transporters. At a concentration of 100\mu\text{M}, donidalorsen is not considered as an inhibitor of human organic anion transporter (OAT) 1, OAT3, organic cation transporter (OCT) 1, OCT2, organic anion transporting polypeptide (OATP) 1B1, OATP1B3, MATE1, MATE2-K, Breast Cancer Resistance Protein (BCRP), P-glycoprotein (P-gp), and BSEP transporters. Donidalorsen is also not a substrate for OAT1, OAT3, OCT1, OCT2, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, MATE1, MATE2-K, and BSEP under the study conditions.
L1270: When assessing donidalorsen (10\mu\text{M}) as a substrate of P-gp and BCRP, the concentration of donidalorsen in all the receiver wells for apical to basolateral flux (absorption) were below lower limit of quantification (LLOQ=1\text{nM}). Some of the receiver wells for basolateral to apical flux (efflux) were below LLOQ, while some had concentrations slightly above the LLOQ ranging from 1.1 to 2.7\text{nM}. The efflux ratio in BCRP or P-gp transfected MDCK-II cells cannot be determined. The results in control cells (without BCRP or P-gp) were also similar. The potential of donidalorsen as a substrate of BCRP and P-gp is low.
L1271: ## 14.1.5. Drug-Drug Interaction Potential for Linker Related Metabolite M8 (Studies ISIS 721744-IS13, ISIS 721744-IS14, and ISIS 721744-IS15)
L1272: An in vitro study was conducted with human hepatic microsomal CYP enzymes (CYP1A2, 2B6, 2C8, 2C9, 2C19, 2D6, and CYP3A4/5) to assess the potential of major linker-related inactive metabolite M8 to act as an inhibitor of human CYP enzymes. Detectable inhibition was only observed for CYP2B6, 2C9, 2C19, and CYP3A4 (with midazolam or testosterone as probe substrates) at concentrations up to 100\mu\text{M}. In all cases, \text{IC}_{50} values were &gt;100\mu\text{M}. No shift in \text{IC}_{50} was noted when enzymes were pre-incubated with M8 in the absence or presence of NADPH.
L1273: An in vitro study was conducted in cryopreserved human hepatocytes to assess the induction potential of M8 on CYP1A2, CYP2B6, and CYP3A4 following 48 hours incubation. M8 did not induce CYP1A2, CYP2B6, or CYP3A4 mRNA at concentrations up to 100\mu\text{M} across three donors.
L1274: An in vitro study was conducted to assess M8 as an inhibitor or a substrate of human OAT1, OAT3, OCT1, OCT2, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, MATE1, MATE2-K, BCRP, P-gp, and BSEP. The assay used MDCK-II cells expressing the transporter of interest or a control vector, except for the BSEP assay, which used *Spodoptera frugiperda* 9 membrane vesicles expressing human BSEP.
L1275: M8 was not found to be a substrate for OAT1, OAT3, OCT1, OCT2, OATP1B1, MATE1, MATE2-K, BCRP, and P-gp under the study conditions. However, M8 is a substrate for OATP1B3 and BSEP with &gt;2-fold of uptake of M8 observed. As M8 is low in abundance in systemic circulation (1.3% relative to parent drug), the inhibition of BSEP or OATP1B3 is not likely to result in clinically meaningful changes in M8 systemic concentrations. However, the impact on M8 concentrations in the liver is unclear.
L1276: At an M8 concentration of 100\muM (about 300-fold higher than concentrations observed in human urine collected over 24 hours post dose [mean concentration 299nM]), 62.9% inhibition was observed for MATE1 (IC_{50} of 62.7\muM). For the remaining transporters evaluated, the mean percent inhibition ranged from 6.30% (OAT3) to 46.1% (BSEP). Therefore, M8 is not considered as an inhibitor of OAT1, OAT3, OCT1, OCT2, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, MATE2-K, BCRP, P-gp, and BSEP at 100\muM. As M8 demonstrates a low abundance in human plasma and is minorly excreted in urine (6.4% of total dose over 24 hours), the potential of M8 to inhibit MATE1 in vivo is low.

L1284: ## 14.2.1. Trial CS1
L1285: ## Trial Design
L1286: CS1 was a phase 1, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, dose-escalation trial conducted in healthy adult subjects. The objective of the trial was to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of donidalorsen following multiple doses of donidalorsen administered subcutaneously. Eight subjects (six active and two placebo) each were randomized to the following four cohorts:
L1287: - Cohort A: 20 mg SC every 4 weeks for 12 weeks (total: 4 doses)
- Cohort B: 40 mg SC every 4 weeks for 12 weeks (total: 4 doses)
- Cohort C: 60 mg SC every 4 weeks for 12 weeks (total: 4 doses)
- Cohort D: 80 mg SC every 4 weeks for 12 weeks (total: 4 doses)
L1288: SC doses were administered using a 100 mg/mL solution in a single use vial. Doses were administered on alternating sites (arm for first and third dose, and abdomen for second and fourth dose). One subject (b)(6) received the second dose in abdomen and third dose in thigh.
L1289: ## PK, PD, and ADA Sampling Time
L1290: Blood samples for assessing plasma donidalorsen concentration was collected at Day 1 (pre-first dose and 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, and 12-hour postdose), Day 2 (24-hour post-first dose), Day 3 (48-hour postdose), Day 8 (anytime), and Day 15 (anytime) as well as at Day 85 (pre-fourth dose and 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, and 12-hour postdose), and Day 86 (24-hour post-fourth dose).
L1291: Urine samples for assessing donidalorsen concentrations were collected over 24 hours after the first (Day 1) and fourth dose (Day 85).
L1292: Blood samples for assessing plasma PKK samples were collected at Screening, Day 1 (predose), Day 15, Day 29 (predose), Day 43, Day 57 (predose), Day 71, Day 85 (predose), Day 92, Day 99, Day 141, and Day 176.
L1293: Blood samples for assessing ADAs were collected at Day 1 (predose), Day 15, Day 29 (predose), Day 92, and Day 176.
L1294: ## PK Results
L1295: A total of 32 subjects were randomized and completed the trial. The mean (SD) age was 56 (9) years. The mean (SD) body weight was 80.6 (12.8) kg. The mean body weight is consistent across treatment groups.
L1296: The plasma donidalorsen concentrations were analyzed based on full-length ASO concentration, which included fully conjugated, partially conjugated (i.e., donidalorsen with 1, 2, or 3 GalNAc sugar deletions), and unconjugated donidalorsen. See Section 14.3 for details about the bioanalytical assay.
L1297: PK profiles and a summary of PK parameters following both single dose (Day 1) and multiple doses (Day 85) are shown in Figure 42 and Table 42. The plasma PK profiles were similar between Day 1 and Day 85 and minimal accumulation was observed in mean plasma C_{max} and AUC_{0-24h} following four doses of donidalorsen. A long terminal half-life was noted. However, the plasma concentration at terminal phase was 1000-fold lower than C_{max}. The effective half-life of donidalorsen in plasma, reflecting tissue distribution, is expected to be much shorter than the terminal half-life.

L1318: ## Dose Proportionality
L1319: Based on the noncompartmental analysis, the plasma exposure (Cmax or AUCtau) on Day 85 increased dose proportionally between 20 and 40 mg, more than dose proportionally between
L1320: 40 mg and 60 mg, and less than dose proportionally between 60 mg and 80 mg. Overall, the AUC_{\tau} on Day 85 was more than dose-proportional over the range of 20 to 80 mg. However, the dose proportionality for C_{\max} is inconclusive given high variability (Figure 44).

L1324: ## Metabolites in Plasma
L1325: In 2-hour postdose samples collected on Day 85, the most abundant oligonucleotide (&gt;90%) in human plasma was the intact donidalorsen (full length ASO with a THA-GalNAc cluster) (Table 43). No oligonucleotide chain shortened metabolite was identified in the plasma after 2 hours postdose, which roughly corresponds to the time of peak donidalorsen concentration.

L1337: ## Urine Excretion
L1338: Urinary excretion of total full-length ASO within 24 hours represented a small fraction (&lt;1%) of the administered dose and was dose-dependent. Urinary excretion after multiple doses was higher than after a single dose but still represents a small fraction of the administered dose (Table 44).

L1347: Note that the long-term stability at -80 °C of donidalorsen in urine samples was evaluated for up to 23 days, which may not be sufficient to support the stability of the storage duration for urine samples in this trial (urine samples were analyzed between November 19, 2018, and January 8, 2019, which was in a 60-day span). The data should be interpreted with caution. See Section 14.3 for details. Despite this, the urinary excretion results for donidalorsen were consistent with other GalNAc conjugated antisense oligonucleotide products that shared the same linker (i.e., eplontersen), which also demonstrated minimal excretion (&lt;1% of administered dose) of total full-length antisense oligonucleotide in urine over 24 hours following both single and multiple doses. Notably, in the case of eplontersen, urine sample stability was adequately supported.10

L1364: ## **Immunogenicity Results**
L1365: In total, 4 out of 26 subjects (16.7%) who received donidalorsen tested positive for ADA. Of these four subjects, two received 40 mg donidalorsen, and two received 60 mg donidalorsen. Given the small sample size, the impact of immunogenicity on pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics was inconclusive.
L1366: ## **14.2.2. Trial CS9**
L1367: ## **Trial Design**
L1368: Trial CS9 was a phase 1, single dose, single site, randomized, open-label, 2-period, 2-sequence, 2-treatment, crossover, bioequivalence trial evaluated at one dose level (donidalorsen 80 mg) in adult healthy subjects. Participants entered an up to 28-day Screening Period. Following Screening, 78 eligible participants were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to one of two treatment sequences. Subjects received donidalorsen 80 mg administered via subcutaneous injection (abdomen only) using either an AI or a single-use vial (syringe with manual injection): Sequence 1 (Treatment Period 1: AI and Treatment Period 2: vial) or Sequence 2 (Treatment Period 1: vial and Treatment Period 2: AI). Participants were administered donidalorsen 80 mg once at the beginning of each Treatment Period. Treatment Period 2 dosing began at least 28 days but no more than 42 days after Treatment Period 1 dosing.
L1369: The drug products used in this trial included a vial product that contained 100 mg/mL donidalorsen (0.8 mL per vial) and an AI that contained 100 mg/mL with a deliverable volume of 0.8 mL. The AI is the proposed to-be-marketed (TBM) product.
L1370: ## **PK, PD, and ADA Sampling Time**
L1371: PK blood samples were collected on Day 1 of each Treatment Period at predose (0 hour) and 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48, 72, 96, 168, and 336 hour postdose. Samples were also collected in the Post-Treatment Follow-Up Period at Day 28, 56, and 91/early termination following last dose of trial drug administration (Treatment Period 2).
L1372: PD blood samples were collected within 1 hour prior to dosing on Day 1 during both Treatment Period 1 and 2. In addition, blood samples were collected on Day 4, Day 8, and Day 15 for Treatment Period 1.
L1373: ADA samples were not collected.
L1374: ## **PK Results**
L1375: A total of 78 subjects were randomized and dosed in the trial. Among them, 76 subjects completed the trial and two subjects (ID: (b) (6) and (b) (6)) discontinued the treatment early due to ineligibility. The mean (SD) baseline body weight for randomized subjects was 77.6 (12.9) kg and mean (SD) age was 43.1 (12.6) years. The mean body weight is consistent across treatment groups. The mean plasma concentration time profile by formulation and bioequivalence analysis are shown Figure 47 and Table 46, respectively. Administration of donidalorsen via AI yielded comparable C_{max} and AUC_{0-336h} as compared with the vial product. For both parameters, the geometric mean ratio point estimates and 90% confidence intervals were contained within the 80% to 125% range.

L1404: ## **PD Results**
L1405: Box plots for PKK plasma concentrations and percent change from baseline in PKK concentrations are shown in **Figure 49** and **Figure 50**, respectively. As a continuous decline in PKK concentrations was observed up to Treatment Period 2 (i.e., at least 28 days apart from Treatment Period 1), it is reasonable to only assess postdose pharmacodynamics in Treatment Period 1. The range of PKK concentrations and percent change from baseline in PKK concentrations were similar between the two drug products.

L1423: ## **14.2.3. Trial CS2**
L1424: ## **Trial Design**
L1425: Trial CS2 was conducted in two parts concurrently with different designs. Part A was randomized, double-blind, and placebo-controlled while Part B was open-label. Subjects were allocated into Part A and B according to type of HAE (HAE Type I or II in Part A and HAE Type III in Part B). In Part A, 20 subjects were randomized 2:1 to receive SC injection of donidalorsen 80 mg or placebo every 4 weeks (weeks 1, 5, 9, and 13). In Part B, three subjects were administered open-label SC injections of donidalorsen-4 and completed the trial. The treatment duration was 12 weeks. After completing the Treatment Period, subjects had the option of enrolling in open-label extension Trial CS3 (refer to Section 14.2.5).
L1426: ## **PK, PD, and ADA Sampling Time**
L1427: PK samples were collected at predose, and 1, 2, 4, and 6 hours postdose on Day 1 and Day 85 in the PK subgroup. For all subjects, predose samples were collected on Day 29, 57, and anytime on Day 15, and during the Post-Treatment Period (Days 113, 141, and 176).
L1428: PD samples were collected at predose on Days 1, 29, 57, 85, and anytime on Day 15 and during the Post-Treatment Period (Days 113, 141, and 176).
L1429: Immunogenicity samples were collected at predose on Days 1, 29, and 57 and anytime on Day 15 and during the Post-Treatment Period (Day 113 and Day 176).
L1430: ## PK Results
L1431: A total of 20 subjects with HAE Type I or II (6 in placebo and 14 in donidalorsen) were randomized in Part A, while 3 subjects with HAE Type III received donidalorsen in Part B. The mean age was and 38.5 (13.9) and 34 (7.9) years for Parts A and B, respectively. The mean (SD) body weight was 83.4 (18.4) and 95.7 (8.2) kg for Parts A and B, respectively.
L1432: In a small PK subgroup from Part A (N=4) who had more intensive samples collected postdose on Day 1 and Day 85, the PK parameters are summarized in Table 50.

L1438: Similar to results observed in CS1, there was no accumulation following administration of multiple doses and the median Tmax was observed at around 1 hour postdose. However, the Cmax in Trial CS2 on Days 1 and 85 was 2- to 3-fold lower compared to that in Trial CS1 following administration of the same dosing regimen (i.e., donidalorsen-4; Cmax values of 0.592 µg/mL and 0.718 µg/mL on Days 1 and 85, respectively). The Applicant attributed the cross-trial difference in part to different median body weights across the two trials (91 kg for PK subgroup in Trial CS2 versus 75 kg in Trial CS1). However, a definitive conclusion cannot be drawn due to small sample size (N=4) and less intensive postdose sampling in Trial CS2.
L1439: No subjects from Part B had intensive PK samples collected. The range of trough concentrations between Part A and Part B was similar during the Treatment Period, as shown in Figure 51. However, the limited sample size from Part B limits interpretation of the data.

L1455: ## **Immunogenicity Results**
L1456: In subjects treated with donidalorsen (Part A and B), the proportion of the ADA-positive patient rate was 52.9% (9 out of 17 subjects). This included three subjects (17.6%) with pre-existing antibodies (ADA titers for these subjects did not increase more than 4-fold from baseline after treatment) and six subjects (35.3%, including two subjects with HAE Type III) with treatment-emergent ADA. The overall median onset of the ADA response in subjects who tested positive for ADA was Day 15 with a range of 1 to 118 days.
L1457: The plasma PKK trough concentrations over time by overall immunogenicity irrespective of baseline ADA titers is shown in Table 52. At Week 17, subjects with positive ADA had lower percent reduction from baseline.

L1467: Both subjects with HAE Type I or II (Part A, N=14) and subjects with HAE Type III (Part B, N=3) who received donidalorsen were included in this assessment of the impact of ADAs on HAE attack rate. As noted above, two subjects with HAE Type III were ADA-positive. Of note, regardless of ADA status, the mean every-4-week attack rates during the Run-In Period (4.32) and the Week-1-to-Week-17 period (1.52) were higher in the three subjects with HAE Type III compared to those in subjects with HAE Type I or II treated with the same dosing regimen of donidalorsen (Run-In Period: 2.82 and Week-1-to-Week-17 period: 0.23). Thus, the assessment of ADA impact on efficacy may be confounded by different responses to donidalorsen treatment among patients with different types of HAE.
L1468: ## 14.2.4. Trial CS5
L1469: ## Trial Design
L1470: For full details on the design of Trial CS5, refer to Section 6.
L1471: A vial presentation (100 mg/mL of donidalorsen, 0.8 mL per vial) was used for administration of donidalorsen in Trial CS5. Alternate injection administration sites (arm, abdomen, and thigh) were used for some subjects during the Treatment Period.
L1472: ## PK, PD, and ADA Sampling Time
L1473: Samples for assessing plasma donidalorsen concentrations were collected at predose and 2 hours postdose on Day 1 (Week 1) and Day 141 (Week 21) for the donidalorsen-4 group or Day 113 (Week 17) for the donidalorsen-8 group. Additional samples were collected at predose on Days 29, 57, 85, and 113 (i.e., Week 5, 9, 13, 17) as well as up to 13 weeks post-last dose.
L1474: Samples for assessing plasma PKK samples were collected predose at Days 1, 29, 57, 85, 113, 141, and 169 (i.e., Week 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21, and 25) as well as up to 13 weeks post-last dose.
L1475: ADA samples were collected at Days 1, 29, 85, 141, and 169 (i.e., Week 1, 5, 13, 21, and 25) as well as 4 and 13 weeks post last dose.
L1476: ## PK Results
L1477: The 2-hour postdose donidalorsen concentrations were similar between donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 groups on both Day 1 (Week 1) and Day 141 (Week 21) or Day 113 (Week 17), as reported in Table 54. The geometric mean trough concentrations on Day 113 (Week 17) were around 2-fold higher in the donidalorsen-4 group than in the donidalorsen-8 group, although high PK variability was noted.

L1504: ## **Immunogenicity Results**
L1505: In the donidalorsen-4 group, 12 (26.7%) subjects were positive for ADA, 4 of whom were positive at baseline. In the donidalorsen-8 group, seven (30.4%) subjects were positive for ADA, two of whom (8.7%) were positive at baseline. In total, nine (20%) and five (21.7%) subjects had treatment-emergent ADAs in the donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 groups, respectively. Of note, subjects with treatment-emergent ADAs included subjects who were ADA-negative at baseline and developed ADAs during the Treatment Period as well as subjects who were ADA-positive at baseline and ADA titers increased during the Treatment Period.
L1506: In subjects who developed treatment-emergent ADAs against donidalorsen, the median time to onset of ADA was longer in the donidalorsen-4 group than in the donidalorsen-8 group (147.0 days versus 88.0 days, respectively). However, the median time to reach peak titer was similar in the donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 groups (147.0 days and 141.0 days, respectively).

L1515: Around 2-fold higher mean C_{max,ss} (collected 2-hours postdose at Week 21 for donidalorsen-4 and Week 17 for donidalorsen-8) was noted in ADA-negative subjects compared to subjects with treatment-emergent ADAs in the donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 groups. However, the median C_{max,ss} values were similar across ADA groups. The greater mean values in the negative ADA subgroup are likely driven by greater maximum values (2190 ng/mL in donidalorsen-4 and 2290 ng/mL in donidalorsen-8) that skew the mean upwards.
L1516: In the donidalorsen-4 group, subjects with treatment-emergent ADAs appear to have 5-fold higher mean C_{trough,ss} as compared to ADA-negative subjects, while the mean C_{trough,ss} was similar across ADA groups in the donidalorsen-8 group. The difference in C_{trough,ss} by ADA status in the donidalorsen-4 group was driven by one extreme value from Subject (b) (6) in the ADA-positive subgroup who presented with a C_{trough,ss} at Week 17 of 37.6 ng/mL. Of note, this subject also presented with the highest ADA titer value at Week 21 (3200) among all ADA-positive subjects.
L1517: The relationship between donidalorsen plasma C_{trough} and ADA titer was further explored. The plasma C_{trough} values for donidalorsen versus ADA titer values obtained at Week 21 for each individual with treatment-emergent ADAs in the donidalorsen-4 group were plotted in Figure 57. The positive relationship between plasma C_{trough} and ADA titers appears to be driven by one subject (Subject (b) (6)), as hypothesized above. Meanwhile another subject with higher ADA titers (i.e., 1600) had similar C_{trough} compared to that in other subjects with low ADA titers (\le 200). However, the small sample size of ADA-positive subjects precludes making a definitive conclusion on the impact of ADA titers on donidalorsen C_{trough}.

There was thus no strong temporal association between high ADA titers and injection site reactions. ADAs were not found to impact safety. However, given the limited sample size of subjects with treatment-emergent ADAs, a definitive conclusion cannot be drawn.
L1546: ## 14.2.5. Trial CS3
L1547: ## Trial Design
L1548: Trial CS3 is an ongoing OLE trial of phase 2 double-blind Trial CS2 (referred to as the Index Trial) to evaluate the long-term safety, efficacy, and alternative dosing of donidalorsen. Subjects from Trial CS2 were enrolled into Trial CS3 if they successfully completed qualification procedures and in the opinion of the investigator, the subject would benefit from continued treatment.
L1549: The trial consisted of four periods including the Qualification Period, a Treatment Period, an Extended Treatment Period, and a Post-Treatment Period. The Treatment Period was composed of a Fixed Dosing Period and a Flexible Dosing Period during which the donidalorsen dosage for each subject could be changed.
L1550: All eligible subjects were to receive donidalorsen-4 from Week 1 to Week 13 (Fixed Dosing Period). Following completion of the first 12-week period, subjects (based on the Investigator and Sponsor Medical Monitor recommendation) had three different dosing options starting at Week 17 (Flexible Dosing Period):
L1551: - Subjects could continue receiving donidalorsen-4.
- For subjects who were attack free for \ge 12 weeks after entering this OLE Trial (the Fixed Dosing Period), the investigator could initiate a dose at a reduced frequency of donidalorsen-8. The reduced frequency dosing could begin at any trial visit starting at or after Week 17. If a subject's disease was not adequately controlled on donidalorsen-8, then dosing could return to donidalorsen-4.
- For subjects who were not attack free for \ge 12 weeks after entering this OLE Trial (the Fixed Dosing Period), the investigator could initiate a higher dose of donidalorsen at 100 mg every 4 weeks. The higher dose could begin at any trial visit starting at or after Week 17. If subjects developed any tolerability or safety issue during treatment, the dose could be reduced back to donidalorsen-4.
L1552: At the end of the 52-week Treatment Period (Fixed Dosing + Flexible Dosing), subjects had the option of receiving donidalorsen in an Extended Treatment Period (during which flexible dosing was maintained) for up to an additional 156 weeks (approximately 3 years) for a Total Treatment Period (Treatment + Extended Treatment) of up to approximately 209 weeks (approximately 4 years), or enter the 12-week Post-Treatment Period.
L1553: ## **PK, PD, and ADA Sampling Time**
L1554: PK, PD, and ADA blood samples were collected at predose at Weeks 1, 5, 9, and 13 in the Fixed Dosing Period, and at predose at Weeks 21, 29, 37, 45, and 53 in the Flexible Dosing Period, and anytime in the Post-Treatment Period (Week 65).
L1555: In the Extended Treatment Period Year 2, PK, PD, and ADA blood samples were collected at predose at Weeks 65, 77, 89, 105, and anytime in the Post-Treatment Period (Week 113).
L1556: In the Extended Treatment Period Year 3, PK, PD, and ADA blood samples were collected at predose at Weeks 117, 129, 141, 157, and anytime in the Post-Treatment Period (at Week 169).
L1557: ## **PK Results**
L1558: In this OLE trial, 20 subjects were enrolled from Index Trial CS2 and received the trial drug, including 17 subjects with HAE Type I/II (12 from Index Q4W and 5 from Index placebo) and 3 subjects with HAE Type III. This interim CSR describes data collected as of the data cutoff date of February 26, 2024. At the time of data cutoff, 15 subjects completed \ge 2 years of trial drug, and 14 subjects completed \ge 3 years of trial drug. During the Flexible Dosing Period, eight subjects with HAE Type I or II changed dosing frequency from donidalorsen-4 during the Fixed Dosing Period to donidalorsen-8. However, three subjects (b) (6) returned to a donidalorsen-4 dosing frequency due to experiencing an HAE attack. The remaining five subjects remained on a donidalorsen-8 dosing frequency.
L1559: The mean plasma trough concentration over time during the Fixed Dosing Period (Week 1 to Week 13 of Trial CS3) is shown in Figure 59. In the Index Placebo group (i.e., did not receive donidalorsen until Trial CS3), the trough concentrations reached steady state by Day 57 (Week 9) following administration of donidalorsen-4. In the Index Q4W group (for both HAE Type I/II and Type III), trough concentrations were relatively stable from the beginning of the Fixed Dosing Period, indicating no significant accumulation of donidalorsen in plasma over time.

L1579: ## **Immunogenicity Results**
L1580: The ADA incidence rate was 70.6% (12 out of 17 subjects) in the overall HAE Type I/II group (4 from Index Placebo and 8 from Index Q4W), out of which 11 subjects (64.7%) had treatment-emergent ADAs, and 1 subject (5.9%) had treatment-unaffected ADAs (pre-existing ADAs that were not boosted following drug administration). Among subjects with HAE Type III, the incidence rate of treatment-emergent ADAs was 100% (three out of three subjects). ADA-positive subjects who rolled over from Trial CS2 remained ADA-positive in Trial CS3.
L1581: ## 14.2.6. Trial CS7
L1582: ## Trial Design
L1583: Trial CS7 is an ongoing open-label trial to evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of donidalorsen in subjects with Type I and II HAE. Two treatment arms were evaluated:
L1584: - OLE subjects who rolled over from Trial CS5 (referred to as the Index Trial).
- Donidalorsen-naïve subjects who were previously maintained on other HAE prophylactic therapies (i.e., lanadelumab, berotralstat, or a C1-esterase inhibitor).
L1585: The trial consists of four periods, including a Qualification Period for OLE subjects (Week -4 to -1) or a Screening Period for new subjects who switched from other HAE prophylactic therapies (Week -10 to -1), a Treatment Period (Week 1 to 53), an Extended Treatment Period (Week 54 to 157), and a Post-Treatment Period (end of treatment +13 weeks).
L1586: For OLE subjects who rolled over from Index Trial CS5 (OLE subjects), subjects who were previously treated with donidalorsen-4 or placebo Q4W in Trial CS5 received donidalorsen-4 beginning 28\pm 3 days after the last dose received in Trial CS5. Subjects who were previously treated with donidalorsen-8 in Trial CS5 received donidalorsen-8 in Trial CS7 beginning 56\pm 3 days after last dose in Trial CS5, unless they were not attack free for \ge 8 weeks (Week 17 to 25 of Trial CS5), in which case they received donidalorsen-4. If subjects participated in the Extended Treatment Period (Week 54 to Week 157), they could change dosing frequency (from donidalorsen-8 to donidalorsen-4 or from donidalorsen-4 to donidalorsen-8), as determined by clinical symptoms (per investigator).
L1587: For donidalorsen-naïve subjects who switched from other HAE prophylactic treatments (Switch Subjects), subjects were treated with donidalorsen-4 during the Treatment Period and had the option to change dose frequency based on clinical symptoms (per investigator). Switch Subjects had to be on a stable dose of prophylaxis treatment with lanadelumab, berotralstat, or a C1-esterase inhibitor for at least 12 weeks prior to the Screening Period and were to continue taking their HAE prophylactic treatment during the Screening Period. The schedule to switch from other prophylactic treatments to donidalorsen is as follows:
L1588: - Lanadelumab: Subject was to take last dose of lanadelumab 14 \text{ days} \pm 3 \text{ days} prior to Day 1.
- Berotralstat: Subject was to continue taking a stable dose of berotralstat for 14 \text{ days} \pm 3 \text{ days} after Day 1.
- C1-esterase inhibitor: Subject was to continue taking a stable dose of C1-esterase inhibitor for 14 \text{ days} \pm 3 \text{ days} after Day 1.
L1589: ## PK, PD, ADA Sampling Time
L1590: ## OLE Subjects
L1591: Plasma samples for assessing pharmacokinetics (donidalorsen plasma concentrations), pharmacodynamics (plasma PKK concentrations) and ADA were collected at predose on
L1592: Weeks 1, 9, 25, 37, 49, and 53 in the Treatment Period, predose on Weeks 65, 77, 89, and 105 in the Extended Treatment Period, and in the Post-Treatment Period up to 13 weeks after the last dose.
L1593: ## Switch Subjects
L1594: Plasma samples for assessing pharmacokinetics (donidalorsen plasma concentrations), pharmacodynamics (plasma PKK concentrations) and ADA were collected at predose on Weeks 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 25, 37, 49, and 53 in the Treatment Period, predose on Weeks 65, 77, 89, and 105 in the Extended Treatment Period, and in the Post-Treatment Period up to 13 weeks after the last dose.

As of the cutoff date, the majority of OLE subjects did not complete the 52-week Treatment Period with a current median exposure duration of 227 days.

L1638: In terms of safety associated with ADA status, Subject [REDACTED](b)(6) was reported to have experienced an anaphylactic reaction during Trial CS7 after the NDA data cutoff. This subject presented with high ADA titers (i.e., &gt;1000) beginning at Week 21 in Trial CS5. ADAs remained elevated during Trial CS7 (based on the adis.xpt datasets for Trial CS5 and Trial CS7). This subject was randomized in Trial CS5 on [REDACTED](b)(6), and the anaphylaxis event was reported on [REDACTED](b)(6), following approximately 3 years of treatment with donidalorsen. Of note, this subject also experienced other hypersensitivity reactions (rash, urticaria etc.) prior to the anaphylaxis event. For additional details, refer to Section 7.6.
L1639: To evaluate the potential association between ADAs and hypersensitivity reactions, the onset of hypersensitivity reactions from all subjects with high ADA titers (&gt;1000) at any time during Trial CS5 or Trial CS7 were compared with the timing of dosing, the most adjacent ADA titer, and donidalorsen plasma Ctrough. The Applicant identified 35 subjects who were treated with donidalorsen and had an ADA titer &gt;1000 during any time in Trial CS5 or Trial CS7, including data collected after the NDA data cutoff. Nine subjects were identified as having hypersensitivity reactions derived from the OCMQ of Hypersensitivity. Of these nine subjects, three ([REDACTED](b)(6)) had hypersensitivity reactions that occurred when ADA titer and donidalorsen plasma Ctrough were high. The remaining subjects experienced hypersensitivity reactions when they were either ADA-negative or presented with low ADA titers. Thus, there is no clear association between high ADA titers and hypersensitivity.

L1658: ## 14.3.1. OSIS Inspection Results
L1659: The Office of Study Integrity and Surveillance (OSIS) inspection was requested for both analytical (b) (4) and clinical sites (Medpace Inc. Cincinnati, OH) for clinical Trial CS9, which provides pivotal evidence to support the use of the proposed AI presentation. The OSIS conducted a Remote Regulatory Assessment for the analytical site in (b) (4), for other NDA (b) (4) and a clinical inspection for the clinical site in September 2024 for another NDA (218614). L1660: ## 14.3.2. Bioanalytical Methods For Donidalorsen in Plasma and Urine
L1661: ## 14.3.2.1. Donidalorsen Concentration in Plasma
L1662: The bioanalytical method for analyzing donidalorsen concentrations in plasma are acceptable.
L1663: Donidalorsen concentrations in human plasma were determined using a hybridization (ECL) method developed by (b) (4) (Method Validation Report: 721744-MV04). The same bioanalytical method was used in support of Trials CS1, CS2, CS3, CS5, CS7, and CS9. This method assessed the total concentration of full-length ASO including fully conjugated, partially conjugated (i.e., donidalorsen with 1, 2, or 3 GalNAc sugar deletions),
L1664: and unconjugated donidalorsen. The reported assay range is 0.02nM to 10nM (i.e., 0.1735 ng/mL to 86.73 ng/mL). The dilution factors of 400- to 10,000-fold were evaluated during method validation and met acceptance criteria. No apparent hook effect was observed up to 5000nM. The method is deemed adequate to detect the full range of donidalorsen concentrations in clinical trials. The assay in-study performance was acceptable for all trials.
L1665: The bioanalytical method is summarized in Table 67.

L1670: The cross-reactivity of the assay was assessed with three putative metabolites ISIS 834440, ISIS 834441, and ISIS 834443, which are 19-mer, 10-mer, and 5-mer metabolites of unconjugated donidalorsen. There was a 105% cross-reactivity with ISIS 834440 (19-mer metabolite of unconjugated donidalorsen), while there was only &lt;0.267% cross-reactivity with both ISIS 834441 (10-mer metabolite) and ISIS 834443 (5-mer metabolite). The cross-reactivity potential with 19-mer metabolites may affect the assessment of systemic exposure of full length donidalorsen. However, 19-mer metabolite was not present either in the plasma collected at 2 hours postdose based on Trial CS01-BA04 or in pooled human urine collected over 24 hours after fourth monthly dose of donidalorsen based on Trial 721744-IS10. Although cross-reactivity with other chain-shortened metabolites from 18-mer to 11-mer were not assessed, 11-mer to 18-mer metabolites were not found in the plasma collected at 2 hours postdose based on Trial CS01-BA04. The data suggest that interference due to the presence of these chain shortened metabolites is not likely.
L1671: This method was designed to evaluate the total concentrations of full-length ASO, which includes fully conjugated, partially conjugated (i.e., donidalorsen with 1, 2, or 3 GalNAc sugar deletions), and unconjugated donidalorsen in plasma. However, the calibration standard was prepared with fully conjugated donidalorsen (ISIS 721744). The ability of the method to quantify unconjugated donidalorsen (ISIS 780124) was assessed by quantitating low (0.06nM) and high
L1672: (7.5nM) QC levels of ISIS 780124 using a fully conjugated donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) standard curve. In addition, to evaluate the ability of the assay to quantitate both full-length ASOs (ISIS 780124 and ISIS 721744) when both are present, low- and high-level QCs of ISIS 780124 and ISIS 721744 were prepared and combined 1:1 to reach both low and high QC levels (0.06nM and 7.5nM, respectively). QC results met the acceptance criteria and demonstrated that the assay is capable of quantifying both total-full length conjugated donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) and unconjugated donidalorsen (ISIS 780124). Based on the principle of the assay (sample is hybridized to a complement capture probe) and results with ISIS 780124 QC samples, the assay is capable of quantifying total full-length ASO regardless of GalNAc conjugation status.
L1673: ## 14.3.2.2. Donidalorsen Concentration In Urine
L1674: There is insufficient information to determine whether the bioanalytical method is acceptable to measure donidalorsen concentrations in urine.
L1675: The bioanalytical method for analyzing donidalorsen concentrations in urine was partially validated at (b) (4) (Method Validation Report: 721744-MV05). The method was used to analyze urine samples from Trial CS1. The detection range was 0.15nM (1.301 ng/mL) to 20nM (173.5 ng/mL). The dilution linearity was assessed between 200-fold and 4000-fold and met acceptance criteria. No apparent hook effect was observed at concentrations up to 53040nM. The bioanalytical method is sufficient to detect the range of donidalorsen urine concentrations in Trial CS1. The summary of bioanalytical method is summarized in Table 68.

L1682: ## 14.3.3. Bioanalytical Method for PKK In Plasma
L1683: The bioanalytical method for analyzing PKK concentrations in human plasma is acceptable.
L1684: Two bioanalytical methods were used in the donidalorsen clinical program. The first method, developed by [REDACTED](b)(4), was used to support Trials CS1 and CS2. The other method, developed by [REDACTED](b)(4), was used to support Trials CS3, CS5, CS7, and CS9. The method is deemed adequate to detect the full range of donidalorsen concentrations in clinical trials. The assay in-study performance was acceptable for all trials.
L1685: The method developed by [REDACTED](b)(4) (Method Validation Report: PKK-BRV02) utilized commercial Prekallikrein and Kallikrein Human ELISA Kit (Abcam, No. ab171015), which was validated and optimized by [REDACTED](b)(4). The detection range is 7.52 to 2560 µg/mL. The minimum required dilution (MRD) of 1:4000 and a maximum allowed dilution (MAD) of 1:32000 were evaluated.
L1686: The method developed by [REDACTED](b)(4) (Method Validation Report: PKK-BRV01) also utilized Human Prekallikrein (Abcam) and was validated and optimized by [REDACTED](b)(4). The detection range was 0.47 ng/mL to 60 ng/mL. The 1:8000 minimum required dilution (MRD) was chosen to ensure all samples were quantified in range. After implementing the MRD, the detection range was 3.76 µg/mL to 480 µg/mL. The detection range after implementing the MRD is sufficient to assess plasma PKK concentrations in clinical samples.

L1693: No cross validation was performed between the two bioanalytical methods and two analytical sites. However, based on PD results obtained from Trial CS2 (assessed by (b) (4)) and Trial CS5 (assessed by (b) (4)) in adult subjects with HAE who received the same dosing regimen (donidalorsen-4), a similar nadir in the percent reduction of plasma PKK trough concentration from baseline was demonstrated (about 61% at Week 17 for Trial CS2 and about 74% at Week 25 for Trial CS5), suggesting that these two methods are comparable.
L1694: The plasma PKK sample long-term stability was evaluated for up to 613 days (18 months) at -80°C. During the assessment of long-term stability at around 1 year (Day 317), results showed a negative bias of 26% to 56% at both low (1.13 ng/mL and 1.55 ng/mL) and middle level (6.72 ng/mL and 8.66 ng/mL) concentrations until a correction factor was applied to the theoretical values. The correction factor was used to justify the difference in antibody concentrations among different commercial kit lots. The difference among different commercial lots was first discovered during the analysis of samples from Trial CS5, when endogenous quality control concentrations obtained from new kit lots demonstrated consistently lower PKK concentrations compared to historical data. A correction factor was therefore used to correct the new sample concentrations using the new kits lot and resulted in consistent values within \pm 20\% of reference results obtained using the qualified kit lots, as shown in Figure 64.

L1698: As the new assay kits consistently result in lower PKK concentrations compared to the previously qualified kit for the same samples, the stability assessment based on a comparison to corrected theoretical values is acceptable. After applying the correction factor, 3 out of 4 QC levels were within the acceptance range in the long-term stability assessment at Day 371 (1.13 ng/mL, 1.55 ng/mL and 8.66 ng/mL), supporting the long-term stability for around 1 year. The long-term stability was further assessed at 18 months. Three out of four QC levels were within the acceptable range (0.67 ng/mL, 0.92 ng/mL and 5.14 ng/mL). Overall, sample stability was demonstrated for up to 18 months. The established long-term stability is sufficient to support the stability of trial samples in Trials CS5 and CS9.
L1699: ## 14.4. Immunogenicity Assessment—Impact of PK/PD, Efficacy, and Safety
L1700: Immunogenicity of donidalorsen was evaluated in a phase 1 trial (CS1) in healthy subjects as well as in four trials in subjects with HAE (CS2, CS3, CS5, and CS7). Refer to the immunogenicity assay review by the Office of Pharmaceutical Quality Research for details regarding the immunogenicity assay validation (DARRTS reference ID: 5643653). The ADA assay is generally acceptable, and data is interpretable.
L1701: Treatment-emergent ADAs were assessed. The definition of treatment-emergent ADAs included both treatment-induced ADAs, defined as ADAs developed de novo following drug administration in a subject without pre-existing ADAs; and treatment-boosted ADAs, defined as pre-existing ADAs that were boosted to a higher-level following drug administration (i.e., any time after the initial drug administration the ADA titer is greater than baseline titer by a factor of 8-fold or more).
L1702: The incidence rate of treatment-emergent ADAs was 16.7% following administration of donidalorsen 20 to 80 mg once every 4 weeks for 12 weeks in healthy participants (Trial CS1, dose-dependence not observed), 35.3% following donidalorsen 80 mg once every 4 weeks for 12 weeks in subjects with HAE (Trial CS2), and 20% to 22% following donidalorsen 80 mg once every 4 weeks or every 8 weeks for 24 weeks in subjects with HAE (Trial CS5), respectively. The incidence rate of treatment-emergent ADAs was generally consistent across populations and similar between the donidalorsen-4 and donidalorsen-8 regimens. Treatment-emergent ADAs were characterized with a median onset ranging from 15 days to 175 days postdose and median peak titer ranged from 25 to 800. A summary of immunogenicity incidence rates and peak titers across trials is shown in Table 70.

L1718: ## **Impact of Immunogenicity on Pharmacokinetics**
L1719: Based on results from Trial CS5 and Trial CS7, an increase in Ctrough was observed in some ADA-positive subjects who also had high ADA titers. The increase in Ctrough was noted in some Rollover subjects from Trial CS5 who continued receiving the same dosing regimen of donidalorsen-4 in Trial CS7. These subjects also experienced an increase in ADA titers during Trial CS7. There is likely an association between presence of ADA and increased Ctrough,ss, possibly due to the binding of ADAs to donidalorsen which extended its plasma half-life. See Section 14.2.6 for more details.
L1720: ## **Impact of Immunogenicity on Pharmacodynamics**
L1721: The impact of ADAs on pharmacodynamics was assessed by comparing trough PKK concentration-time profiles by ADA status. ADAs did not appear to impact the mean PD response, as shown in Figure 65.
L1722: **Figure 65. Mean (SD) PKK Percent Change From Baseline-Time Profiles by ADA Status**
L1723: lines, mean; error bar, standard deviation; circles, individual observations. Nominal time since first dose was used. Note: values below the lower limit of quantification were excluded from the plot.
L1724: Source: Figure 19, Report 721744-PPK01
L1725: Abbreviations: ADA, antidrug antibody; PKK, prekallikrein; SD, standard deviation
L1726: ## **Impact of Immunogenicity on Efficacy**
L1727: There was no apparent effect of ADAs on efficacy based on the HAE attack rate observed in Trial CS5 and Trial CS7. However, the small sample size of ADA-positive subjects precludes making a definitive conclusion. See Sections 14.2.4 and 14.2.6 for more details.
L1728: ## **Impact of Immunogenicity on Safety**
L1729: In Trial CS5, a higher proportion of ADA-positive subjects who received donidalorsen-4 reported injection site reactions, while no ADA-positive subjects from the donidalorsen-8 group reported injection site reactions. Although a higher peak ADA titer was observed among subjects in the donidalorsen-4 group compared to that in the donidalorsen-8 group, the peak titer was reported by Week 13 to Week 21, which was later than the time of the first injection site reaction reported in most subjects. There is thus no clear temporal association between high ADA titers and the onset of injection site reactions. Given the small sample size, a definitive conclusion on the impact of ADAs on safety cannot be drawn. See Section 14.2.4 for more details.
L1730: In Trial CS7, a trend of increase in Ctrough was observed in subjects with high ADA titers (&gt;1000). One subject (b) (6) who had very high ADA titers (102400) during Trial CS7 reported an anaphylaxis reaction after the date of NDA data cutoff. The association between high
L1731: ADA titers and hypersensitivity reactions was explored among subjects who experienced high ADA titers (&gt;1000) at any time during Trial CS5 or Trial CS7. As hypersensitivity reactions were also observed in most subjects who were ADA-negative or had low ADA titers at the time hypersensitivity occurred, there is no clear association between ADA titers and hypersensitivity. See Section 14.2.6 for more details.

L1741: ## 14.5.1.2. Introduction
L1742: The primary objectives of Applicant's analysis were to:
L1743: - Develop a population PK model of donidalorsen using data from healthy volunteers and patients with HAE.

L1744: ## 14.5.1.3. Model Development
L1745: ## 14.5.1.3.1. Data
L1746: ## PK Data
L1747: The PK analyses for donidalorsen were based on PK data from one phase 1 trial in healthy subjects, one bioequivalence trial, one phase 2 trial, and one phase 3 trial in patients with HAE. Brief descriptions of the trials included are presented in Table 72.
L1748: The below limit of quantification (BLQ) samples were excluded from the population PK modeling. It seems to be reasonable to exclude BLQ samples due to the low percent of BLQ samples (&lt;5%). The final NONMEM data file for donidalorsen PK model development contained 4242 donidalorsen observations from 177 subjects, including 101 healthy volunteers and 76 HAE patients.
L1749: Table 73 provides summary statistics of the baseline demographic covariates in the PK analysis dataset.
L1750: ## PD Data
L1751: The PK/PD analyses for donidalorsen were based on PK/PD data from one phase 1 trial in healthy subjects, one bioequivalence trial, one phase 2 trial, and one phase 3 trial in patients with HAE. Brief descriptions of the trials included are presented in Table 72.
L1752: The BLQ samples were excluded from the population PK/PD modeling. It seems to be reasonable to exclude BLQ samples due to the low percent of BLQ samples (&lt;5%). The final NONMEM data file for donidalorsen PK/PD model development contained 1159 donidalorsen observations from 177 subjects, including 101 healthy volunteers and 76 HAE patients.
L1753: Table 73 provides summary statistics of the baseline demographic covariates in the PK/PD analysis dataset.

L1771: ## 14.5.1.3.2. Base Model
L1772: ## PK Base Model
L1773: The population PK model was developed using a nonlinear mixed-effects modeling approach in Phoenix NLME (Version 8.4). The structural base model was initially developed using data from Trials ISIS 721744-CS1, ISIS 721744-CS2, and ISIS 721744-CS9 followed by a graphical assessment of covariates including weight, disease status, site of administration, and drug presentation on relevant PK parameters. The PK data from subjects in Trial ISIS 721744-CS5 was then included in the base model development.
L1774: Interindividual variability was modelled assuming a log-normal distribution for individual level random effects. Residual variability was described using additive error model on log-transformed data. The quality of the model fit was assessed by diagnostic plots.
L1775: ## PK/PD Base Model
L1776: Considering the mechanism of action, an indirect response model was fitted initially to describe the relationship between donidalorsen concentrations and PKK. The population PK/PD model was developed in a similar manner to the population PK model (i.e., sequentially based on available data) and covariates were considered for inclusion into the base model before including data from Trial ISIS 721744-CS5. The PD parameters were estimated using the sequential model building method.
L1777: ## 14.5.1.3.3. Covariate Analysis
L1778: For both PK and PK/PD models, covariate analysis was performed before and after including data from Trial ISIS 721744-CS5 as described under base model development. Covariates of interest were tested using a forward addition process followed by backward elimination. For forward addition and backward elimination, significance levels of 0.01 and 0.001 were utilized, respectively.
L1779: Continuous covariates were evaluated using a power function with the parameter of interest centered at the median value of the covariate in the population. Categorical covariates were parameterized using a proportional structure with the most common level of the covariate being the reference. In addition to covariates in Table 73, covariates evaluated in the development of the PK model included drug presentation and site of administration. The impact of ADA on donidalorsen pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics was explored graphically. No apparent impact of ADA on C_{max} was observed, though increased C_{trough} was observed in some ADA-positive subjects. No apparent impact of ADA on PKK concentrations was observed. PK samples at and beyond the onset of ADA were excluded from the population PK analysis dataset due to lack of correlation between antisense oligonucleotide exposure in liver and plasma.
L1780: ## 14.5.1.4. Final Model
L1781: ## 14.5.1.4.1. PK Final Model
L1782: A 2-compartment model with first-order absorption and elimination adequately described the PK data of donidalorsen (Figure 66 and Figure 67). Statistically significant covariate effects on PK model parameters were the following: body weight on CL/F, Vc/F, Q/F, and Vp/F; site of administration and drug presentation on ka; and disease status on Vc/F and Q/F. Age, sex, race, ethnicity, geographical region, mild hepatic impairment, and mild renal impairment are not significant covariates. The parameter estimates for the final PK model are listed in Table 74. The RSE for all parameters except covariate of site of administration on ka, covariate of drug presentation on ka, correlation between CL/F and ka, correlation between Q/F and ka, and correlation between Vp/F and ka was &lt;30%. All parameters had RSE &lt;41%. Moderate eta-shrinkage (&lt;25%) was observed for all parameters.
L1783: The effects of body weight, disease status, drug presentation, and site of administration on the AUCt,ss, Cmax,ss, and Ctrough,ss of donidalorsen are explored in Figure 68. Body weight was the most influential covariate on PK exposure. The effect of body weight on donidalorsen pharmacokinetics is unlikely to be clinically meaningful due to lack of exposure-response relationship for efficacy and safety. The effects of other covariates are generally small, and unlikely to be clinically meaningful.
