L1810: ## 14.5.1.4.2. PK/PD Final Model
L1811: The final PK/PD model was an indirect effect E_{max} model with inhibition on the rate of PKK production by donidalorsen. Statistically significant covariate effects on PD model parameters were disease status on baseline PKK and IC_{50}. The pooled PD data were adequately described by the final model (Figure 69 and Figure 70). The parameter estimates for the final model are listed in Table 75. The RSE for all parameters were &lt;30%. The precision of parameter estimates is reasonable. Eta-shrinkage was low to moderate for baseline (10.0%), IC_{50} (11.7%), and k_{out} (28.6%). The covariate effect of disease status on the maximum PKK percent change from baseline (nadir) over the steady-state dosing interval and PKK percent change from baseline at the PK C_{trough,ss} were within the 80% to 125% range (Figure 71).

L1838: ## 14.5.1.5. Simulations
L1839: The exposure metrics (AUC_{t,ss}, C_{max,ss}, and C_{trough,ss}) of donidalorsen and PD response following 80 mg Q4W, every month (Q1M), Q8W, or every 2 months (Q2M) were simulated based on the final population PK/PD model and distribution of demographic data in subjects from Trials ISIS 721744-CS2 and ISIS 721744-CS5. The differences in median AUC_{t,ss}, C_{max,ss}, and C_{trough,ss} of donidalorsen between the 80 mg Q4W and Q1M regimens and between the 80 mg Q8W and Q2M regimens was &lt;10% (Table 76 and Figure 72). The median PKK percent change from baseline at the PK C_{trough,ss} was similar for 80 mg Q1M compared to 80 mg Q4W (difference &lt;1%) and for 80 mg Q2M compared to 80 mg Q8W (difference &lt;2%) (Figure 73).

L1857: ## 15. Study/Trial Design
L1858: ## 15.1. Trial CS5
L1859: ## Title
L1860: A phase 3 Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of ISIS 721744 in Patients with Hereditary Angioedema.
L1861: ## Dates
L1862: January 25, 2022, to November 9, 2023; CSR completed July 18, 2024.
L1863: ## 15.1.1. Definition and Collection of HAE Attacks, Trial CS5
L1864: During the trial, subjects were instructed to report details of any HAE attack to the trial site within 72 hours of the onset of the attack. Throughout the Screening (Run-In Period), Treatment, and Post-Treatment Periods, site personnel contacted the subjects approximately weekly, as well as during trial visits, to inquire about attacks.
L1865: For each HAE attack, the following data were collected:
L1866: - Date/time of symptom onset.
- Location and description of symptoms:Peripheral angioedema: cutaneous swelling involving an extremity, face, neck, torso, and/or genitourinary region.
- Abdominal angioedema: abdominal pain, with or without abdominal distension, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.
- Laryngeal angioedema: stridor, dyspnea, difficulty speaking, difficulty swallowing, throat tightening, or swelling of the tongue, palate, uvula, or larynx.
- HAE attack severity:Mild: transient or mild discomfort.
- Moderate: mild to moderate limitation in activity, some assistance needed.
- Severe: marked limitation in activity, assistance required.
- Need for assistance, medical intervention, emergency room (ER) visit, or hospitalization.
- Medications to treat the attack.
- HAE attack course, including if the HAE attack(s) in question was a typical attack for the subject, or if there was an alternative diagnosis.
- Date/time symptoms resolved.
L1867: The presence of these symptoms, including symptoms in one or more of the above locations, was not necessarily considered an investigator-confirmed HAE attack (to be used in efficacy endpoint analyses) unless the diagnosis was confirmed by the investigator. The investigator was permitted to use clinical judgment regarding whether the symptoms represent a HAE attack or not. For example, if the reported event was accompanied by symptoms not consistent with an HAE attack (e.g., urticaria); if the reported event persisted well beyond the typical course of time for an HAE attack (e.g., greater than 7 days); or if there was a likely alternative etiology for the event (e.g., viral gastroenteritis).
L1868: An HAE attack was defined as an event with signs or symptoms consistent with an attack in at least one of the locations noted above. A discrete attack was counted if there was at least a 24-hour symptom-free period between attacks. If there was less than 24 hours between the stop
L1869: date/time of the first event and the start date/time of the next event, the events were combined and counted as one unique attack.
L1870: ## 15.1.2. Data and Safety Monitoring Committee, Trial CS5
L1871: A Data and Safety Monitoring Committee was assembled to review safety and tolerability data collected during this trial.
L1872: ## 15.1.3. Sample Size Considerations, Trial CS5
L1873: The power and sample size estimations were calculated by the Applicant using simulations based on a generalized linear model for count data assuming a Poisson distribution. The primary endpoint was the time-normalized number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) from Week 1 to Week 25. Assuming an HAE attack rate of 13.26 attacks per 6-month period in the placebo group and an HAE attack rate of 1.38 attacks per 6-month period in the donidalorsen-4 group, the sample size of 54 subjects (2:1 ratio) would provide at least 90% power for the primary endpoint, with a 0.05 significance level. A total of approximately 84 subjects (42 in the donidalorsen-4 group, 21 in the placebo group, and 21 in the donidalorsen-8 group) were planned to be enrolled in this trial to account for potential early dropouts and to facilitate some general safety evaluations.
L1874: ## 15.1.4. Protocol Amendments, Trial CS5

There were no substantial changes made for the second amendment (dated July 12, 2022). L1881: ## 15.1.5. Safety Assessments, Trial CS5
L1882: The safety and tolerability assessments included AEs, clinical laboratory parameters (chemistry, coagulation, hematology, and urinalysis), vital signs, physical examinations, and ECG testing according to the Schedule of Assessments (see Table 78). During the Treatment Period, these assessments were generally collected every 4 weeks. A centralized laboratory was used to enhance data quality.
L1883: For this trial, the adverse events of special interest were defined as platelet count &lt;50,000/\text{mm}^3 accompanied by a major bleeding event or clinically relevant non-major bleeding event, or platelet count &lt;25,000/\text{mm}^3, independent of a major bleeding or clinically relevant non-major bleeding event.
L1884: Overall, the safety assessments in Trial CS5 were adequate to inform the safety profile of donidalorsen for the proposed use.

L1914: ## 15.2.1. Trial Design, Trial CS7
L1915: Trial CS7 is an ongoing phase 3b, open-label trial evaluating the long-term safety and efficacy of donidalorsen in subjects with Types I and II HAE. The trial enrolled rollover (referred to in this
L1916: review as Rollover, and by the Applicant as OLE) subjects, who completed Trial CS5 (Index Trial), as well as donidalorsen-naïve (referred to in this review as Naïve, and by the Applicant as Switch) subjects. For additional details regarding the Qualification/Screening Period of Trial CS7, see below. The first subject received a dose of trial treatment on August 11, 2022, and the data cutoff date was February 28, 2024, providing approximately 18 months of data as of the cutoff. The trial schematic is shown in Figure 74.
L1917: Figure 74. Trial Design, Trial CS7
L1918: Source: ISIS 721744-CS7 Clinical Protocol (Appendix 16.1.1)
L1919: Terminology: Open-label Extension patients are also referred to as Rollover patients. Switch patients are also referred to as Naïve patients.
L1920: Abbreviations: ET, early termination; Q4W, every 4 weeks; Q8W, every 8 weeks
L1921: The trial was comprised of four periods, including a Qualification Period for Rollover subjects (Weeks -4 to -1) or a Screening Period for Naïve subjects (Weeks -10 to -1), a Treatment Period (Weeks 1 to 53) for all subjects (Rollover and Naïve), an Extended Treatment Period
L1922: (Weeks 54 to 157), and a Post-Treatment Period (end of treatment +13 weeks). Treatment was administered from a vial or AI. Self-administration or caregiver administration was allowed after dosing instructions and training.
L1923: In the Treatment Period (Weeks 1 to 53), Rollover subjects who rolled over from Trial CS5 were treated as follows:
L1924: - Subjects treated with donidalorsen 80 mg or placebo once every 4 weeks in the Index Trial (Index Trial Cohort A) received the donidalorsen-4 regimen beginning 28\pm 3 days after the last dose in the Index Trial.
- Subjects treated with donidalorsen 80 mg or placebo once every 8 weeks in the Index Trial (Index Trial Cohort B) were to receive the donidalorsen-8 regimen beginning 56\pm 3 days after the last dose in the Index Trial unless they were not attack-free for \ge 8 weeks (Weeks 17 to 25 during the Index Trial), in which case they were to receive the donidalorsen-4 regimen.
L1925: Naïve subjects were to be treated with donidalorsen-4 for the Treatment Period (Weeks 1 to 53).
L1926: Following the Week 53 visit, subjects were to receive donidalorsen for up to an additional 104 weeks in the Extended Treatment Period. In this Extended Treatment Period, subjects (whether Rollover or Naïve) could either continue to receive donidalorsen 80 mg per the dosing schedule prior to Week 53 (every 4 or 8 weeks) or, as determined by clinical symptoms (per investigator), change dose frequency from donidalorsen-4 to donidalorsen-8 or donidalorsen-8 to donidalorsen-4. Change in dose frequency could occur at any time during the Extended Treatment Period. In analyses, the On-Treatment Period includes both the 52-week Treatment Period and the 104-week Extended Treatment Period (i.e., the entire duration of drug administration during Trial CS7). The Integrated Treatment Period (for Rollover subjects only) is the period during which donidalorsen was administered in the Index Trial (CS5).
L1927: Rollover subjects who met the Trial CS7 eligibility criteria and expressed interest in enrollment in Trial CS7 were considered to be in the Qualification Period of Trial CS7 during their final 4 weeks of treatment in Trial CS5. Thus, Rollover subjects who were being treated with donidalorsen during Trial CS5 could continue their treatment (in Trial CS7) without interruption.
L1928: Naïve subjects began with a Screening Period to confirm eligibility up to 70 days prior to administration of donidalorsen. Naïve subjects had to be on a stable dose of prophylaxis treatment with lanadelumab, berotralstat, or a C1-esterase inhibitor for at least 12 weeks prior to Screening and were to continue to take their HAE prophylactic therapy during the Screening Period, and the timing of the switch to donidalorsen was based on the half-life of the individual therapy. No drug-drug interaction with donidalorsen and the prior therapies were anticipated. The schedule for Naïve subjects to take their final dose of the prior HAE prophylactic therapy is summarized in Table 81.
L1929: **Table 81. Schedule for Naïve Subjects to Switch Prophylactic Therapy to Donidalorsen Treatment, Trial CS7**
L1930: Prophylactic Therapy	Schedule
Lanadelumab	Subject was to take the last dose of lanadelumab 14 days \pm3 days prior to Day 1
Berotrastat	Subject was to continue taking a stable dose of berotrastat for 14 days \pm3 days after Day 1
Cl-esterase inhibitor	Subject was to continue taking a stable dose of Cl-esterase inhibitor for 14 days \pm3 days after Day 1
L1931: Source: CS7 clinical study report
L1932: ## 15.2.1.1. Sample Size Assumptions, Trial CS7
L1933: This was an uncontrolled, open-label trial not designed for statistical testing of a hypothesis, but rather for long-term observation of safety and efficacy. The sample size for Trial CS7 was based on the number of subjects enrolled in Trial CS5 and their eligibility to enroll in the open-label extension trial. Eighty-three out of the 90 subjects in Trial CS5 enrolled as Rollover subjects in Trial CS7. For Naïve subjects, sample size was selected based on clinical assessment. A total of 65 Naïve subjects enrolled in Trial CS7.
L1934: ## 15.2.2. Schedule of Assessments, Trial CS7
L1935: In the Treatment Period through Week 53, trial visits, physical examinations, laboratory monitoring, and AE monitoring occurred per the schedules shown in Table 82 and Table 83. Routine clinical testing, including vital signs and coagulation studies, was generally performed every 3 months, while certain tests were performed monthly: hematology, serum chemistry with hepatic function tests, and pregnancy testing. In the Extended Treatment Period, only pregnancy testing occurred monthly, with the other laboratory tests and vital signs evaluated every 3 months (Table 84). The schedules of assessments are acceptable for a phase 3b, open-label extension trial.

L2001: ## 15.2.3. Primary, Secondary, and Exploratory Objectives and Endpoints, Trial CS7
L2002: The primary objective of this trial was to evaluate the long-term safety of donidalorsen as prophylaxis in patients with HAE. The primary endpoint was the incidence and severity of TEAEs.
L2003: The secondary objectives of this trial were to evaluate the long-term efficacy and the effects of donidalorsen on the number of HAE attacks and their impact on the QoL of patients with HAE. The secondary endpoints were:
L2004: - The time-normalized number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) from Week 1 to Week 53.
- The time-normalized number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) from Week 5 to Week 53.
- The percentage of investigator-confirmed HAE attack-free subjects from Week 5 to Week 53.
- The time-normalized number of moderate or severe investigator-confirmed HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) from Week 5 to Week 53.
- The number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) requiring acute HAE therapy from Week 5 to Week 53.
- The Angioedema Quality of Life questionnaire total score over 52 weeks.
L2005: The exploratory objectives of this trial were to characterize the effects of donidalorsen on HAE attacks, additional PROs, and biomarkers. The exploratory endpoints were:
L2006: - All subjects:The time-normalized number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) from Week 1 to Week 157.
- The Angioedema Quality of Life questionnaire total score over 157 weeks.
- Percentage of total days during the Treatment Period that subjects were attack free.
- Percentage of total months during the Treatment Period that subjects were attack free.
- Duration in days of the longest attack-free interval.
- Percent of subjects who were attack free for 6 or 12 consecutive months.
- Mean/median longest attack-free interval.
- Rate of HAE attacks that involve the larynx.
- Plasma PKK levels over 52 weeks.
- AECT over 52 weeks.
- Hereditary Angioedema Quality of Life questionnaire total score over 52 weeks.
L2007: - Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire for Medication, version 11 (TSQM-11) score over 52 weeks.
- Incidence of ER visits, all-cause hospitalization, and total inpatient days over 52 weeks.
- Pharmacokinetic exposure over time and potential exposure-response analysis using relevant exposure parameters and biomarkers.
- Rollover subjects onlyThe time-normalized number of investigator-confirmed HAE attack rate (per 4 weeks) compared to Trial ISIS 721744-CS5 (Index Trial) from Week 1 to Week 53.
- Naïve subjects onlyThe time-normalized number of investigator-confirmed HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) from Week 1 to Week 17.
L2008: ## 15.2.4. Analysis Populations, Trial CS7
L2009: The following analysis sets were defined by the Applicant in the SAP, version 1.0, dated April 3, 2024:
L2010: - The Safety Set was to include all enrolled subjects who received at least one dose of donidalorsen.
- The Full Analysis Set was to include all enrolled subjects who received at least one dose of donidalorsen.
- The Per Protocol Set was to include all subjects in the full analysis population who were treated according to the protocol with no major protocol deviations that could compromise the interpretation of efficacy. Major protocol deviations that could compromise the interpretation of efficacy were to be determined prior to the data cutoff date.
- The PK Set was to include all subjects who enrolled and received at least one dose of donidalorsen and had at least one evaluable PK sample.
L2011: ## 15.2.5. Statistical Analysis Plan, Trial CS7
L2012: For all endpoints, HAE attacks refers to investigator-confirmed HAE attacks.
L2013: For both Rollover and Naïve subjects, the time-normalized number of HAE attacks, as well as the changes and the percent changes from baseline from Week 1 to Week 53, was summarized using descriptive statistics. Trial CS5 Run-In baseline was used for the Rollover subjects, and Trial CS7 baseline was used for the Naïve subjects. For Rollover subjects only, this endpoint was also compared to the Trial CS5 on-treatment baseline. A summary using integrated data from Trial CS5 and Trial CS7 was planned. The time-normalized number of HAE attacks from Trial CS5 Week 1 to Trial CS7 Week 157, and from Index Trial Week 5 to OLE Week 157 was compared to the Trial CS5 Run-In baseline. In addition, a summary of every 4 weeks was provided by grouping HAE attacks into 28-day intervals.
L2014: The time-normalized number of HAE attacks from Week 5 to Week 53 was summarized similarly for both Rollover and Naïve subjects.
L2015: For Naïve subjects only, the time-normalized number of investigator-confirmed attack rate from Week 1 to Week 17 and from Week 5 to Week 17 were summarized using the similar methods. To explore whether attack rates remained stable after transitioning for Naïve subjects, p-values using paired t-tests were provided for Week 1 to Week 17 attack rates compared to baseline attack rates.
L2016: The time-normalized number of moderate or severe HAE attacks from Week 5 to Week 53 was summarized similarly for both Rollover and Naïve subjects.
L2017: The time-normalized number of HAE attacks requiring acute therapy from Week 5 to Week 53 was summarized similarly for both Rollover and Naïve subjects.
L2018: ## 15.2.6. Protocol Amendments, Trial CS7
L2019: The original protocol (dated February 28, 2022) was amended twice. Key changes in Amendment #1 were the addition of the Extended Treatment Period and an increase in the planned enrollment number of Naïve subjects from 30 to 60 to obtain additional safety information. Amendment #2 allowed use of an AI to administer donidalorsen.
L2020: ## 15.2.7. Interim Analyses, Trial CS7
L2021: The interim analyses presented in the Applicant's CSR were performed after the data cutoff date of February 28, 2024 (final database lock on April 10, 2024). The results of the interim analyses were intended for regulatory submission, not to be used for stopping or adapting the trial or adjusting the sample size.
L2022: ## 15.2.8. Data and Safety Monitoring Committee, Trial CS7
L2023: The safety of donidalorsen was continually monitored throughout the trial by the investigator or designee and the Applicant or designee. No Data and Safety Monitoring Committee was utilized for this OLE trial. Safety was evaluated by the collection and measurement of AEs, clinical laboratory parameters (including hematology, serum chemistry, and urinalysis), concomitant medication/procedure information, vital signs, and ECGs.
L2024: ## 15.3. Trial CS2
L2025: ## 15.3.1. Trial Design, Trial CS2
L2026: Results from Trial CS2 support the efficacy and safety of donidalorsen for HAE attack prevention. This was a two-part, phase 2, multicenter trial. Subjects were allocated into Part A or Part B according to type of HAE, with either type I or II in Part A and type III in Part B. Parts A and B were conducted concurrently. The trial visit schedule and procedures were nearly identical in Parts A and B. Part B enrolled three adults with HAE type III for open-label treatment with donidalorsen-4. Because Part B was uncontrolled and had a small sample size, it is not considered adequate and well-controlled, and does not support efficacy or safety; the Agency's review focuses on Part A of Trial CS2 only.
L2027: Part A was a randomized, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial in 20 adults with HAE type I or II in a 2:1 ratio to donidalorsen 80 mg (n=14) or placebo (n=6) SC every 4 weeks. The trial schedule included a Screening Period of up to 8 weeks, a 12-week Treatment Period when subjects received treatment every 4 weeks during 4 on-site trial visits, and a 4- to 13-week Post-Treatment Period, with the duration determined by whether a subject enrolled in Trial CS3, the follow-on OLE trial. Subjects completed post-treatment follow-up visits at Weeks 17, 21, and 26/Early Termination. Alternatively, subjects who completed the Week 17 trial visit and met eligibility requirements started the Treatment Period in Trial CS3 any time after the Week 17 visit and discontinued participation in the Trial CS2 Post-Treatment Period. For subjects not enrolling in the OLE trial, the final trial visit was the Week 26/Early Termination Visit. The trial design is shown in Figure 75.
L2028: The length of trial participation for each subject was up to 8 months. Written and signed informed consent was obtained prior to performance of any trial-related procedures, including Screening. Each enrolled subject was randomized to begin trial treatment as soon as the subject experienced \ge 2 HAE attacks during the Screening Period.

L2044: ## 15.3.3. Primary, Secondary, and Exploratory Objectives and Endpoints, Trial CS2
L2045: The primary objective of Trial CS2 Part A was to evaluate the clinical efficacy of donidalorsen in patients with HAE types I and II. The primary endpoint was the time-normalized number of HAE attacks (per month) from Week 1 to Week 17. HAE attack information was collected as described in Section 15.1.1. An HAE attack was defined as an event with signs or symptoms consistent with an attack in at least one of the following locations: peripheral, abdominal, or laryngeal. A discrete attack was counted if there was at least a 24-hour symptom-free period between attacks. This definition of HAE attacks is subtly different than the investigator-confirmed definition used in the phase 3 trials, but not expected to impact the Agency's overall conclusions, as this trial was intended to provide proof-of-concept and not SEE.
L2046: The secondary objectives of Trial CS2 Part A were to evaluate the safety and tolerability of donidalorsen in patients with HAE types I and II and to evaluate the effects of donidalorsen on plasma PKK and other biomarkers. The secondary endpoints, which were not tested with Type I error control, included:
L2047: - The time-normalized number of HAE attacks (per month) from Week 5 to Week 17.
- The time-normalized number of moderate or severe HAE attacks (per month) from Week 5 to Week 17.
- The number of subjects with a clinical response (defined as a \ge 50\%, \ge 70\%, or \ge 90\% reduction from Baseline in HAE attack rate) by Week 17.
- The number of HAE attacks requiring acute therapy from Week 5 to Week 17.
- Cleaved high molecular weight kininogen (cHK) levels at Weeks 9 and 17.
- Prekallikrein activity at Weeks 9 and 17.
- Consumption of on-demand medication at Weeks 9 and 17.
- Angioedema Quality of Life questionnaire score at Weeks 9 and 17.
L2048: The exploratory objectives were to evaluate PK over time and assess potential PK/PD correlations on biomarkers and clinical outcomes. The exploratory endpoints included:
L2049: - The number of HAE attack-free subjects by Week 17.
- Pharmacokinetic parameters, including, but not limited to: C_{max}, T_{max}, AUC, and half-life (t_{1/2}).
- Potential exposure response analysis using relevant exposure parameters and biomarkers.
L2050: ## 15.3.4. Eligibility Criteria, Trial CS2
L2051: Key eligibility criteria for Part A are summarized below. The trial enrolled subjects \ge 18 years of age with clinically confirmed HAE and an attack frequency that would likely warrant prophylactic HAE therapy. The inclusion and exclusion criteria are acceptable and consistent with those used in previous trials of approved products for HAE prophylaxis.
L2052: ## Key Inclusion Criteria
L2053: - Male or female \ge 18 years of age at the time of informed consent.
- Diagnosed with clinically confirmed C1-INH (Type I or Type II) HAE based on all of the following:Documented clinical history consistent with HAE (SC or mucosal, nonpruritic swelling episodes without accompanying urticaria).
- C1-INH functional level &lt;40% normal level. Patients with a functional level of 40% to 50% of normal could be enrolled if their complement factor C4 level was below the LLN or when a known pathogenic mutation in the *SERPING1* gene had been demonstrated.
- At least one of the following: age at HAE onset \le 30 years; family history consistent with Type I or II HAE; or complement component 1q within the normal range.
- Experienced \ge 2 HAE attacks during the Screening Period.
- Female subjects: nonpregnant, nonlactating, and either surgically sterile, postmenopausal, abstinent, or using acceptable contraceptive methods.
- Male subjects: either surgically sterile or using an acceptable contraceptive method.
L2054: ## Key Exclusion Criteria
L2055: - Concomitant diagnosis of another form of angioedema, such as idiopathic or acquired angioedema, recurrent angioedema associated with urticaria, or Type III HAE.
- Exposure to any of the following medications:ACE inhibitors or any estrogen containing medications with systemic absorption (such as oral contraceptive or hormonal replacement therapy) within 4 weeks prior to Screening.
- Chronic prophylaxis with Takhzyro® (lanadelumab), Haegarda® (C1-esterase inhibitor SQ), Cinryze® and Ruconest® (C1 esterase inhibitor) or Orladeyo® (berotralstat) within 5 half-lives prior to Screening (i.e., Takhzyro within 10 weeks prior to Screening, Haegarda/Berinert 2000/3000® subcutaneously/Cinryze/Ruconest within 2 weeks prior to Screening, Orladeyo within 3 weeks prior to Screening).
- Oligonucleotides within 4 months of Screening (if a single administration) or 12 months of Screening (if multiple doses received); does not apply to vaccines.
- History of acquired coagulopathies or bleeding diathesis (e.g., thrombocytopenia) and inherited bleeding disorders (e.g., hemophilia).
- Any clinically significant renal or hepatic diseases.
L2056: Consistent with the eligibility criteria, continued use of a stable dose of androgens was allowed while on trial. The use of on-demand medication to treat acute HAE attacks was also allowed.
L2057: ## 15.3.5. Statistical Analysis Plan, Trial CS2
L2058: The final SAP, version 1.0, is dated February 17, 2021.
L2059: For Trial CS2, the ITT population included all enrolled or randomized subjects. The per-protocol (PP) population included all subjects in the ITT population who were treated according to the protocol without any major deviations.
L2060: The primary efficacy endpoint, the time-normalized number of HAE attacks per month (defined as 28 days) during the On-Treatment Period from Week 1 to Week 17 (28 days after last dose administration), was compared between donidalorsen-4 and placebo in Part A using a Poisson regression model and Pearson chi-square scaling of standard errors to account for potential overdispersion. The model included a fixed effect for treatment group (categorical), the time-normalized Run-In Period attack rate (continuous) as a covariate, and the logarithm of time in month (days from first dose date to 28 days after last dose administration divided by 28) that each subject was observed during the period as an offset variable. The primary analysis of the primary endpoint was conducted in the ITT population.
L2061: All secondary endpoints that concerned time-normalized varieties of HAE attacks were analyzed using the same method as the primary endpoint.
L2062: The number of subjects with a clinical response (defined as \ge 50\%, \ge 70\%, or \ge 90\% reduction from Baseline in HAE attack rate) by Week 17 was analyzed as a risk difference with a corresponding exact 95% confidence interval and p-value from Fisher's Exact test using the ITT and per-protocol populations. For each subject, a Treatment Period HAE attack rate from Week 5 to Week 17 and Run-In Period HAE attack rate was calculated. The percentage reduction will be calculated as the Treatment Period HAE attack rate from Week 5 to Week 17 minus the Run-In Period HAE attack rate divided by the Run-In Period HAE attack rate. Subjects who discontinued treatment early due to lack of efficacy or AEs were considered as nonresponders and included in the denominator for the calculation of the proportion in the ITT population. Subjects who discontinued due to other reason were excluded from analysis.
L2063: The number and percentage of subjects who achieved HAE attack free (no HAE attacks) by Week 17 (end of the On-Treatment Period) were tabulated by treatment group and by Part. Subjects who discontinued treatment early due to lack of efficacy or AEs were considered as nonresponders and included in the denominator for the calculation of the proportion in the ITT population. Subjects who discontinued due to other reason were excluded from analysis. The risk difference between donidalorsen-4 group to the placebo group in Part A, and the corresponding exact 95% confidence interval were provided along with the Fisher's Exact test p-value. The analysis was conducted in both ITT and per-protocol populations.
L2064: ## 15.3.6. Sample Size Considerations, Trial CS2
L2065: The primary endpoint was the time-normalized number of HAE attacks (per month) from Week 1 to Week 17. From historical data, the placebo group was estimated to have 6.8 HAE attacks per 4-month period. Assuming the donidalorsen-4 group has 2.8 HAE attacks per 4-month period, then with a 0.05 significance level and using Poisson model, the sample size of 18 subjects (12 subjects administered donidalorsen-4, and 6 subjects administered placebo) provided at least 90% power for the primary endpoint, considering a 10% missing data or dropout rate for both active treatment and placebo.
L2066: ## 15.3.7. Data and Safety Monitoring Committee, Trial CS2
L2067: A Data and Safety Monitoring Committee reviewed safety, tolerability, and efficacy (as needed) data collected during the trial.
L2068: ## 15.3.8. Protocol Amendments, Trial CS2
L2069: The original protocol (dated May 3, 2019) was amended three times. Key changes in Amendment #1 were the addition of several exclusion criteria (related to elevated PTT, history of coagulopathy or bleeding diathesis, and renal and hepatic diseases); these were added prior to the first subject's enrollment. Amendment #2 allowed subjects who completed the Week 17 trial visit to pursue enrollment in the OLE trial (CS3) at any time after that. Amendment #3 allowed flexibility to conduct some trial procedures via home healthcare, in response to the COVID-2019 pandemic. These protocol amendments are not expected to have substantially impacted the trial results.
L2070: ## 15.4. Trial CS3
L2071: ## 15.4.1. Trial Design, Trial CS3
L2072: Trial CS3 is an ongoing phase 2, randomized, open-label extension trial for adults with HAE Type I or II who completed Trial CS2. The Trial CS3 CSR submitted with the NDA has a data cutoff date of February 26, 2024. In Trial CS3, 20 subjects were treated with donidalorsen in two dosing periods: the Fixed Dosing Period followed by the Flexible Dosing Period. In the Fixed Dosing Period, every subject received donidalorsen-4 for 12 weeks. In the Flexible Dosing Period, based on Investigator and Sponsor Medical Monitor recommendation, a subject was treated with either: (1) continued donidalorsen 80 mg every 4 weeks; (2) donidalorsen 80 mg once every 8 weeks (if attack free for the prior 12 weeks); or (3) donidalorsen 100 mg once every 4 weeks (if not attack free for the prior 12 weeks). At the end of the 52-week Treatment Period (Fixed Dosing and Flexible Dosing), subjects had the option of: (1) receiving donidalorsen in an Extended Treatment Period (during which flexible dosing was maintained) for up to an additional 156 weeks (approximately 3 years), for a Total Treatment Period (Treatment +
L2073: Extended Treatment) of up to approximately 209 weeks (approximately 4 years); or (2) enter the 12-week Post-Treatment Period. The trial design is shown in Figure 76.
L2074: **Figure 76. Trial Schema, Trial CS3**
L2075: Note: All doses were administered subcutaneously

For patients who were not attack-free for \ge 12 weeks, after entering this OLE Study, the Investigator could initiate a switch to donidalorsen 100 mg every 4 weeks. The switch could begin at any visit starting at Week 17. If patients developed any tolerability or safety issue, the dose could be reduced back to 80 mg every 4 weeks.

L2147: ## 15.4.3. Primary, Secondary, and Exploratory Objectives and Endpoints, Trial CS3
L2148: The primary objective of Trial CS3 was to evaluate the safety of extended dosing and alternative dosing and/or dose frequency of donidalorsen in patients with HAE. The primary endpoint was the incidence and severity of TEAEs.
L2149: The secondary objectives of this trial were to evaluate the efficacy of extended dosing and alternative dosing and/or dose frequency in patients with HAE. The secondary endpoints were:
L2150: - The time-normalized HAE attacks (per 4 weeks) by treatment.
- Consumption of on-demand medications.
L2151: The exploratory objectives of this trial were to characterize the effects of donidalorsen on PKK levels, plasma proenzyme activation, and cHK levels; to evaluate the effects of donidalorsen on the clinical and AE-QoL endpoints; and to evaluate PK exposure over time. The exploratory endpoints were:
L2152: - Prekallikrein levels, plasma proenzyme activation (only during Year 1), and cHK levels.
- Angioedema Quality of Life questionnaire score.
L2153: ## 15.4.4. Analysis Populations, Trial CS3
L2154: The following analysis populations were defined by the Applicant in the final SAP, version 3.0, dated March 14, 2024:
L2155: - The safety population was to include all enrolled subjects who received at least one dose of donidalorsen.
- The ITT population was to include all enrolled subjects.
- The per protocol population was to include all subjects in the ITT population who were treated according to the protocol with no major protocol deviations that could compromise the interpretation of efficacy. Major protocol deviations that could compromise the interpretation of efficacy were to be determined prior to the database lock.
- The PK population was to include all subjects who enrolled and received at least one dose of donidalorsen and had at least one evaluable PK sample.
L2156: ## 15.4.5. Statistical Analysis Plan, Trial CS3
L2157: Per the final SAP, dated March 14, 2024, the primary efficacy endpoint was the time-normalized number of HAE attacks. The HAE attack rates, as well as the changes and the percent changes from baseline during the On-Treatment Period and Fixed Dosing Period, were summarized using descriptive statistics by the Index Trial treatment group and overall for HAE Type I, II, and III. The investigator-confirmed HAE attack rate was calculated for each subject as the number of HAE attacks occurring during the On-Treatment Period divided by number of days the subject contributed to the period multiplied by 28 days.
L2158: For the On-Treatment Period and Fixed Dosing Period, three sets of analysis were performed. For the first set of analysis, the Trial CS2-on-treatment baseline was used to derive change and percent change from baseline, regardless of which trial drug the subjects took in the Index Trial. For the second set of analysis, subjects who took the active drug in the Index Trial used Trial CS2-Run-In baseline and subjects who took placebo in the Index Trial used OLE baseline to derive change and percent change from baseline. For the third set of analysis, all subjects used Trial CS2-Run-In baseline.
L2159: Summaries for all analysis periods during the Flexible Dosing Period were only summarized by dose options, using Trial CS2-Run-In baseline for subjects who took the active drug in the Index Trial and OLE baseline for subjects who took placebo in the Index Trial. The analysis was repeated using Trial CS2-Run-In baseline for all subjects. This analysis was also repeated using the Fixed Dosing Period HAE attack rate as the baseline.
L2160: For subjects who received donidalorsen-4 in the Index Trial, an integrated analysis of HAE attack rates was also done by including data in the Index Trial. Trial CS2-Run-In baseline was used for derivation of change and percent change from baseline. The time-normalized HAE attack rate for each subject was calculated as the number of HAE attacks occurring from first dose of the Index Trial to the end of Treatment Period in the OLE trial divided by number of days in the period multiplied by 28 days. The data were presented by HAE type.
L2161: Similar analyses were performed for the secondary efficacy endpoints of time-normalized number of moderate or severe HAE attacks and time-normalized number of HAE attacks requiring acute therapy. The secondary efficacy endpoints of response rate (subjects who achieve 50%, 70%, 90% reduction from baseline in HAE attack rate) and HAE attack free response rate were summarized by number and percentage of subjects.
L2162: ## 15.4.6. Protocol Amendments, Trial CS3
L2163: The original protocol (dated January 17, 2020) was amended three times. Key changes in each respective amendment were to provide the option for each subject to participate in an additional year of trial participation (with relevant adjustments to the trial schedule of assessments), lengthening the trial duration to 4 years of treatment with Amendment #3. Additionally, Amendment #1 provided the option to reduce dosing to 80 mg every 8 weeks in the event of tolerability or safety issues. Amendment #2 allowed continued flexible dosing of donidalorsen after Week 41.
L2164: ## 15.4.7. Interim Analyses, Trial CS3
L2165: The interim analyses presented in the Applicant's CSR were performed after the data cutoff date of February 26, 2024 (final database lock on March 26, 2024). The results of the interim analyses were intended for regulatory submission, not to be used for stopping or adapting the trial or adjusting the sample size.
L2166: ## 15.4.8. Data and Safety Monitoring Committee, Trial CS3
L2167: The safety of donidalorsen was continually monitored throughout the trial by the investigator or designee and the Applicant or designee. No Data and Safety Monitoring Committee was utilized for this OLE trial (CS3). Safety was evaluated by the collection and measurement of AEs, clinical laboratory parameters (including hematology, serum chemistry, and urinalysis), concomitant medication/procedure information, vital signs, physical examinations, and ECGs.

L2182: ## 16.1.3. Primary Efficacy Results, Trial CS2
L2183: Table 92 summarizes the efficacy results for the time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks from Week 1 to Week 17 for the primary efficacy endpoint comparison between donidalorsen-4 and placebo. After adjusting for baseline attack rate and treatment group, the estimated least square mean time-normalized number of HAE attacks per 4 weeks was lower in the donidalorsen-4 (LS mean=0.22, 95% CI=0.10, 0.50) group compared to placebo (LS mean=2.29, 95% CI=1.54, 3.41). The estimated attack rate ratio for the donidalorsen-4 group relative to placebo was 0.10 (95% CI=0.04, 0.24). Additionally, the percentage reduction in the LS means for the donidalorsen-4 group was 90% (95% CI=76%, 96%) relative to placebo.

L2192: ## 16.1.4. Type III HAE, Trial CS2
L2193: In Trial CS2 Part B, six subjects with HAE-nC1-INH (Type III HAE) were screened, and three subjects were dosed and completed trial treatment. All three subjects were female, the mean age was 34 years (range 25 to 40), all were White, and the mean body mass index was 38.4 kg/m2 (range 36 to 42). All three subjects had experienced prior peripheral and abdominal HAE attacks, and one subject had used lanadelumab and discontinued because it was ineffective. The mean number of attacks in the previous 12 months was 61.3 (range 36 to 100) and the mean HAE attack rate in the Run-In Period was 4.23 (values: 2.3, 3, 7.4). The Treatment Period (Week 1 to Week 17) mean HAE attack rate was 1.52 (values: 0, 0.5, 4.1). The mean reduction in monthly HAE attack rate was 75% (values: 45, 83, 100).
L2194: Due to the open-label conduct and sample size of Trial CS2 Part B, no conclusive evidence about efficacy can be drawn from this trial.

L2269: ## 17.4. 120-Day Safety Update
L2270: The Applicant submitted a 120-day safety update on December 19, 2024. The report included data from ongoing open-label trials (CS3 and CS7) as of the cutoff dates of June 25, 2024, and June 27, 2024, respectively. The report included updated pooled safety data from Trial CS2, Trial CS3, Trial CS5, and Trial CS7; the 176 subjects exposed to donidalorsen in these trials had a median donidalorsen exposure duration of 433 days, versus 168 days for placebo recipients.
L2271: Updated safety data from Trial CS3 and Trial CS7 included one fatal event of completed suicide, recorded as a death, SAE, and permanent treatment discontinuation. This subject was a 48-year-old male with a past medical history of headache, on-trial TEAEs of headache and basilar migraine, and no known history of depression or anxiety. One subject experienced an SAE of cellulitis. One subject permanently discontinued trial treatment due to TEAEs of ALT increased and AST increased (subject met the protocol-defined stopping rules for ALT &gt;5\times ULN). Commonly reported TEAEs were generally consistent with the safety profile observed to date. The safety update did not identify any new safety signals for donidalorsen.
L2272: ## 17.5. Additional Safety Information
L2273: ## 17.5.1. ASKCOV Trial
L2274: ASKCOV was an investigator-initiated, placebo-controlled clinical trial in Brazil, to evaluate whether a single dose of 120 mg SC donidalorsen would lead to improved outcomes for patients with COVID-19 prior to the availability of vaccines. The trial was funded by Ionis. The investigators hypothesized that targeting and inhibiting prekallikrein would prevent abnormal activation of the kallikrein-kinin system that leads to angioedema, lung inflammation, and ultimately vessel blockage, which are complications of severe COVID-19 infections.
L2275: A total of 111 hospitalized patients with moderate to severe COVID-19 on supplemental oxygen were enrolled. There was no statistically significant difference for the primary outcome (number of days subjects were alive and free of oxygen support up to 15 days after randomization). Incidences of mortality at Day 30 and the use of mechanical ventilation within 15 days were approximately doubled in the donidalorsen group versus the placebo group.
L2276: The incidence and pattern of TEAEs in the trial did not reveal a concerning imbalance. No TEAEs led to trial drug discontinuation (as it was a single dose). There were 78 SAEs reported in 32 subjects. The PT of respiratory failure occurred most frequently (26/78 [33%] events), followed by septic shock (9/78 [12%] events), severe acute respiratory syndrome (5/78 [6%] events), cardio-respiratory arrest and chronic kidney disease (4/78 [5%] events). None of these SAEs were reported as related to the trial drug by the investigator. Because all these SAEs are confounded by the background moderate-to-severe COVID-19 infection, applicability of these results to the safety profile of donidalorsen in HAE is very limited.

L2288: This PI review includes a high-level summary of the rationale for major changes to the finalized PI as compared to the Applicant's draft PI (Table 98). L2289: **Table 98. Key Labeling Changes and Considerations**
L2290: Full PI Sections1	Rationale for Major Changes to Finalized PI2 Compared to Applicant's Draft PI
BOXED WARNING	Not applicable.
1 INDICATIONS AND USAGE	Dawnzera™ is indicated for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older.
2 DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION	
The recommended dosage is 80 mg administered subcutaneously every 4 weeks. A dosage of 80 mg every 8 weeks may also be considered. The dosage in final labeling does not indicate switching from a more frequent dosing regimen (every 4 weeks) to a less frequent dosing regimen (every 8 weeks) for all patients based on the disease control for at least 3 months (b) (4).
However, as a positive dose response relationship was demonstrated for every 4 weeks compared to every 8 weeks in OASIS-HAE (Trial CS5), every 4 weeks is the preferred dosing regimen. Every 8 weeks may also be considered for some subjects based on the efficacy demonstrated in Trial CS5 and the sustained efficacy demonstrated in CS7. (b) (4).

4 CONTRAINDICATIONS	Dawnzera is contraindicated in patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, to donidalorsen or any of the excipients in Dawnzera.
5 WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS	Includes a Risk of Hypersensitivity Reactions, including Anaphylaxis because of a case reported during clinical trials.
6 ADVERSE REACTIONS	
The safety of Dawnzera reflects the exposure among patients in three clinical trials (CS5, CS3, and CS7), but one clinical trial, OASIS-HAE (Trial CS5), informed the safety and common adverse reactions observed from treatment with Dawnzera. Trial CS2 was not included as it provided limited safety data due to the small sample size and short trial duration.
Decrease in platelet counts and increase in liver function tests are included due to safety signal from clinical trials with donidalorsen and the known class effect of ASOs.
The incidence of anaphylaxis is not included because there was one case in a rare disease population, which could be misleading.

7 DRUG INTERACTIONS	Omitted because there were no clinically relevant drug interactions.
8 USE IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS (e.g., Pregnancy, Lactation, Females and Males of Reproductive Potential, Pediatric Use, Geriatric Use, Renal Impairment, Hepatic Impairment)	
8.1 Pregnancy and 8.2 Lactation subsections were developed consistent with the PLLR Review Tool and available animal data.
8.4 Pediatric Use subsection includes the pediatric use statement for pediatric patients aged 12 years and older, which is supported
L2291: Full PI Sections1	Rationale for Major Changes to Finalized PI2 Compared to Applicant's Draft PI
by extrapolation from adults in the OASIS-HAE (Trial CS5) trial with additional PK analysis and PD response.
8.5 Geriatric Use: Because only two subjects ≥ 65 years of age were enrolled in Trial CS5, the Geriatric Use subsection includes a statement that clinical studies of Dawnzera did not include sufficient numbers of patients 65 years of age and older to determine whether they respond differently from younger adult patients.
8.7 Hepatic Impairment includes language in which Dawnzera is not recommended in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment. This statement is supported by the following: donidalorsen is distributed to the liver and its accumulation in the liver and long-term safety following repeat dosing in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment is not known as donidalorsen has not been studied in patients with moderate or severe renal impairment.

9 DRUG ABUSE AND DEPENDENCE	Not applicable.
10 OVERDOSAGE	Omitted
12 CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY	12.3 PK subsection was revised to provide general PK information following administration of donidalorsen 80 mg every 4 weeks or every 8 weeks.
13 NONCLINICAL TOXICOLOGY	13.1 Carcinogenesis, Mutagenesis, Impairment of Fertility subsection was revised to provide the results from a long-term animal study that evaluated carcinogenic potential of donidalorsen.
14 CLINICAL STUDIES	
OASIS-HAE (Trial CS5) was a 24-week, multicenter, randomized, double-blind placebo-controlled trial that included patients 12 years of age and older with HAE. The demographics and baseline characteristics of patients in OASIS-HAE are provided in a table.
The efficacy results of HAE attacks per 4 weeks are provided in a table along with a Figure that shows the mean HAE attack rate for both dosages over time. Several secondary endpoints are provided, including the proportion of patients with a percent reduction from baseline in the HAE attack rate, although only 70% and 100% was multiplicity controlled.
Of note, the numbering of the Week in the label is different than in the CSRs and the review. Week 0 in the label = Week 1 elsewhere (e.g. Week 0-24 label = Week 1-25 review/CSRs)

17 PATIENT COUNSELING INFORMATION	Included administration instructions and risk of hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis information for healthcare providers to convey to patients during a counseling discussion.
Product Quality Sections (i.e., DOSAGE FORMS AND STRENGTHS, DESCRIPTION, HOW SUPPLIED/STORAGE AND HANDLING)	Sections 3, 11, and 16 were developed consistent with the considerations for product quality information in PI.
Section 16: Formatted How Supplied information in a table to improve readability.

L2396: ## 1 Executive Summary
L2397: ## 1.1 Introduction
L2398: Ionis Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Applicant) submitted a 505(b)(1) New Drug Application (NDA) for subcutaneous (SC) administration of donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) as 80 mg (b) (4) (or 80 mg (b) (4) in some patients) prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. ISIS 721744 is an N-acetyl galactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated antisense oligonucleotide (ASO), which binds to human prekallikrein (PKK) messenger RNA (mRNA) to reduce PKK protein production. The GalNAc molecule preferentially delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by binding to the asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR) on liver cells.
L2399: This review focuses on the nonclinical safety assessment of extractables and leachables for the donidalorsen drug product container closure system (CCS), which constitutes a staked needle glass prefilled syringe (PFS) closed with a (b) (4) rubber plunger stopper that is assembled into an autoinjector to deliver a single dose of 80 mg donidalorsen in 0.8 mL (100 mg/mL). The extractables and leachables information and study reports were submitted on 08/21/2024 (SDN 1) and 10/11/2024 (SDN 7).
L2400: Refer to **Section 3.3** (Previous Reviews Referenced) for a list of the other nonclinical reviews related to the nonclinical evaluation for NDA 219407.
L2401: ## 1.2 Brief Discussion of Nonclinical Findings
L2402: The extractables and leachables studies for the donidalorsen drug product CCS included a controlled extraction study, accelerated leachable study, and leachable study as part of the stability assessment. As summarized below, there are no nonclinical safety concerns based on results from these extractables and leachables studies.
L2403: In the controlled extraction study, the CCS was filled with aqueous buffer solution (pH 5 or pH 9.5) or water-isopropyl alcohol (50:50 v/v) and sealed with plunger stoppers sterilized by (b) (4) (in order to determine the potential impact of sterilization on the extractables profile). The detected extractables (b) (4)
L2404: are considered common extractables/leachables with the materials of the CCS. These compounds were not detected in the leachable studies (accelerated or stability). Further, it did not appear that the sterilization process (b) (4) affected the extractable profile.
L2405: In the accelerated leachable study (Study #1 equivalent to approximately 1 year at 5°C and Study #2 equivalent to slightly less than 3 years at 5°C), two representative ASO drug products were filled into 1 mL and 2.25 mL PFS CCS comprising a staked needle (b) (4) syringe with a (b) (4) tip cap and (b) (4) gray (b) (4) rubber plunger/stopper (b) (4). No volatile, semi-volatile, or non-
L2406: volatile organic leachables were detected [REDACTED] (b) (4) analytical evaluation thresholds (AETs). [REDACTED] (b) (4) was detected [REDACTED] (b) (4) AET in the filled primary container sample in Study #2 at [REDACTED] (b) (4) µg/mL but was also detected in the control (drug product that has not been in contact with the CCS) at [REDACTED] (b) (4) µg/mL and is likely not a leachable.
L2407: As part of the stability assessment, three registration stability batches of the 100 mg/mL donidalorsen autoinjector have been evaluated for leachables at time point 0 (T0); 6 months at 25°C/65% relative humidity (6 months), and 12 months at 5°C/ambient relative humidity transitioned to 30°C/75% relative humidity 6 weeks prior to the pull date to simulate the patient in-use period (12 months). [REDACTED] (b) (4) was detected as a volatile leachable [REDACTED] (b) (4) AET in three lots at T0 ([REDACTED] (b) (4) µg/mL), 6 months, ([REDACTED] (b) (4) µg/mL), and 12 months ([REDACTED] (b) (4) µg/mL). [REDACTED] (b) (4) is listed as a Class 3 solvent (regarded as less toxic and of lower risk to human health) in ICH Q3C with an amount of ≤50 mg/day considered acceptable without justification. The exposure of patients to potential [REDACTED] (b) (4) from the CCS of the donidalorsen drug product for SC administration based on leachable stability data to date was below 50 mg/day and therefore there is no toxicological concern. [REDACTED] (b) (4) was detected in all lots at T0 ([REDACTED] (b) (4) µg/mL). [REDACTED] (b) (4) is listed as a Class 3 solvent in ICH Q3C and with a permitted daily exposure (PDE) of [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/day. The exposure of patients to potential [REDACTED] (b) (4) from the CCS of the donidalorsen drug product for SC administration based on leachable stability data to date was below [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/day and therefore there is no toxicological concern.
L2408: Refer to **Sections 2.5** (Comments on Extractables and Leachables Studies) and **11** (Integrated Summary and Safety Evaluation).
L2409: Conclusion: Overall, there were no nonclinical safety concerns with potential leachables from the CCS for the donidalorsen drug product for SC administration.

L2427: Structure or Biochemical Description
L2428: The structure of donidalorsen sodium is shown in **Figure 1** (Applicant's Figure).
L2429: ISIS 721744 is a 20-mer chimeric 2'-O-methoxymethyl (2'-MOE)-modified ASO with a  mixed backbone made up of phosphorothioate (PS) and phosphodiester (PO)  internucleotide linkages, which targets the mRNA of human PKK. The ASO is  conjugated to triantennary GalNAc via a trishexylamino (THA)-C6 linker, which  preferentially delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by binding to the ASGPR on liver cells.

L2438: ## 2.3 Drug Formulation
L2439: The donidalorsen drug product is a sterile, single-dose, ready-to-use parenteral solution for SC administration. The drug product formulation is shown in **Table 1** (Applicant's Table). The drug product is packaged in a staked needle glass PFS closed with a (b) (4) rubber plunger stopper and assembled into an autoinjector to deliver 0.8 mL of solution containing 80 mg of donidalorsen (80 mg/0.8 mL = 100 mg/mL).

L2454: ## 2.5 Comments on Extractables and Leachables Studies
L2455: The Applicant provided data from a controlled extraction study and an accelerated leachable study with the donidalorsen drug product CCS. The Applicant also indicated that a leachable study is ongoing as part of the registration stability protocol and available data were provided to the NDA. The Applicant indicated that the extractables and leachables assessment for the CCS was in line with the recommendations for evaluation of primary packaging in USP &lt;1661&gt;, extractables/leachables testing per USP &lt;1663&gt;, USP &lt;1664&gt;, and the Product Quality Research Institute (PQRI) Leachables and Extractables Working Group Initiatives for Parenteral and Ophthalmic Products.1,2,3
L2456: This section describes the donidalorsen drug product CCS as well as the study design and results for the extractables and leachables studies with the CCS. The nonclinical safety evaluation for potential leachables is included in **Section 11** (Integrated Summary and Safety Evaluation).
L2457: Refer to NDA 219407 Office of Pharmaceutical Quality Integrated Quality Assessment dated 05/05/2025 for more details on the extractables and leachables assessment from the quality perspective.
L2458: ## CCS for Donidalorsen Drug Product
L2459: As described by the Applicant (Module 3.2.P.7. Container Closure System): Donidalorsen Solution for Injection, 100 mg/mL, is packaged in a 1 mL Long (1 mL L) staked needle syringe with a plunger stopper (which together constitute the primary CCS). The (b)(4) syringe is the (b)(4) 1 mL L glass syringe with a rigid needle shield (RNS) closure and a 0.5 inch (12.7 mm), 27 gauge, (b)(4) staked needle. The plunger stopper is the (b)(4) rubber plunger stopper. The drug product is filled into the syringe and closed with the plunger stopper to create the filled primary CCS. Of note, none of the components of the staked needle syringe are made with natural rubber latex or any derivatives from natural rubber latex and the formulation used in the plunger stopper is not made with latex or dry rubber. The filled primary CCS is assembled into an integral, single-use, single-dose (b)(4) autoinjector (secondary CCS). The (b)(4) autoinjector is used in other FDA approved combination products.

L2466: ## Controlled Extraction StudyStudy Design
L2467: The Applicant described the study design for the controlled extraction study as follows: The commercial CCS plunger stoppers were sterilized by (b) (4) in order to determine the potential impact of sterilization on the extractables profile. The CCSs were filled with aqueous buffer solution (pH 5 or pH 9.5) or water-isopropyl alcohol (50:50 v/v) and sealed with the plunger stopper. The samples were stored horizontally at 55°C for 72 hours.
L2468: Extracts from the aqueous samples (pH 5.0 and pH 9.5) and individual components of the PFS were analyzed for volatile organic extractables by headspace gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). The individual components of the PFS (glass barrel, plunger stopper, and tip cap) were analyzed directly in place of the organic extract. The Sample IDs of the individual components were identified as follows:
L2469: - Glass Barrel with Needle ((b) (4) 1.0 mL 27G STW 0.5 inch staked PFS with a silicone oil lubricant) Component wt. 3.07682 g
- Stopper/Plunger ((b) (4) 7 mm (b) (4) rubber Grey (b) (4) Component wt. 0.24077 g (b) (4); 0.2422 g (b) (4)
- Black Rubber (b) (4) Component wt. 0.47409 g
L2470: Extracts from water-isopropyl alcohol (50:50 v/v) samples were not analyzed for volatile organic extractables (b) (4).
L2471: Extracts from aqueous samples (pH 5.0 and pH 9.5) and water-isopropyl alcohol (50:50 v/v) samples were analyzed for semi-volatile organic extractables by direct inject GC-MS, non-volatile organic extractables by ultra-high pressure liquid chromatography with photodiode array and quadrupole-time-of-flight mass spectrometry (HPLC-PDA-QTOF-MS), and inorganic extractables by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS).
L2472: The Applicant calculated the AET for the drug product based on a safety concern threshold (SCT) of 1.5 \mu\text{g}/\text{day} (ICH M7 limit for mutagenic impurities), as follows:
L2473: AET = [REDACTED] (b) (4) \mu\text{g}/\text{mL}
L2474: The Applicant applied an uncertainty factor of (b) (4) which resulted in a final AET value of [REDACTED] (b) (4) \mu\text{g}/\text{mL}.
L2475: The Applicant expressed the AET for the individual components as \mu\text{g}/\text{component} to represent the entire surface area of each component, whereas only a fraction is in contact with the drug product.
L2476: AET = [REDACTED] (b) (4) \text{g}/\text{component}
L2477: The Applicant applied an uncertainty factor of (b) (4) which resulted in a final AET value of [REDACTED] (b) (4) \mu\text{g}/\text{component}.
L2478: The Applicant calculated the limit of detection (LOD) expressed in \mu\text{g}/\text{component} as follows:
L2479: LOD \mu\text{g}/\text{g} \times \text{g}/\text{component} = \mu\text{g}/\text{component}.

L2503: ## **Accelerated Leachable Study **
L2504: Study Design
L2505: The Applicant described the study design for the accelerated leachable study as follows:
L2506: Based on the extractable study results for the sterilized stopper (see above), the stoppers sterilized by were considered
L2507: equivalent. As such, the accelerated leachable study used (b) (4) sterilized stoppers on two representative ASO drug products filled into 1 mL and 2.25 mL PFS CCS comprising a staked needle (b) (4) syringe with a (b) (4) tip cap and (b) (4) gray (b) (4) rubber plunger/stopper. The Applicant indicated that the 1 mL and 2.25 mL CCS have identical materials of construction, and the extraction power of ASO drug products are similar as they are aqueous based formulations containing only ASO and inorganic excipients. The Applicant further indicated that the 1 mL CCS is identical to the system used for the 80 mg donidalorsen solution for injection.
L2508: The Applicant described the two accelerated leachable studies as follows:
L2509: - Study #1: 200 mg/mL ASO in water formulated at pH 8.0, filled into a 2.25 mL PFS primary container sealed with (b) (4) stoppers and stored horizontally for 1 month at the accelerated condition of 40°C, which is equivalent to approximately 1 year at 5°C.
- Study #2: 75 mg/mL ASO in isotonic (b) (4) formulated at pH 7.4, filled into a 1 mL PFS primary container sealed with (b) (4) stoppers and stored horizontally for 3 months at the accelerated condition of 40°C, which is equivalent to slightly less than 3 years at 5°C.
L2510: The samples were then analyzed for volatile organic leachables by headspace GC-MS, semi-volatile organic leachables by direct injection GC-MS, non-volatile organic leachables by HPLC-PDA-MS and inorganic leachables by ICP-MS.
L2511: The Applicant set an AET of (b) (4) µg/mL for Study #1 and (b) (4) µg/mL (includes (b) (4) uncertainty factor) for Study #2. The Applicant indicated that the AET's were based on PQRI's SCT of 1.5 µg/day1 and either a (b) (4) mL (Study #1) or (b) (4) mL (Study #2) delivered dose volume.
L2512: ## Results
L2513: ## *Volatile, Semi-Volatile, and Non-Volatile Organic Results*
L2514: No volatile, semi-volatile, or non-volatile organic leachables were detected (b) (4) AETs in either Study #1 or Study #2, respectively.
L2515: ## *Inorganic Results*
L2516: No inorganic leachables were detected (b) (4) AET in Study #1.
L2517: (b) (4) was detected (b) (4) AET in the filled primary container sample in Study #2 at (b) (4) µg/mL but was also detected in the control (drug product that has not been in contact with the CCS) at (b) (4) µg/mL.
L2518: Refer to **Section 11** (Integrated Summary and Safety Evaluation) for the nonclinical safety evaluation of the accelerated leachable study data.
L2519: ## Leachable Study on Stability
L2520: ## Study Design
L2521: The Applicant described the study design for the leachable study on stability as follows:
L2522: Registration stability batches of the 100 mg/mL autoinjector are being monitored on stability. At the time of the NDA submission, three registration stability batches were evaluated at T0, 6 months at 25°C/65% relative humidity, and 12 months at 5°C/ambient relative humidity transitioned to 30°C/75% relative humidity 6 weeks prior to the pull date to simulate the patient in-use period.

L2547: ## 2.7 Regulatory Background
L2548: Provided below is regulatory background for the donidalorsen development program as it relates to extractables and leachables.
L2549: The following comment was provided to the Applicant in IND 142564 Type C written responses dated 12/19/2023:
L2550: "The clinical drug product is packaged with 0.8 mL deliverable volume in an ISO 2R Type (b) (4) clear glass vial that is stoppered with a (b) (4) rubber closure and sealed with an aluminum overseal. During the phase 3 Open Label Extension study, the intended commercial configuration will be introduced, which comprises a glass prefilled syringe (PFS) fitted into an autoinjector (AI). A safety assessment of extractables and leachables should be provided in the NDA for all primary container closure components of the device that are in contact with the drug product during storage (i.e., AI and potentially the vial if it is also used as a commercial configuration), as well as secondary container closure components where there is a potential for migration of leachables into the drug product. See USP Chapters for 1663 and 1664 for the design of extractables and leachables studies, respectively."
L2551: During the filing review of the original submission for this NDA 219407 (SDN 1, 08/21/2024), it appeared that the Applicant had not provided the study reports associated with the extractables and leachables studies. The following information request was sent to the Applicant on 09/27/2024:
L2552: "We are reviewing your August 21, 2024, NDA submission and have the following requests for information:
L2553: The results of extractable and leachable studies conducted with the drug product primary container closure system are summarized in Pharmaceutical Development (Module 3.2.P.2) for the Container Closure System (Module 3.2.P.2.4). To facilitate the review of your application, provide the finalized study reports associated with these studies or provide their specific location in the submission."
L2554: The Applicant provided the following response to the information request on 10/11/2024 (SDN 7):
L2555: "The product-specific study reports for donidalorsen drug product are provided with this response.
L2556: Module 3.2.P.2.4 Section 7.2 provides a detailed extractables and leachables assessment for the container closure system (CCS). The assessment is in line with the recommendations for evaluation of primary packaging in USP &lt;1661&gt;, extractables/leachables testing per USP &lt;1663&gt;, USP &lt;1664&gt;, and the Product Quality Research Institute (PQRI) Leachables and Extractables Working Group Initiatives for Parenteral and Ophthalmic Products.
L2557: To confirm the low risk of leachables from the CCS assessment, a product-specific leachable study is ongoing as part of the registration stability protocol (Module 3.2.P.8.1). Three (3) registration stability batches of the donidalorsen drug product are being monitored on stability. A tabular summary of leachable results obtained through 12 months storage at the long-term storage condition of 2–8 °C (with 6 weeks in use at 30 °C) and at T=0 and 6 months of storage at 25 °C/60% RH are summarized in Module 3.2.P.2.4 Table 20 and the reports associated with these studies are provided as
L2558: Appendix 1 of this response. A commitment to continue the longterm leachable study through the proposed shelf-life of the product (up to 60 months) is provided in Module 3.2.P.8.2."

L2570: ## 11 Integrated Summary and Safety Evaluation
L2571: The Applicant is seeking approval for donidalorsen for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of HAE in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. The recommended dosage is 80 mg administered SC (b) (4). A dosing interval of (b) (4) may be considered in some patients. The donidalorsen drug product is a sterile, single-dose, ready-to-use parenteral solution for SC administration. The drug product is packaged in a staked needle glass PFS closed with a (b) (4) rubber plunger stopper and assembled into an autoinjector to deliver a single dose of 0.8 mL of 80 mg donidalorsen (80 mg/80 mL = 100 mg/mL).
L2572: This review provides a nonclinical safety assessment of potential extractables and leachables from the primary CCS for the donidalorsen drug product for SC administration based on data submitted by the Applicant and other available information. Of note, although the drug product is delivered (b) (4) any comparisons made in this evaluation are based on acceptable levels per day. Adjustments for dosing intervals were not made to provide a conservative safety assessment. In general, for the leachable evaluation, any organic (nonmetal) compound with expected patient exposure below the PQRI thresholds of 5 µg/day (for compounds lacking genotoxic potential and irritant potential) and 1.5 µg/day (for compounds with genotoxic potential) was considered qualified for safety.1 For compounds not qualified for safety based on PQRI thresholds, a nonclinical safety assessment to establish PDE
L2573: levels for each compound based on experimental data from the literature, where available, and considering modifying factors (following the ICH Q3C Guideline 2021) was used. Of note, (b) (4) leachables or other special case leachables (such as (b) (4) would necessitate additional evaluation to determine a qualified threshold.

L2621: The following supportive information is included for internal descriptive purposes only: An ICH Q3E Guideline for Extractables and Leachables is currently being drafted by an Expert Working Group (EWG), which has been discussed extensively within the PTCC Extractables and Leachables Subcommittee. Based on these discussions, (b) (4) and other (b) (4) are considered as Class 3 leachables, which the draft Guidance describes as compounds considered to have relatively low potency for systemic toxicity with derived chronic parenteral PDE in excess of the levels at which leachables are typically observed (i.e., PDE \ge 1 mg/day using the methodology which will be described in the Guideline). Class 3 leachables would not require further safety qualification if observed at daily exposure levels &lt; 1 mg/day. The draft Guideline states that a toxicological evaluation should be conducted for Class 3 leachables present at levels above 1 mg/day (1000 \mug/day). The following (b) (4) are potentially being considered to be included in the guidance as Class 3 leachables: (b) (4) (b) (4).

L2643: ## 1 Executive Summary
L2644: ## 1.1 Introduction
L2645: Ionis Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Applicant) submitted a 505(b)(1) New Drug Application (NDA) for subcutaneous (SC) administration of donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) as 80 mg (b) (4) (or 80 mg (b) (4) in some patients) prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. ISIS 721744 is an *N*-acetyl galactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated antisense oligonucleotide (ASO), which binds to human prekallikrein (PKK) messenger RNA (mRNA) to reduce PKK protein production. The GalNAc molecule preferentially delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by binding to the asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR) on liver cells.
L2646: This review focuses on the nonclinical safety assessment of ISIS 721744 impurities through review of a 13-week repeat-dose SC toxicity and impurity qualification study of ISIS 721744 and associated test article related mixtures (TAMs) in ICR mice and also comparison of impurity levels in the ISIS 721744 clinical batch to the toxicology batch used in the 39-week repeat-dose toxicity study in monkeys.
L2647: Refer to the NDA 219407 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 03/25/2025 and Investigational New Drug (IND) 142564 Nonclinical Primary review dated 08/13/2019 for a review of the nonclinical pharmacology, safety pharmacology, pharmacokinetics/absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (PK/ADME), and general toxicology studies for the ISIS 721744 nonclinical program.
L2648: Refer to the NDA 219407 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 03/05/2025 for a review of the reproductive and developmental toxicology studies with ISIS 721744 (i.e., combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice and pre- and postnatal development [PPND] study in mice).
L2649: Refer to the NDA 219407 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 12/19/2024 for a review of the 6-month carcinogenicity study of ISIS 721744, as well as the mouse surrogate, ISIS 722059, by SC injection in CByB6F1- Tg(HRAS)2Jic Hemizygous Transgenic mice (Tg.rasH2 mice).
L2650: ## 1.2 Brief Discussion of Nonclinical Findings
L2651: The Applicant submitted a 13-week repeat-dose SC toxicity and impurity qualification study in which ICR mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection/solution [saline]) or (b) (4) mg/kg total oligonucleotide dose level of ISIS 721744, TAM 1, and TAM 2 once every two weeks (Q2W) for 13-weeks. The two TAMs that were evaluated in the study were made up of ISIS 721744 and associated impurities (i.e., (b) (4) impurities for TAM 1 and (b) (4) impurity for TAM 2). The findings in TAM 1- and TAM 2-treated groups were similar to those in ISIS 721744-treated groups, which included increases in aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT), increases in
L2652: liver weights, and histopathology findings of mononuclear cell infiltration and karyocytomegaly in the liver and vacuolated granular macrophages at the injection site. Overall, there were no meaningful differences between the findings in either of the TAM groups (ISIS 721744 + associated impurities) compared to the ISIS 721744 group alone and it did not appear that the added impurities affected the toxicity profile of ISIS 721744. Refer to **Sections 2.5 and 6.2**.
L2653: The Applicant conducted a pivotal Good Laboratory Practice (GLP)-compliant 39-week repeat-dose toxicity study of ISIS 721744 (0, 2, 6, 12, and 30 mg/kg/week) in Cynomolgus monkeys with a 13-week interim sacrifice and 26-week treatment-free recovery period (Refer to IND 142564 Nonclinical Primary review dated 08/13/2019). The impurity levels seen in the toxicology batch at the no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL) of 6 mg/kg/week provide support for the proposed impurity limits for the clinical batch. Refer to **Section 2.5**.
L2654: **Conclusion:** Taken together, the 13-week repeat-dose SC toxicity and impurity qualification study in ICR mice and comparisons of impurity levels between the 39-week toxicology study in monkeys and clinical batches of the drug support the proposed impurity limits. There are no outstanding nonclinical concerns.
L2655: ## 1.3 Recommendations

L2657: From the nonclinical perspective, NDA 219407 is recommended for approval. There are no outstanding nonclinical issues.

L2674: Structure or Biochemical Description
The structure of donidalorsen sodium is shown in **Figure 1** (Applicant's Figure).
L2675: ISIS 721744 is a 20-mer chimeric 2'-MOE-modified ASO with a mixed backbone made up of phosphorothioate (PS) and phosphodiester (PO) internucleotide linkages, which targets the mRNA of human PKK. The ASO is conjugated to triantennary GalNAc via a trishexylamino (THA)-C6 linker, which preferentially delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by binding to the ASGPR on liver cells.
L2676: **Figure 1** Structure of Donidalorsen Sodium (Applicant's Figure)
L2677: Chemical structure diagram of Donidalorsen Sodium (Applicant's Figure). The molecule consists of a central GalNAc moiety linked to a phosphorothioate oligonucleotide backbone. The oligonucleotide backbone is composed of alternating deoxyribose sugars and nucleobases (adenine, cytosine, guanine, thymine). The phosphorothioate linkages are indicated by 'S' replacing 'O' in the P=O group, and are associated with sodium ions (\text{Na}^+). The structure shows multiple phosphorylation sites, including \text{Na}^+ \text{O-P=O}, \text{Na}^+ \text{S-P=O}, and \text{Na}^+ \text{P=O} groups. The terminal sugar is linked to a long hydrocarbon chain via an amide bond. The structure is highly branched, featuring multiple GalNAc moieties attached to the backbone. The variable group R is defined as \text{R} = \text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OCH}_3.

L2701: The Quality Reviewer summarized the following information:
L2702: The Applicant provided the structures, origins, and fates for the oligonucleotide-related impurities, including those derived from the starting materials and process-related impurities. L2745: to **Section 6.2**). The two TAMs that were evaluated in the study were made up of ISIS 721744 and associated impurities (i.e., (b) (4) impurities for TAM 1 and (b) (4) impurity for TAM 2). The findings in TAM 1- and TAM 2-treated groups were similar to those in ISIS 721744-treated groups. Overall, there were no meaningful differences between the findings in either of the TAM groups (ISIS 721744 + associated impurities) compared to the ISIS 721744 group alone and it did not appear that the added impurities affected the toxicity profile of ISIS 721744. In this case, based on the concepts presented in Capaldi et al 2017, the toxicology findings observed are likely due to ISIS 721744 rather than the added impurities and, therefore, the amounts of impurities are qualified.

L2751: ## 2.6 Proposed Clinical Population and Dosing Regimen
L2752: Donidalorsen is indicated for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of HAE in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. The recommended dosage is 80 mg administered SC (b) (4). A dosing interval of (b) (4) may be considered in some patients.
L2753: ## 2.7 Regulatory Background
L2754: Provided below is regulatory background for the donidalorsen development program as it relates to impurities.
L2755: The following comment was provided in the IND 142564 Study May Proceed letter dated 09/30/2019:
L2756: "Provide structures of any impurities and degradants of the drug substance and drug product in your IND submission. Monitor impurities and degradation products of all active ingredients and refer to ICH Guidance Q3A(R) and Q3B(R) for possible qualification requirements. The specific impurity thresholds described in these guidances do not apply to oligonucleotide-related impurities; however, the general principles of these guidances do apply. It is expected that you would identify and measure impurities as well as determine appropriate impurity specifications as IND development proceeds. One approach for the determination of appropriate impurity specifications could involve comparisons of impurity levels in toxicology and clinical batches of the drug. If impurity levels at the no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL) of the 39-week monkey study (or 13-week interim sacrifice) provide adequate safety margins over impurity levels at the maximum proposed clinical dose, this could assist in determination of appropriate specifications."
