L2774: ## Key Study Findings
L2775: - In a 13-week repeat-dose toxicity impurity qualification study, ICR mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection/solution [saline]) or [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg total oligonucleotide dose level of ISIS 721744, TAM 1 ([REDACTED] (b) (4) impurities), and TAM 2 ([REDACTED] (b) (4) impurity) Q2W for 13-weeks.
- There were no unscheduled deaths during the study.
- Red blood cell values were minimally decreased only in females at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose TAM 2.
- BUN values were decreased in males and females at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose TAM 2; AST values were increased only in males at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, TAM 1, and TAM 2; ALT values were increased only in males at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, TAM 1, and TAM 2; and triglycerides were decreased in females at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and males at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose TAM 2.
- Liver weights (absolute and/or relative to body weight) were increased only in males at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and TAM 1, and [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose TAM 2.
- Histopathology findings attributed to treatment with ISIS 721744, TAM 1, and/or TAM 2 were noted in the liver and injection site.Liver: Minimal to slight mononuclear cell infiltration in males and/or females at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, TAM 1, and/or TAM 2. Minimal karyocytomegaly in males only at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, TAM 1, and TAM 2, which correlated with minimally increased ALT and AST and increased liver weight in males. Liver karyocytomegaly was attributed to uptake and accumulation of ASOs into the liver.
- Injection Site: Minimal to slight vacuolated granular macrophages in males and females at [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose TAM 1, and [REDACTED] (b) (4) mg/kg/dose TAM 2. Injection site findings were attributed to uptake and accumulation of ASOs into the macrophages.
- Mean concentrations of unconjugated ISIS 721744 in the mouse liver on Day 87 were comparable for ISIS 721744-, TAM 1-, and TAM 2-treated groups.
- **Conclusion: The effects observed in TAM 1- and TAM 2-treated groups were similar to effects observed in ISIS 721744-treated groups. Overall, it did not appear that the added impurities affected the toxicity profile of ISIS 721744.**
L2776: ## Methods
L2777: Doses: **ISIS 721744**: [REDACTED](b) (4) mg/kg total oligonucleotide dose level
L2778: **TAM 1**: [REDACTED](b) (4) mg/kg total oligonucleotide dose level
L2779: **TAM 2**: [REDACTED](b) (4) mg/kg total oligonucleotide dose level
L2780: As stated in the study report: Dose levels represent total oligonucleotide concentration which is inclusive of ISIS 721744 and ASO-related impurities. A [REDACTED](b) (4) mg/kg total oligonucleotide dose yields approximately 4 and 12 mg/kg ISIS 721744, respectively, which has been administered to mice in previous repeat-dose toxicity studies.
L2781: Frequency of dosing: Q2W for 13 weeks (Days 1, 15, 29, 43, 57, 71, and 85; total of seven doses)
L2782: Route of administration: SC
L2783: Dose volume: 10 mL/kg
L2784: Formulation/Vehicle: 0.9% sodium chloride for injection/solution (saline)
L2785: Species/Strain: Mouse/CD-1
L2786: Number/Sex/Group: 10
L2787: Age: 7 to 8 weeks (age range on study)
L2788: Weight: 32.6 to 40.5 g for males and 25.2 to 32.5 g for females at the start of dosing.
L2789: Satellite groups: No
L2790: Unique study design: This study was designed as an impurity qualification study to evaluate the potential toxicity of the ISIS 721744-associated TAM 1 ([REDACTED](b) (4) impurities) or TAM 2 ([REDACTED](b) (4) impurity) as compared to ISIS 721744 alone in CD-1 mice after 13 weeks of SC administration.
L2791: Deviation from study protocol: None of the protocol deviations listed in the study report were deemed to have impacted the integrity or conclusions of the study.

L2861: ## Histological Findings
L2862: Histopathology findings attributed to treatment with ISIS 721744, TAM 1, and/or TAM 2 were noted in the liver and injection site (**Table 11**).
L2863: ## Liver
L2864: Minimal to slight mononuclear cell infiltration was seen in males and/or females at (b) (4) mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, TAM 1, and/or TAM 2.
L2865: Minimal karyocytomegaly was seen in males only at (b) (4) mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, TAM 1, and TAM 2. Hepatocellular karyocytomegaly correlated with minimally increased ALT and AST and increased liver weight in males. This finding was attributed to uptake and accumulation of ASOs into the liver.
L2866: *Reviewer's Note: Karyocytomegaly reflects hepatocyte polyploidy that occurs when there is duplication of nuclear material in the absence of cytokinesis. Changes can consist of increased numbers of diploid nuclei per hepatocyte or an increase in the ploidy level of a single hepatocyte nucleus. Spontaneous occurrence of karyocytomegaly is commonly seen in aging rodents and is not typically associated with increased liver weight. This aging change, often referred to as polyploidy, is more common in mice than in rats (NTP).2*
L2867: ## Injection Site
L2868: Minimal to slight vacuolated granular macrophages were seen in males and females at (b) (4) mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, (b) (4) mg/kg/dose TAM 1, and (b) (4) mg/kg/dose TAM 2. This finding was attributed to uptake and accumulation of ASOs into the macrophages.

L2904: ## 1 Executive Summary
L2905: ## 1.1 Introduction
L2906: Ionis Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Applicant) submitted a 505(b)(1) New Drug Application (NDA) for subcutaneous (SC) administration of donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) as 80 mg (b) (4) (or 80 mg (b) (4) in some patients) prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. ISIS 721744 is an N-acetyl galactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated antisense oligonucleotide (ASO), which binds to human prekallikrein (PKK) messenger RNA (mRNA) to reduce PKK protein production. The GalNAc molecule preferentially delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by binding to the asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR) on liver cells.
L2907: This review focuses on the nonclinical pharmacology, safety pharmacology, pharmacokinetics/absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (PK/ADME), and general toxicology studies for the ISIS 721744 nonclinical program that were not previously reviewed. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 08/13/2019 for the primary pharmacology, safety pharmacology, PK/ADME, and general toxicology studies that were previously reviewed.
L2908: Refer to the NDA 219407 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 12/19/2024 for a review of the 6-month carcinogenicity study of ISIS 721744, as well as the mouse surrogate, ISIS 722059, by SC injection in CByB6F1- Tg(HRAS)2Jic Hemizygous Transgenic mice (Tg.rasH2 mice) and to NDA 219407 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 03/05/2025 for a review of the reproductive and developmental toxicology studies with ISIS 721744 (i.e., combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice and pre- and postnatal development [PPND] study in mice).
L2909: Together, these studies entail the nonclinical studies to support the safety of donidalorsen for marketing approval.
L2910: ## 1.2 Brief Discussion of Nonclinical Findings
L2911: ## *Primary Pharmacology*
L2912: Donidalorsen is a GalNAc-conjugated ASO that binds to PKK mRNA in the liver which causes ribonuclease H1 (RNase H1)-mediated degradation of PKK mRNA to reduce production of PKK protein by the liver. PKK is a pro enzyme for plasma kallikrein, which results in the release of bradykinin, a potent vasodilator causing swelling and pain in HAE. In patients with HAE, C1 inhibitor (C1 INH) deficiency or dysfunction leads to excessive plasma kallikrein activity, bradykinin generation, and angioedema attacks. Donidalorsen lowers PKK concentration, preventing excessive bradykinin production in patients with HAE.
L2913: As described by the Applicant: Over 1300 ASOs were designed to target various sites within the human PKK gene and were evaluated for their ability to inhibit the level of PKK mRNA in vitro in the human hepatocellular carcinoma cell line HepaRG. Of those
L2914: ASOs, ISIS 546254, an unconjugated 2'-O-methoxyethyl (2'-MOE) gapmer ASO with a uniform phosphorothioate (PS) backbone, was identified as a lead candidate. Donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) was derived from ISIS 546254 as a 2'-MOE gapmer ASO with the same nucleobase sequence as ISIS 546254 but with a mixed PS and phosphodiester (PO) backbone and conjugated to a trivalent GalNAc3.
L2915: Specificity analysis of ISIS 721744 to PKK mRNA was performed with the unconjugated PKK ASO, ISIS 546254. ISIS 546254 is perfectly matched to only PKK mRNA in human transcriptome (targets site free of meaningful sequence variation). Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
L2916: In an in vitro study, ISIS 721744 and unconjugated PKK ASO, ISIS 546254, induced a dose-dependent reduction of PKK mRNA in human hepatocytes with supporting stromal with IC50 values of 0.19 mcM vs. 8.73 mcM, respectively. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
L2917: In an in vitro study, unconjugated PKK ASO, ISIS 546254, reduced human PKK mRNA levels by greater than 90% in a concentration-dependent manner in human hepatocellular cell lines HepaRG and Hep3b with corresponding IC50 of 0.31 mcM and 0.35 mcM, respectively.
L2918: In an in vivo study in mice, SC administration of unconjugated PKK ASO mouse surrogate, ISIS 482584, for 3 weeks caused a dose-dependent reduction of PKK liver mRNA and PKK plasma protein. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
L2919: In an in vivo study in mice, SC administration of unconjugated PKK ASO mouse surrogate, ISIS 482584, for 3 weeks caused inhibition of basal vascular permeability, captopril-induced vascular permeability, and C1 INH ASO-induced vascular permeability in the colon of mice. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
L2920: In an in vivo study in mice, SC administration of unconjugated PKK ASO mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 for 3 weeks reduced basal activated high molecular weight kininogen cleavage in blood of male mice. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
L2921: In an in vivo study in human KLKB1/PKK transgenic mice, single SC administration of ISIS 721744 on Day 0 resulted in a dose- and time-dependent reduction of plasma PKK protein that approached 91% at the highest dose tested (10 mg/kg) on Day 14 after treatment. PKK levels were still 20% below baseline levels by Day 56 (last time point evaluated) at 10 mg/kg.
L2922: ## *Safety Pharmacology*
L2923: The safety pharmacology evaluations for the cardiovascular, respiratory, and central nervous system (CNS) were combined into one study in Cynomolgus monkeys. There were no test article-related effects on cardiovascular, respiratory, or CNS parameters in
L2924: male Cynomolgus monkeys evaluated for up to 24 hours after SC administration of 12 and 30 mg/kg ISIS 721744. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
L2925: In the in vitro human ether-a-go-go-related gene (hERG) assay, ISIS 721744 did not inhibit hERG potassium channel current in human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK-293) mammalian cells stably transfected with hERG complementary DNA (cDNA) compared to the vehicle control. In general, oligonucleotides are not thought to interact with the hERG channel.
L2926: ## *PK/ADME*
L2927: In an in vitro evaluation of plasma protein binding of ISIS 721744 (0.5, 5, and 150 mcg/mL) in human, monkey, and mouse plasma, ISIS 721744 was highly bound (\ge 96.81\%) to whole plasma proteins in all three species. The extent of plasma protein binding of ISIS 721744 was similar across all species. Refer to IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
L2928: The in vitro mean blood to plasma ratio of ISIS 721744 was between 0.630 and 0.824 in human, 0.468 and 0.566 in monkey, and 0.501 and 0.661 in rat suggesting that ISIS 721744 distributes mostly in the plasma compartment across the concentrations tested in all three species.
L2929: Based on metabolic profiling and identification of ISIS 721744 oligonucleotide-related metabolites in urine from mice, monkeys, and humans, the Applicant described that the primary route of elimination of donidalorsen is initial rapid hydrolysis of the GalNAc conjugate in tissues (presumed to be primarily in the liver based on directed distribution to the liver), followed by slow nuclease-mediated metabolism of the unconjugated oligonucleotide, and subsequent excretion of chain-shortened metabolites, as well as full-length oligonucleotides, albeit minor in urine and feces. There were no unique metabolites identified in humans compared to animal species.
L2930: Based on metabolic profiling, identification, and quantitation of ISIS 721744 linker-related metabolites in plasma, urine, and/or fecal samples from mice, monkeys, and/or humans, the Applicant described that the GalNAc moiety is hydrolyzed intracellularly following uptake into tissues, and the trishexylamino (THA) linker undergoes extensive oxidative metabolism, and is nearly completely eliminated via biliary excretion, and to a lesser extent, renal excretion, within 24 hours after administration.
L2931: ## *Toxicology*
L2932: In the pivotal Good Laboratory Practice (GLP)-compliant chronic toxicity study in Cynomolgus monkeys (pharmacologically relevant species), monkeys received SC doses of ISIS 721744 at 0, 2, 6, 12, or 30 mg/kg/dose. The monkeys were dosed for 39-weeks (dosing on Days 1, 5, 9, and 14 [loading doses] and once weekly thereafter) with a 13-week interim sacrifice (monkeys at 30 mg/kg/dose were dosed only until the interim sacrifice). A 26-week treatment-free recovery period was included after both the 13-week interim dosing interval (30 mg/kg/dose) and the 39-week dosing interval (0, 2,
L2933: 6, 12 mg/kg/dose) to assess potential reversibility of any observed effects. Refer to Nonclinical Primary Review dated 08/13/2019 for details. In brief, the main test article-related findings included thrombocytopenia in two animals (12 and 30 mg/kg/dose) and histopathology findings of basophilic granules in various organs/tissues (including kidneys, liver, lymph nodes, and injection site) that in the absence of correlating histopathology were considered consistent with oligonucleotide uptake and not considered adverse. There were dose-dependent decreases in hepatic PKK mRNA expression and dose-dependent and time-dependent decreases in PKK plasma protein after treatment with ISIS 721744 at \ge 2 mg/kg/dose at the interim and/or terminal sacrifices. Both hepatic PKK mRNA expression and plasma protein increased by the end of the recovery periods. Tissue concentrations of unconjugated ISIS 721744 in liver or kidney increased in a dose-dependent manner. The no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL) was 6 mg/kg/week based on thrombocytopenia in two monkeys at the higher dose levels of 12 and 30 mg/kg/dose. The NOAEL corresponded to a C_{max} of 6.57 mcg/mL and an AUC_{0-48hr} of 37.6 mcg*hr/mL on Day 273.
L2934: In the pivotal chronic toxicity study in mice (not a pharmacologically relevant species), mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (1, 4, or 12 mg/kg/dose), or mouse surrogate, ISIS 722059, (4 mg/kg/dose) once every two weeks (Q2W) for 26 weeks with a 13-week treatment-free recovery period (vehicle control and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 dose groups only). This study, as designed, could assess potential off-target effects of ISIS 721744 and potential on-target effects using the mouse surrogate, ISIS 722059. Changes in clinical chemistry parameters at the end of the 26-week treatment period included increases in alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), and/or alkaline phosphatase (ALP) in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. Effects on clinical chemistry parameters (including ALT, AST, and ALP) were less clear at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. At the end of the 13-week recovery period, increases in ALT and/or AST were still seen in males and/or females at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, while increases in ALP were no longer seen. The toxicological significance of increases in ALT and AST were unclear as histopathology findings in the liver appeared to be partially reversible and levels of unconjugated ISIS 721744 had declined below the lower limit of quantitation. Histopathology findings after the 26-week treatment period with ISIS 721744 were seen in the liver, skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, inguinal lymph nodes, and spleen. Histopathology findings after the 26-week treatment with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 were seen in the skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, spleen, and testis.
L2935: - Liver: Minimal or slight centrilobular hepatocellular hypertrophy was noted in males at 1, 4, and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and in one female (moderate) at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. This finding correlated with increased mean liver weights at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and increased liver enzymes (AST, ALT, and/or ALP). Despite a background incidence of hepatocyte vacuolation in vehicle control males, there was an increase in the severity (slight to marked) of hepatocyte vacuolation in males at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, which correlated with gross pathology findings of liver discoloration at all dose levels. These changes were attributed to uptake of ISIS 721744 into the liver.
L2936: - **Skin/Subcutis:** Increased incidences and/or severity of infiltrates of mononuclear cells, mixed cells, and/or vacuolated macrophages in the skin/subcutis were noted in males and/or females at 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and/or 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. Increased incidences and/or severity of vacuolated fibrocytes in the skin/subcutis were noted in males and/or females at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. Slight to moderate inflammation in the skin was noted in females at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. These findings in the skin/subcutis correlated with increased leukocyte counts.
- **SC dose sites:** Increased incidences and/or severity of infiltrates of vacuolated macrophages, mononuclear cells, and mixed cells, as well as fibrocyte vacuolation at the SC injection sites were noted in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and/or 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. These findings at the SC injection sites correlated with increased leukocyte counts.
- **Inguinal Lymph Nodes:** Increased incidences and severities (minimal to marked) of increased lymphocytes in males at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and one female at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were noted in the inguinal lymph node. This finding in the inguinal lymph node correlated with increased leukocyte counts. Amyloid in the inguinal lymph node was noted in one male at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
- **Spleen:** Increased incidence and/or severity of extramedullary hematopoiesis in the spleen was noted in males and/or females at 1, 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059 and correlated with increased mean spleen weight in males administered 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744.
- **Testis:** Moderate interstitial cell hyperplasia, minimal sperm stasis, and minimal vacuolation were noted in the testis of males at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
L2937: Histopathology findings after the 13-week recovery period at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were still noted in the liver as hepatocellular vacuolation in males and females, which correlated with increased liver weights. Histopathology findings in the skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, inguinal lymph nodes, and spleen at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were not seen at the end of the recovery period.
L2938: Unconjugated ISIS 721744 was measurable in a dose-dependent manner in the kidney (greater than dose proportional) and liver (dose proportional) after 26 weeks of treatment with ISIS 721744. The mean concentrations of unconjugated ISIS 721744 were similar in the kidney and liver except at 12 mg/kg/dose where mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were greater in the kidney than in the liver. Mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were higher in females than in males in the kidney but similar in the liver. After the 13-week treatment-free recovery period at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were below or near the lower limit of quantitation of 0.107 mcg/g, suggesting complete clearance of ISIS 721744.
L2939: Mouse PKK mRNA in mouse liver was reduced by 77% (statistically significant) compared to vehicle control in mice treated with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 at 4 mg/kg/dose for 26 weeks.
L2940: The NOAEL was 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, as test article-related findings were considered related to the oligonucleotide uptake.
L2941: ## *Conclusions*
L2942: The nonclinical pharmacology and toxicology studies were adequate to support the safety of donidalorsen for marketing. There are no outstanding concerns from the nonclinical perspective.
L2943: ## 1.3 Recommendations
L2944: ## 1.3.1 Appovability
L2945: From the nonclinical perspective, NDA 219407 is recommended for approval. There are no outstanding nonclinical issues.
L2946: ## 1.3.2 Additional Nonclinical Recommendations

L2963: ## Structure or Biochemical Description
L2964: The structure of donidalorsen sodium is shown in **Figure 1** (Applicant's Figure).
L2965: ISIS 721744 is a 20-mer chimeric 2'-MOE-modified ASO with a mixed backbone made up of PS and PO internucleotide linkages, which targets the mRNA of human PKK. The ASO is conjugated to triantennary GalNAc via a THA-C6 linker, which preferentially delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by binding to the ASGPR on liver cells.
L2966: **Figure 1** Structure of Donidalorsen Sodium (Applicant's Figure)
L2967: Chemical structure diagram of Donidalorsen Sodium (Applicant's Figure). The molecule consists of a central GalNAc moiety linked to a PKR-targeted ASO sequence. The GalNAc moiety is attached to a long alkyl chain (R, where R = \text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OCH}_3) and a phosphate group (\text{Na}^+ \text{O-P=O}). The ASO sequence is a 2'-O-methyl oligonucleotide conjugated to a phosphorothioate backbone, featuring multiple internal 2'-O-methyl modifications and terminal modifications (e.g., \text{Na}^+ \text{S-P=O} and \text{Na}^+ \text{O-P=O} groups).
L2968: Pharmacologic Class
L2969: PKK-targeted GalNAc-conjugated ASO

L2972: ## 2.3 Drug Formulation
L2973: The donidalorsen drug product is a sterile, single-dose, ready-to-use parenteral solution for SC administration. The qualitative and quantitative drug product formulation is shown in **Table 1** (Applicant's Table). The drug product is packaged in a staked needle glass prefilled syringe (PFS) closed with a (b) (4) rubber plunger stopper. The PFS is assembled into an autoinjector for the final drug product presentation. The autoinjector delivers a single dose of 80 mg donidalorsen.

L2989: ## 2.6 Proposed Clinical Population and Dosing Regimen
L2990: Donidalorsen is indicated for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of HAE in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. The recommended dosage is 80 mg administered SC (b) (4). A dosing interval of (b) (4) may be considered in some patients.
L2991: ## 2.7 Regulatory Background
L2992: Provided below is a summary of the regulatory background for the donidalorsen development program.
L2993: There was no pre-IND under the associated IND 142564. New IND 142564 was received on 07/15/2019 for a phase 2a clinical study (Protocol No. ISIS 721744-CS2) to assess the clinical efficacy of 80 mg ISIS 721744 (once monthly for 12-weeks) in patients with HAE. The clinical study was allowed to proceed based on the 30-day safety review and subsequently nonhold comments were provided in the Study May Proceed later dated 09/30/2019.
L2994: A Type B End of Phase 2 (EOP2) meeting teleconference meeting between the Sponsor and the FDA occurred on 08/30/2021 to discuss the adequacy of the existing and proposed nonclinical and clinical development package to support a marketing application for ISIS 721744 for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of HAE in patients 12 years of age and older. The Nonclinical Team indicated that the nonclinical evaluation of the metabolism of ISIS 721744 and its THA linker was limited. As such, the Sponsor was asked to provide data that characterizes the metabolism of ISIS 721744 and its THA linker through literature (Sponsor's work and/or non-proprietary literature) and actual metabolism studies in monkey and mouse (as needed) prior to the start of phase 3 clinical studies to demonstrate reasonable comparability to human metabolism. In addition, the FDA agreed that an embryofetal development (EFD) study of ISIS 721744 in rabbits was not needed. Refer to IND 142564 EOP2 Meeting Minutes dated 10/18/2021 for added details. Also, refer to NDA 219407 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 03/05/2025 for added details on the regulatory history related to the reproductive and developmental toxicology program.
L2995: The initial Pediatric Study Plan (iPSP) for ISIS 721744 for HAE was submitted on 11/18/2021, with subsequent revisions submitted on 05/03/2022, and the agreed iPSP submitted on 06/06/2022. As part of the iPSP, the Sponsor indicated that they planned to conduct a 13-week repeat-dose toxicity study of ISIS 721744 in juvenile CD-1 mice with a 6-week recovery period to support the inclusion of patients with HAE between 2 to &lt;12 years of age. FDA communicated that a draft unaudited report of the juvenile toxicity study in mice should be available prior to the start of the pediatric clinical trial and a final report would be expected within 120 days after providing the draft unaudited report. As such, the Sponsor submitted the draft protocol for the juvenile toxicity study in mice on 07/11/2023 (see IND 142564 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 08/28/2023). The FDA communicated comments on the draft protocol to the Sponsor on 08/31/2023.
L2996: A Special Protocol Assessment (SPA) 1 for the 2-year study in rats was submitted on 08/05/2022 and denied on 08/17/2022 due to the lack of SEND datasets for the supporting 16-week dose range finding study in rats. SPA 1 was resubmitted on 09/30/2022 with the SEND datasets. FDA agreed with the proposed 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats on 11/04/2022. SPA 2, which proposed a 6-month carcinogenicity study in Tg.rasH2 mice, was submitted on 10/12/2022, and was agreed
L2997: upon on 11/16/2022 for male mice but not for female mice (as no acceptable basis for dose selection could be identified).
L2998: In pre-NDA meeting preliminary comments (Refer to IND 142564 pre-NDA Meeting Preliminary Comments dated 04/10/2024), the FDA agreed that it would be acceptable to submit the report of the 6-month carcinogenicity study in Tg.rasH2 mice and a summary of the in-life data for the 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats at the time of the NDA submission and to submit the final report as a PMR.
L2999: Refer to the NDA 219407 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 12/19/2024 for added details on the regulatory history related to the genetic toxicology and carcinogenicity programs.
L3000: NDA 219407 for donidalorsen was submitted on 08/21/2024, and the application was filed on 10/20/2024, for standard review, with a user fee goal date of 08/21/2025.

L3034: ## 4 Pharmacology
L3035: ## 4.1 Primary Pharmacology
L3036: As described in **Section 3.1**, most of the primary pharmacology studies for the nonclinical development of ISIS 721744 were previously reviewed (refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019). Included below is a review of two primary pharmacology studies not previously reviewed.
L3037: ## In Vitro Characterization of Human Prekallikrein Antisense Oligonucleotide ISIS 721744 Activity (Study No. ECID129371)
L3038: Two human hepatocellular carcinoma cell lines (HepaRG and Hep3b) were electroporated with ISIS 546254 (unconjugated parent compound of ISIS 721744 with the same sequence) or ISIS 141923 (control oligonucleotide with no matches to any sites within the human transcriptome) and incubated for 24 hours under the experimental conditions of the study, lysed for RNA isolation, and analyzed for human PKK mRNA. As described in the study report, the sequence of ISIS 546254 was identified from screens and dose-response confirmations of over 1300 unconjugated ASOs that were designed throughout the human PKK primary transcript and then determined to be a lead compound for its ability to inhibit the level of PKK mRNA at a single concentration in the human hepatocellular carcinoma cell line, HepaRG.
L3039: As shown in **Figure 2** (Applicant's Figure), ISIS 546254 reduced human PKK mRNA levels by greater than 90% in a concentration-dependent manner in human hepatocellular cell lines HepaRG and Hep3b with corresponding IC_{50} of 0.31 mcM and 0.35 mcM, respectively. The control oligonucleotide ISIS 141923 did not reduce PKK mRNA in either cell line.
L3040: **Figure 2** Concentration-Dependent Reduction of Human PKK mRNA in Human Hepatocellular Carcinoma Cells by ISIS 546254 (Applicant's Figure)
L3041: A.
L3042: B.
L3043: **Figure 2:** Concentration-Dependent Reduction of Human PKK mRNA in Human Hepatocellular Carcinoma Cells upon ISIS 546254 Treatment
L3044: ISIS 546254 was evaluated for its ability to reduce human PKK mRNA in 2 different human hepatocellular carcinoma cell lines (A) HepaRG and (B) Hep3B. Compounds were transfected into the cells with electroporation (t = 24 hours). Results represent the mean \pm standard deviation as percentages relative to UTC (* P &lt; 0.05 vs. UTC).
L3045: ## In Vivo Evaluation of ISIS 721744 Activity in Human KLKB1/PKK Transgenic Mice (Study No. ELN 23-100d)
L3046: Transgenic mice expressing the human KLKB1/PKK gene (n = 2 males/group + 2 females/group) were treated with single SC dose levels of ISIS 721744 at 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, and 10 mg/kg. Blood was collected on Days -1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 42 and 56 and human PKK plasma protein levels were evaluated by ELISA.
L3047: As shown in **Figure 3** (Applicant's Figure), ISIS 721744 reduced plasma human PKK protein in human KLKB1/PKK transgenic mice in a dose- and time-dependent manner. Human PKK protein was reduced up to a maximum of about 91% on Day 14 after treatment with 10 mg/kg ISIS 721744. After Day 14, plasma PKK protein levels gradually increased to baseline levels and were restored by Day 42 or Day 56 at 1 mg/kg or 3 mg/kg ISIS 721744, respectively. At Day 56, PKK levels plasma PKK protein levels at 10 mg/kg were still 20% below baseline levels.
L3048: As shown in **Figure 4** (Applicant's Figure), based on non-linear curve fit analysis, ED50 at Days 7 and 14 after treatment with ISIS 721744 was 0.67 and 0.75 mg/kg, respectively.

L3057: ## 4.3 Safety Pharmacology
L3058: As described in **Section 3.1**, the GLP-compliant safety pharmacology study for the evaluation of cardiovascular, respiratory, and CNS parameters following SC administration of ISIS 721744 in Cynomolgus monkeys was previously reviewed (refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019). Included below is a review of the GLP-compliant hERG assay with ISIS 721744.
L3059: ## Effect of ISIS 721744 on Cloned hERG Potassium Channels Expressed in Human Embryonic Kidney Cells (Study No. 210830.JTJ; 721744-IS08)
L3060: HEK-293 cells were stably transfected with hERG cDNA and treated with ISIS 721744 (30 and 300 mcM) at near-physiological temperature to measure the effect on ionic currents by whole-cell patch-clamp technique.
L3061: ISIS 721744 inhibited hERG current by 0.5% and 1.9% at 30 mcM and 300 mcM, respectively (not statistically significant) versus 2.4% for the vehicle control. The IC50 for
L3062: the inhibitory effect of ISIS 721744 on hERG potassium current was not calculated but was estimated to be greater than 300 \text{mC}\text{M}. The positive control article (60 nM terfenadine) inhibited hERG potassium current by 85.6%. In general, oligonucleotides are not thought to interact with the hERG channel.
L3063: ## 5 Pharmacokinetics/ADME/Toxicokinetics
L3064: ## 5.1 PK/ADME
L3065: As described in **Section 3.1**, the in vitro evaluation of the extent of plasma protein binding of ISIS 721744 in human, monkey, and mouse plasma by ultrafiltration was previously reviewed (refer to IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019). Included below are the PK/ADME studies not previously reviewed.
L3066: ## Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism and Excretion of [3H]ISIS 721744 following a Single Subcutaneous Dose Administration to Sprague Dawley Rats (Study No. IPI/06: 721744-APK02)
L3067: This study determined the ADME properties of [3H]ISIS 721744 (2 or 10 mg/kg) after single SC administration to non-pigmented Sprague Dawley rats.
L3068: - PK parameters and tissue distribution of total radioactivity were evaluated in blood, plasma, and tissues after single SC administration of [3H]ISIS 721744 at 2 mg/kg and a radioactive dose level of 200 \mu\text{Ci}/\text{kg} to male non-pigmented Sprague Dawley rats.
- Mass balance and routes and extent of excretion of total radioactivity were evaluated after single SC administration of [3H]ISIS 721744 at 2 mg/kg and a radioactive dose level of 200 \mu\text{Ci}/\text{kg} to male non-pigmented Sprague Dawley rats.
- Tissue distribution of radioactivity was evaluated using Quantitative Whole Body Autoradiography (QWBA) after single SC administration of [3H]ISIS 721744 at 10 mg/kg and a radioactive dose level of 500 \mu\text{Ci}/\text{kg} to male and female non-pigmented Sprague Dawley rats.
- Metabolite identification and profiling was evaluated after single SC administration of [3H]ISIS 721744 at 10 mg/kg and a radioactive dose level of 500 \mu\text{Ci}/\text{kg} to male and female non-pigmented Sprague Dawley rats.
- One male non-pigmented Sprague Dawley rat served as a control (i.e., received a single SC dose of sterile isotonic saline).
L3069: Following a single SC dose of [3H]ISIS 721744 at 2 mg/kg to male non-pigmented Sprague Dawley rats, C_{\text{max}} of 0.375 and 0.538 \mu\text{g} equiv./mL were reached in the blood and plasma, respectively, at 1 hour for both, after which radioactivity declined in a biphasic manner. The blood:plasma ratio calculated from \text{AUC}_{0..\infty} was 0.76. C_{\text{max}} (\mu\text{g} equiv./g) of 24.40 at 24 hours and 14.89 at 168 hours were reached in the liver and kidney, respectively. Most tissues achieved concentrations similar to or slightly above the blood radioactivity concentrations. Tissue:blood ratios at 24 hours were highest in the liver and kidney (1877 and 850, respectively) consistent with uptake of ISIS 721744. The thyroid gland, pancreas, large and small intestine, spleen, lymph node, and bone marrow had tissue:blood ratios between 24.2 to 69.2 at 24 hours.
L3070: Following a single SC dose of [3H]ISIS 721744 at 2 mg/kg to male non-pigmented Sprague Dawley rats, the mean cumulative recovery (0 to Day 56) of radioactivity in excreta was 76.8% (17.14% from urine + 57.46% from feces + 2.16% from cage wash). Residual radioactivity in the carcass on Day 56 accounted for 5.84% of the administered dose resulting in an overall recovery of 82.6%.
L3071: Following a single SC dose of [3H]ISIS 721744 at 10 mg/kg to male and female non-pigmented rats, radioactivity was distributed to tissues by the first sampling time at 2 hours and reached maximal concentrations within 2 to 48 hours postdose with highest concentrations of radioactivity in the kidney, liver, intestinal mucosa, salivary gland, bone marrow, lymph nodes and splenic red pulp. Concentrations of radioactivity in most organs/tissues decreased by the end of the sampling period at 336 hours, except for the kidney where radioactivity levels remained at similar levels throughout the sampling period.
L3072: Recovery of radioactivity in urine and feces from non-pigmented rats following a single SC dose of [3H]ISIS 721744 at 10 mg/kg was 0.35% and 1.37% of dose, respectively for males and 0.30% and 1.31% of dose, respectively for females. See also below.
L3073: ## **Metabolite Profiling and Identification Studies following a Single Subcutaneous Dose Administration of [3H]ISIS 721744 to Male and Female Rats (Study No. IPI/07; 721744-APK02)**
L3074: This study evaluated the metabolic profile of ISIS 721744 in rat whole blood and plasma, liver and kidney tissues, and in the excreta (urine and feces) by liquid chromatography mass spectrometry (LC-MS) after single SC administration of [3H]ISIS 721744 at 10 mg/kg to male and female non-pigmented rats.
L3075: A summary of metabolites is shown in **Table 2** (Applicant's Table).
L3076: ISIS 721744 was seen in the liver, kidney, plasma and whole blood. ISIS 721744 was the major component at 2 hours in plasma and blood but was not detected at 24 hours in plasma and blood. Unconjugated ISIS 721744 (i.e. ISIS 780124) was the major component in liver (2 and 24 hours) and kidney (24 hours). Two major components were present in the kidney at 2 hours: unconjugated ISIS 721744 (i.e. ISIS 780124) and ISIS 721744 minus 3 GalNAc sugars (i.e. ISIS 721744 -3 GalNAc). Two major components were detected in feces samples at 0 to 24 hours: ISIS 780124 3'N-18 and ISIS 780124 3'N-17. Several ISIS 780124 shortmers were identified as major components in urine at 0 to 24 hours, from ISIS 780124 3'N-10 to ISIS 780124 3'N-14.
L3077: As described in the study report, all identified metabolites were consistent with nuclease-mediated metabolism to chain shortened oligonucleotides with full, partial, or without GalNAc or linker-conjugation.

L3123: ## **Metabolic Profiling and Identification of ISIS 721744 Oligonucleotide-Related Metabolites by HPLC-HRMS in Select Urine Samples from Mice, Monkeys, and Humans (Study No. 727-085, 727-081, ISIS 721744-CS1; 721744-IS10)**
L3124: This study identified ISIS 721744 oligonucleotide containing metabolites (full-length or chain-shortened) from urine samples at steady state from mice, monkeys, and humans treated with multiple SC doses of ISIS 721744 (i.e., 10 mg/kg dose group from 13-week repeat-dose toxicity study in mice [Study No. 721744-AS01]; 30 mg/kg dose group from 39-week repeat-dose toxicity study in monkeys [Study No. 721744-AS02]; and 80 mg dose group from phase 1 study in humans with dosing every four weeks for four total doses [Study No. ISIS 721744-CS1]) using liquid chromatography with a tandem ultraviolet (UV) detector and high-resolution mass spectrometer (HPLC/UV/HRMS) method.
L3125: As described in the study report:
L3126: The oligonucleotide portions of conjugated ASO molecules are metabolized by hydrolysis of the phosphodiester bonds via endo-nuclease and/or exo-nuclease (either 5' and/or 3') enzymes. Metabolism of the GalNAc-conjugation component of ISIS 721744 typically occurs by a sequential loss of the three GalNAc sugar moieties (-1, -2, and -3 GalNAc), followed by the loss of a portion, or all the remaining THA linker.1,2 Complete loss of the THA linker results in the formation of ISIS 780124, the unconjugated version of ISIS 721744. The metabolism of the two portions of ISIS 721744 (oligonucleotide and GalNAc) may occur simultaneously resulting in many potential metabolites with multiple potential metabolic pathways responsible for a single metabolite compound.
L3127: The study report grouped the likely metabolites of ISIS 721744 as follows:
L3128: 1Weidolf L, Björkbom A, Dahlén A, Elebring M, Gennemark P, Hölttä M, Janzén D, Li X, Andersson S. Distribution and biotransformation of therapeutic antisense oligonucleotides and conjugates. Drug Discov Today. 2021 Oct;26(10):2244-2258.
L3129: 2Shemesh CS, Yu RZ, Gaus HJ, Greenlee S, Post N, Schmidt K, Migawa MT, Seth PP, Zanardi TA, Prakash TP, Swayze EE, Henry SP, Wang Y. Elucidation of the Biotransformation Pathways of a Galnac3-conjugated Antisense Oligonucleotide in Rats and Monkeys. Mol Ther Nucleic Acids. 2016 May 10;5(5):e319.
L3130: - Families I through IV arise from multiple routes of sequential hydrolysis of the GalNAc and THA linker portion of ISIS 721744:Family I: Intact GalNAc and linker attached, and loss of the nucleotides at the 3'-end to produce 3' n-X metabolites.
- Family II: Loss of one GalNAc sugar to become ISIS 721744-(\text{GalNAc})_2THA-20-mer, and loss of nucleotides at the 3'-end to produce 3' n-X metabolites.
- Family III: Loss of two GalNAc sugars to become ISIS 721744-(\text{GalNAc})_1THA-20-mer, followed by sequential loss of the nucleotides at the 3'-end to produce 3' n-X metabolites.
- Family IV: Loss of three GalNAc sugars to become ISIS 721744-(\text{GalNAc})_0THA-20-mer, followed by sequential loss of the nucleotides at the 3'-end to produce 3' n-X metabolites.
- Family V: Hydrolysis of the entire linker of ISIS 721744 to form ISIS 780124 (fully unconjugated ISIS 721744) followed by subsequent endo- and exo-nuclease hydrolysis (3'-deletion and 5'-deletion) to produce 3'- and 5' n-X metabolites.
- Family VI: Hydrolysis of the entire linker of ISIS 721744 to form ISIS 780124 (fully unconjugated ISIS 721744), while retaining the 5' phosphate group (5'PO ISIS 780124). This metabolite then undergoes endo- and exo-nuclease hydrolysis (5'-deletion) to produce 5' n-X metabolites.
L3131: X represents the number of nucleotides that have been removed from the full length ASO.
L3132: A diagram of the proposed putative metabolism of donidalorsen is shown in **Figure 5** (Applicant's Figure).
L3133: **Mouse Urine:** ISIS 721744 was the major component (about 53% of total oligonucleotide signal) in mouse urine samples when administered at 10 mg/kg. As described by the Applicant, other oligonucleotide metabolites included the full-length ASO with partial conjugations, fully and partially conjugated donidalorsen with loss of nucleotides from the 3'-end (referred to as 3'-deletion chain-shortened metabolites), and unconjugated donidalorsen with loss of nucleotides from the 5'-end (referred to as 5'-deletion chain-shortened metabolites).
L3134: **Monkey Urine:** ISIS 721744 was the major component (about 41% of total oligonucleotide signal), followed by ISIS 780124 (unconjugated version of ISIS 721744; about 14% of total oligonucleotide signal) in the monkey urine samples when administered at 30 mg/kg. As described by the Applicant, other identified metabolites were 3'-deletion chain-shortened metabolites of donidalorsen (with GalNAc sugar moieties and THA linker attached), as well as metabolites of unconjugated donidalorsen with loss of nucleotides from the 5'-end.
L3135: **Human Urine:** ISIS 780124 (unconjugated version of ISIS 721744) was the major component (about 38% of total oligonucleotide signal) in human urine samples when administered at 80 mg/kg. ISIS 721744 was not detected. As described by the Applicant, the other most abundant metabolites were from unconjugated donidalorsen
L3136: with loss of nucleotides from the 5'-end. However, 3'-deletion chain-shortened metabolites of donidalorsen (with GalNAc sugar moieties and THA linker attached) were also seen.
L3137: There were no unique metabolites found in humans compared to mice or monkeys.

L3140: ## Profiling, Identification, and Quantitation of ISIS 721744 Linker-Related Metabolites by HPLC-MS/MS in Select Plasma, Urine, and Fecal Samples from Mice, Monkeys, and Humans (Study No. 721744-IS12)
L3141: This study identified linker-only-related metabolites of ISIS 721744 (no full-length or chain-shortened oligonucleotide components) from plasma (monkey and human), urine (mouse, monkey, and human), and feces (monkey) after SC dosing of ISIS 721744 (i.e., 2 and/or 10 mg/kg dose groups from 13-week repeat-dose toxicity study in mice [Study No. 721744-AS01]; 2 and/or 30 mg/kg dose group from 39-week repeat-dose toxicity study in monkeys [Study No. 721744-AS02]; and 80 mg dose group from phase 1 study in humans with dosing every four weeks for four total doses [Study No. ISIS 721744-CS1]) by a HPLC-MS/MS method. Eleven total linker metabolites (putative linker metabolites M4 to M14) were monitored in these studies.
L3142: Six linker metabolites were detected in monkey plasma (M5 and M8 to M12) and three linker metabolites were detected in human plasma (M5, M8, and M12).
L3143: Ten linker metabolites (M5 to M14) were similarly detected in mouse, monkey, and human urine. The linker metabolites with the highest peak area ratios were M8, M5, and M12, which were consistent across the three species.
L3144: Ten linker metabolites (M5 to M14) were detected in monkey feces. The linker metabolites with the highest peak area ratios were M8, M10, M11, and M5.
L3145: As described by the Applicant: The THA-linker-related metabolism is generally similar across species with oxidative metabolites being formed and eliminated through urine and bile. The overall metabolic pathways for the THA-linker-related metabolites of donidalorsen involve hydrolysis of GalNAc sugars and oligonucleotide moieties to form M4 metabolite, followed by internal cyclization of M4 to form cyclized linker M5 metabolite which would then undergo mono- and di-oxidation to form M6 and M7 metabolites. Dephosphorylation of M4 metabolite resulted in the formation of M8 metabolite followed by sequential oxidation at each branching arm of M8 metabolite to form mono-, di-, tri-, and tetra-oxidation metabolites (M9- M12 metabolites). Additional metabolites resulting from dealkylation (M13 metabolite), or deamination (M14 metabolite) were also detected. The proposed pathway for the metabolism of linker-related moieties of donidalorsen is shown in **Figure 6** (Applicant's Figure).3
L3146: 3Shemesh CS, Yu RZ, Gaus HJ, Greenlee S, Post N, Schmidt K, Migawa MT, Seth PP, Zanardi TA, Prakash TP, Swayze EE, Henry SP, Wang Y. Elucidation of the Biotransformation Pathways of a Galnac3-conjugated Antisense Oligonucleotide in Rats and Monkeys. Mol Ther Nucleic Acids. 2016 May 10;5(5):e319.
L3147: Figure 6 Proposed Biotransformation Pathway for the Linker-Related Metabolism of Donidalorsen (Applicant's Figure)
L3148: Figure 6 illustrates the proposed biotransformation pathway for the linker-related metabolism of Donidalorsen (ISIS 721744). The pathway starts with ISIS 721744, which undergoes dephosphorylation (Phosphatase) to form M4. M4 is then metabolized sequentially via hydrolysis (-H_2O) to M5, and subsequent oxidation ([O]) steps to M6 and M7. M7 is further oxidized ([O]) to M8. M8 is then oxidized ([O]) to M9, M10, M11, and M12. M8 and M9 are shown to undergo a reaction involving HO^- (indicated by a dashed line and X) leading to M13. M13 is shown to be a precursor for M14, which is formed via oxidation ([O]) of M13.
L3149: ## 6 General Toxicology
L3150: As described in **Section 3.1**, the pivotal GLP-compliant 39-week repeat-dose toxicity study of ISIS 721744 in Cynomolgus monkeys with a 13-week interim necropsy and a 26-week recovery period was previously reviewed (refer to IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019). The monkey is considered a pharmacologically relevant species for ISIS 721744 nonclinical evaluations.
L3151: Reviewed below is the pivotal GLP-compliant 26-week repeat-dose toxicity study of ISIS 721744 and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 in mice with a 13-week recovery period. The mouse is not a pharmacologically relevant species for ISIS 721744 nonclinical evaluations. This study, as designed, could assess potential off-target effects of ISIS 721744 and potential on-target effects using the mouse surrogate, ISIS 722059.
L3152: ## 6.2 Repeat-Dose Toxicity
L3153: ## Study title: A 26-Week Repeat Dose Toxicity Study of ISIS 721744 in Mice with a 13-Week Recovery
L3154: Study no.:	8405032 (721744-AS04)
Study report location:	Electronic Document Room (EDR)
Supporting Document Number (SDN) 1(b) (4)
Conducting laboratory and location:	
Date of study initiation:	03/25/2019
GLP compliance:	Yes
QA statement:	Yes
Drug, lot #, and % purity:	ISIS 721744, bulk test article lot #
CA721744-001, 89.5% purity
ISIS 722059, bulk material API lot #
722059-3, 79.3% purity
L3155: ## Key Study Findings
L3156: - In a repeat-dose toxicity study, mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (1, 4, or 12 mg/kg/dose), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4 mg/kg/dose) Q2W for 26 weeks with a 13-week treatment-free recovery period (vehicle control and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 dose groups only).
- There were no unscheduled deaths during the study that were considered related to treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
- Changes in hematology parameters at the end of the 26-week treatment period included increases in white blood cells, neutrophils, lymphocytes, and/or monocytes in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. At the end of the 13-week recovery period, increases in hematology parameters were no longer seen at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744.
- Changes in clinical chemistry parameters at the end of the 26-week treatment period included increases in ALT, AST, and/or ALP in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. Effects on clinical chemistry parameters (including ALT, AST, and ALP) were less clear at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. At the end of the 13-week recovery period, increases in ALT and/or AST were still seen in males and/or females at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, while increases in ALP were no longer seen. The toxicological significance of increases in ALT and AST were unclear as histopathology findings in the liver appeared to be partially reversible and levels of unconjugated ISIS 721744 had declined below the lower limit of quantitation.
L3157: - Gross pathology findings after the 26-week treatment period with ISIS 721744 were seen in the liver (discoloration in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and enlargement in males at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744) and inguinal lymph nodes (enlarged in males at 1 and 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744). There were no clear gross pathology findings seen after the 26-week treatment period with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059. Gross pathology findings after the 13-week recovery period for 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were noted in the liver (discoloration in males) and subcutaneous injection site (discoloration in males).
- Organ weight changes after the 26-week treatment period with ISIS 721744 included increases in liver weights in males and/or females at 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose and increases in spleen weights in males at 12 mg/kg/dose. There were no organ weight changes after the 26-week treatment period with 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. At the end of the 13-week recovery period for 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, liver weights were still increased in males and/or females.
- Histopathology findings after the 26-week treatment period with ISIS 721744 were seen in the liver, skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, inguinal lymph nodes, and spleen. Histopathology findings after the 26-week treatment with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 were seen in the skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, spleen, and testis.Liver: Minimal or slight centrilobular hepatocellular hypertrophy was noted in males at 1, 4, and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and in one female (moderate) at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. This finding correlated with increased mean liver weights at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and increased liver enzymes (AST, ALT, and/or ALP). Despite a background incidence of hepatocyte vacuolation in vehicle control males, there was an increase in the severity (slight to marked) of hepatocyte vacuolation in males at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, which correlated with gross pathology findings of liver discoloration at all dose levels. These findings were consistent with uptake of ISIS721744.
- Skin/Subcutis: Increased incidences and/or severity of infiltrates of mononuclear cells, mixed cells, and/or vacuolated macrophages in the skin/subcutis were noted in males and/or females at 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and/or ISIS 722059 at 4 mg/kg/dose. Increased incidences and/or severity of vacuolated fibrocytes in the skin/subcutis were noted in males and/or females at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and ISIS 722059 at 4 mg/kg/dose. Slight to moderate inflammation in the skin was noted in females at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. These findings in the skin/subcutis correlated with increased leukocyte counts.
- SC Dose Sites: Increased incidences and/or severity of infiltrates of vacuolated macrophages, mononuclear cells, and mixed cells, as well as fibrocyte vacuolation at the SC injection sites were noted in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and/or 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. These findings at the SC injection sites correlated with increased leukocyte counts.
L3158: - Inguinal Lymph Nodes: Increased incidences and severities (minimal to marked) of increased lymphocytes in males at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and one female at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were noted in the inguinal lymph node. This finding in the inguinal lymph node correlated with increased leukocyte counts. Amyloid in the inguinal lymph node was noted in one male at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
- Spleen: Increased incidence and/or severity of extramedullary hematopoiesis in the spleen was noted in males and/or females at 1, 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059 and correlated with increased mean spleen weight in males administered 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744.
- Testis: Moderate interstitial cell hyperplasia, minimal sperm stasis, and minimal vacuolation were noted in the testis of males at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
- Histopathology findings after the 13-week recovery period for 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were still noted in the liver as hepatocellular vacuolation in males and females, which correlated with increased liver weights. Histopathology findings in the skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, inguinal lymph nodes, and spleen at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were not seen at the end of the recovery period.
- Unconjugated ISIS 721744 was measurable in a dose-dependent manner in the kidney (greater than dose proportional) and liver (dose proportional) after 26 weeks of treatment with ISIS 721744. The mean concentrations of unconjugated ISIS 721744 were similar in the kidney and liver except at 12 mg/kg/dose where mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were greater in the kidney than in the liver. Mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were higher in females than in males in the kidney but similar in the liver. After the 13-week treatment-free recovery period at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were below or near the lower limit of quantitation of 0.107 mcg/g, suggesting complete clearance of ISIS 721744.
- Mouse PKK mRNA in mouse liver was reduced by 77% (statistically significant) compared to vehicle control in mice treated with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 at 4 mg/kg/dose for 26 weeks.
- The NOAEL was 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, as test article-related findings were considered related to the oligonucleotide uptake.

L3168: ## Observations and Results
L3169: ## Mortality
L3170: Animals were checked twice daily (AM and PM) for mortality.
L3171: There were no unscheduled deaths during the study that were considered related to treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
L3172: One male in the vehicle control group (No. M0006) was sacrificed in moribund condition on Day 94 of the treatment period due to a skin lesion in the dorsal cervical area that did not response to initial treatment with topical antibiotic cream on Day 57 and became worse by Day 93.
L3173: One female at 1 mg/kg/dose (No. M0610) was sacrificed in moribund condition on Day 155 of the treatment period due to an injury that was potentially cage-related.
L3174: ## Clinical Signs
L3175: Cageside observations were conducted once daily during the treatment and recovery periods. Detailed observations were conducted once during the predose period, once weekly during the treatment period, and once weekly during the recovery period. Dose site(s) were evaluated prior to dosing on each day of dosing, beginning on Day 15.
L3176: There were no clinical observations during the study that were considered related to treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
L3177: ## **Body Weights**
L3178: Body weights were recorded once during the predose period, weekly during the treatment period, and weekly during the recovery period.
L3179: There were no changes in body weight or body weight gain during the study that were considered related to treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
L3180: ## **Feed Consumption**
L3181: Quantitative food consumption (grams/animal/day) for each cage was determined weekly during the treatment period and recovery period.
L3182: There were no changes in feed consumption during the study that were considered related to treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
L3183: ## **Ophthalmoscopy**
L3184: Ophthalmic examinations of dilated eyes using an indirect ophthalmoscope were conducted by an ophthalmologist once during the predose period, once during Week 26 of the treatment period, and during the final week of the recovery period.
L3185: There were no ophthalmic findings during the study that were considered related to treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
L3186: ## **ECG**
L3187: Not evaluated
L3188: ## **Hematology**

- Lymphocytes were increased in males at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and in females at 1, 4, and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and in males and females at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
- Monocytes were increased in males and females at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and in males and females at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.

L3226: ## Organ Weights
L3227: Adrenal, brain, gall bladder, heart, kidney, liver with gallbladder, lung with large bronchi, ovary with oviduct, prostate, seminal vesicle, spleen, testis, thymus, and uterus with cervix were weighed on Day 185 of the treatment period and on Recovery Day 91 (Day 275) of the recovery period. Paired organs were weighed together.
L3228: Notable organ weight changes at the end of the treatment period sacrifice are shown in **Table 13**. Liver weights (absolute, relative to body weight, and/or relative to brain weight) were increased in males and/or females at 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. Increased liver weights correlated with gross pathology finding of enlarged liver in two males and histopathology finding of hepatocellular hypertrophy in some males
L3229: and one female. Spleen weights (absolute, relative to body weight, and/or relative to brain weight) were increased in males at 12 mg/kg/dose. Increased spleen weight correlated with histopathology finding of increased extramedullary hematopoiesis. There were no organ weight changes at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
L3230: Notable organ weight changes at the end of the recovery period sacrifice at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 are shown in **Table 14**. Liver weights (absolute, relative to body weight, and/or relative to brain weight) were still increased in males and/or females and correlated with histopathology finding of hepatocyte vacuolation.

L3246: ## Peer Review
L3247: Yes. The Applicant conducted an independent peer review of the primary histopathology evaluation. As stated in the study report, a retrospective peer review of the liver and testes was conducted by a different Ionis pathologist than the original contemporaneous peer review.
L3248: ## Histological Findings
L3249: As shown in **Table 16**, histopathology findings at the end of treatment with ISIS 721744 were seen in the liver, skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, inguinal lymph nodes, and spleen. Histopathology findings at the end of treatment with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 were seen in the skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, spleen, and testis.
L3250: - **Liver:** Minimal or slight centrilobular hepatocellular hypertrophy was noted in males at 1, 4, and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and in one female (moderate) at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. This finding correlated with increased mean liver weights at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and increased liver enzymes (AST, ALT, and/or ALP). Despite a background incidence of hepatocyte vacuolation in vehicle control males, there was an increase in the severity (slight to marked) of hepatocyte vacuolation in males at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, which correlated with gross pathology findings of liver discoloration at all dose levels. These findings correlated with uptake of ISIS 721744 into the liver.
- **Skin/Subcutis:** Increased incidences and/or severity of infiltrates of mononuclear cells, mixed cells, and/or vacuolated macrophages in the skin/subcutis were noted in males and/or females at 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and/or 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. Increased incidences and/or severity of vacuolated fibrocytes in the skin/subcutis were noted in males and/or females at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. Slight to moderate inflammation in the skin was noted in females at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. These findings in the skin/subcutis correlated with increased leukocyte counts.
- **SC Dose Sites:** Increased incidences and/or severity of infiltrates of vacuolated macrophages, mononuclear cells, and mixed cells, as well as fibrocyte vacuolation at the SC injection sites were noted in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and/or 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. These findings at the SC injection sites correlated with increased leukocyte counts.
- **Inguinal Lymph Nodes:** Increased incidences and severities (minimal to marked) of increased lymphocytes in males at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and one female at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were noted in the inguinal lymph node. This finding in the inguinal lymph node correlated with increased leukocyte counts. Amyloid in the inguinal lymph node was noted in one male at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
- **Spleen:** Increased incidence and/or severity of extramedullary hematopoiesis in the spleen was noted in males and/or females at 1, 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059 and correlated with increased mean spleen weight in males administered 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744.
L3251: - Testis: Moderate interstitial cell hyperplasia, minimal sperm stasis, and minimal vacuolation were noted in the testis of males at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
L3252: As shown in **Table 17**, histopathology findings at the recovery period sacrifice at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were still noted in the liver as hepatocellular vacuolation in males and females, which correlated with increased liver weights. Histopathology findings in the skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, inguinal lymph nodes, and/or spleen were either not seen or less evident at the end of the recovery period at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744.

L3265: ## Special Evaluation
L3266: ## Exploratory Cytokine/Chemokine Analysis
L3267: Blood was collected for cytokine/chemokine analysis (IFN-\gamma, IL-1\beta, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-10, IL-13, TNF-\alpha, and MCP-1A) using a multiplex assay kit on Day 185 of the treatment period and Recovery Day 91 of the recovery period.
L3268: There were no clear effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on concentrations of IFN-\gamma, IL-1\beta, IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-10, IL-13, TNF-\alpha, and MCP-1A.
L3269: IL-10, IL-13, IL-1\beta, IL-4, and IL-5 concentrations were below the limit of quantitation for samples tested from the vehicle control, ISIS 721744-treated, and ISIS 722059-treated groups.
L3270: IL-6 concentrations were at or below the limit of quantitation (&lt;29.5 pg/mL) for all samples tested in the vehicle control, ISIS 721744-treated, and ISIS 722059-treated groups except for male No. M0006 in the vehicle control group with an elevated IL-6 concentration (202 pg/mL) on Day 94 (animal was terminated for a non-treatment related injury).
L3271: IFN-\gamma concentrations were low or below the limit of quantitation (&lt;2.87 pg/mL) for most samples tested in the vehicle control, ISIS 721744-treated, and ISIS 722059-treated groups except for female No. M0606 at 1 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 with a slight increase in IFN-\gamma concentration (56.4 pg/mL).
L3272: TNF-\alpha concentrations were below the limit of quantitation (&lt;6.60 pg/mL) or just above the limit of quantitation for all samples tested in the vehicle control, ISIS 721744-treated, and ISIS 722059-treated groups.
L3273: MCP-1 was measurable at low concentrations in most samples in the vehicle control, ISIS 721744-treated, and ISIS 722059-treated groups with no clear effect of treatment.
L3274: ## Toxicokinetics
L3275: ## Tissue Analysis
L3276: Liver samples from vehicle control and ISIS 721744-treated groups and kidney samples from ISIS 721744-treated groups were analyzed for unconjugated ISIS 721744 by a validated UPLC-MS/MS analytical method.
L3277: There was no detectable unconjugated ISIS 721744 in the vehicle control liver samples.
L3278: As shown in **Table 18** (Applicant's Table), unconjugated ISIS 721744 was measurable in a dose-dependent manner in the kidney (greater than dose proportional) and liver (dose proportional) after 26 weeks of treatment with ISIS 721744. The mean concentrations of unconjugated ISIS 721744 were similar in the kidney and liver except at 12 mg/kg/dose where mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were greater in the kidney than in the liver. Mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were higher in females than in males in the kidney but similar in the liver. After the 13-week treatment-free recovery period, mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were below or near the lower limit of quantitation of 0.107 mcg/g, suggesting complete clearance of ISIS 721744 at this dose level.

L3285: ## PKK mRNA Analysis
L3286: Liver samples from vehicle control and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 were collected on Day 185 of the treatment period for PKK mRNA analysis by RT-PCR.
L3287: As shown in **Figure 7** (Applicant's Figure), mouse PKK mRNA in mouse liver was reduced by 77% (statistically significant) compared to vehicle control in mice treated with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 at 4 mg/kg/dose for 26 weeks.
