L3289: ## Dosing Solution Analysis
L3290: The test articles were provided preformulated by the Applicant. The Applicant conducted stability analyses on representative ISIS 721744 test articles within the bracketed concentrations of 0.1 and 200 mg/mL (lot # RP721744-009 and lot # RP721744-012, respectively) by a qualified ion-pair high-performance liquid chromatography with ultraviolet detection and mass spectrometry (IP-HPLC-UV-MS) method.
L3291: In the stability analysis for ISIS 721744 at 0.1 mg/mL, degradation impurities were increased &gt;50% in comparison to the ISIS 721744 release results, during the mass spectrum overlay assessment. Upon a more detailed evaluation, the level of degradation impurities was within the bulk drug substance specification limit and the label claim was within the acceptable range of (b)(4)% so the test article was considered suitable for use. There was no change in the impurity profile or stability for ISIS 721744 at 200 mg/mL.
L3292: All formulations were within \pm 15\% of the target concentrations, ranging from 94.8% to 109.5% of theoretical, and met the acceptance criteria for study use.
L3293: ## 11 Integrated Summary and Safety Evaluation
L3294: The Applicant is developing donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) as a prophylaxis to prevent attacks of HAE in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. ISIS 721744 is a GalNAc-conjugated ASO, which binds to human PKK mRNA to reduce PKK protein production. The GalNAc molecule preferentially delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by binding to the ASGPR on liver cells.
L3295: The nonclinical development program included primary pharmacology (in vitro and in vivo), safety pharmacology (in vivo cardiovascular, respiratory, and CNS in monkeys and in vitro hERG) PK/ADME, repeat-dose toxicity (39-week in monkeys and 13- and 26-week in mice), genotoxicity (in vitro Ames assay, in vitro chromosome aberration assay, and in vivo bone marrow micronucleus assay in mice), carcinogenicity (6-month Tg.rasH2 mice), and reproductive and developmental toxicology (combined fertility and development in mice and PPND in mice) studies. The main nonclinical species used in the pharmacology and toxicology studies were monkeys and mice. The sequence targeted by ISIS 721744 has one mismatch to the binding site in Cynomolgus monkey PKK mRNA (position 19). Despite this mismatch, ISIS 721744 showed dose-dependent inhibition of hepatic target mRNA expression and reductions in PKK protein and activity levels in peripheral circulation of Cynomolgus monkeys. ISIS 721744 does not align perfectly to the mouse PKK gene sequence. As such, in vivo studies in mice evaluated mouse-specific PKK ASOs (either unconjugated ISIS 482584 in the pharmacology studies or conjugated ISIS 722059 in the toxicology studies).
L3296: ## Primary Pharmacology
L3297: Donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) is an ASO GalNAc conjugate that causes RNase H1 mediated degradation of PKK mRNA through selective binding to PKK mRNA, which results in reduced production of PKK protein. There is high concordance of the nonclinical pharmacology and clinical efficacy data for inhibition of PKK. PKK is a target of several approved HAE therapies (small molecules and monoclonal antibodies).
L3298: ## In Vitro Pharmacology
L3299: Specificity analysis of ISIS 721744 was performed with unconjugated PKK ASO, ISIS 546254, which has the same sequence. ISIS 546254 is perfectly matched to only PKK RNA in human transcriptome (targets site free of meaningful sequence variation). Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
L3300: Treatment of HepatoPac® (co-culture system of primary human hepatocytes and stromal cells [mouse fibroblasts]) with ISIS 721744 and ISIS 546254 (unconjugated parent compound of ISIS 721744) resulted in a dose-dependent reduction of PKK mRNA. The IC50 for ISIS 721744 and ISIS 546254 were 0.19 mcM and 8.73 mcM, respectively, indicating that ISIS 721744 is about 46-fold more potent than ISIS 546254 (likely due to cellular uptake through hepatocyte-specific ASGPR). Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
L3301: ISIS 546254 reduced human PKK mRNA levels by greater than 90% in a concentration-dependent manner in human hepatocellular cell lines HepaRG and Hep3b with
L3302: corresponding IC_{50} of 0.31 mcM and 0.35 mcM, respectively. The control oligonucleotide ISIS 141923 did not reduce PKK mRNA in either cell line.
L3303: ## In Vivo Pharmacology
L3304: ISIS 721744 does not have perfect alignment to the mouse PKK gene sequence. As such, an unconjugated PKK ASO mouse surrogate (i.e., ISIS 482584) was used for in vivo pharmacology studies in mice. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
L3305: Male C57Bl/6 albino mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle or unconjugated PKK ASO mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 (5, 10, 20, 40, 80, or 160 mg/kg/week) for 3 weeks. ISIS 482584 inhibited PKK liver mRNA and PKK plasma protein expression in a dose-dependent manner. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
L3306: Permeability assays were performed in male C57Bl/6 albino mice treated with unconjugated PKK ASO mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 (80 mg/kg/week) for 3 weeks. Evans Blue tracer was injected into the tail vein of mice and analyzed for its accumulation in the colon tissue. Some mice were also treated intraperitoneally with the angiotensin-converting-enzyme (ACE) inhibitor captopril (1 mg/kg) at the time of Evans Blue tracer injection or with a C1 INH ASO (40 mg/kg/week for 3 weeks) to enhance vascular permeability. ISIS 482584 inhibited basal vascular permeability. Further ISIS 482584 inhibited vascular permeability induced by either captopril or C1 INH ASO. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
L3307: Male C57Bl/6 albino mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle or unconjugated PKK ASO mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 (5, 10, 20, 40, 80, or 160 mg/kg/week) for 3 weeks. ISIS 482584 (10 to 160 mg/kg for 3 weeks) reduced basal activated high molecular weight kininogen cleavage in blood of male mice. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
L3308: Human KLKB1/PKK transgenic mice were treated by SC administration with ISIS 721744 (0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, or 10 mg/kg) on Day 0 and plasma was collected on Day -1, 3, 7, 14, 28, 42 and 56. A single dose of ISIS 721744 resulted in a dose- and time-dependent reduction of plasma PKK protein that approached 91% at 10 mg/kg on Day 14 after treatment. After reaching the lowest point at Days 7 to 14, plasma PKK levels were fully restored by Day 42 for 1 mg/kg or Day 56 for 3 mg/kg dose. PKK levels were still 20% below baseline levels by Day 56 for 10 mg/kg.
L3309: ## Safety Pharmacology
L3310: The safety pharmacology evaluations for the cardiovascular, respiratory, and CNS were combined into one study in Cynomolgus monkeys. Based on cardiovascular and respiratory assessments, there were no test article-related effects on arterial blood pressure parameters (systolic, diastolic, and mean arterial pressure), heart rate, respiratory rate, core body temperature, or ECG parameters (PR interval, QRS duration, QT interval, and RR interval) for up to 24 hours after dosing, or arterial blood gases for
L3311: up to 2 hours after dosing, with 12 and 30 mg/kg ISIS 721744. Based on CNS assessments, there were generally no treatment-related effects noted by functional observational battery (FOB) for up to 24 hours after dosing with 12 and 30 mg/kg ISIS 721744. Although, one animal (No. 072104) receiving 12 mg/kg had signs of hunched posture and tremors at 1 hour and 4 hours postdose, which were not evident at 24 hours postdose. Clinical chemistry and hematology parameters for this animal were normal. These findings were not seen in any other animals at this dose (12 mg/kg) or the higher dose (30 mg/kg). Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
L3312: In the in vitro hERG assay, ISIS 721744 inhibited hERG current in HEK-293 cells by 0.5% and 1.9% at 30 \muM and 300 \muM, respectively (not statistically significant) versus 2.4% for the vehicle control. The IC_{50} for the inhibitory effect of ISIS 721744 on hERG potassium current was not calculated but was estimated to be greater than 300 \muM. In general, oligonucleotides are not thought to inhibit the hERG channel.
L3313: ## PK/ADME
L3314: The in vitro protein binding of ISIS 721744 at concentrations of 0.5, 5, and 150 mcg/mL was evaluated in the whole plasma from human, Cynomolgus monkey, and mouse by ultrafiltration methodology and a nuclease-dependent hybridization ELISA detection method. ISIS 721744 was highly bound (\ge 96.81\%) to whole plasma proteins in human, monkey, and mouse at all three concentrations evaluated. The extent of plasma protein binding of ISIS 721744 was similar across all species. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Review dated 08/13/2019.
L3315: The in vitro mean blood to plasma ratio of ISIS 721744 was between 0.630 and 0.824 in human, 0.468 and 0.566 in monkey, and 0.501 and 0.661 in rat suggesting that ISIS 721744 distributes mostly in the plasma compartment across the concentrations tested in all three species.
L3316: Based on metabolic profiling and identification of ISIS 721744 oligonucleotide-related metabolites in urine from mice, monkeys, and humans, the Applicant described that the primary route of elimination of donidalorsen is initial rapid hydrolysis of the GalNAc conjugate in tissues, followed by slow nuclease-mediated metabolism of the unconjugated oligonucleotide, and subsequent excretion of chain-shortened metabolites, as well as full-length oligonucleotides, albeit minor in urine and feces. There were no unique metabolites found in humans compared to animal species.
L3317: Based on metabolic profiling, identification, and quantitation of ISIS 721744 linker-related metabolites in plasma, urine, and/or fecal samples from mice, monkeys, and/or humans, the Applicant determined that the GalNAc moiety is hydrolyzed intracellularly following uptake into tissues, and the THA linker undergoes extensive oxidative metabolism, and is nearly completely eliminated via biliary excretion, and to a lesser extent, renal excretion, within 24 hours after administration.
L3318: ## Repeat-Dose Toxicity
L3319: In the pivotal GLP-compliant chronic toxicity study in Cynomolgus monkeys (pharmacologically relevant species), monkeys received SC doses of ISIS 721744 at 0, 2, 6, 12, or 30 mg/kg/dose. The monkeys were dosed for 39-weeks (dosing on Days 1, 5, 9, and 14 [loading doses] and once weekly thereafter) with a 13-week interim sacrifice (monkeys at 30 mg/kg/dose were dosed only until the interim sacrifice). A 26-week treatment-free recovery period was included after both the 13-week interim dosing interval (30 mg/kg/dose) and the 39-week dosing interval (0, 2, 6, 12 mg/kg/dose) to assess potential reversibility of any observed effects. Refer to Nonclinical Primary Review dated 08/13/2019 for details. In brief, the main test article-related findings included thrombocytopenia in two animals (12 and 30 mg/kg/dose) and histopathology findings of basophilic granules in various organs/tissues (including kidneys, liver, lymph nodes, and injection site) that in the absence of correlating histopathology were considered consistent with oligonucleotide uptake and not considered adverse. There were dose-dependent decreases in hepatic PKK mRNA expression and dose-dependent and time-dependent decreases in PKK plasma protein after treatment with ISIS 721744 at \ge 2 mg/kg/dose at the interim and/or terminal sacrifices. Both hepatic PKK mRNA expression and plasma protein increased by the end of the recovery periods. Tissue concentrations of unconjugated ISIS 721744 in liver or kidney increased in a dose-dependent manner. The NOAEL was 6 mg/kg/week based on thrombocytopenia in two monkeys at the higher dose levels of 12 and 30 mg/kg/dose. The NOAEL corresponded to a C_{max} of 6.57 mcg/mL and an AUC_{0-48hr} of 37.6 mcg*hr/mL on Day 273.
L3320: In the pivotal chronic toxicity study in mice (not a pharmacologically relevant species), mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (1, 4, or 12 mg/kg/dose), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4 mg/kg/dose) Q2W for 26 weeks with a 13-week treatment-free recovery period (vehicle control and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 dose groups only). Changes in hematology parameters at the end of the 26-week treatment period included increases in white blood cells, neutrophils, lymphocytes, and/or monocytes in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. At the end of the 13-week recovery period, increases in hematology parameters were no longer seen at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. Changes in clinical chemistry parameters at the end of the 26-week treatment period included increases in ALT, AST, and/or ALP in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. Effects on clinical chemistry parameters (including ALT, AST, and ALP) were less clear at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. At the end of the 13-week recovery period, increases in ALT and/or AST were still seen in males and/or females at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, while increases in ALP were no longer seen. Histopathology findings after the 26-week treatment period with ISIS 721744 were seen in the liver, skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, inguinal lymph nodes, and spleen. Histopathology findings after the 26-week treatment with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 were seen in the skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, spleen, and testis.
L3321: - Liver: Minimal or slight centrilobular hepatocellular hypertrophy was noted in males at 1, 4, and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and in one female (moderate) at
L3322: 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. This finding correlated with increased mean liver weights at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and increased liver enzymes (AST, ALT, and/or ALP). Despite a background incidence of hepatocyte vacuolation in vehicle control males, there was an increase in the severity (slight to marked) of hepatocyte vacuolation in males at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, which correlated with gross pathology findings of liver discoloration at all dose levels.
L3323: - **Skin/Subcutis:** Increased incidences and/or severity of infiltrates of mononuclear cells, mixed cells, and/or vacuolated macrophages in the skin/subcutis were noted in males and/or females at 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and/or 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. Increased incidences and/or severity of vacuolated fibrocytes in the skin/subcutis were noted in males and/or females at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. Slight to moderate inflammation in the skin was noted in females at 4 and 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744. These findings in the skin/subcutis correlated with increased leukocyte counts.
- **SC Dose Sites:** Increased incidences and/or severity of infiltrates of vacuolated macrophages, mononuclear cells, and mixed cells, as well as fibrocyte vacuolation at the SC injection sites were noted in males and/or females at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and/or 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. These findings at the SC injection sites correlated with increased leukocyte counts.
- **Inguinal Lymph Nodes:** Increased incidences and severities (minimal to marked) of increased lymphocytes in males at 1, 4, and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and one female at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were noted in the inguinal lymph node. This finding in the inguinal lymph node correlated with increased leukocyte counts. Amyloid in the inguinal lymph node was noted in one male at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
- **Spleen:** Increased incidence and/or severity of extramedullary hematopoiesis in the spleen was noted in males and/or females at 1, 4 and/or 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 and 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059 and correlated with increased mean spleen weight in males administered 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744.
- **Testis:** Moderate interstitial cell hyperplasia, minimal sperm stasis, and minimal vacuolation were noted in the testis of males at 4 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059.
L3324: Histopathology findings after the 13-week recovery period for 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were still noted in the liver as hepatocellular vacuolation in males and females, which correlated with increased liver weights. Histopathology findings in the skin/subcutis, SC dose sites, inguinal lymph nodes, and spleen at 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744 were not seen at the end of the recovery period.
L3325: Unconjugated ISIS 721744 was measurable in a dose-dependent manner in the kidney (greater than dose proportional) and liver (dose proportional) after 26 weeks of treatment with ISIS 721744. The mean concentrations of unconjugated ISIS 721744 were similar in the kidney and liver except at 12 mg/kg/dose where mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were greater in the kidney than in the liver. Mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were higher in females than in males in the kidney but similar in the liver. After the 13-week treatment-free recovery period at 12
L3326: mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, mean unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations were below or near the lower limit of quantitation of 0.107 mcg/g, suggesting complete clearance of ISIS 721744.
L3327: Mouse PKK mRNA in mouse liver was reduced by 77% (statistically significant) compared to vehicle control in mice treated with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 at 4 mg/kg/dose for 26 weeks.
L3328: The NOAEL was 12 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, as test article-related findings were considered related to the oligonucleotide uptake.
L3329: ## Conclusions
L3330: The nonclinical pharmacology and toxicology studies were judged to be adequate to support the safety of donidalorsen for marketing. There are no outstanding concerns from the nonclinical perspective.
L3331: **Recommendation:** From the nonclinical perspective, the NDA is recommended for approval.

L3350: ## 1 Executive Summary
L3351: ## 1.1 Introduction
L3352: Ionis Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Applicant) submitted a 505(b)(1) New Drug Application (NDA) for subcutaneous (SC) administration of donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) as 80 mg (b) (4) (or 80 mg (b) (4) in some patients) prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. ISIS 721744 is an N-acetyl galactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated antisense oligonucleotide (ASO), which targets human prekallikrein (PKK). The GalNAc molecule preferentially delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by binding to the asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR) on liver cells.
L3353: This review focuses on the evaluation of the GLP-compliant reproductive and developmental toxicology studies with ISIS 721744 (i.e., combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice and pre- and postnatal development [PPND] study in mice). ISIS 721744 does not have perfect alignment to the mouse PKK gene sequence. As such, ISIS 721744 is not pharmacologically active in mice and the mouse surrogate ISIS 722059, which targets mouse PKK, was included in both studies in mice to assess potential toxicities related to the intended pharmacology of PKK inhibition. This review also provides a summary of the GLP-compliant reproductive and developmental toxicology studies (i.e., combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice and embryofetal development [EFD] study in rabbits) with the unconjugated parent compound of ISIS 721744 (i.e., ISIS 546254) and/or its unconjugated mouse surrogate (ISIS 482584) which targets mouse PKK to assess potential toxicities related to the intended pharmacology of PKK inhibition.
L3354: ## 1.2 Brief Discussion of Nonclinical Findings
L3355: In the combined fertility and developmental toxicity study, mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (1, 4, or 10 mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4 mg/kg/week). Males were dosed once weekly during the premating, mating, and postmating phases until euthanasia (about 10 weeks total). Females were dosed weekly during the premating and mating phases and then every other day during the gestation period from Gestation Day (GD) 0 to GD 16 (encompassing the periods of implantation and organogenesis). Since ISIS 722059 statistically decreased PKK mRNA expression in the liver of male and female mice by 80% and 75%, respectively. Unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the placenta (up to 0.31 mcg/g) were &gt;10% lower than in the liver (i.e., 3 to 43 mcg/g for 1 to 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 in females on GD 18). SC administration of ISIS 721744 (up to 10 mg/kg/week) or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4 mg/kg/week) did not affect fertility, pregnancy, or embryofetal development in mice.
L3356: In a combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice, SC administration of the unconjugated parent compound of ISIS 721744 (i.e., ISIS 546254) at dose levels up to 84 mg/kg/week or unconjugated mouse surrogate (i.e., ISIS 482584) at 84 mg/kg/week did not affect fertility, pregnancy, or embryofetal development.
L3357: In an EFD study in rabbits, SC administration of the unconjugated parent compound of ISIS 721744 (i.e., ISIS 546254) at dose levels up to 75 mg/kg/week every other day from GD 6 to GD 18 did not result in any fetal external findings, visceral variations or malformations, or skeletal variations or malformations attributed to treatment.
L3358: In the PPND toxicity study, F_0 female mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (5 mg/kg/week) every other day from GD 6 to GD 18 and weekly from Lactation Day (LD) 1 to LD 20 (the treatment period encompassed organogenesis through weaning). Since ISIS 721744 is not active in mice, the mouse-surrogate, ISIS 722059, was included in the study to assess the potential effects related to the target inhibition. ISIS 722059 statistically decreased PKK mRNA expression in the liver of F_0 female mice by 82% on LD 22. ISIS 721744 was present in milk of lactating F_0 females at 10 and 20 mg/kg/week, although the drug is unlikely to be adsorbed systemically in F_1 pups. SC administration of ISIS 721744 (up to 20 mg/kg/week) or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (5 mg/kg/week) did not affect pregnancy in F_0 females or prenatal and postnatal development (including behavioral, fertility, and reproduction function) in F_1 offspring.
L3359: Conclusion: The reproductive and developmental toxicology studies with ISIS 721744 (and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059) were adequate to support the safety of ISIS 721744 for marketing. There are no outstanding concerns from the nonclinical perspective related to reproductive and developmental toxicology.

It consists of a GalNAc moiety linked to a phosphorothioate oligonucleotide backbone. The oligonucleotide sequence is shown, featuring various modified nucleotides (e.g., 2'-O-methyl, 2'-fluoro, and locked nucleic acid (LNA) analogs) and terminal modifications (e.g., 3'-phosphorothioate and 5'-phosphorothioate). The structure is highly complex, involving multiple repeating units of modified nucleotides linked by phosphorothioate bonds, with sodium ions (\text{Na}^+) associated with the phosphate groups. L3387: ## 2.3 Drug Formulation
L3388: The donidalorsen drug product is a sterile, single-dose, ready-to-use parenteral solution for SC administration. The qualitative and quantitative drug product formulation is shown in **Table 1** (Applicant's Table). The drug product is packaged in a staked needle glass prefilled syringe (PFS) closed with a (b) (4) rubber plunger stopper. The PFS is assembled into an autoinjector for the final drug product presentation. The autoinjector delivers a single dose of 80 mg donidalorsen.

L3401: ## 2.6 Proposed Clinical Population and Dosing Regimen
L3402: Donidalorsen is indicated for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of HAE in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. The recommended dosage is 80 mg administered SC (b) (4). A dosing interval of (b) (4) may be considered in some patients.
L3403: ## 2.7 Regulatory Background
L3404: Provided below is the regulatory background for the ISIS 721744 reproductive and developmental toxicology program. In brief, the Agency agreed that an EFD study of ISIS 721744 in rabbits was not needed. The following is excerpted from the Type B End of Phase 2 (EOP2) Meeting Minutes dated 10/18/2021 capturing discussions from the teleconference between the Applicant and the Agency on 08/30/2021.
L3405: ## Question 2
L3406: Does the Agency agree to a waiver from the requirement to conduct an embryo-fetal development study of ISIS 721744 in rabbits?
L3407: ## **FDA Response:**
L3408: Pending review of the available, ongoing, and planned reproductive and developmental toxicity studies with ISIS 721744 and ISIS 546254, unconjugated parent compound of ISIS 721744, (and the mouse surrogates ISIS 722059 and ISIS 482584 [unconjugated]), we agree that an embryo-fetal development study of ISIS 721744 in rabbits is not needed.
L3409: Refer to the ICH M3(R2) Guidance regarding the timing of reproductive toxicology studies and the inclusion of women of childbearing potential in clinical studies.
L3410: The ongoing fertility and early embryonic development toxicity study in CD-1 mice should be available prior to the initiation of the phase 3 clinical trials with ISIS 721744. The planned pre and postnatal development study in CD-1 mice can be conducted in parallel with phase 3 trials and provided with a potential NDA.
L3411: ## **Discussion for FDA Response to Question 2:**
L3412: There was no discussion held for FDA Response to Question 2.

L3424: ## 9 Reproductive and Developmental Toxicology
L3425: ## 9.1 Fertility and Early Embryonic Development
L3426: **Study title:** A Combined Fertility and Developmental Toxicity Study of ISIS 721744 in Mice via Subcutaneous Administration
L3427: Study no.: 727-134 (Applicant No. 721744-AS06)
Study report location: Electronic Document Room (EDR)
Supporting Document Number (SDN) 1
L3428: Conducting laboratory and location:
L3429: Date of study initiation: 11/10/2020
GLP compliance: Yes
QA statement: Yes
Drug, lot #, and % purity: ISIS 721744 bulk test article, lot # CA721744-001, and 89.5% purity
L3430: ISIS 722059 (mouse surrogate) bulk test article, lot # 722059-4, and 88.2% purity
L3431: ## Key Study Findings
L3432: - In a combined fertility and developmental toxicity study, mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (1, 4, or 10 mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4 mg/kg/week). Males were dosed once weekly during the premating (beginning 28 days prior to mating), mating, and postmating phases (10 weeks total). Females were dosed beginning 14 days prior to mating. Females were dosed weekly (Days 1, 8, 15, and 22, as needed) during the premating phase and through the mating phase until positive evidence of copulation was observed, and every other day during the gestation period from GD 0 to GD 16 (i.e., GDs 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, and 16). Unmated females continued to be dosed weekly until termination (following the last GD 18 necropsies).
- There were no estrous cycle changes (i.e., mean number of cycles and mean cycle length) related to treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
- Percent abnormal sperm was increased at 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 (15.6%, statistically significant) and 4 mg/kg/week ISIS 722059 (13.4%), compared to the vehicle control (10.1%), and outside of the conducting laboratory historical control ranges of 3.4% to 10.2%. It did not appear that an increase in percent
L3433: abnormal sperm affected pregnancy indices at 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 or 4 mg/kg/week ISIS 722059.
L3434: - There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on male or female mating performance.
- There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on the number of corpora lutea, implantations, preimplantation and postimplantation losses, or live fetuses.
- There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on fetal body weights.
- There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on fetal external, visceral, or skeletal variations or malformations (i.e., no fetal anomalies) in mice.
- Unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the parental liver of males and females increased with increasing dose of drug. Unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the fetal liver were below the limit of quantitation in all ISIS 721744-treated groups. Notably, unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the placenta (up to 0.31 mcg/g) and testes (up to 1.61 mcg/g) were much lower than in the liver (i.e., 3 to 43 mcg/g for 1 to 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 in F0 females on GD 18 and 7 to 47 mcg/g for 1 to 10 mg/kg/week for males on Day 73). It was unclear if ISIS 721744 or the unconjugated version of ISIS 721744 crossed the placenta to reach fetal tissues.
- Treatment of F0 male and female mice with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 at 4 mg/kg/week statistically decreased hepatic mRNA expression of KIkb1/Pkk by 80% and 75%, respectively.
- The NOAEL for ISIS 721744 on male and female fertility and mating performance, as well as developmental toxicity, was the high dose of 10 mg/kg/week.

L3442: ## Observations and Results
L3443: ## Mortality
L3444: Mortality/cageside observations were made at least twice daily (morning and afternoon) beginning upon arrival through termination/release.
L3445: There were two unscheduled deaths during the study. One male (No. 2021) at 1 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 was euthanized on Day 61 due to severe penile prolapse and decreased urine output. One toxicokinetic (TK) female (No. 7505) at 1 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 was euthanized on GD 12 due to pregnancy complications (red discharge from the vagina and red material present in the cage bedding). These unscheduled deaths were considered incidental and unrelated to treatment with ISIS 721744 as there were no deaths in higher dose groups.
L3446: All other animals survived to scheduled termination.
L3447: ## Clinical Signs
L3448: Detailed clinical observations were made prior to randomization and daily during treatment (predose and about 1.5 hours postdose on dosing days).
L3449: There were no clinical sign observations attributed to treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
L3450: ## Body Weight
L3451: ## Males
L3452: Males were weighed at receipt, prior to randomization, and twice weekly during the premating and postmating phases.
L3453: There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on body weight in males during the study.
L3454: ## Females
L3455: Females were weighed at receipt, prior to randomization, and twice weekly prior to mating. Upon the beginning of the mating phase, females were weighed once weekly or until mating was confirmed (body weight data for the mating phase was not included in the study report). Upon verification of mating, females were weighed on the presumed GDs 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, and 18.
L3456: There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on body weight in females during the premating phase of the study.
L3457: As shown in **Table 3**, mean gestational body weight was increased beginning on GD 10 through GD 18 in females treated with 4 and 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 (+5% to +15% difference from vehicle control). Mean gestational body weight was increased beginning on GD 16 through GD 18 in females treated with 4 mg/kg/week ISIS 722059 (+8% to +9% difference from vehicle control). These increases in mean gestational body weight corresponded with increases in mean gestational body weight gain. The increases in mean gestational body weight gain were not considered adverse. A comparison of the body weight changes between GD 0 and GD 16 (drug treatment period) is shown in **Table 4**.

L3466: ## Feed Consumption
L3467: Qualitative food consumption was recorded weekly prior to mating. Food consumption was not recorded during the mating phase. Following the mating phase, qualitative food consumption for males was recorded on a weekly basis until euthanasia. Qualitative food consumption for females was recorded on the corresponding gestation body weight days.
L3468: There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on food consumption during the study.
L3469: ## Estrous Cyclicity
L3470: Females were examined daily for estrous cyclicity at least 10 days prior to initiation of treatment and until evidence of copulation was observed or the cohabitation period ended.
L3471: There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on estrous cyclicity (i.e., mean number of cycles and mean cycle length).
L3472: ## Sperm Analysis
L3473: At the time of euthanasia, the right testis and epididymis were used for sperm analysis (i.e., sperm motility, sperm count/concentration, and sperm morphology).
L3474: There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on sperm motility or sperm count/concentration.
L3475: As shown in **Table 5** (Applicant's Table), percent abnormal sperm was increased at 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 (15.6%, statistically significant) and 4 mg/kg/week ISIS 722059 (13.4%) compared to the vehicle control (10.1%). These percent abnormal sperm mean values were outside the conducting laboratory historical control ranges of 3.4% to 10.2%. As described in the study report: These differences were mostly driven by a few animals at 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 (up to 36%) and 4 mg/kg/week ISIS 722059 (up to 27.7%) that had individual percent abnormal sperm slightly higher than the concurrent control (up to 24.5%). It did not appear that an increase in percent abnormal sperm affected pregnancy indices at 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 or 4 mg/kg/week ISIS 722059.

L3479: ## Hematology

L3486: ## Clinical Chemistry
L3487: Blood was collected for clinical chemistry evaluations from the second set of 6 animals/sex/group at necropsy (i.e., Day 73 for males and GD 18 for females). A representative panel of clinical chemistry parameters was evaluated.
L3488: As shown in **Table 7**, treatment with 4 and 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 increased AST (1.6x and 1.9x of control, respectively) and ALT (2.7x and 3.0x of control, respectively) in males suggestive of an effect on the liver. Other changes included a decrease in albumin at 4 and 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 in males, an increase in cholesterol at 1,
L3489: 4, and 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 in males, and a decrease in triglycerides at 4 and 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 in males, 1, 4, and 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 in females, and 4 mg/kg/week ISIS 722059 in females. Most of these changes appear to be consistent with the uptake of ISIS 721744 into the liver.

L3493: ## Toxicokinetics
L3494: ## Tissue Bioanalysis
L3495: Parental (liver, testis, and placenta) and fetal (liver) tissue were analyzed using a validated ultra-high performance liquid chromatography with tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS) procedure to determine unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations.
L3496: Parental and fetal tissue concentrations of unconjugated ISIS 721744 are shown in **Table 8** (Applicant's Table). Unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the parental liver of vehicle control males and females were below the limit of quantitation except for one female which had a liver exposure of 1.72 mcg/g. Unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the parental liver of males and females increased with increase in ISIS 721744 dose. Unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the fetal liver were below the limit of quantitation in all ISIS 721744-treated groups. Unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the placenta were below the limit of quantitation at 1 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 and at 0.03 and 0.31 mcg/g at 4 and 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744, respectively. Unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the testes were below the limit of quantitation at 1 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 and at 0.25 and 1.61 mcg/g at 4 and 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744, respectively. Notably, unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the placenta and testes were much lower than in the liver (3 to 43 mcg/g for 1 to 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 in females on GD 18 and 7 to 47 mcg/g for 1 to 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 in males on Day 73). The uptake of ISIS 721744 by the liver was promoted by the GalNAc conjugate, which is subsequently cleaved.

L3509: ## Dosing Solution Analysis
L3510: Samples were collected for concentration and stability analyses from the middle stratum of dose concentrations for ISIS 721744 at 0.07, 0.27, and 0.67 mg/mL and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 at 0.27 mg/mL. The concentration results were within the acceptance criterion of (b) (4)% indicating that the dosing solutions were prepared at the correct concentrations.

L3530: ## Fertility Parameters (Mating/Fertility Index, Corpora Lutea, Preimplantation Loss, etc.)
L3531: ## Mating
L3532: As described in the study report:
L3533: Mating began on Day 29 for males and Day 15 for females. One female was housed with one male from the same treatment group in the cage of the male. Positive evidence of copulation was established by daily inspection for a copulatory plug in situ or vaginal lavage for sperm. The day in which positive evidence of copulation was observed was considered GD 0. After mating, each female was returned to an individual cage. The maximum mating phase was 14 days.
L3534: As shown in **Table 11** and **Table 12** (Applicant's Tables), the male and female mating index was 100% for the vehicle control group as well as for the ISIS 721744 and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 groups. Further, the male and female fertility and pregnancy indices were 92% in ISIS 721744 and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 groups compared to 88% for the vehicle control group. As shown in **Table 12** (Applicant's Table), there were 23 pregnancies in each of the ISIS 721744 groups and the mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 group compared to 22 pregnancies in the vehicle control group.

L3547: ## Fetal Evaluations
L3548: Each fetus was sexed, weighed, and evaluated for external, visceral, and skeletal malformations and variations.

L3550: The fetal sex ratios (% males per litter) were comparable between 1, 4, and 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 (i.e., 48.62%, 48.25%, and 43.58%, respectively), mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (i.e., 46.39%) and the vehicle control group (i.e., 55.67%).

L3575: ## 9.3 Prenatal and Postnatal Development
L3576: ## **Study title: Study for Toxic Effects of ISIS 721744 on Pre- and Postnatal Development, Including Maternal Function in Mice**
L3577: Study no.:	727-142 (Applicant No. 721744-AS09)
Study report location:	EDR SDN 1
Conducting laboratory and location:	(b) (4)
Date of study initiation:	01/11/2023
GLP compliance:	Yes
QA statement:	Yes
Drug, lot #, and % purity:	ISIS 721744 bulk test article, lot #
CA721744-003, 92.6% purity
ISIS 722059 bulk test article, lot #
722059-4, 88.2% purity
L3578: ## Key Study Findings
L3579: - In a PPND toxicity study, F0 female mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (5 mg/kg/week) every other day from GD 6 to GD 18 (GDs 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, and 18) and weekly from LD 1 to LD 20 (LDs 1, 7, 13, and 20).
- There were no deaths in any of the F0 females attributed to treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
- AST (3x and 2x of control, respectively) and ALT (5x and 4x of control, respectively) were increased in F0 females on LD 22 at 10 and 20 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 that was consistent with uptake into the liver.
- Mean ISIS 721744 concentrations in milk from F0 females was below the limit of quantitation for the vehicle control and 5 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 groups and 7.63 and 24.63 ng/mL at 10 and 20 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744, respectively.
- There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on parturition parameters (gestation index, live newborn pups/litter, live birth index, uterine implantation sites, and gestation length).
- Kidney, liver, and/or spleen weights (absolute and/or relative to terminal body weight) on LD 22 were increased in F0 females treated with ISIS 721744 at 5, 10, and/or 20 mg/kg/week. Increases of kidney and liver weights were consistent with uptake of ISIS 721744.
- Unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the kidney and liver of F0 females on LD 22 increased with ISIS 721744 dose, which was consistent with uptake of ISIS 721744.
- Treatment of F0 females with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 at 5 mg/kg/week statistically decreased hepatic mRNA expression of Kikb1/Pkk by 82% on LD 22.
L3580: - There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on F1 pups (preweaning) based on evaluation of survival, clinical signs, body weights, sex ratios, physical development, and gross pathology.
- There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on the F1 generation based on evaluation of survival, clinical signs, sexual maturation, body weights, food consumption, behavioral evaluations (motor activity, Morris Water Maze, acoustic startle response), estrous cyclicity, mating/reproductive/fertility performance indices, GD 13 corpora lutea/uterine implantation data, organ weights, and gross pathology evaluations.
- The NOAEL for maternal toxicity and the PPND study was the high dose of 20 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744.

5, 10, or 20 mg/kg/week

Deviation from study protocol:	Refer to Table 17 (Applicant's Table)
Deviations from the study protocol were described in the study report. None of the deviations appeared to have affected the integrity, results, or conclusions of the study.

L3588: ## Observations and Results
L3589: ## F0 Dams
L3590: ## F0 Survival:
L3591: Mortality/cageside observations for F0 females were conducted at least twice daily (morning and afternoon) beginning upon arrival through termination/release.
L3592: There were no deaths in any of the F0 females attributed to treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
L3593: Two F0 females in the vehicle control group (Nos. 1508 and 1513) were found dead on LD 17 and LD 15, respectively. There were no clinical or gross pathology findings for either animal.
L3594: One F0 female at 5 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 (No. 2515) was found dead on LD 15. There were no clinical or gross pathology findings for this animal. Since two F0 females were in the vehicle control group, and no animals treated with higher doses of ISIS 721744 were found dead, this death was considered incidental and unrelated to treatment with ISIS 721744.
L3595: Two F0 females at 5 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 (Nos. 2503 and 2529) were euthanized on LD 4 and LD 1, respectively, due to no surviving pups (i.e., total litter loss). As described in the study report, Animal No. 2503 delivered one pup which was found dead on PND 3 and Animal No. 2529 delivered three pups which were found dead on PND 0.
L3596: ## F0 Clinical Signs:
L3597: Cageside observations for F0 females were conducted predose on dosing days and once daily on non-dosing days. Detailed clinical observations for F0 females were conducted daily (about 1.5 hours postdose on dosing days).
L3598: There were no clinical sign observations in F0 females attributed to treatment with ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059.
L3599: ## F0 Body Weight:
L3600: Body weights for F0 females were recorded once prior to dosing and on GDs 0, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, and 18 and LDs 1, 4, 7, 10, 14, 17, and 21.
L3601: There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on body weight in F0 females.
L3602: ## F0 Feed Consumption:
L3603: Quantitative food consumption for F0 females was measured on the corresponding body weight days.
L3604: There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on food consumption in F0 females.
L3605: ## F0 Hematology:
L3606: Blood from F0 females was collected for hematology evaluations on LD 22. A representative panel of hematology parameters was evaluated.
L3607: There were no effects of ISIS 721744 or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on hematology parameters in F0 females on LD 22.
L3608: ## F0 Clinical Chemistry
L3609: Blood from F0 females was collected for clinical chemistry evaluations on LD 22. A representative panel of clinical chemistry parameters was evaluated.
L3610: As shown in **Table 18**, AST (3x and 2x of control, respectively) and ALT (5x and 4x of control, respectively) were statistically increased in F0 females on LD 22 at 10 and 20 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744, respectively.
L3611: There were no effects of mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 on clinical chemistry parameters in F0 females on LD 22.

L3626: As shown in **Table 19**, kidney, liver, and spleen weights on LD 22 were increased in F0 females treated with ISIS 721744. Liver weight was statistically increased for absolute weights at 10 and 20 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 (+18% and +22% difference from vehicle control, respectively) and relative to terminal body weight at 5, 10, and 20 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 (+10%, +19%, and +23% difference from vehicle control, respectively). Spleen weight (relative to terminal body weight) was statistically increased at 20 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 (+19% difference from vehicle control). Increased liver and kidney weights were consistent with the uptake of ISIS 721744.

The day on which evidence of mating was observed was designated as GD 0. Upon evidence of mating, the female was removed from the cage of the male and individually housed. Estrous cycle determinations were made on F1 females during mating and until evidence of copulation was observed or the cohabitation period ended.

L3706: ## 11 Integrated Summary and Safety Evaluation
L3707: ISIS 721744 is a GalNAc-conjugated ASO, which targets human PKK. The GalNAc molecule preferentially delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver by binding to the ASGPR on liver cells. SC administration of ISIS 721744 is proposed as 80 mg [REDACTED] (b) (4) (or 80 mg [REDACTED] (b) (4) in some patients) prophylaxis to prevent attacks of HAE in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older.
L3708: This review evaluates the GLP-compliant reproductive and developmental toxicology studies with ISIS 721744 (i.e., combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice and PPND study in mice) to support the safety of ISIS 721744 for marketing approval. ISIS 721744 does not have perfect alignment to the mouse PKK gene sequence. As such, ISIS 721744 is not pharmacologically active in mice and the mouse surrogate ISIS 722059, which targets mouse PKK, was included in both studies in mice to assess potential toxicities related to the intended pharmacology of PKK inhibition.
L3709: This review also provides a summary of the GLP-compliant reproductive and developmental toxicology studies with ISIS 546254 (i.e., combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice and embryofetal development [EFD] study in rabbits). ISIS 546254 is the unconjugated parent compound of ISIS 721744, which has the same sequence as ISIS 721744 (i.e., 5'-TGCAAGTCTCTTGGCAAACA-3'), but with a uniform backbone of phosphorothioate diester internucleotide linkages instead of a mixed backbone like ISIS 721744. Based on specificity analysis against the human transcriptome, ISIS 546254 is completely aligned to only PKK RNA. ISIS 546254 does not have perfect alignment with the mouse PKK mRNA. Since ISIS 546254 is not pharmacologically active in mice, the unconjugated mouse surrogate ISIS 482584, which targets mouse PKK, was included in the combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice to assess potential toxicities related to the intended pharmacology of PKK inhibition. Refer to summaries below.
L3710: ## Fertility and Early Embryonic Development
L3711: In the combined fertility and developmental toxicity study, mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (1, 4, or 10 mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4 mg/kg/week). Males were dosed once weekly during the premating, mating, and postmating phases until euthanasia (about 10 weeks total). Females were dosed weekly during the premating and mating phases and then every other day during the gestation period from GD 0 to GD 16 (encompassing the periods of implantation and organogenesis). Since ISIS 721744 is not active in mice, the mouse-surrogate ISIS 722059 was included in the
L3712: study to assess the potential effects related to the target inhibition. ISIS 722059 statistically decreased PKK mRNA expression in the liver of male and female mice by 80% and 75%, respectively. Notably, unconjugated ISIS 721744 concentrations in the placenta (up to 0.31 mcg/g) were &gt;10% lower than in the liver (i.e., 3 to 43 mcg/g for 1 to 10 mg/kg/week ISIS 721744 in females on GD 18). SC administration of ISIS 721744 (up to 10 mg/kg/week) or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4 mg/kg/week) did not affect fertility, pregnancy, or embryofetal development. It was unclear if ISIS 721744 or the unconjugated version of ISIS 721744 crossed the placenta to reach fetal tissues.
L3713: A summary of the GLP-compliant combined fertility and developmental toxicity study with ISIS 546254 (unconjugated parent compound of ISIS 721744, which has the same sequence as ISIS 721744) and unconjugated mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 (Study No.
L3714: (b) (4) 090.60; Applicant No. 546254-AS04) is provided here.
L3715: - CD-1 mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP), ISIS 546254 (10.5, 42, or 84 mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 (84 mg/kg/week). As described in the study report, animals were dosed every other day and received three or four doses per week; thus, the weekly dose (mg/kg/week) was equivalent to 3.5 times the single mg/kg/dose. Males were dosed every other day during the premating (beginning 4 weeks prior to mating), mating, and postmating phases (10 weeks total). Females were dosed every other day for two weeks prior to mating, during the mating phase, and throughout GD 15 (encompassing the period of organogenesis).
- There was one unscheduled death during the study. One male at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 was euthanized on Day 49 due to declining clinical condition (lack of skin turgor and progressive face swelling). The animal was noted with a SC hemorrhagic mass on top of the skull, which was considered incidental, likely of traumatic origin. There were no remarkable gross findings in the other tissues and organs that were examined. The unscheduled death was considered incidental and unrelated to treatment with mouse surrogate ISIS 482584. All other animals survived to scheduled termination.
- Body weight decreases were noted in females on GD 18 at 10.5 and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 (less than 10% difference from vehicle control). The decreases were not considered adverse.
- Decreases (percent difference from vehicle control) in hematology parameters were noted at 42 and/or 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 in males on Day 71 for RBC (up to -14%), hemoglobin (up to -23%), hematocrit (up to -21%), mean corpuscular volume (MCV) (up to -9%), mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) (up to -11%), and platelets (up to -26%) and females on GD 18 for platelets (up to -21%).
- Decreases (percent difference from vehicle control) in hematology parameters were noted at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 in males on Day 71 for hemoglobin (-18%), hematocrit (-14%), MCV (-14%), MCH (-18%), and platelets (-54%) and in females on GD 18 for platelets (-54%).
- Increases (percent difference from vehicle control) in hematology parameters were noted at 42 and/or 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 in males on Day 71 for
L3716: RBC distribution width (up to +16%), white blood cells (WBC) (up to +63%), neutrophils (up to +58%), and monocytes (up to +207%) and in females on GD 18 for lymphocytes (up to +41%) and monocytes (up to +160%).
L3717: - Increases (percent difference from vehicle control) in hematology parameters were noted at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 in males on Day 71 for RBC distribution (+23%), WBC (+112%), neutrophils (+172%), lymphocytes (+98%), and monocytes (+223%) and in females on GD 18 for WBC (+65%), neutrophils (+77%), lymphocytes (+53%), and monocytes (+276%).
- Decreases (percent difference from vehicle control) in clinical chemistry parameters were noted at 10.5, 42, and/or 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 in males on Day 71 for total protein (up to -11%), albumin (up to -20%), A/G (up to -20%) and in females on GD 18 for triglycerides (up to -54%) and creatine kinase (up to -51%).
- Decreases (percent difference from vehicle control) in clinical chemistry parameters were noted at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 in males on Day 71 for albumin (-9%), A/G (-15%), triglycerides (-44%), total cholesterol (-40%) and in females on GD 18 for triglycerides (-59%) and creatine kinase (-65%).
- Increases (percent difference from vehicle control) in clinical chemistry parameters associated with liver weight changes in most cases were noted at 42 and/or 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 in males on Day 71 for ALT (up to +627%), AST (up to +309%), and ALP (+101%).
- Increases (percent difference from vehicle control) in clinical chemistry parameters associated with liver weight changes were noted at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 in males on Day 71 for ALT (+380%) and AST (up to +402%).
- Increases (percent difference from vehicle control) in organ weights were noted at 10.5, 42, and/or 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 in males for liver (up to +32%) and spleen (up to +38%) and in females for liver (up to +15%) and spleen (+49%).
- Increases (percent difference from vehicle control) in organ weights were noted at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 in males for liver (+29%) and spleen (+117%) and in females for spleen (+93%).
- Decreases (percent difference from vehicle control) in organ weights were noted at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 in males for prostate with seminal vesicle (-21% and -31%, respectively).
- There were no effects of ISIS 546254 or mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 on estrous cyclicity.
- There were no effects of ISIS 546254 or mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 on fertility (mating index) or fecundity (pregnancy index).
- At the time of Cesarean section, mean gravid uterus weights were decreased at 10.5, 42, and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 (-11%, -5%, and -7% difference from vehicle control respectively; not statistically significant) and at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 (-24% difference from vehicle control; statistically significant).
- The number of live fetuses was decreased at 10.5, 42, and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 (12 live fetuses in each group; statistically significant only at 10.5 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254) and at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 (11 live fetuses; statistically significant) compared to the vehicle control (14 live fetuses). This is
L3718: not likely biologically significant. In addition, the fetal viability percentage at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 was statistically decreased compared to the vehicle control (86% vs. 96%).

- There were no effects of ISIS 546254 on mean fetal weight (male or female) although at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 mean fetal weight was decreased for males and females (-11% and -10% difference from vehicle control, respectively; statistically significant in females only).
- The number of early resorptions was increased at 10.5, 42, and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 (1 in each group; not statistically significant) and at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 (1; statistically significant) compared to the vehicle control (0). This is not likely biologically significant. The percent early resorptions/animal was increased at 10.5, 42, and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 and at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 compared to the vehicle control. The embryo-fetal mortality index was increased at 10.5, 42, and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 and at 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 482584 compared to the vehicle control. As described in the study report: Although these changes were noticeable and statistically significant in some groups, they were consistent with what is noted in the control animals in these types of studies, therefore, a clear relationship to either test article cannot be established.
- Overall, there were no fetal external findings, visceral variations or malformations, or skeletal variations or malformations attributed to treatment with ISIS 546254 or mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 in mice.
- There were no effects of ISIS 546254 or mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 on sperm motility, morphology, or sperm count.
- ISIS 546254 concentrations in the parental liver of vehicle control males and females were below the limit of quantitation. ISIS 546254 concentrations in the parental liver of males and females increased with ISIS 546254 dose with higher concentrations in male mice than female mice. ISIS 546254 concentrations in the fetal liver were below the limit of quantitation in all ISIS 546254-treated groups. ISIS 546254 concentrations in the placenta were below the limit of quantitation, 6.73, and 22.3 mcg/g with doses of 10.5, 42, and 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254, respectively. Notably, ISIS 546254 concentrations in the placenta were lower than in the liver (52 to 612 mcg/g for 10.5 to 84 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 in males and females).
- Treatment of male and female mice with mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 at 84 mg/kg/week statistically decreased hepatic mRNA expression of *KlkB1/Pkk* by 94% and 87%, respectively.
- Conclusion: SC administration of ISIS 546254 (up to 84 mg/kg/week) or mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 (84 mg/kg/week) did not affect fertility, pregnancy, or embryofetal development in mice.
L3719: ## Embryofetal Development
L3720: It was agreed upon at the time of the EOP2 meeting that an EFD study in rabbits with ISIS 721744 would not be needed (refer to **Section 2.7**). This was based on the availability of an EFD study in rabbits with ISIS 546254 (unconjugated parent compound of ISIS 721744, which has the same sequence as ISIS 721744). A summary of the
L3721: GLP-compliant EFD study in rabbits with ISIS 546254 (Study No. (b) (4) 090.61; Applicant No. 546254-AS05) is provided here.
L3722: - Pregnant New Zealand white rabbits were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP) or ISIS 546254 (12.5, 25, or 75 mg/kg/week) every other day from GD 6 to GD 18 (i.e., GDs 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, and 18) encompassing the period of organogenesis. As stated in the study report, animals were dosed every other day, thus, the weekly dose (mg/kg/week) was equivalent to 3.5 times the single mg/kg dose.
- There were no unscheduled deaths during the study.
- Food consumption was decreased beginning on GD18 to GD 19 at 12.5, 25, and 75 mg/kg/week (-9%, -5%, and -31% difference from vehicle control, respectively). The decrease was more consistent at 75 mg/kg/week and was statistically decreased from the vehicle control between GD 25 and GD 27 (up to -41% difference from vehicle control). The decrease in food consumption did not appear to affect body weight or body weight gain.
- Changes in hematology parameters in females on GD 28 at 12.5, 25, and/or 75 mg/kg/week included decreases (percent difference from vehicle control) in RBC (up to -16%), hemoglobin (up to -16%), hematocrit (up to -16%), and basophils (up to -48%) and increases in RBC distribution width (up to +7%), WBC (up to +27%), neutrophils (up to +52%), and lymphocytes (up to +27%)
- Changes in clinical chemistry parameters in females on GD 28 at 25 and/or 75 mg/kg/week included decreases (percent difference from vehicle control) for albumin (up to -9%) and ALP (up to -45%) and increases (percent difference from vehicle control) for triglycerides (up to +87%).
- Organ weight changes in females necropsied on GD 28 were noted in the liver, kidneys, and spleen as follows:Liver weight (absolute and relative to body weight) was statistically increased at 25 mg/kg/week (+16% and +18% difference from vehicle control, respectively) and 75 mg/kg/week (+40% and +39% difference from vehicle control, respectively)
- Kidney weight (absolute and relative to body weight) was statistically increased at 75 mg/kg/week (+15% and +14% difference from vehicle control, respectively)Increased liver and kidney weights were consistent with the uptake of ISIS 546254.
- Spleen weight (absolute and relative to body weight) was statistically increased at 75 mg/kg/week (+45% and +44% difference from vehicle control, respectively)
- ISIS 546254 concentrations in the maternal liver of vehicle control females on GD 28 were below the limit of quantitation. ISIS 546254 concentrations increased in the maternal liver of females on GD 20 (TK animals) and GD 28 with increase in ISIS 546254 dose, with concentrations on GD 28 about half of the concentrations on GD 20 (TK animals). ISIS 546254 concentrations in the fetal liver were below the limit of quantitation in all ISIS 546254-treated groups. ISIS 546254 concentrations in the placenta were below the limit of quantitation at 12.5
L3723: mg/kg/week ISIS 546254 and at &lt;10% of maternal exposures at 25 and 75 mg/kg/week ISIS 546254.
L3724: - There was no effect of ISIS 546254 on fecundity as the fecundity index was similar between 12.5, 25, and 75 mg/kg/week (88%, 100%, and 84%, respectively) and the vehicle control (91%).
- There were no effects of ISIS 546254 on gravid uterine weight, the number of corpora lutea, the number of implantations, the implantation index, percent of early or late resorptions, live fetuses, the sex ratio, or fetal viability.
- Mean fetal weight appeared to decrease at 75 mg/kg/week for males (-12.3% difference from vehicle control; statistically significant), females (-10.4% difference from vehicle control), and combined (-11.6% difference from vehicle control; statistically significant)
- The embryo-fetal mortality index at 12.5, 25, and 75 mg/kg/week (5.0%, 5.7%, and 6.7%, respectively) was increased (not statistically significant) compared to the vehicle control (1.3%). The percent of dead fetuses/implantation site at 12.5, 25, and 75 mg/kg/week (1.3%, 0.3%, and 5.8%, respectively) was increased (statistically significant at 75 mg/kg/week only) compared to the vehicle control (0%). As stated in the study report, although these changes were noticeable and statistically significant at 75 mg/kg/week, they were consistent with what is noted in the vehicle control animals in these types of studies, therefore, a clear relationship to test article cannot be established.
- Overall, there were no fetal external findings, visceral variations or malformations, or skeletal variations or malformations attributed to treatment with ISIS 546254 in rabbits.
L3725: ## Prenatal and Postnatal Development
L3726: In the PPND toxicity study, F0 female mice were treated by SC administration with vehicle control (0.9% Sodium Chloride for Injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg/week), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (5 mg/kg/week) every other day from GD 6 to GD 18 and weekly from Lactation Day (LD) 1 to LD 20 (the treatment period encompassed organogenesis through weaning). Since ISIS 721744 is not active in mice, the mouse-surrogate ISIS 722059 was included in the study to assess the potential effects related to the target inhibition. ISIS 722059 statistically decreased PKK mRNA expression in the liver of F0 female mice by 82% on LD 22. SC administration of ISIS 721744 (up to 20 mg/kg/week) or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (5 mg/kg/week) did not affect pregnancy in F0 females or prenatal and postnatal development (including behavioral, fertility, and reproduction function) in F1 offspring. ISIS 721744 was present in milk of lactating F0 females at 10 and 20 mg/kg/week.
L3727: ## Safety Evaluation:
L3728: In the combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice, SC administration of ISIS 721744 (up to 10 mg/kg/week) or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (4 mg/kg/week) did not affect fertility, pregnancy, or embryofetal development. In the PPND toxicity study in mice, SC administration of ISIS 721744 (up to 20 mg/kg/week) or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (5 mg/kg/week) did not affect pregnancy in F0 females or prenatal and postnatal development (including behavioral, fertility, and reproduction
L3729: function) in F1 offspring. The reproductive and developmental toxicology studies with ISIS 721744 did not provide TK of ISIS 721744 from blood (e.g., AUC and Cmax exposures) for which to calculate exposure margins between the animal and clinical studies.
L3730: In a combined fertility and developmental toxicity study in mice, SC administration of ISIS 546254 (up to 84 mg/kg/week), unconjugated parent compound of ISIS 721744, or unconjugated mouse surrogate ISIS 482584 (84 mg/kg/week) did not affect fertility, pregnancy, or embryofetal development. In an EFD study in rabbits, SC administration of ISIS 546254 (up to 75 mg/kg/week) every other day from GD 6 to GD 18 did not result in any fetal external findings, visceral variations or malformations, or skeletal variations or malformations attributed to treatment with ISIS 546254.
L3731: Conclusion: The reproductive and developmental toxicology studies were judged to be adequate to support the safety of ISIS 721744 for marketing. There are no outstanding concerns from the nonclinical perspective with respect to the reproductive toxicity assessment.

L3749: ## 1 Executive Summary
L3750: ## 1.1 Introduction
L3751: Ionis Pharmaceuticals Inc. (Applicant) submitted a 505(b)(1) New Drug Application (NDA) for subcutaneous (SC) administration of donidalorsen (ISIS 721744) as 80 mg (b) (4) (or 80 mg (b) (4) in some patients) prophylaxis to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. ISIS 721744 is an N-acetyl galactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated antisense oligonucleotide (ASO), which targets prekallikrein (PKK). The GalNAc molecule preferentially delivers ISIS 721744 to the liver.
L3752: This review focuses on the evaluation of the 6-month carcinogenicity study of ISIS 721744, as well as the mouse surrogate, ISIS 722059, by SC injection in CByB6F1-Tg(HRAS)2Jic Hemizygous Transgenic mice (Tg.rash2 mice). The mouse is not a pharmacologically relevant species with ISIS 721744 and this study primarily assessed off-target toxicity. As such, the mouse surrogate, ISIS 722059, was included to assess the effect of the intended pharmacology to inhibit synthesis of PKK. The Executive Carcinogenicity Assessment Committee (ECAC) concurred with the doses for the study in male mice but could not recommend doses for female mice (refer to Carcinogenicity Special Protocol Assessment-2 [SPA-2] agreement dated 11/16/2022).
L3753: Of note, a two-year carcinogenicity study in Sprague Dawley (SD) rats is in progress. The Division previously agreed that it would be acceptable to submit a summary of the in-life data for the 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats at the time of the NDA submission and to submit the final report as a post marketing requirement (PMR) (Refer to IND 142564 pre-NDA Meeting Preliminary Comments dated 04/10/2024). Per the Applicant, at the time of the NDA submission, the 2-year rat study was at &gt;Week 74 of treatment. The final study report is expected to be available around Quarter 4 (Q4) of 2025.
L3754: This review also provides an evaluation of the genotoxicity studies with ISIS 721744.
L3755: ## 1.2 Brief Discussion of Nonclinical Findings
L3756: The genotoxic potential of ISIS 721744 was evaluated in the Good Laboratory Practice (GLP)-compliant in vitro Ames assay, in vitro chromosome aberration assay, and in vivo mammalian micronucleus assay in mice. The carcinogenic potential of ISIS 721744 (off-target) and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (intended pharmacology to inhibit PKK synthesis) was evaluated in the GLP-compliant 6-month carcinogenicity study in Tg.rash2 mice.
L3757: The in vitro Ames assay, using the plate incorporation method, was conducted to evaluate the potential mutagenicity of ISIS 721744 (15 to 5000 mcg/plate) in *S. typhimurium* TA98, TA100, TA1535 and TA1537, and *E. coli* WP2uvrA tester strains (with or without 10% S9 mix for metabolic activation). There was no increase in the number of revertant colonies in any tester strain, at any ISIS 721744 concentration up to 5000 µg/plate, with or without metabolic activation. ISIS 721744 was negative for
L3758: mutagenicity up to 5000 µg/plate with or without metabolic activation. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 08/13/2019 for further information.
L3759: The in vitro chromosome aberration assay was conducted to evaluate the clastogenic potential of ISIS 721744 (62.5 to 500 mcg/mL) in Chinese hamster lung (CHL) cells for 6 hours (with or without 2% S9 mix for metabolic activation) and for 22 hours (without S9 mix). No cytotoxicity was noted at up to 500 mcg/mL ISIS 721744 after 6 hours with or without 2% S9 mix and 22 hours without S9 mix. There was no significant increase in the number of metaphases with structural aberrations up to 500 mcg/mL ISIS 721744 after 6 hours (with or without 2% S9 mix) and 22 hours (without S9 mix). ISIS 721744 was negative for clastogenicity up to 500 mcg/mL with or without S9 in cultured CHL cells. Refer to the IND 142564 Nonclinical Primary Review dated 08/13/2019 for further information.
L3760: The in vivo mammalian micronucleus assay was conducted to evaluate the potential clastogenicity of ISIS 721744 (500, 1000, and 2000 mg/kg SC) administered on Days 1 and 3 (48 hours postdose on Day 1) to ICR mice. Mice were sacrificed on Day 4 (24 hours postdose on Day 3) for bone marrow collection. There was no statistically significant increase in the incidence of micronucleated polychromatic erythrocytes (MNPCs) at any dose of ISIS 721744 tested compared to the vehicle control (negative control) group. ISIS 721744 was negative in the in vivo bone marrow micronucleus assay in mice. Refer to **Section 7** for further information.
L3761: **Conclusion: Overall, ISIS 721744 was not genotoxic in a complete battery of genotoxicity assays.**
L3762: The 6-month study in Tg.rasH2 mice was conducted to evaluate the carcinogenic potential of ISIS 721744 (off-target) and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (intended pharmacology to inhibit PKK synthesis). Tg.rasH2 mice (n = 25/sex/group) were administered vehicle control (0.9% sodium chloride for injection, USP), ISIS 721744 (5, 10, or 20 mg/kg/dose for males and 10, 20, or 60 mg/kg/dose for females), or mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 (10 mg/kg/dose) every two weeks (Q2W) for up to 6 months by SC injection. A positive control group was also included in which Tg.rasH2 mice (10/sex) were administered urethane (500 mg/kg/dose) via intraperitoneal (IP) injection on Days 1, 3, and 5. A maximum tolerated dose (MTD) was achieved at the high dose of 20 mg/kg Q2W in males based on histopathology findings in the liver and elevations of glutamate dehydrogenase [GLDH]. The high dose of 60 mg/kg Q2W in females did not meet the criteria for a MTD.
L3763: There was no statistically significant increase or decrease in mortality dose response across the vehicle control and ISIS 721744-treated groups, in either male or female mice. There was a statistically significant decrease in mortality in the male 5 mg/kg/dose group (low dose) compared to the vehicle control group.
L3764: Effects on clinical chemistry included increases in aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and GLDH in males at 10 and 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS
L3765: 721744 and females at 60 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, which correlated with histopathology findings in the liver.
L3766: Neoplastic histopathology findings of hepatocellular adenoma in the liver were seen in 1/25 males at 5 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, 2/25 males at 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, and 1/25 males at 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059. The adenomas at 20 mg/kg/dose were accompanied by several non-neoplastic findings in the liver (see below). Based on the FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation, there was no statistically significant dose response relationship across the vehicle control and the ISIS 721744-treated groups in any tumor types in either male or female mice. The pairwise comparisons also showed no tumor types with a statistically significant increase in tumor incidences in ISIS 721744- or ISIS 722059-treated groups, when compared to the vehicle control group in either male or female mice.
L3767: Non-neoplastic histopathology findings in ISIS-721744-treated and/or ISIS-722059 mice were noted in the **liver** (microvesicular hepatocellular vacuolation, basophilic pigmented macrophages, hepatocellular single cell necrosis, karyocytomegaly, and/or basophilic focus of cellular alteration); **kidney** (epithelial vacuolation and epithelial basophilic granules); **injection site** (macrophage granular vacuolation); **urinary bladder** (urothelial vacuolation); and the **axillary and/or mesenteric lymph nodes** (macrophage vacuolation). All histopathological findings were attributed to or a consequence of oligonucleotide uptake.
L3768: The positive control (urethane) group resulted in neoplastic findings consistent with known effects of urethane administration1 and confirmed the carcinogenic responsiveness of the Tg.rasH2 model.
L3769: The mouse is not a pharmacologically relevant species for ISIS 721744, so the study included one dose group treated with mouse surrogate ISIS 722059. Hepatic PKK mRNA expression was statistically reduced in male and female mice treated with 10 mg/kg/dose ISIS 722059 Q2W for 26 weeks by 94% and 79%, respectively, compared to controls.
L3770: **Conclusion:** Treatment with ISIS 721744 resulted in hepatocellular adenoma in 2/25 males at 20 mg/kg/dose ISIS 721744, which was not statistically significant based on FDA Statistical Review and Evaluation. The ECAC concluded that the carcinogenicity study was adequate for male mice and negative for drug-related tumors. However, the carcinogenicity study was inadequate for female mice because a MTD was not achieved and no other valid basis to support the high dose was discernable.
L3771: 1National Toxicology Program. 15th Report on Carcinogens [Internet]. Research Triangle Park (NC): National Toxicology Program; 2021 Dec 21. Urethane: CAS No. 51-79-6. Available from: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK590786/
L3772: ## 1.3 Recommendations
L3773: The final study results for the 6-month carcinogenicity study of ISIS 721744, as well as the mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 in Tg.rasH2 mice were presented to the ECAC on 12/10/2024. The ECAC concluded that the carcinogenicity study was adequate for male mice and negative for drug-related tumors. However, the carcinogenicity study was inadequate for female mice because a MTD was not achieved and no other valid basis to support the high dose was discernable.

L3821: ## 2.6 Proposed Clinical Population and Dosing Regimen
L3822: Donidalorsen is indicated for prophylaxis to prevent attacks of HAE in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. The recommended dosage is 80 mg administered SC (b) (4). A dosing interval of (b) (4) may be considered in some patients.
L3823: ## 2.7 Regulatory Background
L3824: At the pre-NDA meeting, the Division agreed that it would be acceptable to submit the report of the 6-month carcinogenicity study in Tg.rasH2 mice and a summary of the in-life data for the 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats at the time of the NDA submission and to submit the final report as a PMR (Refer to IND 142564 pre-NDA Meeting Preliminary Comments dated 04/10/2024). This replaced comments conveyed from the End of Phase 2 (EOP2) meeting in which the Applicant was requested to provide reports for the 6-month carcinogenicity study in Tg.rasH2 mice and the 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats at the time of an NDA (Refer to IND 142564 EOP2 Meeting Minutes dated 10/18/2021).
L3825: In the EOP2 meeting package, the Applicant had indicated their plan to conduct a 6-month carcinogenicity study in Tg.rasH2 mice and to seek a waiver for a 2-year rat carcinogenicity study for ISIS 721744. Based on input from the ECAC, the conduct of a 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats could not be waived. As such, it was recommended that the protocols for the 6-month carcinogenicity study in Tg.rasH2 mice and the 2-year carcinogenicity study in rats, along with supporting dose range-finding (DRF) studies, be submitted for evaluation by the ECAC (Refer to IND 142564 EOP2 Meeting Minutes dated 10/18/2021).
L3826: The carcinogenicity SPA-2 for a 6-month study in Tg.rasH2 mice with ISIS 721744 and mouse surrogate ISIS 722059 was submitted on 10/12/2022 (SDN 36). The 14-week DRF study in Tg.rasH2 and proposed protocol were reviewed (refer to Nonclinical Primary Review dated 12/12/2022) and presented to the ECAC on 11/15/2022.
L3827: ECAC Recommendations and Conclusions for 6-Month Study in Tg.rasH2 Mice
L3828: - The Committee concurred with doses of 0 (0.9% sodium chloride for injection, USP), 5, 10, and 20 mg/kg Q2W via SC injection in male mice with the high dose based on a MTD (i.e., incidences of karyocytomegaly and increases of ALT, AST, and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) in male mice at higher doses in the 14-week DRF study). The mid and low doses are based on adequate dose spacing.
- For female mice, the Committee could not recommend doses for the proposed study, as no acceptable basis for dose selection could be identified. If the Sponsor would like ECAC concurrence for dose selection, a new DRF study should be conducted to identify an acceptable high dose as outlined in ICH S1C(R2) or ICH S1B(R1).
- The Committee noted that the 6-month carcinogenicity study will be performed in a different facility than used in the 14-week DRF study. The carcinogenicity study may not be acceptable if toxicity is significantly different due to this change such that dose selection would have been altered.
- The Committee noted that the planned ophthalmic examinations in the proposed carcinogenicity study are not needed by FDA.
- If there are survival issues during the study, the Sponsor should contact the Review Division before any changes are made.
L3829: Refer to IND 142564 ECAC Protocol Minutes dated 11/16/2022 for more details.

L3845: ## Key Study Findings
L3846: The in vivo mammalian micronucleus assay was conducted to evaluate potential clastogenicity of ISIS 721744 (500, 1000, and 2000 mg/kg SC) administered on Days 1 and 3 (48 hours postdose on Day 1) to ICR male mice. Mice were sacrificed on Day 4 (24 hours postdose on Day 3) for bone marrow collection. There was no statistically significant increase in the frequencies of MNPCEs at any dose of ISIS 721744 tested compared to the vehicle control (negative control) group. ISIS 721744 was negative for clastogenic potential in the in vivo bone marrow micronucleus assay in mice.
L3847: ## Methods (Table 2, Applicant's Table)
L3848: Doses in definitive study:	500, 1000, or 2000 mg/kg ISIS 721744

There were no mortality, abnormal clinical signs, or body weight changes in either male or female mice at ISIS 721744 doses up to 2000 mg/kg (limit dose for studies of 14 days or less). As such, the ISIS 721744 doses for the definitive micronucleus study were chosen to be 500, 1000, and 2000 mg/kg (limit dose according to OECD TG No. 474 and ICH S2(R1)).
Negative control:	Sterile 0.9% sodium chloride
